readings.translation: He did (it). / He made (it).
readings.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the simple/unmarked past (no restriction to a time-frame)

notes.role: लुङ् — past action without a time restriction → the aorist → अकार्षीत्

readings.vyakhya: सामान्ये भूते लुङ्। अकार्षीत् — न अद्यतनानद्यतनविशेषः। कृ-धातोः सिजन्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The लुङ् aorist is the UNMARKED past: plain "did," with none of the today/before-today restrictions that लङ् (अकरोत्, imperfect) and लिट् (चकार, perfect) carry — 3.2.110 simply says लुङ् for past action. √कृ → अकार्षीत् "he did," with the augment अ and the सिच् marker. So √कृ now spans all four pasts-and-presents: करोति · अकरोत् · चकार · अकार्षीत्, plus the future करिष्यति. The full time-axis of one root.

readings.translation: The boy cooks; the rice is cooked.
readings.teaches: कर्तरि शप् vs कर्मणि यक् — the विकरण (stem-marker) shows the voice: active शप् (अ) vs passive यक् (य)

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — in the active, the विकरण शप् (अ) → पच् + अ + ति → पचति

words.gloss: the rice — subject of the passive clause

notes.en: the object, raised to nominative in the passive

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — in the passive, the विकरण यक् (य) → पच् + य + ते → पच्यते

readings.vyakhya: कर्तरि शप्, कर्मणि यक्। पच् + अ → पचति; पच् + य → पच्यते। विकरणः प्रयोगं सूचयति।
readings.vyakhya_en: What tells active from passive is the विकरण — the little stem-marker between root and ending. Active uses शप्, अ (3.1.68 कर्तरि शप्): पच् + अ + ति → पचति "cooks." Passive uses यक्, य (3.1.67 सार्वधातुके यक्): पच् + य + ते → पच्यते "is cooked." Same root पच्, same tense; the विकरण अ vs य, and the ending परस्मै- vs आत्मनेपद, carry the whole voice contrast.

readings.sentence: भवामि भवावः भवामः। भवसि भवथः भवथ। भवति भवतः भवन्ति।
readings.translation: Present tense of भू "be", all nine cells: I/we-two/we am/are; you/you-two/you-all are; he/those-two/they are.
readings.teaches: the whole present-tense paradigm — three पुरुष across three वचन

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — the ending series; 1sg मिप् → भवामि
तिप्तस्झि… → 3sg तिप् → भवति
बहुषु बहुवचनम् → plural → भवन्ति

readings.vyakhya: लटि परस्मैपदस्य नव तिङः — त्रयः पुरुषाः त्रीणि वचनानि च। भू + शप् + तिङ् = भवति इत्यादि।
readings.vyakhya_en: You met the तिङ् frame one cell at a time (ex014–016, ex092). Here is the WHOLE present-tense paradigm of भू "be" in one place — the verbal counterpart to the देव declension table (ex094). Read across each row for a person (उत्तम / मध्यम / प्रथम), down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl). The nine endings come from one master sūtra, तिप्तस्झि… (3.4.78); the stem is भू + शप् (अ) → भव-. Learn these nine and every parasmaipada present (गच्छति, पठति, वदति) falls into place.

chapters.title: सन्धि — the sound-changes at word and morpheme joins

readings.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
readings.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

readings.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
readings.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

readings.translation: "not here" → नेह
readings.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
readings.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

readings.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
readings.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

readings.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
readings.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades of इ and उ.

readings.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
readings.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

readings.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
readings.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

readings.translation: Hari dwells among the sages.
readings.teaches: one sentence, both sibilant outcomes — हरिः takes visarga, ऋषिषु takes ष्

notes.en: nominative — the ending स् stands at a pause before a vowel

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of the ending → visarga → हरिः
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the स् of सु → ष् after the इ → ऋषिषु

readings.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये द्वौ सकारौ द्वयोः गत्योः — हरिः इति विसर्जनीयः, ऋषिषु इति षत्वम्। उभयत्र इकारः पूर्वः, फलम् तु भिन्नम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Both words end their stem in इ and both have an ending in स्, and the two स् go different ways: हरिः becomes visarga, ऋषिषु becomes ष्. What separates them is where the स् stands — at the end of the word in हरिः, with nothing after it to give it a place, and inside the word in ऋषिषु, with a उ following. The इ before it is the same in both.

readings.translation: "again and again" — पुनर् at the pause shows as पुनः
readings.teaches: रु → visarga before a hard consonant and at the pause (खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः)

notes.text: the word ends in र्; before a vowel or soft sound it stays पुनर् — पुनर् अपि

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — र् → visarga before a खर् consonant and at the pause

notes.text: the second one stands at the pause, and takes the visarga for that reason alone

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — अवसान, the pause, is the other trigger

readings.vyakhya: खरि अवसाने च रोः विसर्जनीयः। पुनर् → पुनः। स्वरे तु पुनर् अपि इति तिष्ठति।
readings.vyakhya_en: One rule, two triggers. The र् of पुनर् becomes visarga both before a hard consonant (पुनः कः) and at a pause, where nothing follows at all — पुनः पुनः shows the second case twice over. Before a vowel the र् survives: पुनर् अपि. So the visarga is not part of the word; it is what the word's final र् turns into when the surroundings give it nothing voiced to lean on.

readings.translation: "in the fires" → अग्निषु
readings.teaches: षत्व — the ending's स् becomes ष् after an इ (आदेशप्रत्ययोः)

notes.text: the ending is सु; its स् meets the इ of अग्नि

notes.role: आदेशप्रत्ययोः — a प्रत्यय's स् goes ष् after an इण् vowel → अग्निषु

readings.vyakhya: प्रत्ययस्य सकारः इण्कुभ्याम् उत्तरः षकारः। अग्नि + सु = अग्निषु। न तु सर्वः सकारः — प्रत्ययस्य एव।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locative plural ending सु carries a स्, and after the इ of अग्नि that स् retroflexes to ष् — अग्निषु. The rule is narrow in a way worth noticing: it applies to the स् of an ending, not to every स् in the language. A स् that belongs to the stem itself is untouched by it, which is why the same इ does nothing to the स् of a following separate word.

readings.translation: "speech here" → वाग् अत्र
readings.teaches: जश्त्व — a word-final hard stop softens to its voiced counterpart

notes.en: the soft (voiced) stops ग् ज् ड् द् ब्

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a stop at word's end becomes its जश् (voiced) counterpart; क् → ग्

notes.text: वाक् → वाग्

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते झलां जश्। क् → ग्, यथा वाक् → वाग्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A hard stop standing at the end of a word softens to its voiced partner: क्→ग्, त्→द्, प्→ब्. So वाक् "speech" appears as वाग् before अत्र. The word's lemma is वाक्; its sentence-form follows the join.

readings.translation: "and that" → तच्च
readings.teaches: श्चुत्व — a dental meeting a palatal becomes palatal

notes.text: तत् + च: dental त् meets palatal च

notes.en: the palatal series श् च् छ् ज् झ् ञ्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — a dental (त-class/स) next to a palatal (च-class/श) turns palatal; त् → च्

notes.text: त् → च् → तच्च

readings.vyakhya: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुत्वम्। त् + च → च् + च = च्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A dental sound touching a palatal is pulled into the palatal series: तत् + च → तच्च. The त् becomes च् to match the following च. Assimilation — the first sound takes on the place of the second.

readings.translation: "the forest laughs" → वनं हसति
readings.teaches: a word-final म् becomes anusvāra (ं) before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — a word-final म् before a consonant becomes anusvāra; म् → ं

notes.text: वनम् → वनं (before हसति)

readings.vyakhya: पदान्ते मकारस्य हलि अनुस्वारः। वनम् → वनं हसति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A म् at the end of a word, when a consonant follows, contracts to the anusvāra ं: वनम् हसति → वनं हसति. (Before a vowel, or at a true pause, the म् stays — so it is the following consonant that triggers the change.)

readings.translation: "by Rāma": रामेन → रामेण (न becomes ण after र)
readings.teaches: णत्व — न् becomes ण् after र्/ष् in the same word

notes.text: राम + इन (instr.sg ending ट्→इन): the न् stands after the र् of राम

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्
अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि → the change still applies across an intervening vowel/guttural/labial (here the ए) → रामेण

readings.vyakhya: रेफात् परः नकारः णकारः समानपदे, अट्-व्यवधानेऽपि। रामेन → रामेण।
readings.vyakhya_en: Within one word, a न् turns cerebral (ण्) when an र् or ष् precedes it (8.4.1) — even when a vowel, guttural, or labial stands between them (8.4.2). So राम + the instrumental -इन gives रामेण, not *रामेन*: the र् of राम reaches across the ए to retroflex the न्. This णत्व is why we say रामायण, ब्राह्मणः, नारायण.

readings.translation: "Rāma the sixth" → रामष्षष्ठः (स/त-series cerebralised by ष)
readings.teaches: ष्टुत्व — स् and the dentals turn cerebral (ष्/ट-series) next to ष् or a cerebral

notes.text: रामस् + षष्ठः: a dental स् meets the cerebral ष्

notes.en: cerebralisation — स्/तवर्ग → ष्/टवर्ग in contact with ष् or a cerebral

notes.role: ष्टुना ष्टुः → स् and the dentals next to ष्/टवर्ग become ष्/टवर्ग → रामष्षष्ठः

readings.vyakhya: षकारटवर्गसन्निधौ सकारतवर्गयोः ष्टुत्वम्। रामस् षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Mirror of श्चुत्व (which palatalised before श्/च-series): ष्टुत्व *cerebralises*. A dental स् or त-series sound, meeting a cerebral ष् or ट-series sound, itself becomes cerebral (8.4.41). रामस् + षष्ठः → रामष्षष्ठः; तत् + टीका → तट्टीका. The articulation simply assimilates to its neighbour's place — the same logic as जश्त्व and श्चुत्व, one row over.

readings.sentence: सम् कृतम् → संस्कृतम् (सङ्… → the nasal homorganic).
readings.translation: "well-made" सम्+कृत → the nasal matches the following stop
readings.teaches: अनुस्वार → परसवर्ण — anusvāra becomes the nasal of the following class

notes.text: सम् + कृत: final म् → anusvāra (8.3.23), then the anusvāra may take the class-nasal

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः → word-final म् before a consonant → anusvāra (संकृत)

notes.en: the nasal homogeneous with the following sound

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः → the anusvāra becomes the class-nasal of the following यय् consonant

readings.vyakhya: मकारः अनुस्वारः, सः ययि परसवर्णः। सम् + कृत → संकृत → सङ्… परसवर्णेन।
readings.vyakhya_en: A final म् before a consonant first becomes anusvāra (8.3.23, the rule that gave वनं); then that anusvāra may take the *homorganic* nasal — the nasal belonging to the following sound's class (8.4.58). सम् + कृतम् → संस्कृतम्; सम् + गतः → सङ्गतः (the guttural ङ् before ग). The nasal quietly tunes itself to whatever stop follows.

readings.translation: "homage to thee": the विसर्ग returns to स् before त
readings.teaches: विसर्ग → स् — a visarga becomes स् before a hard dental (खर्)

notes.en: a join — the two words are written as one

notes.text: नमः + ते: the visarga of नमः meets the त् of ते

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः → a visarga → स् before a खर् consonant → नमस्ते

notes.text: नमस् here is a गति/preverb-like form; 8.3.40 also fixes its स् → नमस्ते, नमस्कारः

readings.vyakhya: विसर्गस्य सकारः खरि। नमः + ते → नमस्ते। पुनः सकारः प्रत्येति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The visarga is not the end of the story — before a hard consonant (खर्) it can revert to स् (8.3.34): नमः + ते → नमस्ते, नमः + कारः → नमस्कारः. The final स् of नरः became visarga before pause (8.2.66 → 8.3.15); here the reverse environment pulls the visarga back to स्. Sandhi is contextual all the way down: the same sound shows different faces by what stands next.

readings.translation: He too goes.
readings.teaches: visarga → ओ before a voiced sound (अतो रोः → उ, then गुण ओ); the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ

notes.text: विग्रह: सः + अपि; the अः before a voiced sound → ओ, and अ of अपि elides (ऽ)

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — अः (from रु) becomes उ before a voiced sound → स उ
आद्गुणः — अ + उ → गुण ओ → सो; the following अ drops (पूर्वरूप), marked ऽ

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: अतो रोः उत्वम्, ततः गुणः। सः + अपि = सोऽपि। लोपे अवग्रहः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The commonest visarga outcome: सः before a voiced sound. The अः (a visarga from रु, 8.2.66) becomes उ (6.1.113), then अ + उ fuse by गुण to ओ (6.1.87) → सो; the following short अ then drops, written with the अवग्रह ऽ. सः + अपि → सोऽपि "he too." This is why सः appears as सो only before voiced sounds — before a vowel other than अ, or a consonant, it shifts differently.

readings.translation: Salutation to you.
readings.teaches: visarga → स् before a त्-class stop (विसर्जनीयस्य सः)

notes.text: विग्रह: नमः + ते; the visarge before त् becomes स् (its homorganic sibilant)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before a sibilant/dental-स् context → नमस्

readings.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः सवर्णे। नमः + ते = नमस्ते।
readings.vyakhya_en: Before a dental, the visarga assimilates to स् (8.3.34, विसर्जनीयस्य सः). नमः + ते → नमस्ते "salutations to you" — the visarga of नमः becomes स् before the त् of ते. The same gives दुस्तर (दुः + तर), निस्तेज (निः + तेज): visarga takes the sibilant of the place that follows.

readings.translation: He covers over.
readings.teaches: छ-doubling (तुक्) — a short vowel before छ inserts त् → च्छ (छे च)

notes.text: विग्रह: आ + छादयति; before छ a त् (तुक्) is inserted → च्छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel (here the आ-preverb context) before छ takes the augment तुक् (त्) → च्छ

readings.vyakhya: छकारे परे तुक् (त्); त् + छ = च्छ। आ + छादयति = आच्छादयति।
readings.vyakhya_en: छ never stands alone after a vowel: छे च (6.1.73) inserts the augment तुक् (त्), and त् + छ surfaces as च्छ. आ + छादयति → आच्छादयति "covers over." The same doubling gives तच्छ्रुत्वा (तत् + छ्रुत्वा... via श्), शिवच्छाया (शिव + छाया "Śiva's shade"): a vowel + छ always becomes -च्छ-.

readings.translation: For this (is so).
readings.teaches: before ह, a stop voices and doubles it — here त् + ह gives द्ध

notes.text: विग्रह: एतत् + हि; final त् → द् (जश्त्व) before voiced ह, and ह → ध (झयो हः)

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — final त् voices to द् before a voiced sound
झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् — ह after a झय् stop optionally becomes its voiced aspirate → ध

notes.en: "for, indeed" (the ह that triggers the change)

readings.vyakhya: अन्त्यस्य जश्त्वम् (त्→द्), झयः परस्य हस्य घोषवदादेशः (ह→ध)। एतत् + हि = एतद्धि।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two changes meet at त् + ह. First जश्त्व: the final त् voices to द् before the voiced ह (8.2.39). Then the ह, now after a voiced stop, optionally becomes that stop's voiced aspirate — झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् (8.4.62) — so ह → ध and the cluster surfaces as द्ध: एतत् + हि → एतद्धि. The same gives तद्धित (तत् + हित), वाग्घरि (वाक् + हरि): a stop + ह coalesces into a doubled voiced aspirate.

readings.translation: He delights again.
readings.teaches: visarga → र् before a voiced sound — the other outcome, beside सोऽपि

notes.text: पुनः ends in रु; before a voiced sound the visarga surfaces as र् (not ओ)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — word-final स् → रु; its visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
अतो रोः — applies to अ-final रु (सः→सो); पुनर् keeps र् because its base is पुनर्, not अतः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: रेफान्तस्य रुत्वम् घोषे। पुनः + रमते = पुनर् रमते। (अतो भिन्नत्वात् न ओत्वम्।)
readings.vyakhya_en: Not every visarga becomes ओ. Words whose underlying final is -र् (पुनर्, अन्तर्, प्रातर्) show र् before a voiced sound, NOT the अ + उ → ओ fusion of ex155. पुनः + रमते → पुनर् रमते "delights again." Contrast सोऽपि (सः, base स-अः → सो) with पुनर् (base पुनर्): the visarga's outcome depends on what stands under it — an अ that fuses to ओ, or an र् that simply reappears.

readings.sentence: रामः च लक्ष्मणः च → रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च।
readings.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
readings.teaches: visarga → श् before a च्-class stop (श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant)

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः + च; visarga → स् (8.3.34), then स् → श् before च् (श्चुत्व)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before the following stop
स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — स्/त् before a च्-class sound become श्/च् → रामश्च

notes.text: same change: लक्ष्मणः + च → लक्ष्मणश्च

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः → श् before च

readings.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सः, ततः श्चुत्वम्। रामः + च = रामश्च। द्वयोः योगे चकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The visarga before a च-class stop ends up as श्. First it becomes स् (8.3.34); then स् before च् is cerebralised — really palatalised — to श् by स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40). रामः च → रामश्च, लक्ष्मणः च → लक्ष्मणश्च, the standard "X and Y" linkage. The visarga's three sibilant outcomes — स् (before त्, ex156), श् (before च्, here), ष् (before ट्) — all follow the place of the stop that comes next.

chapters.title: समास — compounds: two words joined into one

readings.sentence: नीलोत्पलम् जले तिष्ठति। ग्रामगतः बालः तत् पश्यति। असत्यम् न वदति, गोहितम् च करोति।
readings.translation: A blue lotus stands in the water. A boy who has gone to the village sees it. He speaks no untruth, and does what is good for cattle.
readings.teaches:
four तत्पुरुष/कर्मधारय subtypes, each named by its विग्रह — नीलोत्पलम् (कर्मधारय),
ग्रामगतः (द्वितीया-), असत्यम् (नञ्-), गोहितम् (चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष).

notes.en: descriptive — नीलम् उत्पलम्, both members in the same case, one qualifying the other

notes.text: विग्रह: नीलम् उत्पलम् — "the lotus which is blue"

notes.role: विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम् — an adjective compounds with its noun → कर्मधारय

notes.en: determinative — ग्रामम् गतः, the first member is the द्वितीया goal

notes.text: विग्रह: ग्रामम् गतः — "gone to the village"

notes.role: द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतितगतात्यस्तप्राप्तापन्नैः — a द्वितीया word compounds with गत etc. → द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष

notes.text: विग्रह: न सत्यम् — "untruth"

notes.role: नञ् — नञ् (न) compounds with a following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: determinative — गोभ्यो हितम्, the first member is the चतुर्थी beneficiary

notes.text: विग्रह: गोभ्यो हितम् — "good for the cattle"

notes.role: चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थबलिहितसुखरक्षितैः — a चतुर्थी word compounds with हित etc. → चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: चत्वारः तत्पुरुषभेदाः — नीलोत्पलम्, ग्रामगतः, असत्यम्, गोहितम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Four sub-classes of the same family, each told apart by its विग्रह.
नीलोत्पलम् is a कर्मधारय — नीलम् उत्पलम्, adjective and noun in one case
(2.1.57). ग्रामगतः is a द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष — ग्रामम् गतः, "gone TO the village"
(2.1.24). असत्यम् is the नञ्-तत्पुरुष, न सत्यम् "untruth" (2.2.6). And गोहितम्
is a चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष — गोभ्यो हितम्, "good FOR cattle" (2.1.36). The compound
hides the case; the विग्रह restores it.

readings.translation: the king's man (विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: तत्पुरुष — the second member is primary, and the first qualifies it

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the man of the king"

notes.role: प्राक् कडारात् समासः — from here the combinations are named समास

notes.en: determinative — the second member is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: उत्तरपदार्थप्रधानः तत्पुरुषः। राजपुरुषः — पुरुषः प्रधानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In a तत्पुरुष the second member is the head and the first qualifies it: राजपुरुषः is a kind of पुरुष (man) — the king's. Resolve it (विग्रह) as राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the man of the king." The compound is whatever its last member is.

readings.translation: Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च)
readings.teaches: द्वन्द्व — members are coordinate ("and"); none subordinate

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः च कृष्णः च

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: dual — two people, so the compound is dual

readings.vyakhya: उभयपदार्थप्रधानः द्वन्द्वः। रामः च कृष्णः च = रामकृष्णौ।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्वन्द्व joins members that would each stand with "and" — none is subordinate, both are heads: रामः च कृष्णः च collapses to रामकृष्णौ, "Rāma and Kṛṣṇa." Two people, so the compound itself is dual.

readings.translation: the yellow-clothed one [Viṣṇu] (विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः)
readings.teaches: बहुव्रीहि — neither member is the head; the compound points outside itself

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.text: विग्रह: पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य सः

notes.en: possessive / exocentric — denotes someone characterised by the members

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

readings.vyakhya: अन्यपदार्थप्रधानः बहुव्रीहिः। पीतम् अम्बरम् यस्य — सः विष्णुः।
readings.vyakhya_en: A बहुव्रीहि names neither member: पीताम्बरः is not "yellow" and not "garment" but the one who has a yellow garment — Viṣṇu. The sense lies OUTSIDE the compound (अन्यपदार्थ). Resolve with यस्य: "he whose (यस्य) garment is yellow."

readings.translation: near Kṛṣṇa (विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम्)
readings.teaches: अव्ययीभाव — the first member, an indeclinable, is primary, and the whole behaves as one

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णस्य समीपम् — उप = "near"

notes.en: adverbial — the compound behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable (here उप) is अव्ययीभाव

readings.vyakhya: पूर्वपदार्थप्रधानः अव्ययीभावः। उप कृष्णस्य समीपम् — सर्वम् अव्ययम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: In an अव्ययीभाव the first member — an indeclinable like उप ("near") — is primary, and the whole compound becomes an indeclinable itself: उपकृष्णम्, "near Kṛṣṇa," fixed in form. Four types, four answers to one question: which member carries the sense?

readings.translation: a great man (विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः)
readings.teaches: कर्मधारय — a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case (adjective + noun)

notes.text: विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः — "a man who is great"

notes.en: a तत्पुरुष of adjective + noun, both in the same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — a तत्पुरुष whose members are co-referential (same case) is कर्मधारय
विशेषणं विशेष्येण — a qualifier (महत्) combines with the qualified (पुरुष)

readings.vyakhya: समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः कर्मधारयः। महान् च असौ पुरुषः च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A कर्मधारय is a तत्पुरुष where the two members refer to the SAME thing — adjective and noun, both nominative: महान् पुरुषः → महापुरुषः, "great man." Unlike राजपुरुषः (the king's man — two different things, genitive relation), here महत् simply describes पुरुष. (महत् → महा in the compound.)

readings.translation: the three worlds (विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः)
readings.teaches: द्विगु — a numeral-first तत्पुरुष, denoting an aggregate

notes.text: विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — "the aggregate of three worlds"

notes.en: a numeral-first compound, naming a counted aggregate

notes.role: संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः — a तत्पुरुष with a number (त्रि) as its first member is द्विगु

readings.vyakhya: संख्यापूर्वः तत्पुरुषः द्विगुः। त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A द्विगु is a तत्पुरुष whose first member is a numeral: त्रि (three) + लोक (world) → त्रिलोकी, "the three worlds" taken as one set. It names a counted aggregate — द्वि-गु itself means "worth two cows." Same तत्पुरुष frame (second member heads), special first member: a number.

readings.translation: The boy gone-to-Kṛṣṇa (who has taken refuge with Kṛṣṇa).
readings.teaches: द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the accusative (कृष्णं श्रितः); named by that case

words.gloss: gone to / having resorted to Kṛṣṇa

notes.text: विग्रह: कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛष्ण"; the first member is logically accusative

notes.role: द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतित… — a 2nd-case word compounds with श्रित etc. → द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: द्वितीयान्तं श्रितादिभिः समस्यते। कृष्णं श्रितः = कृष्णश्रितः।
readings.vyakhya_en: तत्पुरुष compounds are NAMED by the case the analysis (विग्रह) would use. Here the विग्रह is कृष्णं श्रितः — "resorted-to Kṛṣṇa," with कृष्ण in the द्वितीया (accusative) — so the compound is a द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष (2.1.24). The later member श्रित heads it, as in every तत्पुरुष; only the internal case-relation differs. This is the template: each case gives a named sub-type.

readings.translation: Bring the wood for the sacrificial post.
readings.teaches: चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses a dative of purpose: यूपाय दारु, "wood for a post"

notes.text: विग्रह: यूपाय दारु — "wood for-a-post"; first member is logically dative (purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थ… — a 4th-case (purpose) word compounds → चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: object of आनय (accusative neuter, unchanged in form)

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → आनय

readings.vyakhya: चतुर्थ्यन्तं तदर्थेन समस्यते। यूपाय दारु = यूपदारु।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dative-of-purpose तत्पुरुष: यूपाय दारु, "wood FOR a sacrificial post," compounds to यूपदारु (2.1.36). The विग्रह's चतुर्थी (purpose, "for") names it. Compare कृष्णश्रितः (द्वितीया, ex143): same heads-later frame, the internal case is what the name records.

readings.translation: The king's man comes.
readings.teaches: षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष — the commonest तत्पुरुष; the विग्रह uses the genitive (राज्ञः पुरुषः)

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the king's man"; first member is logically genitive

notes.role: षष्ठी → a 6th-case word compounds with what it relates to → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: षष्ठ्यन्तं सुबन्तेन समस्यते। राज्ञः पुरुषः = राजपुरुषः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष is the workhorse compound: राज्ञः पुरुषः "the king's man" → राजपुरुषः (2.2.8). Whenever the relation between two nouns is the plain "of / 's" (the genitive, षष्ठी शेषे), it can compound this way — देवदत्तस्य गृहम् → देवदत्तगृहम्, and so on. It is the तत्पुरुष you meet most.

readings.sentence: महाबलः नृपः प्रतिदिनम् देवगृहम् अगच्छत्। तत्र सः देवम् अपश्यत्, नमः च अकरोत्।
readings.translation: The mighty king went to the temple every day. There he saw the god, and made obeisance.
readings.teaches:
three compound types in one errand — महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि), प्रतिदिनम्
(अव्ययीभाव), देवगृहम् (तत्पुरुष).

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the one whose strength is great

notes.text: विग्रह: महत् बलं यस्य सः — "he whose strength is great"

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

notes.en: adverbial — प्रति heads it (distributive), and the whole is indeclinable

notes.text: विग्रह: दिनं दिनं प्रति — "day by day"

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: determinative — गृहम्, the second member, is the head; देवस्य गृहम्

notes.text: विग्रह: देवस्य गृहम् — "the house of the god"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (देवस्य) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: the thing made — नमः + कृ, "to make obeisance"

readings.vyakhya: त्रयः समासाः एकस्मिन् वाक्ये — महाबलः, प्रतिदिनम्, देवगृहम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
One short errand carries three of the compound types. महाबलः is a बहुव्रीहि,
the one whose strength is great — the king, not the strength. प्रतिदिनम् is an
अव्ययीभाव, प्रति heading it in the distributive "day by day" and the whole
going indeclinable. And देवगृहम् is a तत्पुरुष — देवस्य गृहम्, the god's house,
the temple — its second member the head.

readings.translation: A man skilled at dice.
readings.teaches: सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष — the विग्रह uses the locative (अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice")

notes.text: विग्रह: अक्षेषु शौण्डः — "expert at dice"; first member is logically locative

notes.role: सप्तमी शौण्डैः — a 7th-case word compounds with शौण्ड etc. → सप्तमी-तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: सप्तम्यन्तं शौण्डादिभिः समस्यते। अक्षेषु शौण्डः = अक्षशौण्डः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The locative तत्पुरुष: अक्षेषु शौण्डः, "expert AT dice," → अक्षशौण्डः (2.1.40). The विग्रह's सप्तमी (the locus of the skill) names it. With ex143–146 you now have the four case-तत्पुरुषes — द्वितीया, चतुर्थी, षष्ठी, सप्तमी — each the same heads-later compound, distinguished only by which case the analysis restores.

readings.translation: This one is a non-brahmin.
readings.teaches: नञ्-तत्पुरुष — negation by नञ् (न → अ before a consonant); "non-X"

notes.text: विग्रह: न ब्राह्मणः — "not a brahmin"; नञ् (न) prefixes, surfacing as अ before a consonant

notes.role: नञ् → the negative नञ् compounds with the following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

readings.vyakhya: नञः समासे न-कारस्य अ-आदेशः (हलि)। न ब्राह्मणः = अब्राह्मणः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The नञ्-तत्पुरुष negates: न ब्राह्मणः "not a brahmin" → अब्राह्मणः (2.2.6). The particle नञ् surfaces as अ- before a consonant (and as अन्- before a vowel — अनश्वः "non-horse"). This is the productive "non-/un-/a-" prefix of Sanskrit: अधर्मः, अहिंसा, असत्य — every one a नञ्-तत्पुरुष.

readings.translation: The eminent teacher instructs.
readings.teaches: प्रादि-तत्पुरुष — a preverb/particle (here प्र "forth, eminent") compounds as the first member

notes.text: विग्रह: प्रगतः आचार्यः — "a foremost teacher"; प्र (preverb) is the first member

notes.role: कुगतिप्रादयः → कु, गति-words, and the प्र-class particles compound (तत्पुरुष)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: प्रादयः सुबन्तेन समस्यन्ते (कुगतिप्रादयः)। प्रगतः आचार्यः = प्राचार्यः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The प्रादि-तत्पुरुष lets a preverb or particle head a compound: प्र "forth, eminent" + आचार्य → प्राचार्यः, "a foremost teacher" (2.2.18, कुगतिप्रादयः — कु "bad," the गति preverbs, and the प्र-series). The same rule gives अतिराजः "surpassing a king," कुपुरुषः "a wretched man." It rounds out the तत्पुरुष: not only case-relations but particles can occupy the first slot.

chapters.title: पाठाः — real passages (Hitopadeśa → Purāṇa → Upaniṣad → Saṃhitā)

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 1.14 — the mark of the wise
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; compounds kept whole); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_1.14)

readings.sentence: मातृवत् परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु लोष्ट्रवत्। आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति सः पण्डितः॥
readings.translation: He who looks on others' wives as on a mother, on others' wealth as on a clod of earth, on all beings as on himself — he is the wise one.
readings.teaches:
the वति suffix — "just like ___": मातृवत् "as (one would toward) a mother,"
लोष्ट्रवत् "like a clod," आत्मवत् "as oneself." One little suffix turns a
noun into an adverb of comparison.

notes.en: adverb of likeness — मातृ "mother" + वति "just as with a ___"

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः — when an action is done "equally with / just as toward" something, वति is added → मातृ + वति → मातृवत्
तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → लोष्ट्र + वति → लोष्ट्रवत् "just as (toward) a clod"
तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → आत्म + वति → आत्मवत् "just as toward oneself"

readings.vyakhya: वतिप्रत्ययप्रधानः श्लोकः। मातृवत् लोष्ट्रवत् आत्मवत् इति तुल्यक्रियायां वतिः (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः) — अव्ययम्। परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु सर्वभूतेषु इति विषयसप्तमी। यः … सः इति नित्यसम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse turns on one suffix: **वति**, "just as with ___." Add it to a noun
and you get an indeclinable adverb of comparison — मातृ-वत् "as (one behaves)
toward a mother," लोष्ट्र-वत् "as toward a clod," आत्म-वत् "as toward oneself"
(5.1.115, तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः, "when the action is equal-to that"). The
locatives परदारेषु / परद्रव्येषु / सर्वभूतेषु are the "in the matter of ___"
sphere-locative, and यः … सः is the relative-correlative frame that holds the
definition together: the one who sees this way *is* the wise one.

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 1.71 — the whole earth a family
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; वसुधैव kept fused to show the सन्धि); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_1.71)

readings.sentence: अयम् निजः परः वा इति गणना लघुचेतसाम्। उदारचरितानाम् तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्॥
readings.translation: 'This one is my own, that one a stranger' — such reckoning belongs to the small-minded. For the noble-hearted, the whole earth is but one family.
readings.teaches:
the बहुव्रीहि, the possessive compound that points outside itself:
लघुचेतसाम् "of those whose mind is small," उदारचरितानाम् "of those whose
conduct is noble" — neither word names mind or conduct as its subject.

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words compound to denote a third thing (the possessor) → लघु + चेतस् → लघुचेतस् "small-minded"
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming the possessor → उदार + चरित → उदारचरित
वृद्धिरेचि — आ/अ before ए/ओ becomes the वृद्धि vowel → वसुधा + एव → वसुधैव

readings.vyakhya: बहुव्रीहिप्रधानः सुप्रसिद्धः श्लोकः। लघुचेतसाम् उदारचरितानाम् इति बहुव्रीही (अनेकमन्यपदार्थे) — न चेतः न चरितं मुख्यम्, किन्तु तद्वान् पुरुषः। वसुधैव इति वसुधा-एव इति वृद्धिसन्धिः (वृद्धिरेचि)। षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse everyone quotes — and it turns on the **बहुव्रीहि**, the compound
that describes something *outside* its own members. लघुचेतस् does not mean
"small mind"; it means "one whose mind is small" — the person, not the mind,
is what the word points to (2.2.24, अनेकमन्यपदार्थे, "denoting another
thing"). Same with उदारचरित "one whose conduct is noble." Both stand in the
genitive of belonging: the reckoning belongs to the small-minded, the earth-
as-family to the noble. And वसुधैव hides the vṛddhi सन्धि — वसुधा + एव → वसुधैव
(6.1.88).

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 0.6 — knowledge gives humility
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_0.6)

readings.sentence: विद्या ददाति विनयम् विनयात् याति पात्रताम्। पात्रत्वात् धनम् आप्नोति धनात् धर्मम् ततः सुखम्॥
readings.translation: Knowledge gives humility; from humility one reaches worthiness; from worthiness one gains wealth; from wealth, dharma; and from that, happiness.
readings.teaches:
a chain of ablatives — विनयात्, पात्रत्वात्, धनात्, each "from ___," the
अपादान case of a source; and the abstract-noun suffixes त्व/तल् (पात्रता,
पात्रत्व, "the state of being fit").

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी — the source from which something proceeds (अपादान) takes the पञ्चमी → विनयात् "from humility"

notes.en: abstract noun — पात्र "fit vessel" + तल् (→ ता) "the state of being fit"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — the "state/quality of being X" is expressed by त्व or तल् → पात्र + तल् → पात्रता

notes.en: abstract noun — पात्र + त्व, the same "fitness" (neuter)

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व, the other abstract suffix → पात्र + त्व → पात्रत्व

readings.vyakhya: पञ्चमीश्रृङ्खला। विनयात् पात्रत्वात् धनात् इति अपादाने पञ्चमी — "अमुष्मात् एतत्" इति। पात्रता पात्रत्वम् इति भावप्रत्ययौ (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ) — तल् स्त्रियाम्, त्वं नपुंसके। श्लोकः सोपानक्रमेण विद्यायाः फलम् आचष्टे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A ladder built out of **ablatives**. Each rung names a *source*: विनयात्
"from humility," पात्रत्वात् "from worthiness," धनात् "from wealth" — the
अपादान कारक, in the पञ्चमी (2.3.28, "the point one proceeds from"). The verse
also pairs the two **abstract-noun** suffixes of 5.1.119 (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ):
तल् gives feminine पात्र-ता, त्व gives neuter पात्र-त्व — both "the state of
being a fit vessel." Read it as a single sentence and it is a chain: knowledge
→ humility → worth → wealth → dharma → happiness.

source.ref: Manu 4.138 — speak truth, speak kindly
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated per GRETIL's analysis segmentation; every form is Manu's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_manusmRti, Manu_4.138)

readings.sentence: सत्यम् ब्रूयात् प्रियम् ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यम् अप्रियम्। प्रियम् च न अनृतम् ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः॥
readings.translation: One should speak the truth, one should speak what is kind; one should not speak an unkind truth. And one should not speak a pleasant falsehood — this is the eternal law.
readings.teaches:
the optative of precept, four times over — ब्रूयात् "one should speak," the
लिङ् of ब्रू; and two नञ्-compounds, अप्रियम् "unkind" and अनृतम्
"untruth," which shows नञ् in its अन्- shape before a vowel.

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — in the sense of precept (विधि), the optative लिङ् → ब्रू + लिङ् → ब्रूयात्
नञ् — the negative नञ् compounds with प्रिय → अप्रिय; before a consonant नञ् appears as अ
नञ् — नञ् + ऋत "truth" → अनृत; before a vowel नञ् takes its अन्- shape → अन् + ऋत

readings.vyakhya: विध्यर्थलिङ्प्रधानः श्लोकः। ब्रूयात् इति ब्रुवः विधिलिङि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम् (चतुर्वारम्)। अप्रियम् अनृतम् इति नञ्समासौ — व्यञ्जने अ, अचि अन् (अनृतम्)। एष धर्मः सनातनः इति समापने।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse is built on a single form repeated four times: **ब्रूयात्** "one
should speak," the optative (लिङ्) of ब्रू in its precept sense (3.3.161).
This is the mood of moral instruction — "one ought." Two नञ्-compounds carry
the balance of the thought: अप्रियम् "unkind" (नञ् as अ- before a consonant)
and अनृतम् "untruth" (नञ् as **अन्-** before the vowel of ऋत). Four clauses,
one rule of conduct: truth, but kind; kindness, but true.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1.42 — the wise man and the king
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; compounds kept whole); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_1.42||)

readings.sentence: राजानम् एव संश्रित्य विद्वान् याति पराम् गतिम्। विना मलयम् अन्यत्र चन्दनम् न प्ररोहति॥
readings.translation: Only by taking refuge with a king does the learned man reach the highest station — sandalwood grows nowhere but the Malaya hills.
readings.teaches:
the gerund of a prefixed root — संश्रित्य "having resorted to," which is
ल्यप् (not क्त्वा) precisely because सम्- is prefixed; and the strong-stem
accusative राजानम्.

notes.en: gerund of सम्-श्रि "resort to, depend on"

notes.role: समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् — when the root carries a prefix (सम्-), the क्त्वा gerund is replaced by ल्यप् (-य) → संश्रि + ल्यप् → संश्रित्य

notes.en: the gerund suffix for prefixed roots

readings.vyakhya: ल्यबन्तप्रधानः श्लोकः। संश्रित्य इति सोपसर्गात् श्रयतेः क्त्वो ल्यप् (समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप्) — उपसर्गयुक्ते धातौ क्त्वा न, किन्तु ल्यप्। राजानम् इति नकारान्तस्य सर्वनामस्थाने बलवद्रूपम्। विना इति द्वितीयायोगे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse turns on one form: **संश्रित्य** "having resorted to." You already
know the gerund क्त्वा (गत्वा, कृत्वा) — but the moment a root takes a prefix,
क्त्वा is replaced by **ल्यप्** (7.1.37, समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप्): सम् +
श्रि → संश्रित्य, not *संश्रित्वा. That -य ending is the mark of every prefixed
gerund (आदाय, विहाय, प्रणम्य). Beside it: राजानम्, the strong-stem accusative
of राजन्, and विना "except," which here governs the accusative मलयम्.

source.ref: Rāmāyaṇa 1.1.1 — Vālmīki questions Nārada
source.curated: the whole opening verse, word-separated (pausa forms shown; compounds kept whole); every form is Vālmīki's. Text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_rAmAyaNa, R_1.001.001)

readings.sentence: तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतम् तपस्वी वाग्विदाम् वरम्। नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिः मुनिपुंगवम्॥
readings.translation: Vālmīki the ascetic questioned Nārada — the best of the eloquent, that bull among sages, ever devoted to austerity and study.
readings.teaches:
the very first verse of the Rāmāyaṇa — and with it the perfect tense,
परिपप्रच्छ "questioned" (लिट्, the reduplicated past of "remote" narration),
a verb of asking that takes the person asked as its object.

notes.en: compound — "engaged in (निरत) tapas and svādhyāya," a तत्पुरुष qualifying नारदम्
the best OF the eloquent — governed by वरम्
in apposition to नारदम् — "the best (of the eloquent)"
the one questioned — object of परिपप्रच्छ (a verb of asking, अकथितं च)

notes.role: अकथितं च — प्रच्छ् "ask" takes the person asked as कर्मन् → नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ
परोक्षे लिट् — for a remote (परोक्ष) past, the लिट् (perfect) is used; प्रच्छ् reduplicates → परि + पप्रच्छ

notes.en: compound — पुंगव "bull" as "best of" → "the foremost of sages" (उपमान)

readings.vyakhya: आदिश्लोकः। परिपप्रच्छ इति प्रच्छेः लिटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम् (परोक्षे लिट्, द्वित्वम्)। नारदम् इति प्रच्छेः द्विकर्मकत्वात् पृष्टः कर्म (अकथितं च)। तपस्वी इति तपस्शब्दात् विनिः; वाग्विदाम् मुनिपुंगवम् इति समासौ; वरम् इति षष्ठ्यन्तेन योगे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The Rāmāyaṇa opens on a single sentence, and it brings the **perfect tense**:
परिपप्रच्छ "questioned," the लिट् of परि-प्रच्छ्, its reduplication (प + प्रच्छ)
the tense's signature. The लिट् is the tense of *remote*, narrated past — 3.2.115
परोक्षे लिट् — the register in which epics tell of long ago. Notice too that
प्रच्छ् "ask" takes the **person asked** as its object: नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ (the
same अकथितं च, 1.4.51, you met with याच्). Everything else is the epic's dense
apposition — तपस्वी (तपस् + विनि), वाग्विदाम् and मुनिपुंगवम् (compounds), वरम्
"the best of…" — all bending toward the one accusative, नारदम्.

source.ref: Manu 3.56 — where women are honored
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated per GRETIL's analysis segmentation (avagraha/vṛddhi sandhi shown split); every form is Manu's. Text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_manusmRti, Manu_3.56)

readings.sentence: यत्र नार्यः तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः। यत्र एताः तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वाः तत्र अफलाः क्रियाः॥
readings.translation: Where women are honored, there the gods rejoice; where they are not honored, all rites are fruitless.
readings.teaches:
the passive voice on the page — पूज्यन्ते "are honored," with the यक्
passive-marker, the honored women standing as the grammatical subject; and
a यण्-सन्धि (नारी → नार्यः) and a नञ्-compound (अफलाः "fruitless").

notes.en: relative adverb of place (correlative of तत्र)

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (here ī) becomes the corresponding semivowel य् before a vowel → नारी + अस् (जस्) → नार्यः

notes.en: the honored ones — grammatical subject of the passive (कर्मणि उक्त)
the passive विकरण — inserted between root and ending in the कर्मणि

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — before a सार्वधातुक ending in the कर्मणि/भावे, यक् is the विकरण → पूज् + यक् → पूज्य…

notes.en: subject of the passive न पूज्यन्ते

notes.role: नञ् — the negative नञ् (न → अ) compounds with फल → अफल "fruitless"

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगप्रधानः श्लोकः। पूज्यन्ते इति यकि लट् कर्मणि (सार्वधातुके यक्)। नार्यः इति ईकारस्य यणादेशः (इको यणचि)। अफलाः इति नञ्समासः बहुव्रीहिः। यत्र…तत्र इति नित्यसम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A verse in the **passive**. पूज्यन्ते "are honored" and न पूज्यन्ते "are not
honored" show the कर्मणि प्रयोग — the thing-acted-upon (the women) becomes the
grammatical subject in the nominative, and the verb carries the passive marker
**यक्** (3.1.67, सार्वधातुके यक्). Two more points earn their place: नार्यः,
where the ī of नारी turns to य् before the ending (6.1.77 इको यणचि, the
यण्-सन्धि), and अफलाः "fruitless," a नञ्-compound (2.2.6). The frame is the
यत्र … तत्र correlative — "where … there."

source.ref: Rāmāyaṇa 1.32.7 — forgiveness, the ornament
source.curated: the first hemistich, a maxim on its own; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_rAmAyaNa, R_1.032.007ab)

readings.sentence: अलंकारो हि नारीणाम् क्षमा तु पुरुषस्य वा॥
readings.translation: Forgiveness is the ornament of women — and of a man as well.
readings.teaches:
a balanced maxim of genitives: नारीणाम् "of women" (with णत्व, न → ण after
the र of नारी) and पुरुषस्य "of a man" (the अ-stem genitive स्य).

notes.role: रषाभ्यां नो णः — a dental न् becomes retroflex ण् when a र् or ष् precedes (even across vowels); the र of नारी retroflexes the न of the नाम् ending → नारीणाम्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an अ-stem, the genitive-singular ending ङस् is replaced by स्य → पुरुष + स्य → पुरुषस्य

notes.en: "or, as well" — extending the claim to men

readings.vyakhya: सुभाषितम्। नारीणाम् इति नारीशब्दस्य षष्ठीबहुवचनम् — रेफात् नकारस्य णत्वम् (रषाभ्यां नो णः)। पुरुषस्य इति अकारान्तस्य ङसः स्यादेशः (टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः)। क्षमा प्रथमा; अलंकारो विसर्गसन्धौ ओकारः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A single-line subhāṣita, and a tidy pairing of genitives. नारीणाम् "of
women" is where you catch **णत्व** at work: the न् of the genitive-plural
ending नाम् turns retroflex ण् because the र of नारी precedes it (8.4.1
रषाभ्यां नो णः — र/ष retroflex a following न even across vowels). Its partner
पुरुषस्य "of a man" shows the ordinary अ-stem genitive singular, the ending
ङस् becoming स्य (7.1.12). Between them sits क्षमा, an आ-stem feminine
nominative, the whole balanced by तु … वा "for women — and for men too."

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1.5 — the world befriends the rich
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_1.5||)

readings.sentence: इह लोके हि धनिनाम् परोऽपि स्वजनायते। स्वजनोऽपि दरिद्राणाम् सर्वदा दुर्जनायते॥
readings.translation: In this world, even a stranger behaves as kin toward the rich; even one's own kin always behaves as an enemy toward the poor.
readings.teaches:
the denominative — a whole verb built from a noun: स्वजनायते "acts as one's
own," दुर्जनायते "acts as a foe," the क्यङ् formation "behave like X."

notes.en: possessive derivative — धन "wealth" → धनिन् "having wealth, rich"

notes.role: अत इनिठनौ — after an अ-final stem denoting a possessum, इनि (and ठन्) in the "possessing" sense → धन + इनि → धनिन्

notes.en: genitive plural — "for/toward the rich" (the one behaved-toward)
denominative — a verb made from the noun स्वजन "one's own kin," "to act like/as ___"

notes.role: उपमानादाचारे — from a standard-of-comparison (उपमान), in the sense of behaving toward someone like it (आचार), a denominative affix is introduced
कर्तुः क्यङ् — that affix is क्यङ् (आत्मनेपद) when the behaving is self-referential → स्वजन + क्यङ् → स्वजनायते

notes.en: genitive plural — "for/toward the poor" (the one behaved-toward)
denominative from दुर्जन "a wicked man, foe" — "to act like a foe"

notes.role: कर्तुः क्यङ् (उपमानादाचारे) — दुर्जन + क्यङ् → दुर्जनायते "behaves like a foe"

readings.vyakhya: नामधातुप्रधानः श्लोकः। स्वजनायते दुर्जनायते इति उपमानात् आचारे क्यङ् — "स्वजन इव आचरति" इत्यर्थे। धनिनाम् दरिद्राणाम् इति शेषे षष्ठी (आचरितव्यविषये)। धनिन् इति धनशब्दात् इनिः मतुबर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A verse built on the नामधातु — the denominative verb. Sanskrit can turn
almost any noun into a verb; here स्वजन "one's own" → स्वजनायते "acts as one's
own," and दुर्जन "a foe" → दुर्जनायते "acts as a foe." The rule is
3.1.10–11: from an उपमान (a standard of comparison), in the sense of
**आचार** (behaving toward someone as if they were that thing), a root is
formed, and it takes **क्यङ्** with आत्मनेपद endings (-आयते). Around it:
धनिनाम् and दरिद्राणाम् are genitives of the one behaved-toward, and धनिन्
itself is धन + इनि (5.2.115), the "possessing wealth" derivative — the same
इनि you meet in दण्डिन्, बलिन्, मनस्विन्.

source.ref: Bhāgavata 1.2.11 — Brahman, Paramātman, Bhagavān
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_bhAgavatapurANa, ||BhP_01.02.011||)

readings.sentence: वदन्ति तत् तत्त्वविदस् तत्त्वम् यज् ज्ञानम् अद्वयम्। ब्रह्मेति परमात्मेति भगवान् इति शब्द्यते॥
readings.translation: The knowers of truth declare that truth — the knowledge that is without-a-second — and it is named "Brahman," "Paramātman," "Bhagavān."
readings.teaches:
the नञ्-तत्पुरुष अद्वयम् ("not-two"), and a passive naming — शब्द्यते, "is
called," of what the knowers declare.

notes.en: compound — तत्त्वं विदन्ति, "who know the truth" (उपपद-तत्पुरुष)
relative pronoun (यत् → यज् before ज, श्चुत्व)

notes.text: विग्रह: न द्वयम् — "not two"

notes.role: नञ् — नञ् (न) compounds with a following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: nominative — the name given; ब्रह्म + इति → ब्रह्मेति (अ + इ → ए)
nominative — a second name; परमात्मा + इति → परमात्मेति (आ + इ → ए)
possessive derivative — भग + मतुप् → भगवत् ("having fortune")

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — भग + मतुप् → भगवत्
सान्तमहतः संयोगस्य — penult lengthening in the strong stem → भगवान्
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive शब्द्यते

readings.vyakhya: तत्त्वविदः तत् तत्त्वम् अद्वयम् ज्ञानम् वदन्ति; तत् ब्रह्म परमात्मा भगवान् इति शब्द्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The knowers of truth declare तत्त्वम्, and name it three ways. What they
declare is अद्वयम् ज्ञानम् — "knowledge not-two," a नञ्-तत्पुरुष, न द्वयम्
(2.2.6). And the naming is passive: ब्रह्म, परमात्मा, भगवान् — इति शब्द्यते,
"is called," the passive of the denominative शब्द् (3.4.69). भगवान् itself is
the मतुप् possessive भगवत्, "the one having fortune."

source.ref: Hit_0.7 — the two knowledges
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.7||); the final vowel-sandhi द्वितीया आद्रियते is shown unjoined for reading.

readings.sentence: विद्या शस्त्रम् च शास्त्रम् च द्वे विद्ये प्रतिपत्तये। आद्या हास्याय वृद्धत्वे द्वितीया आद्रियते सदा॥
readings.translation: Knowledge is of two kinds — weapon-craft and the śāstra — two knowledges for mastery. The first is for ridicule in old age; the second is honored always.
readings.teaches:
two derived nouns of purpose. प्रतिपत्तये is the क्तिन् action-noun "for
mastery"; हास्याय is the ण्यत् gerundive "for (being) laughed at."

notes.en: nominative (neuter) — one of the two kinds
the क्तिन् feminine action-noun — प्रति + पद् + क्तिन् → प्रतिपत्ति

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — क्तिन् forms a feminine action-noun → प्रतिपत्ति ("attainment")

notes.en: the ण्यत् gerundive suffix (with वृद्धि) — हस् → हास्य

notes.role: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् — ण्यत् after a हल्-final root → हस् + ण्यत् → हास्य
तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → वृद्ध + त्व → वृद्धत्व
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive आद्रियते

readings.vyakhya: विद्या द्विविधा — शस्त्रम् शास्त्रम् च; प्रतिपत्तये द्वे। आद्या हास्याय, द्वितीया सदा आद्रियते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two derivations carry the sense. प्रतिपत्तये is the क्तिन् action-noun of
प्रति-पद्, "for mastery" (3.3.94), in the dative of purpose; हास्याय is the
ण्यत् gerundive of हस्, "for being laughed at" (3.1.124), the same dative. The
first knowledge — weapon-craft — comes to that, हास्याय वृद्धत्वे, "ridicule in
old age" (वृद्धत्व, the त्व abstract); the second, the śāstra, आद्रियते सदा,
"is honored always" — the passive of आ-दृ.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1.2 — nothing is unattained by wealth
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_1.2||)

readings.sentence: न हि तद् विद्यते किञ्चिद् यद् अर्थेन न सिध्यति। यत्नेन मतिमान् तस्माद् अर्थम् एकम् प्रसाधयेत्॥
readings.translation: There is nothing at all that is not achieved by wealth; therefore the wise man should, by effort, secure wealth above all.
readings.teaches:
an optative maxim. प्रसाधयेत् is विधिलिङ्, "should secure"; मतिमान् is the
मतुप् possessive "the one having wit"; अर्थेन / यत्नेन are the तृतीया of means.

notes.en: किम् + चित् — the indefinite "anything" (किंचित् → किञ्चिद् before य)
the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having wit" (मति + मतुप् → मतिमत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — मति + मतुप् → मतिमत् → मतिमान्

notes.en: from that — the causal ablative (तस्मात् → तस्माद् before अ)

readings.vyakhya: अर्थेन सर्वम् सिध्यति; तस्मात् मतिमान् अर्थम् एकम् प्रसाधयेत्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A maxim in the optative. Nothing, तद् किञ्चित्, is found यद् — which — is not
achieved अर्थेन, "by wealth" (the तृतीया of means, as is यत्नेन "by effort").
So the मतिमान्, the one who HAS wit (मति + मतुप्, 5.2.94), should — प्रसाधयेत्,
the विधिलिङ् "ought to secure" — wealth एकम्, above all. The whole force sits in
that optative: not "does" but "should."

source.ref: Rāmāyaṇa 1.2.14 — the आदिश्लोक, Vālmīki's curse on the hunter
source.curated: the whole verse, the first śloka of poetry; text from Ambuda's critical edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_rAmAyaNa, R_1.002.014)

readings.sentence: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठाम् त्वम् अगमः शाश्वतीः समाः। यत् क्रौञ्चमिथुनाद् एकम् अवधीः काममोहितम्॥
readings.translation: May you never, O hunter, reach rest for the long years to come — since you killed one of the pair of krauñca birds, deluded by passion.
readings.teaches:
the first verse of Sanskrit poetry. मा with the aorist forbids — मा … अगमः,
"may you not reach"; अवधीः is the aorist "you killed" of हन्.

notes.en: prohibitive particle — with the aorist, a negative wish/command
aorist — with मा it is the prohibitive ("may you not reach")
duration — "for the years" (the द्वितीया of extent of time)

words.gloss: from the pair of krauñca birds

notes.en: compound — क्रौञ्चयोः मिथुनम्, "the pair of the two krauñcas"
source — the one taken from the pair

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी — the point of separation takes पञ्चमी → क्रौञ्चमिथुनात्

notes.en: aorist — 2nd sg of हन् (the वध्-substitute), "you slew"

readings.vyakhya: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वम् अगमः — यत् क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् एकम् अवधीः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse grief wrung from Vālmīki, and with it Sanskrit poetry began. मा
with the aorist is the prohibition: मा … अगमः, "may you never reach"
प्रतिष्ठाम्, a resting place, शाश्वतीः समाः, for the endless years. The reason
follows on यत्: because from the क्रौञ्च-pair (क्रौञ्चमिथुनात्, the ablative of
what one is taken FROM) you killed एकम्, one — अवधीः, the aorist of हन् — while
it was काममोहितम्, lost in love.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 0.2 — the maṅgala verse (Viṣṇuśarman and the five tantras)
source.curated: the opening benedictory verse, whole; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_0.2||)

readings.sentence: सकलार्थशास्त्रसारं जगति समालोक्य विष्णुशर्मेदम्। तन्त्रैः पञ्चभिर् एतच् चकार सुमनोहरं शास्त्रम्॥
readings.translation: Having surveyed in the world the essence of all the treatises on statecraft, Viṣṇuśarman composed this charming work in five tantras.
readings.teaches:
the Pañcatantra's own opening — a long तत्पुरुष सार-compound as object of the
ल्यप् gerund समालोक्य, and the perfect चकार "he composed."

words.gloss: the essence of all the treatises on statecraft

notes.en: determinative — सारम्, the head, is qualified by the rest; सकलानाम् अर्थशास्त्राणाम् सारम्

notes.text: विग्रह: सकलानाम् अर्थशास्त्राणाम् सारम् — "the essence of all the arthaśāstras"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose last member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

notes.en: gerund — a कृदन्त that does not decline
the ल्यप् suffix — a क्त्वा-gerund WITH a preverb (सम्-आ), so आगत्य-style

notes.role: समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् — क्त्वा becomes ल्यप् after a preverb → -आलोक्य

notes.en: सम् + आ — the preverbs that select ल्यप् over क्त्वा
agent — विष्णुशर्मा, the one who composed
nominative — an अन्-stem, so the न् drops (विष्णुशर्मा)

notes.text: विष्णुशर्मा + इदम् → विष्णुशर्मेदम् (आ + इ → ए, गुणसन्धि); इदम् = "this work," द्वितीया

notes.en: instrument — "by means of the five books"

notes.text: पञ्चभिः + एतत् → पञ्चभिर् (visarga → र् before a voiced sound)
एतत् + चकार → एतच् चकार (त् → च् before च, श्चुत्व 8.4.40)

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार → चकार

readings.vyakhya: सकलार्थशास्त्रसारं समालोक्य विष्णुशर्मा पञ्चभिः तन्त्रैः शास्त्रम् चकार।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The Pañcatantra names itself in its second verse. The object of the gerund is
one long तत्पुरुष — सकल-अर्थशास्त्र-सारम्, "the essence of all the treatises on
statecraft" — which Viṣṇuśarman, having surveyed (समालोक्य, the ल्यप् gerund),
made into a charming work. चकार is the perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115), the tense of
reported past: "he composed it." तन्त्रैः पञ्चभिः, "by five books" — the five
that give the book its name.

source.ref: Hit_0.36 — उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति (effort, not wishes)
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.36||)

readings.sentence: उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति कार्याणि न मनोरथैः। न हि सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य प्रविशन्ति मुखे मृगाः॥
readings.translation: By effort deeds succeed, not by wishes. For deer do not walk into the mouth of a sleeping lion.
readings.teaches:
a famous Hitopadeśa maxim. कार्याणि is the ण्यत् gerundive ("things to be
done"); सुप्तस्य is a क्त participle qualifying सिंहस्य; success comes उद्यमेन
(तृतीया, by means).

notes.en: gerundive — "that which is to be done" (declines, neuter)
the ण्यत् gerundive suffix on a हल्-final root

notes.role: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् — ण्यत् after an ऋ/हल्-final root → कृ + ण्यत् → कार्य ("to be done")

notes.en: instrument — "by mere wishes" (मनसः रथः, "a chariot of the mind")

readings.vyakhya: उद्यमेन कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति, न मनोरथैः। सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य मुखे मृगाः न प्रविशन्ति।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two instrumentals set the maxim: things get done उद्यमेन "by effort," not
मनोरथैः "by wishes." कार्याणि is itself a गерundive — कृ + ण्यत् → कार्य, "what
is to be done" (3.1.124), the very word Pāṇini's rule forms. The second line
is the image: सुप्तस्य सिंहस्य, "of a sleeping lion" — सुप्त the क्त participle
of स्वप् — into whose mouth (मुखे) the deer do not walk. Nothing comes without
the effort of the doing.

source.ref: Hit_0.11 — यौवनं धनसम्पत्तिः (each alone is ruin)
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.11||)

readings.sentence: यौवनं धनसम्पत्तिः प्रभुत्वम् अविवेकिता। एकैकम् अप्य् अनर्थाय किम् उ यत्र चतुष्टयम्॥
readings.translation: Youth, abundance of wealth, power, and want of judgment — each one alone leads to ruin; how much more where the four are together.
readings.teaches:
four nouns, then the twist. धनसम्पत्तिः carries the क्तिन् action-noun सम्पत्ति;
प्रभुत्वम् and अविवेकिता are the त्व/तल् abstracts — "power," "indiscretion."

notes.en: determinative — धनस्य सम्पत्तिः, "attainment of wealth"; सम्पत्ति is the head

notes.text: सम्पत्ति = सम् + पद् + क्तिन् — the feminine action-noun "attainment"

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — क्तिन् forms a feminine action-noun → सम् + पद् + क्तिन् → सम्पत्ति

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being प्रभु (a lord)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → प्रभु + त्व → प्रभुत्वम्

notes.en: the तल् abstract suffix (→ -ता, feminine) — "the state of being अविवेकिन्"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — तल् (→ ता) for "the state of" → अविवेकिन् + तल् → अविवेकिता

notes.en: एक + एक (आम्रेडित) — "one by one, each singly"
agent — the one that leads to ruin
interrogative — "किम् उ" = "how much more, let alone"
subject of the elliptical clause ("where the four [are present]")

readings.vyakhya: यौवनं धनसम्पत्तिः प्रभुत्वम् अविवेकिता — एकैकम् अपि अनर्थाय, किम् उ चतुष्टयम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Four things are named, three of them abstractions the तद्धित makes: सम्पत्तिः,
the क्तिन् noun of सम्-पद् "attainment" (3.3.94); प्रभुत्वम्, the त्व abstract
"lordship"; अविवेकिता, the तल् abstract "want of judgment." एकैकम् अपि — "even
each single one" — leads अनर्थाय, to ruin (the dative of purpose); किम् उ, "how
much more," where all four (चतुष्टयम्) come together.

source.ref: Hit_0.9 — the four books, drawn from the Pañcatantra
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.9||)

readings.sentence: मित्रलाभः सुहृद्भेदो विग्रहः सन्धिर् एव च। पञ्चतन्त्रात् तथान्यस्माद् ग्रन्थाद् आकृष्य लिख्यते॥
readings.translation: Winning friends, splitting friends, war, and peace — [these four]; drawn from the Pañcatantra and from another work besides, it is written.
readings.teaches:
the book naming its own four parts. लाभः and भेदः are घञ् action-nouns;
पञ्चतन्त्रात् / ग्रन्थात् are the ablative source (पञ्चमी), and लिख्यते is passive.

notes.en: determinative — मित्रस्य लाभः, "the gaining of a friend"; लाभः is the head

notes.text: लाभ = लभ् + घञ् — the action-noun "gaining"

notes.role: भावे घञ् — घञ् forms the action-noun → लभ् + घञ् → लाभ ("gaining")

notes.en: determinative — सुहृदः भेदः, "the estranging of a friend"; भेदः is the head

notes.text: भेद = भिद् + घञ् — the action-noun "splitting"; सुहृद्भेदः → सुहृद्भेदो (अः + व → ओ)

notes.role: भावे घञ् — घञ् forms the action-noun → भिद् + घञ् → भेद ("splitting")

notes.text: सन्धिः + एव → सन्धिर् एव (visarga → र् before a vowel)

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी — the source of an action takes पञ्चमी → पञ्चतन्त्रात्

notes.text: तथा + अन्यस्मात् → तथान्यस्माद् (आ + अ → आ); तथा = "likewise," अन्यस्मात् → अन्यस्माद् before ग्

notes.en: gerund — a कृदन्त that does not decline
the ल्यप् suffix — a क्त्वा-gerund WITH a preverb (आ), so आगत्य-style
आ — the preverb that selects ल्यप् over क्त्वा
passive — the work is the thing written; no expressed agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (here लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive लिख्यते

readings.vyakhya: मित्रलाभः सुहृद्भेदः विग्रहः सन्धिः च — चत्वारि तन्त्राणि। पञ्चतन्त्रात् ग्रन्थात् च आकृष्य इदम् लिख्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The book names its own four parts — मित्रलाभः "winning friends," सुहृद्भेदः
"splitting friends," विग्रहः "war," सन्धिः "peace." Two of them are घञ्
action-nouns: लभ् → लाभ, भिद् → भेद (3.3.18). And it says where it comes from:
पञ्चतन्त्रात्, ग्रन्थात् — the ablative of source (पञ्चमी) — having drawn (आकृष्य,
the ल्यप् gerund) from them, it लिख्यते, "is written," the passive of लिख्.

source.ref: Hit_0.4 — विद्या is the unsurpassed wealth
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.4||)

readings.sentence: सर्वद्रव्येषु विद्यैव द्रव्यम् आहुर् अनुत्तमम्। अहार्यत्वाद् अनर्घत्वाद् अक्षयत्वाच् च सर्वदा॥
readings.translation: Among all forms of wealth they call knowledge alone the unsurpassed wealth — because it cannot be stolen, is priceless, and is imperishable, always.
readings.teaches:
three त्व-abstracts giving the reason in the ablative — अहार्यत्वात् (unstealable),
अनर्घत्वात् (priceless), अक्षयत्वात् (imperishable); "they call" is the perfect आहुः.

notes.text: सर्व + द्रव्य — "all substances / all wealth"
विद्या + एव → विद्यैव (आ + ए → ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धि); एव = "alone, indeed"

notes.en: predicate object of आहुः ("call it wealth")
perfect — the defective root अह् survives only in the परोक्ष (आह, आहुः)

notes.text: आहुः → आहुर् before अ (visarga → र्)

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अहार्य (not to be stolen)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अहार्य + त्व → अहार्यत्व

notes.en: ablative of cause — "because of ___" (अहार्यत्वात् → अहार्यत्वाद् before अ)
the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अनर्घ (priceless)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अनर्घ + त्व → अनर्घत्व

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अक्षय (imperishable)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अक्षय + त्व → अक्षयत्व

notes.en: ablative of cause (अक्षयत्वात् → अक्षयत्वाच् before च)

readings.vyakhya: सर्वद्रव्येषु विद्या एव अनुत्तमम् द्रव्यम् — अहार्यत्वात् अनर्घत्वात् अक्षयत्वात् च।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Of all wealth, knowledge alone (विद्यैव) they call the unsurpassed — द्रव्यम्
and अनुत्तमम् both द्वितीया, the double object of आहुः "they call." The reason
comes in three त्व-abstracts in the ablative of cause: अहार्यत्वात्, "because it
cannot be stolen"; अनर्घत्वात्, "because it is priceless"; अक्षयत्वात्, "because
it never runs out" — each the त्व noun (5.1.119) of a quality, and सर्वदा,
always so.

source.ref: Hit_0.8 — why the teaching comes as story
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.8||)

readings.sentence: यन् नवे भाजने लग्नः संस्कारो नान्यथा भवेत्। कथाच्छलेन बालानां नीतिस् तद् इह कथ्यते॥
readings.translation: Since an impression set on a new vessel cannot become otherwise, statecraft is here told to children through the guise of story.
readings.teaches:
the book's method, and a passive. लग्नः is a क्त participle; भवेत् is the
optative; and नीतिः कथ्यते — "is told" — is the passive (कर्मणि) of कथ्.

notes.en: relative — "in that / since" (यत् → यन् before न, परसवर्ण)
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — "stuck, set" (लग् → लग्न)
nominative (संस्कारः → संस्कारो before न, visarga उत्व)
adverb — "otherwise"; न + अन्यथा → नान्यथा (आ + अ → आ), "not otherwise"

words.gloss: by the guise of a story

notes.en: determinative — कथायाः छलम्, "the pretext of a story"
the thing told — subject of the passive verb
pronoun — resuming नीतिः (तत् → तद् before इ)
passive — नीतिः is what is told; no expressed agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive कथ्यते

readings.vyakhya: नवे भाजने लग्नः संस्कारः अन्यथा न भवेत् — तथा कथाच्छलेन बालानां नीतिः कथ्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
An image explains the method. As a संस्कार, an impression लग्नः "set" (the क्त
participle) on a नव भाजन, a new vessel, cannot नान्यथा भवेत् "become otherwise"
(the optative), so — कथाच्छलेन, "by the guise of story" — statecraft is taught
to the young while their minds are new. नीतिः कथ्यते, "is told": कथ्यते is the
passive of कथ् (3.4.69), the नीति the thing told.

source.ref: Pañcatantra, कथामुख — the ministers' counsel
source.curated: the ministers' reply in the frame story, lightly abridged; the words are the text's own

readings.sentence: तत्र एकः अब्रवीत् — देव, व्याकरणम् एव द्वादश वर्षाणि अध्येतव्यम्। ततः धर्मशास्त्राणि अर्थशास्त्राणि च। एवं व्यतीते काले बुद्धिः प्रबुध्यते इति।
readings.translation: One of them said — "Your Majesty, grammar alone must be studied for twelve years. After that, the treatises on dharma and on statecraft. When time has passed in this way, the intellect awakens."
readings.teaches:
the ministers' counsel. व्यतीते काले is a locative absolute — "when the
time had passed", with no "when" in the Sanskrit.

notes.en: past — ब्रू is अदादि, so no शप् between root and ending
vocative — the ordinary way to address a king
what is to be studied — the gerundive's object stands in the nominative
accusative — a numeral agreeing with वर्षाणि
duration — how long the studying lasts, not what it acts on
accusative plural, the case of extent in time
gerundive — obligation, standing as the whole predicate

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → अध्येतव्यम्

notes.en: neuter nominative plural — the same compound shape on a second stem

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → एवं

notes.en: past participle in the locative — half of the सति सप्तमी
the locative absolute — "when time had passed in this way"
प्र + बुध् in the middle — it wakes of itself

readings.vyakhya: व्यतीते काले — सति सप्तमी। द्वादश वर्षाणि — कालद्वितीया।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two constructions here do work that English gives to conjunctions.
व्यतीते काले is a noun and a participle both in the locative, and together
they mean "when the time had passed" — no "when" anywhere in the Sanskrit.
Once recognised, it is everywhere in classical prose.

And द्वादश वर्षाणि is accusative, though nothing is being acted on. The
accusative also marks extent — how long, how far — so "for twelve years"
takes the same case as an object would.

source.ref: Pañcatantra, कथामुख — Viṣṇuśarman's offer
source.curated: Viṣṇuśarman's undertaking, lightly abridged; the words are the text's own

readings.sentence: अथ विष्णुशर्मा नाम ब्राह्मणः अवदत् — देव, एतान् राजपुत्रान् षण्मासाभ्यन्तरे नीतिशास्त्रज्ञान् करिष्यामि। यदि न करोमि तदा देवः मम नाम त्यजतु।
readings.translation: Then a brahmin named Viṣṇuśarman said — "Your Majesty, within six months I will make these princes knowers of the science of policy. If I do not, then let Your Majesty discard my name."
readings.teaches:
the promise the Pañcatantra hangs on. नीतिशास्त्रज्ञान् is the second
accusative of "make X into Y"; त्यजतु stakes an oath.

notes.en: nominative — an अन्-stem, so the न् drops in the bare form
षट् मासाः — a numeral compound, then "within" compounded onto it
locative — the span inside which the thing happens

words.gloss: knowers of the science of policy

notes.en: नीतिशास्त्रं जानन्ति इति — the object sits inside the compound with ज्ञ
the SECOND accusative — "make them INTO knowers"

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → करिष्यामि

notes.en: present — कृ is तनादि, taking उ rather than शप्
agent — the king referred to in the third person, as courtesy requires
object of त्यजतु — a different नाम from the indeclinable above
imperative, third person — a formal undertaking, not a command

notes.role: लोट् च — the imperative → त्यजतु

readings.vyakhya: नाम इति द्विः — अव्ययं नाम, नाम्नः नाम च। संदर्भः भेदं दर्शयति।
readings.vyakhya_en:
नाम appears twice and is not the same word. विष्णुशर्मा नाम ब्राह्मणः is
the indeclinable, "by name"; मम नाम त्यजतु is the noun नामन् in the
accusative, the thing to be discarded. Nothing but position and sense
separates them.

And note त्यजतु. A third-person imperative aimed at the king is not an
order — it is how a formal oath is staked: let my name be thrown away if I
fail. The grammar is imperative; the force is a wager.

source.ref: Pañcatantra, कथामुख — the frame
source.curated: the opening of the frame story, lightly abridged; the words are the text's own

readings.sentence: अस्ति दाक्षिणात्ये जनपदे महिलारोप्यं नाम नगरम्। तत्र अमरशक्तिर् नाम राजा बभूव। तस्य त्रयः पुत्राः परमदुर्मेधसः आसन्। ततः राजा मन्त्रिणः आहूय उवाच — किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् इति।
readings.translation: There is, in a southern country, a city named Mahilāropya. There ruled a king named Amaraśakti. He had three sons, exceedingly dull-witted. Then the king, having summoned his ministers, said — "What is to be done here?"
readings.teaches:
the Pañcatantra frame, in the same अस्ति … नाम नगरम् formula. Closes on
किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् — a whole question with no verb in it.

notes.en: the same opening formula as the Hitopadeśa passage
"belonging to the south" — from दक्षिण with vṛddhi

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → महिलारोप्यं

notes.en: अमरशक्तिः + नाम — the visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
nominative — the न् of राजन् drops in the bare form

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the final न् of the stem drops → राजा

notes.en: the perfect — reduplicated भू → बभूव, beside आसन् below

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — the perfect for what lies outside the speaker's sight → बभूव

notes.en: genitive — Sanskrit says "of him were three sons" for "he had"
परम + दुर्मेधस् — "extremely of-bad-intellect", one word in Sanskrit
past plural — the imperfect beside the perfect बभूव above
the gerund with a preverb — आ + ह्वे, the summoning before the speaking

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले — the earlier of two acts by one agent → आहूय

notes.en: the perfect — a third narrative past in four sentences
neuter nominative — the subject of the gerundive
the gerundive — obligation, and it needs no verb to predicate it

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → कर्तव्यम्

readings.vyakhya: अस्ति नाम नगरम् — कथामुखस्य रूढा रीतिः। हितोपदेशे अपि सैव।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The same three words open this as opened the Hitopadeśa passage: अस्ति,
then a place, then नाम and the name. It is a formula, and recognising it
is worth more than parsing it — a classical story announces itself this way
and the reader can stop working until the कथा actually starts.

किम् अत्र कर्तव्यम् has no verb in it. कर्तव्यम् is a gerundive, "to-be-done",
and that is the whole predicate: what, here, is to-be-done. Sanskrit builds
a complete question out of a participle and two indeclinables.

source.ref: Hitopadeśa, मित्रलाभ — the frame of the कथामुख
source.curated: the opening of the frame story, lightly abridged; the words are the text's own

readings.sentence: अस्ति भागीरथीतीरे पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं नगरम्। तत्र सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः सुदर्शनो नाम नरपतिः आसीत्। सः भूपतिः एकदा केनचित् पठ्यमानं श्लोकद्वयं शुश्राव।
readings.translation: There is, on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, a city named Pāṭaliputra. There lived a king called Sudarśana, endowed with every quality of a sovereign. One day that lord of the earth heard two verses being recited by someone.
readings.teaches:
the Hitopadeśa frame opens. Three long compounds — भागीरथीतीरे,
पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं, सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः — of the kind classical prose runs on.

notes.en: present — the storyteller's opening, "there is / there was"

words.gloss: on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī

notes.en: भागीरथ्याः तीरे — "the bank OF the Gaṅgā", compounded

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं

notes.en: "having Pāṭaliputra as its name" — the compound describes the city, not itself
neuter nominative — what अस्ति asserts the existence of

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → नगरम्

words.gloss: endowed with every quality of a sovereign

notes.en: सर्वस्वामिगुणैः उपेतः — a four-member compound, resolved from the end backwards
उपेत is a past participle — "come near to, endowed with"
सुदर्शनः + नाम — the visarga becomes ओ before a voiced sound
past of अस् — the frame shifts from अस्ति to आसीत्
भुवः पतिः — a second compound for the same man, as classical prose prefers
the agent of the passive participle — who was doing the reciting
instrumental, with the indefinite particle चित्
the present participle of the PASSIVE — पठ् + य + मान
the passive विकरण — what is recited, not who recites

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — यक् in the passive → पठ्यमान
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → श्लोकद्वयं

notes.en: द्वौ श्लोकौ — a numeral compound, taken as a single neuter aggregate
the perfect — reduplicated श्रु → शुश्राव, the narrative past of a told tale

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — the perfect for a past outside the speaker's sight → शुश्राव

readings.vyakhya: कथामुखम् — अस्ति इति आरम्भः। समासबहुला गद्यरीतिः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Up to here the attested readings have been single-line maxims. This is
narrative, and it moves differently: three of its nouns are compounds
several members deep — भागीरथीतीरे, सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः, पाटलिपुत्रनामधेयं —
and unpacking them is most of the work of reading classical prose.

Take सर्वस्वामिगुणोपेतः from the back: उपेत, "endowed with"; endowed with
गुण, qualities; whose qualities — those of a सर्वस्वामिन्, an absolute
lord. English needs a clause where Sanskrit uses one word.

source.ref: Hitopadeśa, मित्रलाभ — the verses the king overhears
source.curated: the two ślokas of the frame, as the text gives them

readings.sentence: अनेकसंशयोच्छेदि परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम्। सर्वस्य लोचनं शास्त्रं यस्य नास्त्य् अन्ध एव सः॥
readings.translation: Destroying many doubts, revealing what lies beyond sight — learning is the eye of everyone; he who has it not is blind indeed.
readings.teaches:
the verse the king overhears. परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम् — an agent-noun takes
the षष्ठी where the sense is transitive.

notes.en: अनेकान् संशयान् उच्छिनत्ति इति — the object stands inside the compound
genitive governed by दर्शकम् — an agent-noun takes the षष्ठी, not the द्वितीया

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — before a कृत् form, the object stands in the षष्ठी → परोक्षार्थस्य
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → लोचनं
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → शास्त्रं

notes.en: neuter nominative — the subject of the whole verse
genitive of possession — "of whom there is not"
न + अस्ति — the vowels merge, and the ि becomes य् before the next vowel

notes.role: इको यणचि — इ before a vowel becomes य् → नास्त्य् अन्धः

notes.en: nominative — the predicate, with no verb needed

readings.vyakhya: शास्त्रं लोचनम्। यस्य तत् नास्ति सः अन्धः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The verse says learning is an eye, and then does not soften it: whoever
lacks it is blind — अन्ध एव सः, with एव refusing the metaphor any room.

परोक्षार्थस्य दर्शकम् is worth slowing on. दर्शक is "one who shows", and
what it shows stands in the genitive rather than the accusative. That is
regular before a कृत् form and catches most readers the first time: the
sense is transitive, the case is not.

readings.translation: Knowledge gives humility.
readings.teaches: a line of Hitopadeśa, read whole — an आ-stem feminine agent, a कर्मन् in the द्वितीया, a present verb

notes.text: an आ-stem feminine (formed with टाप्)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — feminines like विद्या take टाप् (the आ-ending); विद्या stands in प्रथमा
वर्तमाने लट् → present tense
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → विनय is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → विनयम्

readings.vyakhya: विद्या कर्त्री, विनयः कर्म, ददाति क्रिया — सर्वं पूर्वोक्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first real sentence, from the Hitopadeśa — and you can already read it. विद्या (knowledge) is the कर्तृ in प्रथमा; विनयम् (humility) is the कर्मन् in द्वितीया; ददाति (gives) is a present-tense verb. Every piece is grammar you have met on toy sentences; here it stands in real Sanskrit, unchanged.
