source.curated: second quarter of the same verse as rd001; taken whole

readings.translation: From humility one attains worthiness.
readings.teaches: the next quarter of the same verse — विनयात् is अपादान, the पञ्चमी of "from"

notes.en: source — that from which one proceeds

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the starting point (humility, whence worthiness comes) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → विनयात् (→ विनयाद् before the voiced य, by जश्त्व)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पात्रता is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पात्रताम्

readings.vyakhya: विनयात् इति अपादानम्, पात्रताम् इति कर्म। एकस्माद् गुणाद् अन्यः फलति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse continues: from humility (विनयाद्, अपादान/पञ्चमी) one attains worthiness (पात्रताम्, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). Note विनयात् → विनयाद् — the final त् softens to द् before the voiced य (जश्त्व, the consonant-sandhi you met). Real text, real sandhi, all grammar you hold. The chain so far: knowledge → humility → worthiness.

source.ref: Hit_0.6 (pāda c)
source.curated: third quarter; taken whole

readings.translation: From worthiness one obtains wealth.
readings.teaches: third link of the same chain — the अपादान→कर्मन् pattern is now a rhythm

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the source (worthiness) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → पात्रत्वात् (→ पात्रत्वाद् before the voiced ध, जश्त्व)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → धनम्

readings.vyakhya: पात्रत्वाद् इति अपादानम्, धनम् इति कर्म — स एव विधिः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same shape a third time: from worthiness (पात्रत्वाद्, पञ्चमी) one obtains wealth (धनम्, द्वितीया). Once you see the अपादान→कर्मन् rhythm — "from X, attain Y" — the verse reads itself. पात्रत्वात् → पात्रत्वाद् again by जश्त्व before ध.

source.ref: Hit_0.6 (pāda d)
source.curated: fourth quarter, completing the verse; taken whole

readings.translation: From wealth, righteousness; from that, happiness.
readings.teaches: the closing link, with the repeated verb left unspoken — आप्नोति is understood

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → धनात् (→ धनाद् before voiced ध, जश्त्व)
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → धर्मं

notes.text: धर्मम् → धर्मं (final म् → anusvāra before त, the sandhi you met)

notes.en: indeclinable adverb (= "from that", standing for तस्मात्)

readings.vyakhya: धनाद् धर्मः, धर्मात् सुखम् — क्रिया अनुवर्तते। विद्यायाः सुखपर्यन्तः क्रमः।
readings.vyakhya_en: The verse closes: from wealth, righteousness (धर्मं); from that (ततः), happiness (सुखम्). The verb आप्नोति is not repeated — it is understood, carried over (अनुवृत्ति) from the previous line, exactly as a sūtra carries words forward. You have now read a whole verse: विद्या → विनय → पात्रत्व → धन → धर्म → सुख, knowledge leading step by step to happiness.

readings.sentence: सुतप्तम् अपि पानीयं शमयत्य् एव पावकम्।
readings.translation: Even well-heated water puts out fire.
readings.teaches: the first line of Pañcatantra — a complete maxim, with the particle अपि

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → सुतप्तम्

notes.en: adjective qualifying पानीयम् (agrees with it — neuter, प्रथमा)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → पानीय (water) is the agent
अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem प्रथमा → पानीयम् (→ पानीयं, anusvāra before श)
वर्तमाने लट् → present
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पावक (fire) is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पावकम्

readings.vyakhya: पानीयं कर्तृ, पावकम् कर्म, शमयति क्रिया। अपि-शब्देन विरोधः सूच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: A complete Pañcatantra maxim, and it parses cleanly: पानीयं (water, कर्तृ/प्रथमा) शमयति (extinguishes) पावकम् (fire, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). The particle अपि ("even") + सुतप्तम् ("well-heated") carry the twist — even water that has itself been heated still quells fire. Real text, real rhetoric, grammar you hold.

readings.sentence: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतोऽपि गुणवान् पूज्यते नरः।
readings.translation: A virtuous man, though born of whomever, is honored.
readings.teaches: a genitive relative यस्य कस्य, and a passive verb पूज्यते

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् is a सर्वनाम (pronoun)
षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive → यस्य

notes.text: यस्य कस्य together = "of no matter whom"

notes.en: agent (a past participle agreeing with नरः)

notes.text: प्रसूतः → प्रसूतो before अपि (visarga sandhi)

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.text: passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) — "is honored", as भुज्यन्ते earlier

notes.en: agent (here the grammatical subject of the passive)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → नर

readings.vyakhya: यस्य कस्य प्रसूतः अपि — सम्बन्धः अनिश्चितः; गुणवान् नरः पूज्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The genitive pair यस्य कस्य ("of whomsoever") waives the question of birth; अपि ("even/though") concedes it; and the verse turns on पूज्यते — "is honored," a passive, the same कर्मणि form you met in नरैः फलानि भुज्यन्ते. The sense: a man of merit (गुणवान्) is honored whatever his lineage. A relative clause and a passive, working together in real Sanskrit.

readings.sentence: न अग्निस् तृप्यति काष्ठानां न अपगानां महोदधिः।
readings.translation: Fire is not sated with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers.
readings.teaches: a genitive plural for what one is sated with, and the कर्मधारय compound महा + उदधि

notes.text: the इ-stem अग्नि you declined (अग्निः); न+अग्निः → नाग्निः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — the thing one is sated OF

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the relational genitive; "sated of logs" takes षष्ठी

notes.en: compound — महा (great) + उदधि (ocean), adjective+noun same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — महा+उदधि is a कर्मधारय (महा+उदधि → महोदधि by सन्धि)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः काष्ठानां न तृप्यति, महोदधिः अपगानां न — षष्ठी तृप्तेः विषये।
readings.vyakhya_en: Two parallel clauses: fire (अग्निः) is not sated of logs (काष्ठानां, genitive plural), the great ocean (महोदधिः, a कर्मधारय compound = महा "great" + उदधि "ocean") not of rivers. The genitive marks what one is sated *of*; the verb तृप्यति is shared across both halves. You now meet your own grammar — इ-stem, षष्ठी, कर्मधारय — in a real Pañcatantra verse.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निमी॑ळे पु॒रोहि॑तं य॒ज्ञस्य॑ दे॒वमृ॒त्विजं॑। होता॑रं रत्न॒धात॑मं॥
readings.translation: I praise Agni, the chosen priest, god, minister of the sacrifice, the invoker, lavisher of treasure.
readings.teaches: the accent marks appear for the first time — ॒ anudātta and ॑ for the udātta context. The grammar is already familiar: accusatives in apposition, a present verb

notes.en: "accent — the marks ॒ (anudātta, low) and ॑ (udātta/svarita); the underline on अ॒ is anudātta"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अग्निम् (the इ-stem अग्नि you declined, here accusative)
तङानावात्मनेपदम् — ईळे is आत्मनेपद (the middle voice you met in पचते)

words.gloss: the one placed in front — the chosen priest

notes.text: padapāṭha shows the compound split: पुरः-हित (saṃhitā पुरोहितम्)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → यज्ञस्य

words.gloss: the sacrificing priest, minister of the rite
the invoker (the priest who calls the gods)

notes.en: an ऋ-stem (होतृ, like कर्तृ) in the accusative → होतारम्

notes.text: padapāṭha split रत्न-धातम (saṃhitā रत्नधातमम्)

readings.vyakhya: सर्वाणि कर्माणि अग्निविशेषणानि — द्वितीयायाम्। स्वराः उपरि अधश्च चिह्निताः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Your first Vedic verse, and the grammar is already yours: ईळे "I praise" governs a string of accusatives all in apposition to अग्निम् — पुरोहितम्, देवम्, ऋत्विजम्, होतारम्, रत्नधातमम् — "I praise Agni: priest, god, minister, invoker, treasure-giver." The ONE new thing is accent: the underline ॒ marks anudātta (low pitch), the stroke ॑ marks the raised/svarita pitch. Each word's accent is shown in its padapāṭha (isolated) form — पुरोहितं appears word-alone as पुरः-हितम्. Read it aloud with the pitches: this is how the Veda is chanted.

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निः पूर्वे॑भि॒र्ऋषि॑भि॒रीड्यो॒ नूत॑नैरु॒त। स दे॒वाँ एह व॑क्षति॥
readings.translation: Agni, worthy to be praised by ancient seers and by new ones too — may he bring the gods here.
readings.teaches: the second verse of the same hymn — अग्नि now stands as कर्तृ, and the agents come in the instrumental plural

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → Agni is now the agent (नॉम, vs अग्निम् acc in verse 1)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → "by the ancient seers" takes तृतीया (the -भिः ending you met in नरैः)

notes.text: a gerundive (कृत्य) of ईड् "praise" — "fit to be praised"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः (he), the तद् pronoun
कर्मणि द्वितीया → देवान् (acc. plural)

notes.text: a future/subjunctive sense — "he will/may bring"

readings.vyakhya: अग्निः पूर्वैः नूतनैश्च ऋषिभिः ईड्यः; स देवान् इह आ वक्षति।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same hymn's second verse, and the frame holds: अग्निः is now the कर्तृ (nominative — last verse he was अग्निम्, the object). The seers who praise him stand in the तृतीया (पूर्वेभिः, ऋषिभिः, नूतनैः — "by the ancient, by the seers, by the new"), the same instrumental "by" you met in नरैः. ईड्यः is a gerundive — "to-be-praised." Then सः (he) देवान् (the gods, acc.) आ … वक्षति — "may bring here." One word, अग्नि, you now know in two cases and with its accent.

source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.translation: Through Agni one may win wealth and growth day by day — glorious, most rich in heroes.
readings.teaches: अग्नि now in the instrumental — अग्निना "through," the करण sense — beside the आम्रेडित दिवेदिवे "day after day"

words.gloss: through Agni, by means of Agni

notes.en: instrument — that by which the gain is won

notes.role: साधकतमं करणम् — Agni is the करण (the most effective means)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → अग्निना (the इ-stem, now तृतीया — a third case for अग्नि)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → रयिम् (an इ-stem accusative, like अग्निम्)

notes.text: a subjunctive (लेट्) sense — "may/shall win"

notes.en: object (a second thing won, alongside रयिम्)

notes.text: an आम्रेडित — the word दिवे doubled (दिवे-दिवे) to mean "day after day"

notes.en: adjective qualifying रयिम् (an अस्-stem in द्वितीया)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वीरवत्-तम (saṃhitā वीरवत्तमम्)

notes.en: superlative adjective qualifying रयिम् (a वत्-stem + तम superlative)

readings.vyakhya: अग्निना इति करणम्, रयिं पोषं च कर्म। दिवेदिवे इति आम्रेडितम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now अग्नि steps into a third case: अग्निना, the तृतीया — "through Agni." You have met this stem as object (अग्निम्), as agent (अग्निः), and here as instrument (अग्निना): one इ-stem across three कारकas. Through Agni one wins रयिम् (wealth) and पोषम् (growth), both accusatives, qualified by यशसं वीरवत्तमं ("glorious, hero-rich"). दिवेदिवे — दिवे doubled — is an आम्रेडित, "day after day."

readings.sentence: अग्ने॒ यं य॒ज्ञम॑ध्व॒रं वि॒श्वतः॑ परि॒भूरसि॑। स इद्दे॒वेषु॑ गच्छति॥
readings.translation: O Agni, the sacrifice, the rite which you encompass on every side — that alone goes to the gods.
readings.teaches: a Vedic relative-correlative यं … सः, the vocative अग्ने "O Agni," and असि "you are"

notes.role: सम्बोधने च — the vocative; अग्ने (a fourth use of अग्नि, now address)
सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → यद् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits परि-भू (saṃhitā परिभूः); परि "around" + भू "be"

notes.en: 2nd person — "you are" (the मध्यम you met in गच्छसि)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → देवेषु (सप्तमी, locative plural)

readings.vyakhya: अग्ने इति सम्बोधनम्; यं यज्ञं परिभूः असि, स इत् देवेषु गच्छति।
readings.vyakhya_en: A relative-correlative, Vedic style: यं … (यज्ञम् अध्वरं) … सः — "which sacrifice … that one." अग्ने is the सम्बोधन (vocative, "O Agni") — your fourth case-use of this one stem. असि is "you are," 2nd person (मध्यमपुरुष), matching the सम्बोधन. The sense: the rite that Agni encloses on every side (विश्वतः परिभूः) — *that one alone* (स इत्) reaches the gods (देवेषु, locative).

source.ref: RV 1.1.5 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ क॒विक्र॑तुः स॒त्यश्चि॒त्रश्र॑वस्तमः। दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒रा ग॑मत्॥
readings.translation: Agni the invoker, wise in will, true, most brilliant in fame — a god, may he come with the gods.
readings.teaches: nominative epithets predicated without a verb, a बहुव्रीहि compound, and the instrumental of accompaniment

notes.en: epithet (in apposition to अग्निः) — an ऋ-stem nominative होता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits कवि-क्रतु (saṃhitā कविक्रतुः); कवि "sage" + क्रतु "will"

notes.en: possessive compound — "(one) whose क्रतु is that of a कवि"

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming an external possessor

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्रश्रवः-तम; चित्र "bright" + श्रवस् "fame" + तम superlative

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने → the accompanier takes तृतीया → देवेभिः ("with the gods")

notes.text: an aorist-subjunctive (लुङ्/लेट्) sense — "may he come"

readings.vyakhya: होता कविक्रतुः सत्यः चित्रश्रवस्तमः देवः — सर्वाणि अग्निविशेषणानि प्रथमायाम्। देवेभिः इति सहार्थे तृतीया।
readings.vyakhya_en: Verse 1 strung accusatives; this one strings NOMINATIVES. होता, कविक्रतुः, सत्यः, चित्रश्रवस्तमः, देवः — all प्रथमा, all naming अग्निः (predication, no copula needed). कविक्रतुः is a बहुव्रीहि: "(one) whose क्रतु is a sage's." Then देवेभिः is the तृतीया of accompaniment — "with the gods" — the सह-sense you met in पुत्रेण सह. आ गमत्: "may he come hither."

source.ref: RV 1.1.6 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: यदं॒ग दा॒शुषे॒ त्वमग्ने॑ भ॒द्रं क॑रि॒ष्यसि॑। तवेत्तत्स॒त्यमं॑गिरः॥
readings.translation: Whatever good you will do for the worshipper, O Agni — that, indeed, is your truth, O Aṅgiras.
readings.teaches: दाशुषे "for the giver" as सम्प्रदान in the चतुर्थी, and करिष्यसि in the future

notes.en: relative — here introducing the whole clause

words.gloss: for the worshipper, for the giver (of offerings)

notes.en: recipient — the one for whom the good is done

notes.role: कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् → the worshipper is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने
लृट् शेषे च → future → करिष्यसि (√कृ; 2sg, "you will do")
षष्ठी शेषे → तव ("your")

notes.en: vocative — a second address to Agni

readings.vyakhya: यत् भद्रं दाशुषे करिष्यसि, तत् तव सत्यम्। दाशुषे इति सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थी।
readings.vyakhya_en: A यत्…तत् sentence with two new turns. दाशुषे is the सम्प्रदान — the dative (चतुर्थी), "for the worshipper," the same "for whom" case you met in नमो देवेभ्यः. करिष्यसि is a FUTURE (लृट्), "you will do" — √कृ now in the future, 2nd person. Two vocatives frame it: अग्ने and अङ्गिरः (a name of Agni). The sense: whatever blessing you will do for the giver — *that* is your truth.

source.ref: RV 1.1.7 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: उप॑ त्वाग्ने दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ दोषा॑वस्तर्धि॒या व॒यं। नमो॒ भरं॑त॒ एम॑सि॥
readings.translation: To you, O Agni, day by day, by night and dawn, we come in thought, bearing homage.
readings.teaches: a first-person plural verb एमसि "we come," with वयम् and धिया "by thought" as the means

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

notes.text: the आम्रेडित दिवे-दिवे (met in rd010) — "every day"
padapāṭha splits दोषा-वस्तः; दोषा "at night" + वस्तर् "at dawn"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → धिया (तृतीया of the ई-stem धी)

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) agreeing with वयम् — "(we) bearing"

readings.vyakhya: वयं धिया नमो भरन्तः दिवेदिवे त्वा उप आ इमसि। एमसि इति उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The worshippers speak now in their own voice: वयम् "we," and एमसि (उप…आ…इमसि) "we come" — a 1st-person PLURAL verb (उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन), the same person you met as -मि in गच्छामि, now plural. To you (त्वा, accusative) we come, day by day (दिवेदिवे), at night and dawn (दोषावस्तः), in thought (धिया, तृतीया of means), bearing homage (नमः भरन्तः). A whole sentence of grammar you already hold.

source.ref: RV 1.1.8 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole — the object-string of verse 7 continued. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: राजं॑तमध्व॒राणां॑ गो॒पामृ॒तस्य॒ दीदि॑विं। वर्ध॑मानं॒ स्वे दमे॑॥
readings.translation: (To you,) ruling over the rites, the guardian of truth, the shining one, growing in your own home.
readings.teaches: accusative epithets continuing from the previous verse, with अध्वराणां "of the rites" in the genitive plural and स्वे दमे "in his own home" in the locative

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the accusative — "(you who are) ruling"

notes.en: accusative (apposed to the त्वा of verse 7)
genitive plural — that over which one rules

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → अध्वराणाम् ("of/over the rites")
षष्ठी शेषे → ऋतस्य

notes.text: a middle present participle (शानच्) in the accusative — "(you) growing"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → स्वे (सप्तमी, agreeing with दमे)

words.gloss: in the home, in the abode

readings.vyakhya: राजन्तं गोपां दीदिविं वर्धमानं — सर्वाणि कर्माणि (पूर्वस्या ऋचः त्वा-शब्दस्य विशेषणानि)। अध्वराणाम् ऋतस्य च षष्ठी; स्वे दमे इति सप्तमी।
readings.vyakhya_en: This verse has no new finite verb — it continues verse 7's "to you we come," piling accusative epithets onto that त्वा: राजन्तम् (ruling), गोपाम् (guardian), दीदिविम् (shining), वर्धमानम् (growing). Two participles (राजन्तम् active, वर्धमानम् middle) decline like nouns in the accusative. The genitives अध्वराणाम् (over the rites) and ऋतस्य (of truth) mark domain; स्वे दमे — सप्तमी — locates it: "in his own home." Cases you hold, stacked into Vedic praise.

source.ref: RV 1.1.9 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the hymn
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; the final verse of the hymn. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: स नः॑ पि॒तेव॑ सू॒नवेऽग्ने॑ सूपाय॒नो भ॑व। सच॑स्वा नः स्व॒स्तये॑॥
readings.translation: Be to us, O Agni, easy of approach, as a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.
readings.teaches: the simile पिता इव "like a father," datives of the one addressed — सूनवे, नः, स्वस्तये — and the imperatives भव and सचस्व

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → नः ("for us")

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पिता-इव; पिता (nom, the ऋ-stem you met) + इव "like"

notes.en: recipient — "(as a father) to a son"

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सूनवे (an उ-stem dative, गुण → सूनवे, like अग्नये)
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-उपायन; सु "well, easy" + उपायन "approach"

notes.en: predicate adjective of भव — "be (one) easy to approach"
imperative — "be!" (the command mood you met in गच्छतु)

notes.role: लोट् च — imperative → भव (2sg "be!")
लोट् च — imperative → सचस्व

notes.text: नः again — here "with us" (object/goal of सचस्व)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → स्वस्तये (an इ-stem dative, like अग्नये)

readings.vyakhya: पिता सूनवे इव, अग्ने नः सूपायनः भव; नः स्वस्तये सचस्व। चतुर्थ्यः बह्व्यः — सूनवे नः स्वस्तये।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with a prayer, dense with the चतुर्थी (dative): नः "for us," सूनवे "to a son," स्वस्तये "for well-being" — three datives, all the "for whom" case (सम्प्रदान). The heart is a simile: पिता इव सूनवे — "as a father (is) to a son." Two imperatives (लोट्) carry the request: भव "be!" and सचस्व "abide!" — the command mood you met in गच्छतु, here in real Vedic. With this you have read the whole first hymn of the Ṛgveda, end to end, with its accent.

source.ref: RV 1.2.1 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — opens the Vāyu hymn
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole — first verse of a new hymn. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वाय॒वा या॑हि दर्शते॒मे सोमा॒ अरं॑कृताः। तेषां॑ पाहि श्रु॒धी हवं॑॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu, come, beautiful one; these Soma-draughts are made ready — drink of them, hear our call.
readings.teaches: a new hymn (वायु); the invocation pattern — सम्बोधन (वायो) answered by imperatives (आ याहि, पाहि, श्रुधि)

notes.en: vocative — direct address (उ-stem वायु → वायो, गुण, like गुरो)

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → the vocative; वायो addresses the god
लोट् च — imperative → याहि

words.gloss: O beautiful one, O visible one

notes.en: vocative epithet — addressing Vāyu as "fair to see"
demonstrative pronoun "this" (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सोमाः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → इदम् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अरम्-कृत; अरम् "enough, fitly" + कृत "made"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → तद्
षष्ठी शेषे → तेषाम् (drink OF them)
लोट् च → पाहि
लोट् च → श्रुधि
कर्मणि द्वितीया → हवम् ("hear the call")

readings.vyakhya: वायो इति सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि पाहि श्रुधि इति लोडर्थाः। सोमाः कर्तारः, तेषां पाहि — षष्ठ्यर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new god — but the grammar is the invocation pattern you just met closing hymn 1. वायो is the सम्बोधन (vocative of the उ-stem वायु, गुण → वायो like गुरो), and it is answered by a volley of imperatives (लोट्): आ याहि "come!", पाहि "drink!", श्रुधि "hear!". The Somas (सोमाः, nominative plural) stand ready (अरंकृताः); drink *of them* — तेषाम्, a genitive (षष्ठी) in the partitive sense — and hear the call (हवम्, accusative). The whole verse is address + command, the heartbeat of Vedic prayer.

source.ref: RV 1.2.2 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वाय॑ उ॒क्थेभि॑र्जरंते॒ त्वामच्छा॑ जरि॒तारः॑। सु॒तसो॑मा अह॒र्विदः॑॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns — Soma-pressers who know the days.
readings.teaches: the worshippers named as agents — जरितारः, an ऋ-stem nominative plural — with उक्थेभिः "with hymns" as the means

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो

notes.en: means — that with which they praise

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → उक्थेभिः (तृतीया plural, Vedic -एभिः for -ऐः)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → त्वाम् ("you")

notes.en: indeclinable — "toward" (governs the praising directed AT Vāyu)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → जरितारः (the agents; an ऋ-stem nom. plural, like कर्तारः)

words.gloss: those who have pressed the Soma

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सुत-सोम; सुत "pressed" + सोम

notes.en: possessive compound — "(those) by whom Soma is pressed"

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अहः-विद्; अहर् "day" + विद् "knowing"

readings.vyakhya: जरितारः कर्तारः, त्वां कर्म, उक्थेभिः इति करणम्। सुतसोमाः अहर्विदः च तेषां विशेषणे।
readings.vyakhya_en: Hymn 1 ended with "we come"; here the worshippers are NAMED — जरितारः, "the singers," the agents (कर्तृ, an ऋ-stem nominative plural like कर्तारः). They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

source.ref: RV 1.2.3 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: वायो॒ तव॑ प्रपृंच॒ती धेना॑ जिगाति दा॒शुषे॑। उ॒रू॒ची सोम॑पीतये॥
readings.translation: O Vāyu, your nourishing stream goes to the worshipper, broad, for the Soma-drinking.
readings.teaches: a feminine subject धेना "stream," तव in the genitive of possession, and two datives — दाशुषे and सोमपीतये, the second one of purpose

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो
षष्ठी शेषे → तव

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्र-पृञ्चती; प्र + पृच् "fill, mingle"

notes.en: present participle (feminine, शतृ + ई) qualifying धेना

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → धेना (the subject)

notes.en: recipient — to whom the stream goes

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे (the dative you met in hymn 1)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सोम-पीतये; सोम + पीति "drinking"

notes.en: purpose — "for the sake of" (the dative of purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सोमपीतये (इ-stem dative, like स्वस्तये)

readings.vyakhya: तव धेना दाशुषे जिगाति। दाशुषे सोमपीतये च चतुर्थ्यौ — सम्प्रदाने तादर्थ्ये च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

source.ref: RV 1.2.4 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole. Accent verbatim (traditional Devanagari svara) from sri-aurobindo.co.in

readings.sentence: इंद्र॑वायू इ॒मे सु॒ता उप॒ प्रयो॑भि॒रा ग॑तं। इंद॑वो वामु॒शंति॒ हि॥
readings.translation: O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed (Somas) are here — come with delights; the drops long for you both.
readings.teaches: the dual arrives all at once — the paired deity इन्द्रवायू, the imperative आ गतम् "come, you two," and वाम्

notes.en: a dual द्वन्द्व compound — इन्द्र + वायु, two deities as one pair

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः → इन्द्रवायू ("Indra and Vāyu")

notes.en: demonstrative (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सुताः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → इदम्

notes.en: subject — the offerings (past participle of सु "press", used as noun)

words.gloss: with delights, with offerings of joy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्रयः-भिः; प्रयस् "delight, dainty" (अस्-stem)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → प्रयोभिः (तृतीया plural)

notes.en: imperative — but DUAL: "come, you two" (मध्यम द्विवचन)
subject (second clause) — the bright drops (उ-stem nom. plural)
object — whom the drops long for

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्रवायू इति द्वन्द्वः द्विवचने; आ गतम् इति द्विवचनलोट्; वाम् इति द्विवचनम्। द्वौ देवौ, द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

readings.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, you two take note of the pressed (Somas), O rich in plenty — come, you both, swiftly.
readings.teaches: the dual through the whole verse: चेतथः "you two perceive," the epithet वाजिनीवसू, and तौ

readings.vyakhya: वायुः इन्द्रश्च — द्वौ; चेतथः यातम् इति द्विवचने तिङन्ते। सर्वं द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

readings.teaches: निष्कृतं as the goal they come up to, सुन्वतः as the genitive of the one pressing, and the dual vocative नरा

notes.text: padapāṭha splits निः-कृत; निस् + कृत "made ready"

notes.en: goal of motion — "up to the readied (offering)"

readings.vyakhya: सुन्वतः निष्कृतम् उप आ यातम् — गत्यर्थे द्वितीया। नरा इति द्विवचनसम्बोधनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The pair is called again — यातम्, "come, you two" — but now with a goal: उप … निष्कृतम्, "up to the prepared offering," where the goal of motion takes the accusative (द्वितीया, just as a destination does). सुन्वतः ("of the presser") is a genitive: whose offering it is. धिया ("by thought") is the instrumental of means you already hold. And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

readings.translation: I call Mitra of pure discernment and Varuṇa the foe-destroyer, who make perfect the lucid thought.
readings.teaches: Mitra and Varuṇa enter as accusative objects, with हुवे "I call" and the dual participle साधन्ता

readings.vyakhya: मित्रं वरुणं च हुवे — द्वितीयायाम्। साधन्ता इति द्विवचनं कृदन्तम्, तयोः विशेषणम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

readings.vyakhya: ऋतेन इति करणम्; मित्रावरुणौ ऋतावृधौ ऋतस्पृशा — द्विवचनसम्बोधनानि; बृहन्तं क्रतुम् आशाथे — लिटि द्विवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Now Mitra-Varuṇa are ADDRESSED, as a single dual द्वन्द्व: मित्रावरुणौ (vocative dual), with two dual epithets, ऋतावृधौ ("Truth-increasers") and ऋतस्पृशा ("Truth-touchers"). The line opens with ऋतेन — "by the Truth," the instrumental of means. And the verb is new: आशाथे, "you two have attained" — a PERFECT (लिट्, the tense of चकार) in the DUAL. Tense, number, and compound all converge on the pair.

padapāṭha splits उरु-क्षय; उरु "wide" + क्षय "dwelling"

readings.vyakhya: कवी मित्रावरुणा तुविजाता उरुक्षया — द्विवचनप्रथमायाम्; नः दक्षम् अपसं दधाते — द्विवचनतिङन्तम्। हिमवत् सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with the pair as SUBJECTS, all in the nominative dual: कवी ("two seers"), मित्रावरुणा (now agents, not addressed), तुविजाता ("mightily born"), उरुक्षया ("wide-dwelling"). They दधाते — "the two hold" — a present DUAL verb of √धा, the same root as ददाति "gives." For us (नः, dative) they hold दक्षम् अपसम् ("a working skill," accusative). You have now read the whole second hymn, and through it drilled the entire dual — noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, and verb across three tenses.

readings.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new dual pair: the अश्विन्s, the twin horsemen, addressed throughout in the dual vocative — अश्विना, द्रवत्पाणी ("swift-handed"), शुभस्पती ("lords of bliss"), पुरुभुजा ("of many bounties"). They are asked to चनस्यतम् — "take pleasure, you two" — a DUAL imperative (लोट्), the same dual-of-command you met as आ गतम् in rd020. What they enjoy is यज्वरीः इषः, "the worshipper's offerings," an accusative PLURAL object (कर्मन्). The dual you drilled across RV 1.2 now carries to a fresh pair.

readings.vyakhya_en: The Aśvins again, addressed as नरा — which is नरौ, the dual of नर, the first noun this whole reader ever declined, now standing in a Vedic hymn. They are to वनतम् ("win, you two," dual imperative) the गिरः, "songs of praise" (accusative plural object). The means is शवीरया धिया, "with forceful thought" — an INSTRUMENTAL (करण, तृतीया), the same धी "thought" you met as धिया in rd014. One verse braids three threads you already hold: the dual address, the accusative object, and the instrument of means.

readings.vyakhya_en: The triplet to the Aśvins closes with a NOMINATIVE string describing the offering: युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — "the pressed (soma), yearning for you, with sacred grass strewn." These are predicates: the rite is ready. The pair, addressed as दस्रा ("wondrous"), नासत्या ("truthful"), रुद्रवर्तनी ("of Rudra's path"), are bidden आ यातम् — "come, you two" — the very dual imperative you first met as आ गतम् in rd020. The Aśvin hymn is complete.

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र चित्रभानो — सम्बोधने एकवचनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम् (द्विवचनयातमः प्रतियोगि); सुताः इमे त्वायवः पूतासः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; अण्वीभिः तना — तृतीया करणे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn turns from the pair to a single god, and the grammar turns with it: इन्द्र is a SINGULAR vocative, and he is bidden आ याहि — "come!" — a 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative, exactly the dual आ यातम् of rd028 with one fewer. Hold the two side by side: यातम् = "come, you two," याहि = "come, you one." The soma is described in a nominative string (सुताः … त्वायवः … पूतासः, "pressed … longing for you … purified"), strained अण्वीभिः, "through the fine filter" (instrumental of means). The dual you drilled all through RV 1.2 now has its singular foil.

readings.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि धि॒येषि॒तो विप्र॑जूतः सु॒ताव॑तः। उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि वा॒घतः॑॥
readings.translation: Come, O Indra, urged on by the thought, hastened by the seers — up to the prayers of the soma-pressing worshipper.
readings.teaches: आ याहि again in the singular, उप governing ब्रह्माणि "the prayers" as its goal, and धिया as the means

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → याहि

notes.en: instrument — "urged BY the thought" (the धी met in rd027)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → धिया

notes.text: इषित = क्त-participle of इष् "impel" — "(you,) urged on"
padapāṭha splits विप्र-जूतः; विप्र "inspired seer" + जूत "sped, urged"

words.gloss: of the soma-presser, of him who has pressed (soma)

notes.text: सुतावत् = सुत "pressed soma" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"

notes.en: preverb — "toward," directing the motion to ब्रह्माणि
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ब्रह्माणि (neut. acc. pl.)

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the reciter

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धिया — तृतीया करणे; इषितः विप्रजूतः — क्तान्तविशेषणे; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया कर्मणि गत्यर्थे; सुतावतः वाघतः — षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The same call — आ याहि, "come" — but now Indra is moved BY something and moves TO something. He is धिया इषितः, "urged on by the thought" (instrumental of means, the धी you met as धिया in rd027), and विप्रजूतः, "hastened by the seers." Where to? उप ब्रह्माणि वाघतः — "up to the prayers of the worshipper," where उप is a preverb steering the verb of motion onto an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि), and वाघतः is a genitive ("of the worshipper"). Means in the instrumental, goal in the accusative, possession in the genitive — three cases you hold, in one line of the Veda.

readings.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि॒ तूतु॑जान॒ उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि हरिवः। सु॒ते द॑धिष्व न॒श्चनः॑॥
readings.translation: Come, O Indra, hastening, up to the prayers, O lord of the bay steeds; at the pressing take delight in us.
readings.teaches: सुते "at the pressing" as a locative of occasion, the middle imperative दधिष्व "take, for yourself," and नः in the dative

notes.en: 2nd person — singular imperative (third time in the triplet)

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → याहि

notes.text: तूतुजान = perfect middle participle of तुज् "speed" — "(you,) hastening"

notes.en: preverb directing motion to ब्रह्माणि (as in rd030)
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ब्रह्माणि (neut. acc. pl.)

words.gloss: O lord of the bay steeds

notes.text: हरिवत् = हरि "bay horse" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"; here vocative हरिवः

words.gloss: at the pressing, when (the soma) is pressed

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press," here LOCATIVE — "at the pressed (soma)"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → अधिकरण → सुते

notes.en: "hold, place, take" — the same √धा of दधाते (rd025), here MIDDLE imperative
2nd person — singular MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative "take for yourself"

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → दधिष्व

notes.en: for us / in us — the enclitic नः
object — "take delight" (the चन- of चनस्यतम्, rd026, now as a noun)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → चनः

readings.vyakhya: इन्द्र हरिवः — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे; सुते — सप्तमी अधिकरणे; दधिष्व — लोटि आत्मनेपदम्; नः चनः — आत्मने ग्रहणम्। इन्द्रसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The third and last call to Indra adds one new case: सुते, a LOCATIVE — "at the pressing," the occasion when the soma is pressed (अधिकरण, सप्तमी, by 2.3.36). The verb दधिष्व is √धा again — the root of दधाते "the two hold" in rd025 — but here a MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative, "take FOR YOURSELF," carrying delight (चनः, the noun of the very चनस्यतम् "take pleasure" that opened the hymn in rd026). The triplet to Indra is complete: three times "come," each adding a case — instrument, goal, and now occasion.

readings.sentence: ओमा॑सश्चर्षणीधृतो॒ विश्वे॑ देवास॒ आ ग॑त। दा॒श्वांसो॑ दा॒शुषः॑ सु॒तं॥
readings.translation: O helpers, upholders of men, O All-Gods, come — you bestowers, to the soma of the worshipper.
readings.teaches: the address turns plural — after the dual Aśvins and Indra alone, the All-Gods as a crowd: विश्वे देवासः in the vocative plural, and आ गत "come, you all"

notes.text: ओमास् = Vedic nom./voc. pl. of ओमन् "helper, friend"

notes.en: vocative PLURAL — a whole company addressed
plural (contrast dual अश्विना rd026, singular इन्द्र rd029)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चर्षणि-धृतः; चर्षणि "men, peoples" + धृत् "holding, upholding"

notes.en: "all" — qualifying देवासः, the standard epithet विश्वे देवाः "All-Gods"

notes.text: देवासः = Vedic voc./nom. pl. of देव (classical देवाः)

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as आ गतम् (dual, rd020)
2nd person — PLURAL imperative ("you all, come"), vs dual गतम्, sg याहि

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → गत

notes.text: दाश्वस् = perfect active participle of दाश् "give, worship" — "having given"

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the giver

notes.text: दाशुषः = genitive sg of the SAME दाश्वस् stem — here "of the (human) worshipper"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्

readings.vyakhya: ओमासः चर्षणीधृतः विश्वे देवासः दाश्वांसः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; आ गत — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचनम्; दाशुषः — षष्ठी; सुतम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि।
readings.vyakhya_en: The number completes its circle. RV 1.3 has now addressed a DUAL (the Aśvins, आ यातम्), a SINGULAR (Indra, आ याहि), and here a PLURAL — विश्वे देवासः, "all the gods," a whole company, bidden आ गत, "come, you all." Set the three imperatives of √गम्/√या side by side: यातम् (two), याहि (one), गत (many). Every vocative here is plural too — ओमासः, चर्षणीधृतः, दाश्वांसः. They come दाशुषः सुतम्, "to the worshipper's pressed soma" (genitive + accusative goal). One hymn has now drilled the entire तीन वचन.

readings.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒प्तुरः॑ सु॒तमा गं॑त॒ तूर्ण॑यः। उ॒स्रा इ॑व॒ स्वस॑राणि॥
readings.translation: O All-Gods, crossing the waters, swift, come to the soma — like cattle to their pastures.
readings.teaches: the plural imperative again in आ गन्त, and a simile with इव — "like cattle to their pastures," a locative of goal inside a comparison

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अप्-तुरः; अप् "waters" + तुर् "crossing, speeding"

notes.en: goal of motion — "(come) to the soma"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्
लोट् च → imperative → गन्त

words.gloss: like cows, like the ruddy cattle

notes.text: उस्राः "cattle" (nom. pl.) + इव "like" — the subject of the simile

notes.en: standard of comparison — "as cattle (come to pastures)"

words.gloss: to the pastures, to the home-stalls

notes.en: goal within the simile — "(as cattle come) to the pastures"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → स्वसराणि (neut. acc. pl.)

readings.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अप्तुरः तूर्णयः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; सुतम् आ गन्त — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे लोटि बहुवचनम्; उस्राः इव स्वसराणि — उपमा (इव), द्वितीया गत्यर्थे।
readings.vyakhya_en: The plural call repeats — सुतम् आ गन्त, "come to the soma, all of you" — but the verse closes with a SIMILE: उस्राः इव स्वसराणि, "like cattle (coming) to their pastures." इव "like" marks the comparison; उस्राः ("cattle") is the standard (nominative), and स्वसराणि ("pastures") is its accusative goal, mirroring सुतम्, the gods' own goal. The grammar of the simile is the grammar of the main clause — a goal-of-motion accusative in both halves. As cattle to the fold, so the gods to the soma.

readings.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒स्रिध॒ एहि॑मायासो अ॒द्रुहः॑। मेधं॑ जुषंत॒ वह्न॑यः॥
readings.translation: The All-Gods, unfailing, of ever-approaching power, free of malice — may they, the bearers (of sacrifice), enjoy the offering.
readings.teaches: the verse turns from address to statement: the gods now stand in the nominative, and जुषन्त "may they enjoy" closes the hymn on a wish

notes.en: "all" — now NOMINATIVE (the gods as subject, not addressed)

notes.text: देवासः — here NOMINATIVE (subject), not vocative as in rd032-033
अ-स्रिध् "not failing" (privative अ + स्रिध् "err")

words.gloss: of ever-approaching power, whose wisdom comes near

notes.text: padapāṭha splits एहि-मायासः; एहि "come!" + माया "power, wisdom" — bahuvrīhi
अ-द्रुह् "not hostile" (privative अ + द्रुह् "harm")

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → मेधम्

words.gloss: may they enjoy, let them take pleasure in

notes.en: "enjoy, take pleasure in" — 3rd-person PLURAL (injunctive, wish sense)
the Vedic subjunctive (लिङर्थे लेट्, 3.4.7) — the wish "may they enjoy"
3rd person plural — "may they enjoy" (the gods as subject)

words.gloss: the bearers (of the sacrifice), the conveyers

notes.text: वह्नि "bearer, conveyer" (from वह् "carry") — in apposition to देवासः

readings.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अस्रिधः एहिमायासः अद्रुहः वह्नयः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; मेधम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; जुषन्त — प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनम्। विश्वेदेवसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The hymn's grammar turns one last time: from ADDRESS to STATEMENT. Through rd032–033 the gods were vocatives ("O All-Gods, come!"); here देवासः is NOMINATIVE — the SUBJECT — qualified by a string of nominative adjectives (अस्रिधः "unfailing," एहिमायासः a bahuvrīhi "whose power approaches," अद्रुहः "guileless," वह्नयः "bearers"). The verb is no longer an imperative TO them but a 3rd-person wish ABOUT them: मेधं जुषन्त, "may they enjoy the offering." The same noun in two cases across one triplet — vocative when called, nominative when described — is the whole lesson of address vs predication. The Viśvedevas triplet, and three-quarters of RV 1.3, complete.

readings.sentence: पा॒व॒का नः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ वाजे॑भिर्वा॒जिनी॑वती। य॒ज्ञं व॑ष्टु धि॒याव॑सुः॥
readings.translation: Purifying Sarasvatī, rich in plenitudes through her abundances, treasure of thought — may she desire our sacrifice.
readings.teaches: one feminine subject — सरस्वती, an ī-stem nominative — with वष्टु "may she desire" and वाजेभिः as accompaniment

notes.text: पावका = feminine of पावक "purifier" (टाप् आ by 4.1.4)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् → feminine आ → पावका

notes.text: सरस्वती — feminine ई-stem (the नदी class you met as नदी in rd010)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → वाजेभिः

notes.text: वाजिनीवती = वाजिनी "abundance" + मतुप् (वत्), feminine ई — "she who has abundance"

notes.en: object — what she is to desire

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

words.gloss: may she desire, let her wish

notes.en: 3rd person singular — a wish-imperative addressed about her

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → वष्टु

words.gloss: treasure of thought, rich through insight

notes.text: padapāṭha splits धिया-वसुः; धी "thought" + वसु "wealth" — "wealthy through thought"

readings.vyakhya: पावका सरस्वती वाजिनीवती धियावसुः — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; वाजेभिः — तृतीया; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; वष्टु — लोटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: The last triplet of the hymn turns to a single FEMININE deity: सरस्वती, an ई-stem noun of the same नदी class you first declined in rd010. She is the subject (nominative), wrapped in feminine epithets — पावका ("purifying," with the टाप् feminine-आ of 4.1.4), वाजिनीवती ("rich in abundance"), धियावसुः ("treasure of thought"). The verb वष्टु is a 3rd-person SINGULAR imperative — "may she desire" — a wish made ABOUT her, not a command TO her. After the dual, singular-Indra, and plural triplets, the hymn closes on one goddess, in the feminine.

readings.sentence: चो॒द॒यि॒त्री सू॒नृता॑नां॒ चेतं॑ती सुमती॒नां। य॒ज्ञं द॑धे॒ सर॑स्वती॥
readings.translation: Impeller of true sayings, awakener of right thoughts — Sarasvatī has upheld the sacrifice.
readings.teaches: two feminine agent-nouns governing the genitive — चोदयित्री … सूनृतानाम्, "impeller of true words" — and the perfect दधे "she has upheld"

notes.text: चोदयित्री = feminine agent-noun (तृच् → तृ + ई) of चुद् "impel" — "the urger"

notes.en: feminine agent-noun in apposition to सरस्वती (nominative)
genitive governed by the agent-noun — "impeller OF true words"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सूनृतानाम्

notes.text: चेतन्ती = feminine present participle (शतृ + ई) of चित् "perceive" — "awakening"

notes.en: feminine participle in apposition to सरस्वती

words.gloss: of right thoughts, of good intentions

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-मतीनाम्; सु "good" + मति "thought"

notes.en: genitive governed by the participle — "awakener OF good thoughts"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुमतीनाम्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

words.gloss: she has upheld, she has established

notes.en: "hold, establish" — the √धा of दधाते (rd025) and दधिष्व (rd031), here PERFECT
3rd person singular — perfect middle "she has held"

readings.vyakhya: चोदयित्री चेतन्ती सरस्वती — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; सूनृतानां सुमतीनाम् — षष्ठी कर्तृकर्मसम्बन्धे; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; दधे — लिटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Sarasvatī is named by two feminine agent-words: चोदयित्री ("the impeller," a तृच्-agent-noun made feminine with ई) and चेतन्ती ("awakening," a present participle, शतृ + ई). Both GOVERN a genitive — चोदयित्री सूनृतानाम् "impeller OF true words," चेतन्ती सुमतीनाम् "awakener OF good thoughts" — the षष्ठी शेषे relation (2.3.50). Her act is दधे, "she has upheld," a PERFECT of √धा, the same root you have now seen as a present dual (दधाते, rd025), a middle imperative (दधिष्व, rd031), and now a perfect. One root, four tenses-and-moods, across the Saṃhitā.
