readings.sentence: यः कंसः चिरम् कृष्णस्य वधम् इच्छति स्म, सः एव अधुना भयेन कम्पते। कृष्णः मथुराम् प्रविश्य रङ्गभूमौ मल्लान् अहन्। ततः सः उच्चासनात् कंसम् आकृष्य भूमौ अपातयत्। यम् राजानम् सर्वे जनाः अबिभयुः, सः कृष्णेन क्षणेन एव हतः। एवम् अधर्मस्य अन्तः, धर्मस्य च जयः अभवत्।
readings.translation: He who for long had wished for Kṛṣṇa's death — that very one now trembles with fear. Kṛṣṇa, having entered Mathurā, killed the wrestlers in the arena. Then he dragged Kaṃsa down from his high throne and threw him to the ground. The king whom all people had feared — he was killed by Kṛṣṇa in but a moment. Thus came the end of unrighteousness, and the victory of dharma.
readings.teaches: climax — two relative-correlatives (यः…सः on the subject, यम्…सः on the object); अपादान (भयस्य source → उच्चासनात् ablative, अबिभयुः with 5th); causative अपातयत्; षष्ठी of object with कृत् (कृष्णस्य वधम्, 2.3.65); passive close (हतः)

readings.vyakhya: कथायाः शिखरम् — द्वौ सम्बन्धौ यद्-तद्। कर्तरि यः…सः (यः इच्छति स्म सः कम्पते); कर्मणि यम्…सः (यं अबिभयुः सः हतः)। अपादानम् द्विधा — उच्चासनात् (departure), भयस्य हेतुः भी-धातुना अबिभयुः। वधम् इति कृत्, तत्र कर्म षष्ठ्याम् (कृष्णस्य वधम्)। अन्ते कर्मणि हतः — कथार्धम् सर्वम् कर्मणि समाप्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: The climax, and it gathers everything. Two relative-correlatives frame it, one on each axis: यः … सः on the **subject** ("he who long wished Kṛṣṇa's death — that one now trembles") and यम् … सः on the **object** ("the king whom all feared — he was killed"). Two ablatives of separation: उच्चासनात् "from the high throne" (2.3.28) and the fear-source folded into अबिभयुः. The action-noun वधम् "killing" takes its object in the **genitive** — कृष्णस्य वधम् "the killing OF Kṛṣṇa" (2.3.65, the कृत्-षष्ठी). The arc that began with butter and a rope ends as it must, in the passive: हतः "was killed" — and the whole Kṛṣṇa-childhood sequence closes on its grammatical signature, the कर्मणि क्त, now carrying the weight of a death rather than a game.

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् वने भासुरको नाम सिंहः वसति स्म। सः बलवान् आसीत्, किन्तु अतीव क्रूरः। प्रतिदिनम् सः बहून् पशून् अहन्। तेन सर्वे मृगाः भयेन कम्पन्ते स्म। ते मिलित्वा सिंहम् ऊचुः — "हे स्वामिन्, मा सर्वान् पशून् हन्। वयम् एव प्रतिदिनम् एकम् पशुम् तव आहाराय प्रेषयिष्यामः।"
readings.translation: In a certain forest there lived a lion named Bhāsuraka. He was strong, but exceedingly cruel. Every day he killed many animals. Because of this all the beasts trembled with fear. They, having gathered, said to the lion — "O master, do not kill all the animals. We ourselves will send one animal every day for your food."
readings.teaches: the fable opens: कस्मिंश्चित् as an indefinite locative, the prohibitive मा with लङ् in मा हन्, a first-person plural future प्रेषयिष्यामः, आहाराय as a dative of purpose, and ऊचुः in the perfect

readings.vyakhya: नूतनकथारम्भः — पञ्चतन्त्रात्। कस्मिंश्चित् वने इति लोकप्रसिद्धम् आख्यानारम्भपदम्। मा हन् इति प्रतिषेधे लुङ् अनद्यतनः अनागमकः। आहाराय इति तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी; प्रेषयिष्यामः इति लृट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने।
readings.vyakhya_en: A new story begins — from the Pañcatantra, and it opens with the formula every Sanskrit tale is built on: कस्मिंश्चित् वने "in a certain forest" (कः + चित् = the indefinite "some"). One genuinely new construction: the **prohibitive** — मा with an augmentless past (मा … हन् "do not kill"), the standard way Sanskrit says "don't." Against it stands the animals' **future promise** — प्रेषयिष्यामः "we will send" (लृट्, 1st plural). The dative आहाराय "for food" is the dative of purpose (तादर्थ्य). All the rest — past tenses, gerund मिलित्वा, instrumental of cause भयेन — is grammar you already own, now carrying a fable instead of a god.

readings.sentence: एकदा शशकस्य वारः आगच्छत्। सः बुद्धिमान् शशकः चिरम् विचिन्त्य एकम् उपायम् अकरोत्। सः मन्दम् मन्दम् सिंहस्य समीपम् अगच्छत्। क्रुद्धः सिंहः अपृच्छत् — "किमर्थम् त्वम् विलम्बेन आगतः?" शशकः अवदत् — "मार्गे अन्यः बलवान् सिंहः माम् अरुणत्। सः त्वाम् एव स्वामिनम् न मन्यते।" तत् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धः सिंहः तम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति स्म।
readings.translation: One day the rabbit's turn came. That clever rabbit, after thinking for a long time, devised a plan. He went very slowly toward the lion. The angry lion asked — "Why have you come late?" The rabbit said — "On the road another strong lion stopped me. He does not regard you alone as master." Having heard that, the angry lion wished to see him.
readings.teaches: longer dialogue — किमर्थम् (why?), past participle as predicate (आगतः "have come"), gerund विचिन्त्य + श्रुत्वा, accusative of person stopped (माम् अरुणत्), infinitive of purpose (द्रष्टुम्), मन्यते आत्मनेपद

readings.vyakhya: संवादः दीर्घतरः। किमर्थम् इति हेतुप्रश्ने; आगतः इति निष्ठा कर्तरि ("त्वम् आगतः")। माम् अरुणत् इति रुध्-धातोः सप्तमगणे लङ्। स्वामिनम् इति द्विकर्मके मन्यतेः अभिन्ननिर्देशे। द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति तुमुन् इष्-धातुना।
readings.vyakhya_en: The dialogue lengthens — the trick is told, not just narrated. New touches: किमर्थम् "why? for what purpose?" (the interrogative of cause); the past participle as a finite-like **predicate** — त्वम् … आगतः "you have come" (क्त standing in for "you came/are come"); and a double-accusative with मन्यते — त्वाम् स्वामिनम् न मन्यते "does not regard you AS master," the object and its predicate-complement both accusative. The infinitive द्रष्टुम् इच्छति "wishes to see" closes on the hook that will spring the trap. Everything else is consolidation: four लङ् pasts, two gerunds (विचिन्त्य, श्रुत्वा), locatives, the मतुप् adjectives बलवान्/बुद्धिमान्.

readings.sentence: पुरा मिथिलायाम् एका राज्ञी वसति स्म। तस्याः नगरे विद्वान् आचार्यः आसीत्। सः प्रतिदिनम् शिष्यम् वेदम् अध्यापयत्। एकदा बालः आचार्यम् द्रष्टुम् ग्रामम् अगच्छत्। तत्र आचार्यः तम् धर्मम् अबोधयत्। बोधेन सः बालः पण्डितः अभवत्। राज्ञी अपि तम् अपूजयत्।
readings.translation: Long ago in Mithilā there lived a queen. In her city there was a learned teacher. Every day he taught a student the Veda. One day a boy went to the village in order to see the teacher. There the teacher made him understand dharma. By that understanding the boy became learned. The queen too honored him.
readings.teaches:
the causative in the wild: शिष्यम् वेदम् अध्यापयत् "taught the student the
Veda" — the one made to act (शिष्यम्) turns into an object, so the causative
carries two accusatives. And the causer himself is the हेतु-agent.

भावे घञ् — the घञ् suffix in the sense of the action itself → बुध् + घञ् → बोधः "understanding"
ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् — न्-final stem → ङीप् → राज्ञी

readings.vyakhya: णिजन्तप्रधाना कथा। अध्यापयत् इति अधि-इणो णिचि लङ्; शिष्यम् वेदम् इति द्विकर्मकम् — बुद्ध्यर्थे मूलकर्ता कर्म भवति (गतिबुद्धि…)। सः इति प्रयोजकः हेतुः। ग्रामम् अगच्छत् इति गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीया। बोधेन इति बुधेः भावे घञ्। राज्ञी इति राजन्शब्दात् ङीप्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A causative-centered story. The engine is 3.1.26 हेतुमति च — when there is a
हेतु (a causing agent), the root takes णिच्: बुध् → बोधयति, अधि-इ → अध्यापयति.
Two things follow. First, the causer is the **हेतु**-agent by 1.4.55
(तत्प्रयोजको हेतुश्च) — सः, nominative. Second, and the reason this reading
exists: with verbs of **knowing, going, and eating**, the base agent (the one
made to act) does not stay instrumental — it becomes the **object**
(1.4.52). So शिष्यम् वेदम् अध्यापयत् and तम् धर्मम् अबोधयत् each carry *two*
accusatives: the one taught, and the thing taught. Around this: ग्रामम्
अगच्छत् (2.3.12, the goal of a motion verb in the accusative), बोधेन (3.3.18
भावे घञ्, an action-noun as means), and the feminine राज्ञी (4.1.5, राजन् + ङीप्).

source.ref: the father and his two sons — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: पुरा एकः पिता आसीत्। तस्य द्वौ पुत्रौ आस्ताम्। पिता पुत्रयोः समम् स्नेहम् अकरोत्। एकदा सः पुत्राभ्याम् धनम् अयच्छत्। ज्येष्ठः पुत्रः तत् धनम् द्यूतेन अनाशयत्। कनिष्ठः तु तेन धनेन क्षेत्रम् अक्रीणात्। तथैव कनिष्ठः सुखम् अलभत। तदा पिता तम् एव अपूजयत्।
readings.translation: Long ago there was a father. He had two sons. The father loved both sons equally. One day he gave wealth to the two of them. The elder son destroyed that wealth by gambling; but the younger bought a field with that wealth. Just so, the younger obtained happiness. Then the father honored him alone.
readings.teaches:
the shapes of the endings themselves: पिता (the ऋ-stem nominative), पुत्रयोः
and पुत्राभ्याम् (the dual obliques of an अ-stem), and the accusatives धनम्,
क्षेत्रम् — each a small सन्धि rule doing its quiet work.

notes.role: ऋदुशनस्पुरुदंसोऽनेहसां च — an ऋ-stem agent-noun lengthens its ऋ to the आ-shaped अनङ् in the nominative singular → पितृ → पिता
ओसि च — before the ओस् ending (gen./loc. dual), the final अ of an अ-stem becomes ए → पुत्र + ओस् → पुत्रयोः
अमि पूर्वः — before the अम् ending, अ + अम् coalesce to a single अ (पूर्वरूप) → स्नेह + अम् → स्नेहम्; every अ-stem accusative singular is this rule
सुपि च — before a सुप् ending beginning with a consonant (here भ्याम्), the final अ of an अ-stem lengthens to आ → पुत्र + भ्याम् → पुत्राभ्याम्

notes.en: causative of नश् "perish" → "cause to perish, destroy"

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — a/ā followed by ए/ओ/ऐ/औ becomes the वृद्धि vowel → तथा + एव → तथैव

readings.vyakhya: सुप्तिङन्तरूपप्रधाना कथा। पिता इति ऋदन्तस्य प्रथमैकवचनम् (७.१.९४)। पुत्रयोः इति ओसि ए-आदेशः (७.३.१०४); पुत्राभ्याम् इति भ्यामि अकारस्य दीर्घः (७.३.१०२)। स्नेहम् धनम् क्षेत्रम् इति अमि पूर्वरूपम् (६.१.१०७)। तथैव इति वृद्धिसन्धिः (६.१.८८)।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A story that shows off the **endings** rather than a new construction. The
quiet machinery of declension: पिता, the ऋ-stem nominative singular (7.1.94,
पितृ → पिता); the two dual obliques of an अ-stem — पुत्रयोः (genitive, 7.3.104
अ → ए before ओस्) and पुत्राभ्याम् (dative, 7.3.102 अ → आ before भ्याम्); and
the accusative singular धनम् / स्नेहम् / क्षेत्रम्, which is 6.1.107 अमि पूर्वः
(the stem-अ and the ending-अ of अम् fuse to one अ) on every page you will ever
read. Even तथैव hides a rule — तथा + एव → तथैव is the vṛddhi सन्धि (6.1.88).

source.ref: the beggar and the giving king — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: एकदा भिक्षुः नृपम् धनम् अयाचत। नृपः अचिन्तयत् — दीनेभ्यः सदा धनम् दद्यात् इति। ततः सः भिक्षवे बहु धनम् अददात्। भिक्षुः तुष्टः अभवत्।
readings.translation: One day a beggar asked the king for wealth. The king thought — "One should always give wealth to the needy." Then he gave much wealth to the beggar. The beggar became satisfied.
readings.teaches:
a two-object verb — नृपम् धनम् अयाचत "asked the king for wealth": the thing
asked-for is the plain object, but the person asked is a second, "residual"
object. And दद्यात् "one should give," the optative of precept.

notes.en: the "residual" second object — the person asked

notes.role: अकथितं च — with verbs like याच् (ask), दुह् (milk), प्रच्छ् (ask the way), a second participant not otherwise named takes the कर्मन् संज्ञा → नृपम् धनम् अयाचत

notes.en: the principal object — what is asked for

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — in the senses of precept, invitation, request (विधि etc.), the लिङ् (optative) is used → दा + लिङ् → दद्यात्

notes.en: quotative — marks the end of the reflected thought
dative singular (उ-stem — भिक्षु + ए → भिक्षवे, गुण)

notes.role: निष्ठा — the क्त participle → तुष्ट

readings.vyakhya: द्विकर्मकयाचिना सह कथा। नृपम् धनम् अयाचत इति अकथितं च (१.४.५१) — याचेः द्वे कर्मणी, प्रधानम् धनम्, अकथितः नृपः। दद्यात् इति विध्यर्थे लिङ् (विधिनिमन्त्रण…)। भिक्षवे इति उदन्तस्य चतुर्थ्येकवचनम् (गुणः → भिक्षवे)।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two grammar points sit at the center. First, a **two-object verb**: याच्
"ask for" governs *two* accusatives — नृपम् धनम् अयाचत, "asked the king (for)
wealth." The thing wanted (धनम्) is the plain object; the person asked
(नृपम्) is the कर्मन् only because 1.4.51 (अकथितं च) sweeps up such a
"residual," otherwise-unnamed participant into the object category. The same
rule covers दुह् "milk (a cow of milk)" and प्रच्छ् "ask (someone the way)."
Second, the **optative of precept**: दद्यात् "one should give," लिङ् in the
विधि sense (3.3.161). Around them, भिक्षवे is the उ-stem dative singular
(भिक्षु → भिक्षवे).

source.ref: how conduct is learned — our own telling, in the passive voice
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: आचार्येण कथा कथ्यते। शिष्यैः सा श्रूयते। तया कथया सदाचारः शिक्ष्यते। एवम् बालाः धर्मेण रक्ष्यन्ते।
readings.translation: By the teacher a story is told. By the students it is heard. By that story good conduct is learned. Thus the children are protected by dharma.
readings.teaches:
the passive voice, and the case that comes with it: the doer stands in the
instrumental — आचार्येण "by the teacher," शिष्यैः "by the students" — while
the thing done becomes the subject. Every verb here carries यक्.

notes.en: the agent — in the passive the doer is not the subject

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — an unexpressed agent (कर्तृ) or instrument (करण) takes the तृतीया → आचार्येण

notes.en: what is told — grammatical subject of the passive

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — passive विकरण before a सार्वधातुक ending → कथ् + यक् → कथ्यते
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — the agent takes तृतीया → शिष्यैः
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया — the instrument takes तृतीया → कथया

readings.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगाभ्यासः। कथ्यते श्रूयते शिक्ष्यते रक्ष्यन्ते इति सर्वाणि यगन्तानि (सार्वधातुके यक्)। आचार्येण शिष्यैः इति कर्तरि तृतीया, कथया धर्मेण इति करणे — उभयत्र कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया। कर्म तु प्रथमायाम् — कथा सदाचारः बालाः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A drill in the **passive**. Four verbs, all built with यक् (3.1.67):
कथ्यते, श्रूयते, शिक्ष्यते, रक्ष्यन्ते. The point to feel is the case-shift the
passive forces: the **agent leaves the nominative** and goes to the
instrumental — आचार्येण, शिष्यैः — sharing that case with the plain instrument
कथया, धर्मेण (both by 2.3.18, कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया). What is left holding the
nominative is the **object**: कथा "the story," सदाचारः "good conduct," बालाः
"the children." Read it beside an active sentence and the machinery is clear.

source.ref: the teacher's instructions — our own telling, in commands
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: गुरुः शिष्यम् अवदत् — पठ। सत्यम् वद। आलस्यम् त्यज। मातरम् पितरम् च सेवस्व। ततः त्वम् सुखी भविष्यसि।
readings.translation: The teacher said to the student — "Study. Speak the truth. Give up laziness. Serve your mother and father. Then you will become happy."
readings.teaches:
two new tenses at once — the imperative (पठ, वद, त्यज, सेवस्व, "do this!")
and the simple future भविष्यसि "you will become." Plus the two ऋ-stem
accusatives मातरम्, पितरम्.

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — an ऋ-stem takes गुण (ऋ → अर्) before a strong ending → मातृ + अम् → मातरम्
लृट् शेषे च — for the (non-immediate) future, लृट् is used → the future भविष्यति/भविष्यसि
स्यतासी लृलुटोः — before लृट्, the स्य marker attaches → भू + स्य → भविष्य…

readings.vyakhya: लोड्लृटोः प्रवेशः। पठ वद त्यज सेवस्व इति लोटि (आज्ञायाम्); सेवस्व इति आत्मनेपदे। भविष्यसि इति लृटि — स्यप्रत्ययः (स्यतासी लृलुटोः)। मातरम् पितरम् इति ऋदन्तयोः द्वितीयैकवचनम् (गुणः अर्)।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two moods/tenses enter here. The **imperative** (लोट्) is the mood of
command: पठ "study!", वद "speak!", त्यज "give up!", and the आत्मनेपद सेवस्व
"serve!". Then the **simple future** (लृट्): भविष्यसि "you will become," formed
with the स्य marker (3.1.33, 3.3.13). Set into the frame is a pair of ऋ-stem
accusatives — मातरम्, पितरम् — where the ऋ strengthens to अर् before the ending
अम्. A single sentence that quietly triples the reader's verb inventory.

source.ref: which boy was greater — our own telling, in degrees
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: द्वौ बालौ आस्ताम्। रामः श्यामात् बलवत्तरः आसीत्। श्यामः तु रामात् बुद्धिमत्तरः आसीत्। सर्वेषु बालेषु रामः बलवत्तमः। श्यामः तु सर्वेषु बुद्धिमत्तमः।
readings.translation: There were two boys. Rāma was stronger than Śyāma. But Śyāma was more intelligent than Rāma. Among all the boys Rāma was the strongest; but Śyāma was the most intelligent of all.
readings.teaches:
the two degrees of comparison: the comparative in -तर (बलवत्तरः "stronger,"
with the thing compared-against in the ablative — श्यामात् "than Śyāma"),
and the superlative in -तम (बलवत्तमः "strongest," among a locative field).

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — comparing two, the तरप् (or ईयसुन्) degree suffix → बलवत् + तरप् → बलवत्तर

notes.en: the field of the superlative — "among all"

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — for the highest degree (अतिशायन), the तमप् (or इष्ठन्) suffix → बलवत् + तमप् → बलवत्तम

readings.vyakhya: तरप्तमबोः अभ्यासः। बलवत्तरः बुद्धिमत्तरः इति द्वयोः तुलने तरप् (द्विवचनविभज्ये…); श्यामात् रामात् इति तुलनायां पञ्चमी। बलवत्तमः बुद्धिमत्तमः इति अतिशायने तमप्; सर्वेषु बालेषु इति निर्धारणे सप्तमी।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The two degrees, side by side. **Comparative** — बलवत्-तर "stronger," the
तरप् suffix used when *two* are weighed (5.3.57), and the one compared-against
stands in the **ablative**: श्यामात् "than Śyāma," रामात् "than Rāma."
**Superlative** — बलवत्-तम "strongest," तमप् for the highest degree (5.3.55),
with the field it tops named in the **locative**: सर्वेषु बालेषु "among all
the boys." The bases here are themselves मतुप्-adjectives (बलवत्, बुद्धिमत्),
so you see two suffixes stacked — possession, then degree.

source.ref: when the sun rises — our own telling, in the locative absolute
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: सूर्ये उदिते कमलानि विकसन्ति। मेघे गर्जति मयूराः नृत्यन्ति। गुरौ आगते शिष्याः उत्तिष्ठन्ति। एवम् काले गते ज्ञानम् वर्धते।
readings.translation: When the sun has risen, lotuses open. When the cloud thunders, peacocks dance. When the teacher has come, the students rise. Thus, as time passes, knowledge grows.
readings.teaches:
the locative absolute — a whole clause folded into the locative: सूर्ये उदिते
"the sun having risen," गुरौ आगते "the teacher having come." Both the noun and
its participle stand in the seventh case.

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् — the noun whose action marks the time of another action stands in the सप्तमी (the locative absolute) → सूर्ये … उदिते

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of उद्-इ "rise," agreeing in the locative
present participle (शतृ) of गर्ज् "thunder," in the locative — "the cloud thundering"
past participle (क्त) of आ-गम् "come," in the locative
past participle (क्त) of गम्, in the locative

readings.vyakhya: सतिसप्तमी (भावलक्षणसप्तमी) अभ्यासः। सूर्ये उदिते, गुरौ आगते, काले गते इति द्वयोः पदयोः सप्तमी — यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम्। मेघे गर्जति इति शत्रन्तेन। एतत् "सति सप्तमी" इति प्रसिद्धम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The **locative absolute** — a compressed "when/while" clause. Its shape is
fixed: a noun and its participle *both* in the locative, standing apart from
the main sentence. सूर्ये उदिते "the sun having risen," गुरौ आगते "the teacher
having come," काले गते "time having passed." The rule is 2.3.37 (यस्य च भावेन
भावलक्षणम्) — the circumstance whose occurrence marks the time of the main
action goes in the seventh case; grammarians nickname it **सति सप्तमी**. The
participle is usually क्त (completed), but a present शतृ works too: मेघे गर्जति
"while the cloud thunders."

source.ref: the ascetic and the boy — our own telling, in compounds
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: वने एकः तपस्वी अवसत्। एकदा ग्रामगतः बालः तत्र अगच्छत्। सः सरसि नीलोत्पलम् अपश्यत्। तपस्वी बालाय फलानि अयच्छत्। इदम् बालहितम् इति सः अवदत्।
readings.translation: In the forest lived an ascetic. One day a village-going boy came there. In the lake he saw a blue lotus. The ascetic gave the boy fruits. "This is for the boy's good," he said.
readings.teaches:
three kinds of तत्पुरुष compound in one story — ग्रामगतः "gone to the village"
(accusative-type), बालहितम् "good for the boy" (dative-type), and नीलोत्पलम्
"blue lotus" (the कर्मधारय, qualifier + qualified).

notes.en: compound — ग्रामं गतः "gone to the village"

notes.role: द्वितीया श्रितातीतपतितगतात्यस्तप्राप्तापन्नैः — an accusative combines with गत etc. into a द्वितीया-तत्पुरुष → ग्रामम् + गतः → ग्रामगतः

notes.en: compound — नीलम् उत्पलम् "blue lotus," qualifier + qualified

notes.role: विशेषणं विशेष्येण बहुलम् — a qualifier compounds with its qualified noun into a कर्मधारय → नील + उत्पल → नीलोत्पल

notes.en: compound — बालाय हितम् "good for the boy"

notes.role: चतुर्थी तदर्थार्थबलिहितसुखरक्षितैः — a dative combines with हित etc. into a चतुर्थी-तत्पुरुष → बाल + हित → बालहित

readings.vyakhya: समासप्रधाना कथा। ग्रामगतः इति द्वितीयातत्पुरुषः (द्वितीया श्रितातीत…)। बालहितम् इति चतुर्थीतत्पुरुषः (चतुर्थी तदर्थ…)। नीलोत्पलम् इति कर्मधारयः (विशेषणं विशेष्येण)। त्रयः समासभेदाः एकत्र।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Three flavors of तत्पुरुष, side by side. In each, a case-related word is
swallowed into a compound and the case-ending disappears. **ग्रामगतः** = ग्रामं
गतः "gone to the village" — an *accusative* relation (2.1.24). **बालहितम्** =
बालाय हितम् "good for the boy" — a *dative* relation (2.1.36). And
**नीलोत्पलम्** = नीलम् उत्पलम् "blue lotus," the कर्मधारय, where the two members
simply describe one thing, adjective and noun (2.1.57). Learn to unfold a
compound back into its case phrase and half of Sanskrit prose opens up.

source.ref: the thirsty crow — our own longer telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: एकदा एकः काकः तृषितः अभवत्। सः जलम् अन्वेष्टुम् इतस्ततः अभ्रमत्। ततः मार्गे एकम् घटम् अपश्यत्। तस्मिन् घटे अल्पम् जलम् आसीत्। काकः चञ्च्वा जलम् प्राप्तुम् न अशक्नोत्। तदा सः बुद्धिम् अकरोत्। सः पाषाणान् आनीय घटे अक्षिपत्। शनैः जलम् उपरि आगच्छत्। एवम् बुद्धिमान् काकः जलम् अपिबत् तृप्तः च अभवत्।
readings.translation: One day a crow grew thirsty. It wandered here and there to look for water. Then on the road it saw a pot. In that pot there was a little water. With its beak the crow could not reach the water. Then it had an idea. It brought stones and dropped them into the pot. Slowly the water rose up. Thus the clever crow drank the water and was satisfied.
readings.teaches:
a whole little story, to read at length: infinitives of purpose
(अन्वेष्टुम्, प्राप्तुम्), a prefixed gerund (आनीय, ल्यप्), a masculine
accusative plural (पाषाणान्), and eight past-tense verbs carrying the action.

notes.en: qualifying जलम् (the water in the pot)

notes.role: तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — after an अ-stem in the masculine, the accusative-plural शस् becomes आन् → पाषाण + शस् → पाषाणान्
समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् — a prefixed root takes ल्यप् (-य), not क्त्वा → आ-नी → आनीय

readings.vyakhya: दीर्घतरा कथा — पूर्वाभ्यस्तानां संग्रहः। तुमुन् (अन्वेष्टुम् प्राप्तुम्), ल्यप् (आनीय), शसि आन् (पाषाणान्), अष्ट लङन्तानि क्रियापदानि, क्तप्रत्ययाः (तृषितः तृप्तः) च एकत्र। कथाक्रमेण पठनाभ्यासाय।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A longer read — nothing new in isolation, everything together, the way real
prose comes. Watch the machinery you have met do its work across a whole
story: two infinitives of purpose (अन्वेष्टुम्, प्राप्तुम्), the prefixed
gerund आनीय (ल्यप्), the masculine accusative plural पाषाणान् (शस् → आन्,
6.1.103), क्त participles as predicate (तृषितः, तृप्तः), and eight लङ् past
verbs driving the plot. The goal here is fluency: read it straight through,
and let the grammar stay in the background where it belongs.

source.ref: the brahmin of Mathurā — our own telling, in derivatives
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: मथुरायाम् एकः माथुरः ब्राह्मणः आसीत्। सः रामायणम् अपठत्। तत्र दाशरथेः चरितम् आसीत्। तत् पठित्वा सः प्रसन्नः अभवत्।
readings.translation: In Mathurā there was a certain Māthura (Mathurā-born) brahmin. He read the Rāmāyaṇa. In it was the story of Dāśarathi (the son of Daśaratha). Having read that, he became pleased.
readings.teaches:
two तद्धित derivatives of naming — माथुरः "one born in Mathurā" (the "situated
there" sense) and दाशरथिः "descendant of Daśaratha" (the patronymic) — the
everyday machinery by which Sanskrit turns a place or a father into an adjective.

notes.en: 'situated/born in ___' derivative — मथुरा → माथुर (अण्, with आदिवृद्धि)

notes.role: तत्र भवः — "arising in / native to that place" is expressed by अण् on the place-name → मथुरा + अण् → माथुर

notes.en: the derivative suffix (with आदिवृद्धि म → मा)

notes.role: तस्यापत्यम् — the "offspring of ___" sense governs the तद्धित → दशरथ → दाशरथि (इञ्, आदिवृद्धि)
समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले — the earlier of two acts by one agent takes क्त्वा → पठित्वा

readings.vyakhya: तद्धितनामप्रधाना कथा। माथुरः इति मथुराशब्दात् तत्र भवः इत्यर्थे अण् (आदिवृद्धिः)। दाशरथेः इति दशरथस्य अपत्यम् इति इञ् (तस्यापत्यम्)। द्वौ अपि नामतद्धितौ — स्थानतः, जन्मतः च।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Two everyday **तद्धित** derivatives, both about identity. माथुरः "of Mathurā"
comes from the place-name by the "born/found there" sense — मथुरा + अण्, with
the first vowel strengthened (आदिवृद्धि: म → मा), 4.3.53 तत्र भवः. दाशरथिः "son
of Daśaratha" is the patronymic — दशरथ + इञ्, again with आदिवृद्धि, 4.1.92
तस्यापत्यम्. This is how Sanskrit makes an adjective out of a where or a whose:
a Māthura brahmin, the Dāśarathi prince. Around them, a plain gerund पठित्वा
"having read" ties the two clauses.

source.ref: the craftsmen of the village — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: ग्रामे बहवः कारवः वसन्ति स्म। कुम्भकारः घटान् अकरोत्। स्वर्णकारः अलंकारान् अरचयत्। ग्रन्थकारः शास्त्राणि अलिखत्। सर्वे स्वेन कर्मणा सुखम् अलभन्त।
readings.translation: In the village lived many craftsmen. The potter made pots. The goldsmith fashioned ornaments. The author wrote treatises. All of them found happiness by their own work.
readings.teaches:
the agent-compound — कुम्भकारः "pot-maker," स्वर्णकारः "gold-maker,"
ग्रन्थकारः "book-maker": a root of doing (कृ → कार) with its object built
right in, the everyday way Sanskrit names a trade.

notes.role: कर्मण्यण् — a root compounded with its object takes अण् as an agent-noun (उपपद-समास) → कुम्भ + कृ + अण् → कुम्भकार
तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — masc. अ-stem accusative plural शस् → आन् → घटान्
कर्मण्यण् — object + root + अण् → स्वर्णकार
कर्मण्यण् → ग्रन्थ + कृ + अण् → ग्रन्थकार

readings.vyakhya: उपपदसमासप्रधाना कथा। कुम्भकारः स्वर्णकारः ग्रन्थकारः इति कर्मण्यण् — कर्मणि उपपदे कृञः अण् (उपपदसमासः)। घटान् अलंकारान् इति पुंसि शसः आन् (तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि)। शास्त्राणि इति नपुंसके नुम्। स्वेन कर्मणा इति करणे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A page of **agent-compounds**. Sanskrit names a trade by folding the object
straight into the verb: कुम्भ-कार "pot-maker," स्वर्ण-कार "gold-worker,"
ग्रन्थ-कार "book-maker" — each is कृ "make/do" with its object as the first
member, taking अण् (3.2.1, कर्मण्यण्). Notice the accusative plurals feeding
them: घटान्, अलंकारान् — masculine शस् surfacing as -आन् (6.1.103) — beside
the neuter शास्त्राणि (with its नुम्). The tools you already own, doing new work.

source.ref: what one must do — our own telling, in gerundives
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: राज्ञा प्रजाः रक्षणीयाः। गुरवे सेवा देया। सत्यम् वक्तव्यम्। धर्मः पालनीयः। एतत् सर्वैः ज्ञेयम्।
readings.translation: The subjects must be protected by the king. Service is to be given to the teacher. The truth must be spoken. Dharma must be upheld. All this must be known by everyone.
readings.teaches:
the gerundive — the "must / to-be-done" verbal adjective: देया "to be given"
and ज्ञेयम् "to be known" (the यत् suffix on vowel-final roots), beside
रक्षणीयाः, वक्तव्यम्, पालनीयः (the अनीयर् and तव्य suffixes).

notes.en: the agent — a gerundive puts its doer in the instrumental
what is to be protected — grammatical subject

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — the "ought/to-be-done" sense is expressed by तव्यत्, तव्य, or अनीयर् → रक्ष् + अनीयर् → रक्षणीय

notes.en: what is to be given — subject

notes.role: अचो यत् — after a vowel-final root, the gerundive suffix is यत् → दा + यत् → देय (feminine देया)

notes.en: the gerundive suffix for vowel-final roots
what is to be spoken — subject

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य, another gerundive suffix → वच् + तव्य → वक्तव्य

notes.en: what is to be upheld — subject
what is to be known — subject

notes.role: अचो यत् — vowel-final ज्ञा takes यत् → ज्ञा + यत् → ज्ञेय

notes.en: the gerundive suffix for vowel-final roots

readings.vyakhya: कृत्यप्रत्ययप्रधाना कथा। रक्षणीयाः पालनीयः इति अनीयर्; वक्तव्यम् इति तव्य; देया ज्ञेयम् इति अजन्तधातुभ्यः यत् (अचो यत्)। सर्वेषु कर्तरि तृतीया (राज्ञा सर्वैः), कर्म प्रथमायाम् — कृत्यानां कर्मणि प्रयोगः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The **gerundive** (कृत्य) — the verbal adjective of obligation, "to be ___,
must be ___." Three suffixes do the job (3.1.96 तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः): अनीयर्
(रक्षणीय, पालनीय), तव्य (वक्तव्य), and — after a vowel-final root — यत्
(देय from दा, ज्ञेय from ज्ञा; 3.1.97 अचो यत्). Like the passive, a gerundive
is कर्मणि: the thing-to-be-done stands in the nominative (प्रजाः, सत्यम्,
धर्मः) and the doer in the instrumental (राज्ञा "by the king," सर्वैः "by
all"). This is the register of rule and duty — half of the dharma texts speak in it.

source.ref: the eager student — our own telling, in desideratives
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: शिष्यः विद्याम् जिज्ञासते। सः गुरोः समीपम् गन्तुम् इच्छति। गुरुः अपि तम् शिक्षितुम् चिकीर्षति। एवम् द्वौ अपि ज्ञानम् इच्छतः।
readings.translation: The student wishes to know knowledge. He wants to go to the teacher's side. The teacher too wishes to instruct him. Thus both of them desire knowledge.
readings.teaches:
the desiderative — a verb that means "wishes to ___," built by reduplicating
the root and adding सन्: जिज्ञासते "wants to know" (from ज्ञा), चिकीर्षति
"wants to do" (from कृ).

notes.role: धातोः कर्मणः समानकर्तृकादिच्छायां वा — when one wishes to do the action oneself, the root takes सन् (with reduplication) → ज्ञा → जिज्ञास "want to know"
धातोः… इच्छायां वा — कृ "do" + सन् (reduplicated) → चिकीर्ष "want to do"

readings.vyakhya: सन्नन्तप्रधाना कथा। जिज्ञासते इति ज्ञाधातोः इच्छायां सन् (धातोः कर्मणः समानकर्तृकादिच्छायां वा); चिकीर्षति इति कृञः सन् — द्वित्वेन। "स्वयम् कर्तुम् इच्छति" इत्यर्थे सन्नन्तः, "अन्यम् प्रति इच्छति" इति तु इष्धातुना (इच्छति गन्तुम्)।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The **desiderative** (सन्नन्त) — one verb for "wishes to ___," when the wisher
would do the deed himself. Reduplicate the root and add सन्: ज्ञा → जि-ज्ञास
"want to know," कृ → चि-कीर्ष "want to do" (3.1.7). Compare the two ways of
saying "want": जिज्ञासते / चिकीर्षति *build the wish into the verb*, whereas
गन्तुम् इच्छति uses a separate verb इष् "wish" + an infinitive. Sanskrit lets
you do either — the desiderative is the tighter, more idiomatic one.

source.ref: the king's five sons — our own telling, in numbers
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: राज्ञः पञ्च पुत्राः आसन्। प्रथमः शूरः आसीत्। द्वितीयः पण्डितः। तृतीयः धनी। चतुर्थः दाता। पञ्चमः तु सर्वेषु श्रेष्ठः आसीत्।
readings.translation: The king had five sons. The first was brave. The second, learned. The third, rich. The fourth, a giver. But the fifth was the best of all.

notes.en: cardinal "five" (used without a case-ending here, agreeing with पुत्राः)

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — the agent-noun suffix तृच् → दा + तृच् → दातृ
ऋदुशनस्… — the ऋ-stem nom.sg lengthens → दातृ → दाता
तस्य पूरणे डट् — "the one that completes the count of N" is formed with पूरण suffixes (here मट्) → पञ्चन् → पञ्चम

readings.vyakhya: संख्यापूरणप्रधाना कथा। पञ्च इति कर्मधारयवत् संख्या। प्रथमः … पञ्चमः इति पूरणाः (तस्य पूरणे डट् इत्यादि) — क्रमवाचिनः। दाता इति तृच्प्रत्ययान्तम् ऋदन्तम् (ऋदुशनस्… दाता)। श्रेष्ठः इति इष्ठन्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Counting, two ways. The **cardinal** पञ्च "five" simply numbers the sons. The
**ordinals** प्रथम, द्वितीय, तृतीय, चतुर्थ, पञ्चम "first … fifth" are पूरण
derivatives — literally "the one that *fills up* the count of N" (5.2.48 and
its neighbors supply the suffixes डट्/थ/म). Tucked in is दाता "a giver," the
तृच् agent-noun of दा (3.1.133), showing again the ऋ-stem nominative आ
(7.1.94), and श्रेष्ठ, the इष्ठन् superlative of प्रशस्य "good."

source.ref: a father and son speak — our own telling, with address
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

readings.sentence: पिता पुत्रम् अवदत् — हे पुत्र, शृणु। सत्यम् वद, धर्मम् चर। पुत्रः अवदत् — हे तात, तव वचनम् पालयिष्यामि।
readings.translation: The father said to the son — "O son, listen. Speak the truth, walk in dharma." The son said — "O father, I will keep your word."
readings.teaches:
direct address — the vocative: हे पुत्र "O son," हे तात "O father." When you
call to someone, the naming word stands in the सम्बोधन (the "calling" case).

notes.en: the calling particle — marks an address

notes.role: सम्बोधने च — in address (सम्बोधन), the naming word takes the first-case form used for calling → पुत्र
सम्बोधने च — address form → तात
लृट् शेषे च — the simple future लृट् → पालयिष्यामि

readings.vyakhya: सम्बोधनप्रधानः संवादः। हे पुत्र, हे तात इति सम्बोधने प्रथमारूपम् (सम्बोधने च)। शृणु वद चर इति आज्ञायां लोट्। पालयिष्यामि इति उत्तमपुरुषे लृट्। संवादे आमन्त्रणम्, आज्ञा, प्रतिज्ञा च दृश्यन्ते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A little dialogue, to hear the **vocative** — the case of calling out. हे पुत्र
"O son," हे तात "O father": when you address someone, the naming word takes the
सम्बोधन form (2.3.47, सम्बोधने च), often flagged by the particle हे. Around it,
the imperatives शृणु / वद / चर give the commands, and पालयिष्यामि "I will keep"
answers in the first-person future (लृट्) — a small, complete exchange of
address, instruction, and promise.

chapters.title: कृत् — primary affixes: agent, action, and participle suffixes

readings.translation: The brahmin gives food; he is a giver.
readings.teaches: तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता "giver" from दा.

notes.en: the root दा, as finite verb

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ → तृच् on दा → दातृ → दाता (agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: दा-धातोः तृच्प्रत्यये दातृशब्दः सिध्यति, प्रथमैकवचने दाता इति रूपम्। यो ददाति स दाता।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ) every root may take तृच् (the affix तृ) to name its agent. On दा "give" this yields the stem दातृ, whose nominative singular is दाता "giver". The agent-noun simply names the one who performs the verb's action — here, the one who gives.

readings.translation: Devadatta is a habitual doer.
readings.teaches: तृन् forms a habitual-agent noun कर्तृ → कर्ता from कृ.

notes.en: primary derivative naming the habitual agent

notes.role: तृन् on कृ → कर्तृ → कर्ता (habitual agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: तृन्प्रत्यये कृ-धातोः कर्तृशब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने कर्ता। यः शीलेन करोति स कर्ता उच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.135 (तृन्) the affix तृन् (तृ) comes after a root to name one who does the action habitually or by disposition (शील). On कृ "do" it gives the stem कर्तृ, nominative singular कर्ता. Unlike a plain agent, this names a characteristic doer — one whose nature it is to act.

readings.translation: The boy habitually goes to the village.
readings.teaches: णिनि with an उपपद forms the habit-agent गामिन् → गामी from गम्.

notes.en: the word-in-composition (द्वितीया) standing with the affix
primary derivative naming the habitual agent (ताच्छील्य)

notes.role: णिनि on गम् with उपपद ग्रामम् → गामिन् → गामी (habit agent-noun)

readings.vyakhya: ताच्छील्ये गम्यमाने उपपदे सति गम्-धातोः णिनिप्रत्यये गामिन्शब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने गामी। यः शीलेन ग्रामं गच्छति स ग्रामं गामी।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.78 (सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छील्ये) the affix णिनि (इन्) attaches to a root when habit (ताच्छील्य) is meant and an उपपद — a noun in composition — stands with it. With उपपद ग्रामम् and root गम् "go", this yields the stem गामिन्, nominative singular गामी. The whole phrase ग्रामं गामी names one who customarily goes to the village.

readings.translation: The cooking (the act of cooking) is pleasing.
readings.teaches: घञ् makes a भाव action-noun from a root; पच् → पाकः.

notes.en: the घञ् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: भावे घञ् → पच् → पाकः (action-noun in -अ)

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: धातोः भावे घञ् प्रत्ययः। पच् इत्यस्मात् पाकः इति कृदन्तं नाम जायते। तत् प्रथमायां कर्तृ।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.18 the affix घञ् is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव). From पच् "to cook" we get पाकः, "the act of cooking", a कृदन्त noun. Here it stands in the nominative as the subject of रोचते.

readings.translation: He wishes for victory.
readings.teaches: अच् makes a भाव action-noun from an इ/ई-final root; जि → जयः.

notes.en: the अच् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: एरच् → जि → जयः (action-noun in -अ)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: इवर्णान्तात् धातोः भावे अच् प्रत्ययः। जि इत्यस्मात् जयः इति कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.56 (एरच्) the affix अच् is added to a root ending in इ/ई to name the action (भाव). From जि "to conquer" we get जयः, "victory". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of इच्छति.

readings.translation: He begins the going (the departure).
readings.teaches: ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun in -अन; गम् → गमनम्.

notes.en: the ल्युट् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: ल्युट् च → गम् → गमनम् (neuter action-noun in -अन)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: धातोः भावे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः, तस्य अन इति आदेशः। गम् इत्यस्मात् गमनम् इति नपुंसकं कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
readings.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.115 the affix ल्युट् (realized as -अन) is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव), giving a neuter noun. From गम् "to go" we get गमनम्, "going". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of आरभते.

readings.translation: Wealth is to be given to the brahmin.
readings.teaches: यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on vowel-final roots (दा → देयम्).

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → ब्राह्मणाय

words.gloss: "to be given" — fit to be given

notes.role: अचो यत् → दा (vowel-final) → देयम् (gerundive)

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: अचो यत् इति वचनात् अजन्तात् धातोः दा इत्यस्मात् यत्प्रत्ययः। देयम् इति कृत्यम्। कर्म प्रथमायां, कर्ता तृतीयायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By अचो यत् (3.1.97) a root ending in a vowel takes the कृत्य affix यत्; so दा becomes देयम्, "to be given." Like every gerundive it governs case exactly as the passive does: the patient (धनम्) stands in the nominative, and an agent, if expressed, would stand in the instrumental. Here the recipient ब्राह्मणाय is in the dative (सम्प्रदान).

readings.translation: The task is to be done by me.
readings.teaches: ण्यत् forms a कृत्य gerundive on ऋ-final / consonant-final roots (कृ → कार्यम्).

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → agent in the instrumental (तृतीया)

words.gloss: "the task / to be done" — fit to be done

notes.role: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् → कृ (ऋ-final) → कार्यम् (gerundive)

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः → तव्य → कर्तव्यम्

readings.vyakhya: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् इति ऋवर्णान्तात् हलन्ताच्च धातोः ण्यत्प्रत्ययः। कृ इत्यस्मात् कार्यम्। कर्ता मया इति तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By ऋहलोर्ण्यत् (3.1.124) a root ending in ऋ (short or long) or in a consonant takes the कृत्य affix ण्यत्; so कृ becomes कार्यम्, "to be done, a task." The construction mirrors the passive: the agent मया is in the instrumental (तृतीया, by 2.3.18) and the patient stands in the nominative.

readings.translation: The lesson is to be read by the student.
readings.teaches: अनीयर् (-अनीय) forms a कृत्य gerundive (पठ् → पठनीयः).

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → agent in the instrumental (तृतीया)

words.gloss: "to be read" — fit to be read

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः → अनीयर् variant → पठ् → पठनीयः (gerundive)

notes.en: agrees with the patient in the nominative, as in the passive

readings.vyakhya: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः इति धातोः अनीयर्प्रत्ययः। पठ् इत्यस्मात् पठनीयम्। कर्ता शिष्येण तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: By तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः (3.1.96) a root may take तव्यत्, तव्य, or अनीयर्; here the अनीयर् variant gives पठ् → पठनीयः, "to be read." As with all कृत्य gerundives the syntax is passive-like: the agent शिष्येण stands in the instrumental (तृतीया, 2.3.18) and the patient पाठः in the nominative.

readings.translation: The potter makes a pot.
readings.teaches: अण् (कर्मण्यण्) forms an agent-noun whose object stands as उपपद in one compound.

notes.en: the object कुम्भ stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: कर्मण्यण् → कुम्भ + कृ + अण् → कुम्भकारः

words.gloss: "pot" — a clay pot (object of the verb)

readings.vyakhya: कुम्भं करोतीति कुम्भकारः। कर्मणि उपपदे कृधातोः अण्प्रत्ययः। उपपदं कर्म च समस्यते एकपदे।
readings.vyakhya_en: When an object (कर्मन्) stands as उपपद beside a root, the root takes अण् to form an agent-noun. Here कुम्भ "pot" joins कृ "make" and the affix अण् gives कुम्भकारः "pot-maker." The object does not stay a separate accusative word; it merges into a single तत्पुरुष compound with the agent-noun.

readings.translation: The cow-giver gives a cow to the brahmin.
readings.teaches: क (आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः) suffixes an आ-final root with an object-उपपद and no उपसर्ग.

notes.en: the object गो stands in composition with the agent-noun

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः → गो + दा + क → गोदः (आ-final दा, no उपसर्ग)

notes.en: dative — the one to whom the gift is given

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → ब्राह्मणाय

readings.vyakhya: गां ददातीति गोदः। आकारान्तात् दाधातोः अनुपसर्गात् कर्मण्युपपदे कप्रत्ययः। एवं धनदः जलदश्च।
readings.vyakhya_en: A root ending in long आ, with no उपसर्ग before it and an object standing as उपपद, takes क instead of अण्. Thus गो "cow" + दा "give" + क yields गोदः "cow-giver." The same pattern gives धनदः "wealth-giver" and जलदः "water-giver" (the cloud). The object गो merges with the agent-noun into one तत्पुरुष compound.

readings.translation: The delighting son gladdens his mother.
readings.teaches: ल्यु (→ अन) forms an agent-noun from नन्दि-group roots.

notes.role: नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः → नन्द् + ल्यु (अन) → नन्दनः

notes.en: agent-noun in अन from the नन्दि-group

readings.vyakhya: नन्दतीति नन्दनः। नन्दिग्रहिपचादिगणे नन्दिधातोः ल्युप्रत्ययः, यस्य अनादेशः।
readings.vyakhya_en: Roots of the नन्दि-group take ल्यु, and ल्यु is replaced by अन, giving agent-nouns like नन्दनः "the delighting one, the son." Unlike अण् and क above, this ल्यु-formation needs no उपपद object to attach; the affix alone names the doer. The same rule routes ग्रहि-roots to णिनि and पच्-group roots to अच्.

chapters.title: संज्ञा व परिभाषा — the grammar's own technical terms & meta-rules

readings.translation: ā, ai, au — these bear the name "vṛddhi."
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा वृद्धि — Pāṇini's name for the strongest vowel grade (आ ऐ औ); the term every "vṛddhi" rule invokes

notes.en: a technical term DEFINED here, used everywhere after

notes.role: वृद्धिरादैच् — आत् (आ) and ऐच् (ऐ, औ) are named वृद्धि

words.gloss: ā and the ऐच् pair (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: आत् = आ; ऐच् = the प्रत्याहार for ऐ, औ — together the वृद्धि vowels

readings.vyakhya: आ ऐ औ इति वृद्धिसंज्ञकाः। एषा संज्ञा "आदिवृद्धिः" "वृद्धिरेचि" इत्यादिषु प्रयुज्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en: Before any rule can SAY "take vṛddhi," the term must be DEFINED — and 1.1.1, the very first sūtra of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, does it: वृद्धिः = आ, ऐ, औ, the strongest vowel grade. You have already SEEN वृद्धि act — दशरथ → दाशरथिः (आदिवृद्धि, ex080), तव + एव → तवैव (ex with वृद्धि-sandhi). Now you know its name. This is metalanguage: a संज्ञा is a label the grammar pins on a set of sounds so later rules can refer to them in one word.

readings.translation: a, e, o — these bear the name "guṇa."
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा गुण — the middle vowel grade (अ ए ओ); the term behind every गुण operation (अग्नये, नयति)

notes.role: अदेङ् गुणः — अत् (अ) and एङ् (ए, ओ) are named गुण

words.gloss: the इक् vowels (इ उ ऋ ऌ) — what guṇa/vṛddhi apply TO

notes.text: इको गुणवृद्धी (1.1.3): गुण/वृद्धि, when ordered without specifics, fall on the इक् vowels

notes.role: इको गुणवृद्धी — गुण and वृद्धि operate on इक् (इ उ ऋ ऌ)

readings.vyakhya: अ ए ओ इति गुणसंज्ञकाः; इको गुणवृद्धी इति इकां गुणवृद्धी भवतः। नी → ने (नयति), अग्नि → अग्नये।
readings.vyakhya_en: गुण, the MIDDLE grade, is named in 1.1.2: अ, ए, ओ. And 1.1.3 (इको गुणवृद्धी) says where it lands — on the इक् vowels (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ): इ→ए, उ→ओ, ऋ→अर्. You have watched this everywhere — अग्नि → अग्नये (इ→ए, ex029), गुरु → गुरवे (उ→ओ, ex048), पितृ → पितरम् (ऋ→अर्, ex044). गुण and वृद्धि are the two strengthenings; इक् is what they strengthen. Three sūtras (1.1.1–3) underwrite half the sandhi and declension you have done.

readings.translation: Sounds made at the same place with the same effort are "savarṇa" (homorganic).
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा सवर्ण — same-place-and-effort sounds; the term behind सवर्णदीर्घ (अ+अ→आ)

notes.role: तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम् — same आस्य (place) + प्रयत्न (effort) → सवर्ण

notes.text: आस्य = the mouth-position (कण्ठ, तालु…); प्रयत्न = the manner/effort

readings.vyakhya: समानस्थानप्रयत्नौ वर्णौ सवर्णौ। अ इ-वर्गादीनां स्वस्ववर्गे सावर्ण्यम्। अतः अ + अ → आ (सवर्णदीर्घः)।
readings.vyakhya_en: Why does अ + अ fuse to आ but अ + इ to ए? Because the first pair is सवर्ण — "homorganic," made at the same place with the same effort (1.1.9) — and the second is not. This संज्ञा is the hinge of सवर्णदीर्घ (दधि + इन्द्रः → दधीन्द्रः, ex with 6.1.101): two सवर्ण vowels lengthen into one. The term sorts every sound into क-class, च-class, and so on — the grid behind both sandhi and the सवर्ण-exclusions in declension.

readings.sentence: उपदेशे हल् अन्त्यम् इत्, तस्य लोपः।
readings.translation: A consonant at the end of an affix-citation is an "it"-marker — and it drops.
readings.teaches: the इत् mechanism — affixes carry silent marker-letters that trigger rules, then vanish (क्विप्, तृच्, ण्वुल् are all named by their इत्s)

notes.role: हलन्त्यम् — a final consonant in an उपदेश (citation form) is इत्
उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् — a nasalised vowel in citation is also इत्
तस्य लोपः — that इत् is then dropped, leaving only its effect

readings.vyakhya: उपदेशे अन्त्यो हल् इत्संज्ञकः, स च लुप्यते; कार्यं तु करोति। यथा तृच् → तृ (च् इत्); क्विप् → शून्यम् (सर्वे इतः)।
readings.vyakhya_en: Affixes are cited with extra letters that never appear in the final word — they are इत्, silent markers (1.3.3 for a final consonant, 1.3.2 for a nasal vowel) that DROP by तस्य लोपः (1.3.9), having done their job of triggering rules. तृच् is really just तृ — the च् is an इत् (it conditions accent/operations). क्विप् is ALL इत् — every letter vanishes, which is why it leaves the bare root (ex161, भूः). Decoding इत्-markers is how you read Pāṇini's affix-names: शतृ = अत्, ल्युट् = अन, घञ् = अ.

readings.translation: A genitive (in a rule) means "in the place of"; and the substitute is the one nearest (to the original).
readings.teaches: the two परिभाषाs that drive every substitution (आदेश) — what the षष्ठी means in a rule, and how to pick the replacement

words.gloss: "in-the-place-of" — how a rule's genitive is read

notes.role: षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा — a षष्ठी in a sūtra means "in the place of X" (X is replaced)
स्थानेऽन्तरतमः — among possible substitutes, the one closest to the original is chosen

readings.vyakhya: सूत्रस्थषष्ठी स्थानिनं सूचयति (तस्य स्थाने आदेशः); बहुषु आदेशेषु अन्तरतमः ग्राह्यः। एताभ्यां सर्वः आदेशविधिः प्रवर्तते।
readings.vyakhya_en: These two are not about Sanskrit words — they are about reading the GRAMMAR. 1.1.49: when a rule puts a word in the genitive (इकः, अचः…), it means "IN THE PLACE OF that" — a substitution. 1.1.50: when several substitutes are possible, take the अन्तरतम, the one nearest in place/effort to the original. Together they govern every आदेश you have met — why ऋ becomes अर् (the nearest गुण) and not something else, why इ + vowel goes to य् (the nearest semivowel, यण्). The परिभाषाs are the operating system under the rules.

readings.translation: A form ending in a सुप् (noun-ending) or तिङ् (verb-ending) is a "pada" (word).
readings.teaches: the संज्ञा पद — what counts as a finished word, which decides where पद-level sandhi and the final-consonant rules apply

notes.role: सुप्तिङन्तं पदम् — what ends in सुप् or तिङ् is a पद

words.gloss: ending in a सुप् or a तिङ्

notes.text: सुप् = the 21 noun-endings (4.1.2); तिङ् = the 18 verb-endings (3.4.78)

notes.en: "that which has सुप्/तिङ् at its end"

readings.vyakhya: यत् सुबन्तं तिङन्तं वा तत् पदम्। पदान्ते एव जश्त्वादीनि, पदयोः सन्धिः च प्रवर्तते। नरः, गच्छति — पदे।
readings.vyakhya_en: Many rules say "at the end of a पद" or "between पदs" — so the term must be fixed: a पद is anything ending in a noun-ending (सुप्) or a verb-ending (तिङ्), by 1.4.14. नरः (सुबन्त) and गच्छति (तिङन्त) are both पदs; a bare stem नर or root गम् is not. This संज्ञा gates the whole final-tail of the grammar — जश्त्व (वाक्→वाग्), न-lopa (राजन्→राजा), म्→anusvāra all fire at पद-end, and external sandhi happens between पदs. The word-boundary is itself a defined object.

chapters.title: सङ्ग्रह — consolidation passages: everything met, nothing new

readings.sentence: महाबलः नृपः सभाम् आगच्छत्। तस्य पार्श्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ आस्ताम्। नीलाम्बरः दूतः प्रविश्य उपसभम् अतिष्ठत्। सः महाबलम् अवदत् — शत्रुसेना पराजिता, राष्ट्रम् च रक्षितम्।
readings.translation: The mighty king came to the assembly. At his side were the minister-and-priest. A blue-clad messenger, having entered, stood near the assembly. He said to the mighty one — "The enemy-army is defeated, and the kingdom protected."
readings.teaches:
the four compound types again, none of them new: महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि),
मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ (द्वन्द्व), उपसभम् (अव्ययीभाव), शत्रुसेना (तत्पुरुष).

words.gloss: the mighty one (whose strength is great)

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; it names the one who HAS great strength

readings.vyakhya: चत्वारः समासाः एकस्मिन् दृश्ये — महाबलः, मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ, उपसभम्, शत्रुसेना।
readings.vyakhya_en:
All four kinds in one scene, and each doing ordinary work. महाबलः is a
बहुव्रीहि — not "great" and not "strength" but the one who HAS great strength,
the king. मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ is a द्वन्द्व, minister and priest taken as a pair.
उपसभम् is an अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying it and the whole going indeclinable. And
शत्रुसेना is a तत्पुरुष — शत्रोः सेना, the enemy's army — whose defeat the
passive participle पराजिता reports without a finite verb.

readings.sentence: पीताम्बरः गुरुः शिष्यैः सह उपवनम् अगच्छत्। ते सर्वे धर्मशास्त्राणि अपठन्। तेषु रामकृष्णौ पटुतमौ आस्ताम्। ज्येष्ठः बालः गुरुम् अपृच्छत् — कः धर्मः इति।
readings.translation: The yellow-robed teacher went with his pupils to the forest's edge. They all read the treatises on dharma. Among them Rāma and Kṛṣṇa were the cleverest. The eldest boy asked the teacher — "What is dharma?"
readings.teaches:
the compounds again, and the superlative beside them: पीताम्बरः (बहुव्रीहि),
उपवनम् (अव्ययीभाव), धर्मशास्त्राणि (तत्पुरुष), रामकृष्णौ (द्वन्द्व), and the
तमप्/इष्ठन् pair पटुतमौ, ज्येष्ठः.

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the one whose garment is yellow

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the wearer) form a बहुव्रीहि

notes.en: adverbial — उप heads it, and the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: determinative — शास्त्राणि, the second member, is the head; धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि

notes.text: विग्रह: धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि — "the treatises of dharma"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (धर्मस्य) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: secondary derivative — पटु + the superlative तमप्
the तमप् superlative suffix — "most" of the whole set

notes.en: secondary derivative — the इष्ठन् superlative on the root-grade
the इष्ठन् superlative suffix — "most" (irregular base, वृद्ध → ज्येष्ठ)
degree of comparison — the superlative sense

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — तमप्/इष्ठन् in the sense of the highest degree

readings.vyakhya: पञ्च समासा-अतिशायनानि एकस्मिन् दृश्ये — पीताम्बरः, उपवनम्, धर्मशास्त्राणि, रामकृष्णौ, पटुतमौ, ज्येष्ठः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The compound types recur here in a quieter scene, and the superlative sits
among them. पीताम्बरः is a बहुव्रीहि, the one whose robe is yellow — the
teacher, not the colour. उपवनम् is an अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying वन and the whole
going indeclinable. धर्मशास्त्राणि is a तत्पुरुष — धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि, the
treatises of dharma. रामकृष्णौ pairs two names as a द्वन्द्व. And of the pupils
पटुतमौ (पटु + तमप्) and ज्येष्ठः (the इष्ठन् base) name the highest degree —
the same superlative sense in its two suffixes.

readings.sentence: अद्य राजा सभाम् अगमत्। तत्र दूतः अवादीत् — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः च रक्षिताः। राजा तत् अश्रौषीत्, मन्त्रिणः च अपृच्छत् — केन एतत् कृतम्। मन्त्रिणः अवादिषुः — यः स्वयम् न भाषते सः एव अकार्षीत्। ततः राजा तम् वीरम् आह्वयत्, वरम् च अददात्। सः वीरः तूष्णीम् आसीत्, न च किञ्चित् अयाचत।
readings.translation: Today the king went to the assembly. There a messenger spoke — "The enemies are defeated, and the villages protected." The king heard that, and asked the ministers — "By whom was this done?" The ministers spoke — "He who does not speak of himself is the very one who did it." Then the king summoned that hero, and gave a boon. That hero was silent, and asked for nothing.
readings.teaches:
अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अवादिषुः, अकार्षीत् — five aorists in one
scene. पराजिताः and रक्षिताः stand as predicates without a verb.

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अगमत्
खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — final स् → visarga → शत्रवः

notes.en: past passive participle (क्त) with परा — predicate, no verb

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the plural स् → visarga → ग्रामाः
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the सिच् स् goes ष् after the ओ

notes.en: nominative plural — the same form as the accusative above

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अवादिषुः
लुङ् — past action → अकार्षीत्
खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of ततस् → visarga

notes.en: neuter accusative with the indefinite particle

readings.vyakhya: पञ्च लुङः एकस्मिन् प्रसङ्गे — अगमत् अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् अवादिषुः अकार्षीत्। पराजिताः रक्षिताः कृतम् इति कर्मणि क्तानि, तिङन्तम् अन्तरेण। मन्त्रिणः इति द्वितीयाबहुवचने प्रथमाबहुवचने च समानम्।
readings.vyakhya_en: Five aorists carry the scene, and three of the sentences have no finite verb at all — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः रक्षिताः, केन एतत् कृतम् all rest on a participle. मन्त्रिणः appears twice, first as the accusative of the persons asked and then as the nominative of the persons answering; nothing in the form distinguishes them, only the verb each one stands beside. The hero's silence is the point of the last sentence and also its grammar — तूष्णीम् आसीत् and न किञ्चित् अयाचत say it twice, once with an indeclinable and once with a verb.

readings.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् ग्रामे मुनिः वसति स्म। जनाः तम् अपृच्छन् — किम् कुर्याम। मुनिः अवदत् — दानम् कुरुत, सत्यम् वदत। दानेन सुखम् भवति, असत्येन च दुःखम्। यः सत्यम् वदेत् सः श्रेष्ठः। रामेण एतत् वचनम् स्मृतम्।
readings.translation: In a certain village there lived a sage. The people asked him — "What should we do?" The sage said — "Practise giving, speak the truth. From giving comes happiness, and from untruth, sorrow. He who speaks truth is the best." These words were remembered by Rāma.
readings.teaches:
दानम् and असत्येन name acts as things; कुर्याम and वदेत् ask what ought to be
done. कस्मिंश्चित् opens with a श्चुत्व join and रामेण closes with णत्व.

notes.en: कस्मिन् + चित् — the न् goes श् before च्

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व at the join → कस्मिंश्चित्

notes.en: the optative, first person plural — asking for an obligation

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → कुर्याम

notes.en: the act named as a thing — giving, not a giver

notes.role: ल्युट् च — the neuter भाव action-noun → दानम्

notes.en: imperative plural — an instruction, against the optative above
cause — the same action-noun, now in the instrumental
negation compounded in front — न + सत्य
the optative in a general statement — whoever may speak

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → वदेत्

notes.en: the agent of a passive participle

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व reaches across the ए → रामेण

notes.en: what was remembered — nominative under the participle
past participle — no finite verb needed

readings.vyakhya: दानम् दानेन — एकम् नाम, द्वे विभक्ती। कुरुत आज्ञा, कुर्याम प्रश्नः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
दानम् and दानेन are one word twice: the act as the thing given, then the act
as the reason something follows. And कुरुत orders where कुर्याम asks — the
people want to know what they ought to do, the sage tells them.

readings.sentence: गुरुः अवदत् — शिष्यः पठेत्, न तु शयीत। तस्य पठनम् एव धर्मः। एकदा सः शिष्यः न अपठत्, वनम् अगच्छत् च। तत् श्रुत्वा गुरुः अक्रुध्यत्। रामेण तत् वचनम् श्रुतम्। सः चिन्तयत् — अहम् सदा पठेयम् इति।
readings.translation: The teacher said — "A student should study, and not sleep. His studying alone is his dharma." One day that student did not study, and went to the forest. Hearing that, the teacher grew angry. Rāma heard those words. He thought — "I will always study."
readings.teaches:
पठेत् and पठेयम् in one exchange, against अपठत् and अगच्छत्. पठनम् names
the act rather than the actor; श्रुत्वा and श्रुतम् are built from one root.

notes.en: the optative — what ought to be done, not what is

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative for an obligation → पठेत्

notes.en: a second optative, आत्मनेपद — शी takes the middle

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → शयीत

notes.en: the action-noun — the studying, not the one who studies

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun → पठनम्

notes.en: the past — the same root as पठेत्, and only the ending differs
gerund — the hearing precedes the anger
past — क्रुध् is दिवादि, so श्यन् and no गुण
the agent of a passive participle — instrumental

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व reaches across the ए → रामेण

notes.en: what was heard — nominative under the participle
past participle from the same root as श्रुत्वा above
the optative in the first person — a resolve rather than an obligation

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → पठेयम्

readings.vyakhya: पठेत् पठेयम् अपठत् — एकः धातुः, त्रीणि रूपाणि।
readings.vyakhya_en:
पठ् appears three times and means three different things by its ending
alone: पठेत् is what a student ought to do, पठेयम् is what this one resolves
to do, अपठत् is what he did not do. The root never changes.

readings.sentence: नद्याः तीरे तिष्ठन् राजा दूरात् आगच्छन्तम् भ्रातरम् अपश्यत्। भ्राता श्रान्तः आसीत्। राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् इति मन्त्री अवदत्। राजा स्वयम् जलम् अददात्। पिता तत् पश्यन् अवदत् — एतत् एव राज्ञः कर्म, न अन्यत्। स्मरणीयम् एतत् सर्वैः।
readings.translation: Standing on the bank of a river, the king saw his brother coming from afar. The brother was tired. The minister said that water was to be given by the king. The king himself gave water. The father, seeing that, said — "This alone is a king's work, not anything else. This is to be remembered by all."
readings.teaches:
three participles set against three finite verbs, with two gerundives in
between: दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम्, both stating obligation with no verb.

notes.en: genitive — the ई of नदी becomes य् before the ending
present participle — where he was while he saw

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → तिष्ठन्

notes.en: nominative — the न् of राजन् drops

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् drops → राजा

notes.en: the same participle in the accusative, qualifying भ्रातरम्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → आगच्छन्तम्
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — lengthening in the strong cases → भ्रातर्

notes.en: strong nom.sg — the ऋ lengthens to आ

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण of the ऋ-stem in the strong cases → भ्राता

notes.en: past participle used as a predicate
the agent of a gerundive — instrumental
what is to be given — nominative under the gerundive
gerundive — obligation, with no finite verb

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → दातव्यम्

notes.en: nominative — an इन्-stem, the न् dropping and the इ lengthening
strong nom.sg of an ऋ-stem, like भ्राता above

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण in the strong cases → पिता

notes.en: the weak stem — the अ drops before a vowel ending

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् is gone in राज्ञ् too

notes.en: neuter nominative — an अन्-stem, the न् dropping
the अनीयर् gerundive beside दातव्यम् above

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — अनीयर् forms the gerundive → स्मरणीयम्

notes.en: the agent of the gerundive, again instrumental

readings.vyakhya: तिष्ठन् आगच्छन्तम् पश्यन् — शतृ। दातव्यम् स्मरणीयम् — कृत्य। क्रिया अन्यथा अपि उच्यते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Six of the words here would be verbs in English and are not. तिष्ठन्,
आगच्छन्तम् and पश्यन् are participles; दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम् are
gerundives. Only अपश्यत्, आसीत्, अवदत् and अददात् are finite.

राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् has no verb at all — an instrumental agent, a
nominative object, and a word meaning "to-be-given". Sanskrit says a great
deal this way, and it reads as ordinary statement once it stops being
turned into an English passive.

readings.sentence: राजा सभायाम् आसीत्। तत्र भगवान् मुनिः आगच्छत्। राज्ञः पिता अपि तत्र। मुनिः राजानम् अवदत् — पितरम् पश्य, धनवान् सः न, तथापि श्रेष्ठः। राज्ञा तत् श्रुतम्। ततः सः पितरि भक्तिम् अकरोत्। भगवतः वचनेन राजा शान्तः अभवत्।
readings.translation: The king was in the assembly. There the Blessed One, a sage, came. The king's father was there too. The sage said to the king — "Look at your father; he is not wealthy, yet he is the better man." That was heard by the king. Then he showed devotion to his father. By the Blessed One's words the king became calm.
readings.teaches:
consonant stems in one scene, each in both grades: राजा / राज्ञः / राजानम्,
भगवान् / भगवतः, पिता / पितरम्.

notes.en: nominative — the bare form loses the final न् of राजन्

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् drops → राजा

notes.en: the strong form — नुम् inserted, then the vowel lengthens

notes.role: उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः — a उगित् stem takes नुम् in the strong cases → भगवान्

notes.en: the WEAK stem — the अ of राजन् drops before a vowel ending, giving राज्ञ्
strong nom.sg — the ऋ of पितृ lengthens to आ

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण of an ऋ-stem in the strong cases → पिता

notes.en: strong again — the न् returns and the अ lengthens

notes.role: सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — lengthening in the strong cases → राजान्

notes.en: strong stem पितर् — the same word as पिता, one clause later
a second उगित् stem taking नुम् — भगवान् and धनवान् are built alike

notes.role: उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः — नुम् in the strong cases → धनवान्

notes.en: nominative — a superlative used as a predicate
the agent of a passive participle — instrumental
instrumental — the weak stem राज्ञ् again
what was heard — nominative under the participle
past passive participle — no finite verb needed
the locative of the person shown devotion
locative — a third grade of पितृ, beside पिता and पितरम्
past — कृ is तनादि, taking उ rather than शप्
the WEAK stem — plain भगवत् with no नुम्, against भगवान् above
past participle used as a predicate adjective

readings.vyakhya: राजा राज्ञः राज्ञा राजानम् — एकं नाम, चत्वारः आदेशाः। भगवान् भगवतः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
राजन् appears four times and looks different every time: राजा with the न्
gone, राज्ञः and राज्ञा with the अ squeezed out, राजानम् with the न् back
and the vowel long. भगवत् does the same in two: भगवान् with नुम् inserted,
भगवतः plain.

Nothing about the king or the sage changes between those forms. What
changes is whether the ending that follows belongs to the strong set, and
the stem answers accordingly. Learning consonant declension is learning to
read four shapes as one word.

readings.sentence: गुरुणा शिष्याः पाठ्यन्ते। तैः शास्त्राणि पठ्यन्ते, वचनानि च श्रूयन्ते। गुरुः तान् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति। श्वः ते ग्रामम् गमिष्यन्ति। तत्र धनम् धान्यम् च लप्स्यन्ते। नद्याः तीरे तिष्ठन्ति, जलम् पिबन्ति च।
readings.translation: The students are taught by the teacher. By them the treatises are read, and the sayings are heard. The teacher wishes to see them. Tomorrow they will go to the village. There they will obtain wealth and grain. They stand on the river's bank, and drink water.
readings.teaches:
four passives against two actives. The same students appear as शिष्याः,
तैः, ते and तान् — the case follows what the verb's ending points at.

notes.en: the agent of a passive — unexpressed by the ending, so it takes a case
what is taught — expressed by the ending, so it stands nominative

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म — what the agent most aims at is the कर्मन् → शिष्याः

notes.en: the passive विकरण on a causative stem — पाठि + य + अन्ते

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — आत्मनेपद endings in the passive → पाठ्यन्ते
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → शास्त्राणि

notes.en: the plain passive beside the causative passive above — पठ् + य + अन्ते
neuter nominative plural — the same नुम् as शास्त्राणि

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before शि → वचनानि

notes.en: a third passive — श्रु + य + अन्ते

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — the passive takes आत्मनेपद → श्रूयन्ते

notes.en: now an ACTIVE agent — nominative, because the ending expresses it

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → गुरुः

notes.en: the object of an ACTIVE verb — accusative, not nominative
infinitive — what the wishing is directed at

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् — the infinitive → द्रष्टुम्

notes.en: इष् appears as इच्छ् + अ + ति
the ending expresses the agent — contrast the four passives above

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — final स् → रु → visarga → श्वः
लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → गमिष्यन्ति

notes.en: joined with धान्यम् by च — two things counted together

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate pair धनम् धान्यम् च

notes.en: a second future, this one आत्मनेपद — लभ् is middle

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — the future → लप्स्यन्ते

notes.en: genitive — ī-stem, the ई becoming य् before the ending

notes.role: इको यणचि — इ/ई before a vowel becomes य् → नद्याः

notes.en: स्था appears as तिष्ठ् + अ + न्ति
object of an active verb — accusative again
पा appears as पिब् + अ + न्ति

readings.vyakhya: तैः पठ्यन्ते, ते गच्छन्ति। एकः कर्ता, द्वे विभक्ती।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The same students appear four times and are named three different ways.
शिष्याः when the passive points at them, तैः when the passive points past
them at what they read, ते when the verb is active and points at them
again, तान् when someone else's verb points at them.

Nothing about the students changed. Each time, the case answers one
question: has the verb's ending already said this? If yes, प्रथमा. If no,
whatever case the role calls for.

readings.sentence: दाशरथिः माथुरम् नगरम् गच्छति। सः धनवान् बलवान् च। तस्य गुरुत्वम् सर्वे जनाः जानन्ति। काषायम् वस्त्रम् धारयति सः, ब्राह्मणवत् च अधीते। ग्रामतः आगताः जनाः तम् पश्यन्ति। अयम् पटुतरः, सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः इति ते वदन्ति।
readings.translation: The son of Daśaratha goes to the city of Mathurā. He is wealthy and strong. All people know his weightiness. He wears an ochre robe, and studies like a brahmin. People come from the village and see him. "This one is cleverer; among all the clever ones, the cleverest," they say.
readings.teaches:
तद्धित words in use rather than in their विग्रह — दाशरथिः as a name,
माथुरम् qualifying a city. धनवान् declines; ब्राह्मणवत् does not.

notes.en: the इञ् patronymic suffix, अर्थ = अपत्य; इञ् with vṛddhi, दशरथ → दाशरथि

notes.role: अत इञ् — इञ् forms the patronymic from an अ-stem → दाशरथिः

notes.en: nominative — used here as a name, not as a derivation
the sense 'belonging to a place' — अण् with vṛddhi, मथुरा → माथुर

notes.role: तत्र भवः — the place-relational affix → माथुरम्

notes.en: गम् appears as गच्छ् + अ + ति

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — the possessive → धनवान्

notes.en: nominative — a वत्-stem in its strong form
the same affix on a second stem, बल + मतुप्
the abstract — "the state of being गुरु"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व makes the abstract noun → गुरुत्वम्

notes.en: present plural — ज्ञा takes श्ना, not शप्
the sense 'dyed with X' — अण् with vṛddhi, कषाय → काषाय

notes.role: तेन रक्तं रागात् — the dye-affix → काषायम्

notes.en: the sense 'in the manner of X' — the affix makes an indeclinable, not a noun

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः — the comparison-affix → ब्राह्मणवत्

notes.en: indeclinable — it takes no ending, unlike धनवान् above
the affix -तस् in the ablative sense — an adverb, not a case-form

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the sense of the पञ्चमी → ग्रामतः

notes.en: past participle, nominative plural agreeing with जनाः
दृश् appears as पश्य् + अ + न्ति

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — the comparative → पटुतरः

notes.en: the सप्तमी of selection — "of all, the most"
the superlative — the same stem पटु, one affix further

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — the superlative → पटुतमः

readings.vyakhya: तद्धितान्तं पदम् — न विग्रहः। दाशरथिः नाम, न तु दशरथस्य अपत्यम् इति वाक्यम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Every तद्धित reading before this one is a विग्रह — दशरथस्य अपत्यं दाशरथिः,
the analysis and the word side by side. That shows how the word is made and
never shows it working. Here दाशरथिः is simply his name.

Watch धनवान् against ब्राह्मणवत्. Both are built with a वत्-shaped affix,
and they behave completely differently: धनवान् is a noun and declines,
ब्राह्मणवत् is an indeclinable and does not. The affix decides what kind of
word comes out, not just what it means.

readings.sentence: वाग् अत्र शुभा। तच्च सत्यं वदति। वनं हसति, नदी च शोभते। रामेण सह मुनिर्गच्छति। संस्कृतं वचनं तेषां प्रियम्। नमस्ते गुरो, इति ते वदन्ति।
readings.translation: Speech here is auspicious. And it speaks the truth. The forest laughs, and the river shines. The sage goes with Rāma. Refined speech is dear to them. "Homage to you, teacher," they say.
readings.teaches:
consonant joins inside sentences rather than shown as transformations:
वाग्, तच्च, वनं, संस्कृतं, रामेण, नमस्ते.

notes.en: वाक् + अत्र — the final क् voices to ग् before a vowel

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — a final stop takes its voiced counterpart → वाग्

notes.en: तत् + च — त् becomes च् before a च्-class stop

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व assimilates the dental to the palatal → तच्च
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → सत्यं

notes.en: वनम् + हसति — final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — म् → anusvāra at a word join → वनं

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — शुभ् → शोभ्
राम + इन → रामेन, then न् becomes ण् because र् precedes

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व applies across the intervening vowel → ण्

notes.en: मुनिः + गच्छति — the visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the रु/visarga alternation → मुनिर्

notes.en: सम् + कृत — the nasal takes the point of the following स्क्

notes.role: अनुस्वारस्य ययि परसवर्णः — the nasal goes homorganic → संस्कृतम्
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → वचनं

notes.en: वचनम् + तेषाम् — म् → anusvāra again, a second instance

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → तेषां
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → प्रियम्

notes.en: नमः + ते — the visarga becomes स् before त्
ते is dative — नमस् governs the चतुर्थी

readings.vyakhya: यत्र पदं पदेन मिलति तत्र सन्धिः। वाग्, तच्च, वनं, रामेण — सर्वत्र।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Six joins here and none of them announced. वाक् voices to वाग् because a
vowel follows; त् becomes च् because च follows; म् goes to anusvāra twice;
न् turns ण् in रामेण because an र् sits two syllables back.

That last one is worth noticing — the trigger is not adjacent. र् and न्
are separated by ए, and the rule still reaches across. Sandhi is not only
about what touches what.

readings.sentence: राजपुरुषः उपकृष्णम् आसीत्। तत्र रामकृष्णौ अपि आगच्छताम्। राजपुरुषः तौ अपश्यत् — रामः श्यामः, कृष्णः पीताम्बरः। सः पीताम्बरं ननाम, यतः पीताम्बरः एव विष्णुः।
readings.translation: The king's man was near Kṛṣṇa. There Rāma-and-Kṛṣṇa also arrived. The king's man saw the two of them — Rāma dark, Kṛṣṇa yellow-clad. He bowed to the yellow-clad one, because the yellow-clad one is Viṣṇu himself.
readings.teaches:
all four compound types back to back, doing no new work: राजपुरुषः
(तत्पुरुष), उपकृष्णम् (अव्ययीभाव), रामकृष्णौ (द्वन्द्व), पीताम्बरः
(बहुव्रीहि).

notes.en: determinative — the second member, पुरुष, is the head

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

notes.en: adverbial — headed by the indeclinable उप, the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

words.gloss: the one whose garment is yellow

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the compound points at Kṛṣṇa

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

readings.vyakhya: चत्वारः समासाः एकत्र। राजपुरुषः, उपकृष्णम्, रामकृष्णौ, पीताम्बरः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
All four kinds side by side, none announced: राजपुरुषः is a तत्पुरुष (पुरुष
is the head), उपकृष्णम् an अव्ययीभाव (उप carries it, and the whole goes
indeclinable), रामकृष्णौ a द्वन्द्व (Rāma and Kṛṣṇa, equally heads), and
पीताम्बरः a बहुव्रीहि — it names neither "yellow" nor "garment" but the one
who wears them, and that one turns out to be Viṣṇu.

readings.sentence: अग्निः ज्वलति। नरः जलम् नयति। बालः वनम् गच्छति। गुरुः शिष्यम् बोधति। सः धर्मम् वदति। जनाः शृण्वन्ति। अग्नयः ज्वलन्ति, नराः च पश्यन्ति।
readings.translation: The fire blazes. The man leads the water. The boy goes to the forest. The teacher instructs the student. He speaks dharma. The people listen. The fires blaze, and the men watch.
readings.teaches:
seven present verbs built the same way: an अ between root and ending, and
the root vowel strengthened before it. नी → नयति, बुध् → बोधति.

notes.en: ज्वल् + अ + ति — the अ between root and ending

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — the शप् विकरण inserted after the root → ज्वल् + अ

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — नी → ने → नय्
नी + अ + ति, and ई strengthens to ए — ने + अ gives नय्

notes.role: सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — गुण of the root vowel before शप् → नयति

notes.en: the same अ, on a root that also changes shape — गम् appears as गच्छ्
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — बुध् → बोध्
बुध् + अ + ति, and उ strengthens to ओ — the same step as in नयति
वद् + अ + ति — अ already, so nothing to strengthen
present plural — श्रु takes श्नु, not शप्, so the stem is शृणो/शृण्व्
nominative plural — इ strengthens before the ending, अग्नि → अग्नय्

notes.role: जसि च — गुण before the plural ending → अग्नयः

notes.en: same stem ज्वल + अ, a different ending — ज्वलति beside ज्वलन्ति
present plural — दृश् appears as पश्य्

readings.vyakhya: धातोः परं शप्, तस्मात् पूर्वं गुणः। नी → ने → नय्। बुध् → बोध्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Between the root and the ending there is almost always a अ. It is not part
of either — it is inserted, and it is why भू gives भवति rather than भूति.
Once it is there, a short इ उ ऋ in the root strengthens in front of it:
नी becomes ने and then नय्, बुध् becomes बोध्.

वद् shows nothing happening, because अ cannot strengthen further. शृण्वन्ति
shows a root that takes a different insert altogether. The अ is the default,
not the rule without exception.

readings.sentence: राजपुरुषः सभाम् आगच्छति। सः महापुरुषः, पीताम्बरः च। रामकृष्णौ तम् पश्यतः। अब्राह्मणः अपि तत्र तिष्ठति। उपकृष्णम् जनाः सीदन्ति। राज्ञः पुरुषः धर्मम् कथयति।
readings.translation: The king's man comes to the assembly. He is a great man, and yellow-robed. Rāma and Kṛṣṇa see him. A non-brahmin stands there too. The people sit near Kṛṣṇa. The king's man speaks about dharma.
readings.teaches:
the four compound types in prose: राजपुरुषः, पीताम्बरः, रामकृष्णौ,
उपकृष्णम्. The passage opens on राजपुरुषः and closes on राज्ञः पुरुषः —
compounded and not.

notes.en: the second member is what the compound names; राजन् qualifies it

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — the class where the last member is primary

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case — महा describes पुरुष
names neither पीत nor अम्बर but the man wearing them

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the compound points outside itself → पीताम्बरः

notes.en: both members stand equal — the dual ending counts them

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate compound → रामकृष्णौ

notes.en: dual verb — रामकृष्णौ is two people, so the verb follows
negation compounded in front — न becomes अ before a consonant
the thematic अ between root and ending
the preverb उप leads, and the whole behaves as an indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — the first member governs and the compound is invariable

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the uncompounded विग्रह of राजपुरुषः — weak stem राज्ञ्
nominative — two words now, where the opening had one

readings.vyakhya: राजपुरुषः इति समासः, राज्ञः पुरुषः इति विग्रहः। एकः अर्थः, द्वे रूपे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The passage opens with राजपुरुषः and closes with राज्ञः पुरुषः. Same man,
same sense — one written as a single word, the other with the genitive
showing. That second form is the विग्रह, the analysis a compound can always
be unpacked into, and knowing which विग्रह a compound answers to is what
tells you its type.

पीताम्बरः is the one that will not unpack that way. Neither पीत nor अम्बर
is what the word names; it names a man neither member mentions.

readings.sentence: राजा सभाम् आगच्छति। जनाः राजानम् पश्यन्ति। गुरुः अपि तत्र। राजा गुरवे धनम् यच्छति, गुरुः च राज्ञे धर्मम् कथयति। गमनम् श्रेयः इति राजा वदति। ततः राजानौ अपि आगच्छतः।
readings.translation: The king comes to the assembly. The people see the king. The teacher is there too. The king gives wealth to the teacher, and the teacher tells the king about dharma. "Going is better," says the king. Then the two kings also arrive.
readings.teaches:
राजन् in four grades — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञे, राजानौ — with गुरुः / गुरवे
alongside. गमनम् closes as an action-noun.

notes.en: nominative — the bare पद loses its final न्, leaving राजा

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the final न् of राजन् drops → राजा

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the strong stem — the न् returns and the अ lengthens
indeclinable — the sentence needs no verb
dative — उ takes गुण, गुरु → गुरवे

notes.role: घेर्ङिति — गुण before the ङित् ending → गुरवे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the weak stem — राजन् loses its अ before a vowel ending, giving राज्ञ्
neuter nominative — the act itself, not the one who acts

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes the action-noun गमनम् from गम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
strong again, now in the dual — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञे, राजानौ

readings.vyakhya: राजा राजानम् राज्ञे राजानौ — एकं नाम, त्रयः आदेशाः।
readings.vyakhya_en:
राजन् appears four times and looks different each time: राजा without its
