न्, राजानम् and राजानौ with the न् back and the vowel long, राज्ञे with the
अ squeezed out. The word never changes its meaning. What changes is which
ending follows, and whether that ending belongs to the strong set.

readings.sentence: यः पठति सः जानाति। सा अपि पठति, तस्यै गुरुः पुस्तकम् यच्छति। तस्मै बालाय अपि यच्छति। ते पठन्ति, ताः च पठन्ति। गच्छन् बालः पुस्तकम् वहति। अहम् तान् पश्यामि।
readings.translation: He who reads, knows. She reads too; the teacher gives her a book. He gives one to that boy as well. They read, and they (the women) read. Walking along, the boy carries the book. I see them.
readings.teaches:
तद् and यद् through their forms: सः, सा, ते, ताः, तान्. तस्मै and बालाय
sit in one clause — both datives, different endings.

notes.en: the relative pronoun, opening the correlative frame

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — यद् and तद् belong to the सर्वनाम class

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
nominative feminine — सा beside masculine सः
the सर्वनाम dative — स्यै, where a noun would take आय

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → पुस्तकम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the masculine of तस्यै — स्मै, again not the noun ending

notes.role: सर्वनाम्नः स्मै — the सर्वनाम dative singular → तस्मै

notes.en: the ordinary noun dative — आय, beside तस्मै in the same clause
nominative plural feminine — ताः beside masculine ते
present participle — carries a second action without a second verb

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → गच्छन्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the speaker — अस्मद् has no stem-form here, अहम् is suppletive

readings.vyakhya: सर्वनाम्नः स्मै, नाम्नः आय। तस्मै बालाय — एकस्मिन् वाक्ये उभे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
तस्मै and बालाय stand side by side in one clause, both datives, both
pointing at the same boy. One takes स्मै because तद् is a सर्वनाम; the
other takes आय because बाल is an ordinary noun. The सर्वनाम class is not
a meaning — it is a list of stems that decline differently, and this is
where the difference shows.

readings.sentence: गुरुः शिष्यम् वदति — ग्रामम् गच्छ, तत्र धर्मम् पश्य। शिष्यः चिन्तयति — अहम् गच्छेयम्, किन्तु मार्गः दीर्घः। गुरुः वदति — यः धर्मम् इच्छति सः गच्छेत्। शिष्यः सुखी भूयात् इति गुरुः आशास्ते।
readings.translation: The teacher says to the student — "Go to the village; see dharma there." The student thinks — "I would go, but the road is long." The teacher says — "He who wants dharma should go." "May the student be happy," the teacher blesses.
readings.teaches:
three moods in one exchange: गच्छ orders, गच्छेत् recommends, भूयात्
wishes. One root, three endings.

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
imperative — a bare command, no ending at all in the 2nd sg.

notes.role: लोट् च — the imperative for a command → गच्छ

notes.en: a second imperative alongside the first
optative, first person — what the speaker might or would do

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → गच्छेयम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the same optative, third person — advice rather than an order
nominative — इन्-stem, न् drops in the nom.sg
the benedictive — a wish, distinct in form from गच्छेत्

readings.vyakhya: आज्ञा गच्छ, विधिः गच्छेत्, आशीः भूयात्। एकः अर्थः, त्रीणि रूपाणि।
readings.vyakhya_en:
गच्छ orders, गच्छेत् recommends, भूयात् wishes. All three point at an action
that has not happened yet, and nothing in the root or the sense separates
them — only the ending does. That is what a लकार is: not a tense in the
English sense, but a slot that carries mood and time together.

readings.sentence: अहम् ग्रामम् गच्छामि। त्वम् अपि ग्रामम् गच्छसि। नरः ग्रामे भवति। नरौ ग्रामम् गच्छतः। बालाः ग्रामात् आगच्छन्ति। अहम् तत्र न अगच्छम्। त्वम् तत्र अगच्छः।
readings.translation: I go to the village. You too go to the village. The man is in the village. The two men go to the village. The boys come back from the village. I did not go there. You went there.
readings.teaches:
one stem across three persons and three numbers, then the past: गच्छामि,
गच्छसि, गच्छति, गच्छतः, आगच्छन्ति, अगच्छम्.

notes.en: the मि ending — first person singular

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — मिप् for the speaker, giving गच्छामि

notes.en: the सि ending — same stem गच्छ्, different person
the ति ending — भू takes गुण before शप्, भो → भव्
the तस् ending — the verb answers the dual agent
the अन्ति ending — third person plural
the past — the augment अ in front, and the ending shortens to अम्

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् — the past before today → अगच्छम्

notes.en: the same augment, second person — अगच्छम् beside अगच्छः

readings.vyakhya: एकः धातुः, नव रूपाणि। पुरुषः वचनं च अन्ते दृश्येते।
readings.vyakhya_en:
गम् does not change. गच्छ् is the same stem in all seven verbs here; what
moves is the ending — मि, सि, ति, तः, अन्ति — and then the augment अ that
marks the past. Sanskrit puts person and number where English puts a
pronoun, which is why अहम् and त्वम् can be dropped without loss.

readings.sentence: रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च वनमगच्छताम्। तत्रर्षिरुवाच — नमस्ते वीर, सोऽपि धर्मं रक्षति। तयोर्गुरुराच्छादयति वनम्। पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो नरौ।
readings.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went to the forest. There a sage said — "Homage to you, hero; he too protects dharma." Their teacher covers the forest. The two men come back to the village again.
readings.teaches:
sandhi as it appears in text — joined and unmarked: रामश्च, तत्रर्षिरुवाच,
सोऽपि, पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो. The word-list gives the constituents.

notes.en: रामः + च — the visarga becomes श् before a च्-class stop

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant → रामश्च

notes.en: लक्ष्मणः + च — the same join, immediately repeated
वनम् + अगच्छताम् — the म् simply carries onto the following vowel
वनम् is कर्मन्, goal of motion; अगच्छताम् is dual past (लङ्)
तत्र + ऋषिः + उवाच — अ + ऋ merge, then the visarga of ऋषिः → र्

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — तत्र + ऋषिः gives तत्रर्षिः

notes.en: नमः + ते — the visarga becomes स् before a त्-class stop
ते is dative — नमस् governs the चतुर्थी
सः + अपि — visarga → ओ, and the अ of अपि elides, marked by ऽ

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — रु → उ, then गुण gives सो, and अपि loses its अ

notes.en: accusative — written with anusvāra before the following र्
the thematic अ between root and ending
तयोः + गुरुः + आच्छादयति — two visargas → र्, then आ + छ doubles the छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel before छ takes the तुक् augment → आच्छादयति

words.gloss: come back to the village again

notes.en: पुनः + ग्रामम् + आगच्छतः — visarga → र्, then final visarga → ओ before न्

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the रु/visarga alternation running twice in one word-group

notes.en: nominative dual — agreeing with the dual verb आगच्छतः

readings.vyakhya: सन्धिः पदच्छेदे ज्ञायते, न तु योजने। यत् पठसि तत् विभज।
readings.vyakhya_en:
A sandhi rule is usually shown from the pieces inward: रामः + च, and watch
them join. Text runs the other way. It gives you रामश्च and तत्रर्षिरुवाच
whole, and the work is taking them apart. That is पदच्छेद — sandhi is not
something performed in writing so much as undone in reading.

Nothing in the sentence is marked. The joins are easier to hear than to
see — रामश्च and पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो resolve on the tongue before they
resolve on the page. The word-list carries the constituents for the ones
that don't.

readings.sentence: नरः ग्रामे वसति। नरस्य पुत्रः बालः। नरः ग्रामात् गच्छति। सः पादाभ्याम् गच्छति। वृक्षात् फलम् पतति। नरः फलम् बालाय यच्छति। ततः नरः ग्रामम् आगच्छति।
readings.translation: A man lives in a village. The man's son is a boy. The man goes from the village. He goes on foot. A fruit falls from a tree. The man gives the fruit to the boy. Then the man comes back to the village.
readings.teaches: ग्राम in three cases in one passage: ग्रामे, ग्रामात्, ग्रामम्.

notes.en: agent — the one acting on its own
the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — a relation between two nouns, NOT one of the six कारकas
nominative — two nominatives, no verb; the sentence equates them
source — the fixed point moved away from
the thematic अ between root and ending
nominative — stands in for नरः, so the sentence need not repeat it

words.gloss: on foot (lit. by the two feet)

notes.en: instrument — the means by which the going happens
source again — same rule, different noun and different verb
agent here — the fruit is what falls
neuter nominative — फलम् serves as both प्रथमा and द्वितीया
the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — the one the giving is aimed at
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा appears as the stem यच्छ्
indeclinable — a narrative connective, takes no ending
goal of motion — what the agent reaches
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — आ reverses the direction of गम्

readings.vyakhya: एकं ग्रामपदम् — त्रिषु विभक्तिषु। ग्रामे, ग्रामात्, ग्रामम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
ग्राम appears three times: ग्रामे where the man lives, ग्रामात् where he
leaves from, ग्रामम् where he returns to. One noun, three endings, and the
ending alone says which relation the village has to the verb. That is what
a कारक is — not a meaning the word carries, but a role the sentence
assigns it.

readings.sentence: तापसः गिरौ वसति। जटाभिः सः तापसः ज्ञायते। अन्नस्य हेतोः बालः तम् गच्छति। पुत्रेण सह सः आगच्छति। धनेन न सुखम्, धर्मेण सुखम् इति तापसः वदति। गवाम् स्वामी नृपः अपि तम् शृणोति।
readings.translation: An ascetic lives on a mountain. By his matted hair he is recognized as an ascetic. For the sake of food a boy goes to him. He comes with his son. "Happiness is not from wealth; happiness is from dharma," says the ascetic. Even the king, lord of cattle, listens to him.
readings.teaches:
the instrumental past its plain करण sense: जटाभिः as a mark of
recognition, पुत्रेण सह for accompaniment. धनेन and धर्मेण stand in one
sentence as competing causes.

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the MARK by which someone is recognized — not an instrument proper

notes.role: इत्थंभूतलक्षणे — the identifying mark takes तृतीया → जटाभिः

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings
passive — the ascetic is what is known, not the knower
genitive — with हेतोः, BOTH words stand in the षष्ठी

notes.role: षष्ठी हेतुप्रयोगे — when हेतु is used, the cause takes षष्ठी → अन्नस्य हेतोः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने — the accompanying party takes तृतीया → पुत्रेण सह

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
cause — the तृतीया of motive, not of instrument

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → सुखम्

notes.en: the same cause-instrumental, set against धनेन
indeclinable — marks the end of reported speech
the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive plural — what is owned stands in the षष्ठी

notes.role: स्वामीश्वराधिपति… — with "lord/owner" words the thing owned takes षष्ठी → गवाम् स्वामी

notes.en: nominative — इन्-stem, न् drops in the nom.sg
present — श्रु takes the श्नु विकरण, श्रु → शृणो

readings.sentence: भगवान् वदति। तस्य वचनम् पिता शृणोति। पितरम् पुत्रः पश्यति। दण्डी अपि आगच्छति। दण्डिनम् पितरः पश्यन्ति। भगवतः वचनेन ते तुष्यन्ति। ततः राजानौ अपि आगच्छतः।
readings.translation: The Blessed One speaks. The father hears his words. The son sees the father. A staff-bearing ascetic also arrives. The fathers see the staff-bearer. By the Blessed One's words they are satisfied. Then the two kings also arrive.
readings.teaches:
three stems in both grades: भगवान् / भगवतः, दण्डी / दण्डिनम्, पिता /
पितरम् / पितरः. The meaning does not change between them.

notes.en: the STRONG stem — नुम् augment + lengthening give भगवान्

notes.role: उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थानेऽधातोः — नुम् in the strong cases → भगवान्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → वचनम्

notes.en: agent — ऋ-stem strong nom.sg, ऋ → आ
strong stem पितर् — the SAME word as पिता, one clause later
the thematic अ between root and ending
strong nom.sg — the न् of दण्डिन् drops and the इ lengthens
the thematic अ between root and ending
the न् RETURNS before a vowel ending — the foil to दण्डी above
strong plural — गुण अर्, a third grade of the same stem
the thematic अ between root and ending
the WEAK stem — plain भगवत् + ङस्, no नुम्; contrast भगवान् above
the thematic अ between root and ending
strong DUAL — राजन् lengthens to राजान् before the dual ending

readings.vyakhya: एकं पदम् — बलवत् दुर्बलं च। भगवान् भगवतः, दण्डी दण्डिनम्, पिता पितरम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Three stems, each appearing twice, each time in a different grade:
भगवान् / भगवतः, दण्डी / दण्डिनम्, पिता / पितरम् / पितरः. Nothing about the
meaning changes between the two forms of a pair — भगवान् and भगवतः are the
same person. What changes is the ending attached, and whether that ending
belongs to the सर्वनामस्थान (strong) set.

readings.sentence: यः अन्नम् ददाति सः दाता। दानम् तस्य धर्मः। नित्यम् कर्ता सः नरः, न तु भोक्ता। गमनम् आरभते, ग्रामम् गामी भवति। तस्य पाकः अपि रोचते। कर्तारम् तम् जनाः पश्यन्ति।
readings.translation: He who gives food is a giver. Giving is his dharma. That man is a constant doer, not an enjoyer. He begins the going, becomes a goer to the village. His cooking, too, is pleasing. People see him as the doer.
readings.teaches:
agent-nouns beside action-nouns, so the affix makes the difference: दाता /
दानम्, कर्ता / गमनम्. Then कर्ता declines into कर्तारम्.

notes.en: nominative — the relative, answered by सः
agent-noun from दा — the one who does the action

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → दानम्

notes.en: action-noun suffix — the ACT (भाव), not the actor; set directly against दाता
the HABITUAL agent — तृन्, not तृच्; the habit is what नित्यम् marks
another agent-noun, from भुज् — same affix, different root
action-noun in -अन from गम् — the going, not the goer

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun → गमनम्

notes.en: the उपपद — the goal, standing before the agent-noun
habit-agent with an उपपद — ग्रामं गामी "one who goes to the village"
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — भू → भो → भव्
the thematic अ between root and ending
action-noun from पच् with vṛddhi — पच् → पाकः
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — the one pleased would stand in the चतुर्थी
कर्ता DECLINES — the agent-noun is an ऋ-stem, strong अर् in the acc.
the thematic अ between root and ending

readings.vyakhya: दाता ददाति, दानम् दीयते। कर्ता करोति, करणम् क्रियते। कर्तुः कर्म भिन्नम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
दाता and दानम् come from the same root by different affixes, and the affix
is the whole difference: one names the giver, the other the giving. So with
कर्ता and गमनम्, भोक्ता and पाकः. A कृत् affix does not add a meaning to the
root so much as decide WHICH PART of the action the new word names — the
doer, the deed, or the instrument.

Then कर्ता becomes कर्तारम्. The agent-noun is not a frozen label; it is an
ऋ-stem noun and declines like पितृ. Both facts are usually met apart from
each other; here they arrive in one paragraph.

readings.sentence: बालः वने वृकात् बिभेति। सः मात्रे क्रुध्यति, यतः सा तम् वनम् न नयति। मुनिः गिरिम् अधिशेते। बालः मुनये श्लाघते, मुनेः फलेभ्यः च स्पृहयति। मुनिः बालाय फलानि यच्छति। बालाय फलानि रोचन्ते। सः गृहम् आगच्छति, मातुः च न बिभेति।
readings.translation: In the forest the boy is afraid of a wolf. He is angry at his mother, because she does not take him to the forest. A sage lies upon the mountain. The boy flatters the sage, and longs for the sage's fruits. The sage gives the boy fruits. The fruits please the boy. He comes home, and is no longer afraid of his mother.
readings.teaches:
six verbs, each choosing its own case. वृकात् and मात्रे sit in adjacent
clauses: two objects of emotion, two different cases.

notes.en: the thing feared — treated as what one shrinks away FROM

notes.role: भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः — with verbs of fearing, the cause of fear is अपादान → वृकात्

notes.en: the one angered at — NOT the accusative one might expect

notes.role: क्रुधद्रुहोरुपसृष्टयोः… — the target of क्रुध् is सम्प्रदान → मात्रे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — नी → ने → नय्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — नी + शप् → गुण ने → नय्
the locus turned OBJECT — अधि+शी makes it द्वितीया, not सप्तमी

notes.role: अधिशीङ्स्थासां कर्म — with अधि + शी/स्था/आस्, the locus becomes कर्मन् → गिरिम्

notes.en: शी is आत्मनेपदी — the ending is ते, not ति
the one whose favour is courted
dative — इ-stem takes गुण in the oblique, मुनि → मुनये
genitive — a relation, not a कारक
the thing desired — स्पृह् makes its object सम्प्रदान

notes.role: स्पृहेरीप्सितः — what is longed for is सम्प्रदान → फलेभ्यः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — here the ORDINARY dative, not a special government

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → फलानि

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा has the stem यच्छ्
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present plural — the FRUITS are the agent here, not the boy

notes.role: रुच्यर्थानां प्रीयमाणः — the one pleased is सम्प्रदान → बालाय

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
भी again — a SECOND meeting with the rule, different noun

readings.vyakhya: क्रियया विभक्तिः नियम्यते। भीत्रार्थे पञ्चमी, क्रुधार्थे चतुर्थी — एकस्मिन् वाक्ये उभे।
readings.vyakhya_en:
The boy fears the wolf and is angry at his mother in consecutive clauses.
Both are objects of an emotion; neither takes the accusative; and they take
DIFFERENT cases — वृकात् ablative, मात्रे dative. Nothing about the nouns
explains that. Only the verb does.

That is the whole content of special government, and a sentence like
बालः वृकेभ्यः बिभेति cannot show it, because with one verb on the page
there is no choice being made. Here the verb arrives first and the case
follows from it.

readings.sentence: नरः ग्रामे वसति। तस्य पुत्रः बालः। प्रभाते नरः बालः च वनम् गच्छतः। वने वृक्षाः सन्ति। नरः वृक्षात् फलानि आहरति। बालः फलानि इच्छति। नरः बालाय फलम् यच्छति। बालः फलम् खादति। ततः नरौ ग्रामम् आगच्छतः।
readings.translation: A man lives in a village. His son is a boy. At dawn the man and the boy go to the forest. In the forest there are trees. The man brings down fruits from a tree. The boy wants the fruits. The man gives the boy a fruit. The boy eats the fruit. Then the two of them come back to the village.
readings.teaches:
all six कारकas across nine sentences of connected prose. प्रभाते and वने
share the सप्तमी — time and place take the same case. The dual opens and
closes the passage.

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — a relation, not a कारक
nominative — a nominal sentence, no verb needed
locus in TIME — the same सप्तमी that marks place
indeclinable — joins two agents, so the verb goes dual
dual verb — two agents joined by च take the तस् ending
goal of motion — what the agent reaches
locus — now the scene, not the goal
plural — अ-stem नर-type, so वृक्ष + जस् → वृक्षाः
source — the fixed point departed from

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → फलानि

notes.en: neuter plural — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, so फलानि serves either
the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — the one the giving is aimed at
object — singular now, against the plural फलानि above
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा has the irregular stem यच्छ्
the thematic अ between root and ending
dual — the man and the boy, taken together

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two of them, so द्विवचन → नरौ

notes.en: dual verb — तस् ending agrees with नरौ, closing the frame

readings.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये यत् पृथक् दृष्टं तत् अत्र सङ्गतम्। षट् कारकाणि एकस्याम् कथायाम्।
readings.vyakhya_en:
Nothing here is new, and none of it is the point. ग्रामे is where the man
lives, not an example of the सप्तमी; वृक्षात् is where the fruit comes
from, not a demonstration of अपादान.

sequence.translation: The man goes.
sequence.teaches: bare कर्तृ + verb; the प्रथमा as the base case

notes.role: नर is the कर्तृ — the independent agent
प्रथमा for the bare prātipadika-sense → नरः
सुप्: सु (nom.sg) on नर

notes.text: नर + सु, then नरस् → नरः

notes.role: नरस्: final स → रु
रु → visarga before pause → नरः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् — present tense

sequence.vyakhya: नरः स्वतन्त्रः, अतः प्रथमा।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Two words, and the second one is the verb. नरः is the man; गच्छति is what
he does. The ः on the end of नरः is not decoration — it is the ending that
marks him as the one acting, and Sanskrit will change that ending every time
his part in the sentence changes. The next six sentences change nothing but
that.

sequence.translation: The man goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: adds कर्मन् → द्वितीया

notes.en: object — what the agent reaches (the goal of motion)

notes.role: ग्राम is कर्मन् — what the agent reaches
कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: यत् कर्तुः ईप्सिततमम् तत् कर्मन्, कर्मणि द्वितीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
One word longer than the last. ग्रामम् is where he is going, and the म् on
the end says so — the village is what the going reaches. Change that ending
and the village stops being the destination.

sequence.translation: The man goes to the village on foot.
sequence.teaches: adds करण → तृतीया

notes.role: पाद is करण — the most effective means

notes.en: dual — a man has two feet

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → पादाभ्याम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: पादौ साधकतमम् करण, कर्तृकरणयोः तृतीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
पादाभ्याम् is "by the two feet" — how the going is done rather than where it
goes. A third role, a third ending. The word for feet is dual here because
a man has two of them, and Sanskrit counts that separately from singular
and plural.

sequence.translation: The man comes from the village.
sequence.teaches: adds अपादान → पञ्चमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अपादान — the fixed point of departure
अपादाने पञ्चमी → ग्रामात्

notes.text: आ +

notes.en: "come" — आ adds "toward," motion toward the speaker

sequence.vyakhya: ध्रुवम् अपाये अपादान, अपादाने पञ्चमी।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The same village as two sentences ago, and a different ending: ग्रामम् when
he went to it, ग्रामात् now that he comes from it. Nothing about the village
changed. What changed is its part in the sentence, and only the ending
records that.

sequence.translation: The man gives fruit to the boy.
sequence.teaches: adds सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: बाल is सम्प्रदान — the one aimed at, the recipient
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → बालाय

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणा यम् अभिप्रैति सः सम्प्रदान, चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Three nouns now, each with its own ending: नरः gives, फलम् is what he
gives, बालाय is who he gives it to. Nothing in the word order tells you
which is which — the endings do all of it, and the same three words in any
order would still mean the same thing.

sequence.translation: The man lives in the village.
sequence.teaches: adds अधिकरण → सप्तमी

notes.role: ग्राम is अधिकरण — the locus of the action
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → ग्रामे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: आधारः अधिकरण, सप्तमी अधिकरणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A third ending on the same village. ग्रामम् when he went to it, ग्रामात्
when he came from it, ग्रामे now that he lives in it. Three sentences, one
noun, and the ending is the only thing carrying the difference.

sequence.translation: The man's son lives in the village.
sequence.teaches: adds षष्ठी (a relation, not a कारक)

words.gloss: of the man, the relation whose

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे — the remaining relation (genitive) → नरस्य

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: कारकभिन्नः सम्बन्धः शेष, तत्र षष्ठी।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
नरस्य means "of the man" — not something he does or has done to him, just
who the son belongs to. That is a relation between two nouns rather than a
part in the action, and Sanskrit gives it its own ending like everything
else. Notice the man is no longer the one acting: पुत्रः is.

sequence.sentence: नरः ग्रामे वसति। नरस्य पुत्रः बालः। नरः ग्रामात् गच्छति। सः पादाभ्याम् गच्छति। वृक्षात् फलम् पतति। नरः फलम् बालाय यच्छति। ततः नरः ग्रामम् आगच्छति।
sequence.translation: A man lives in a village. The man's son is a boy. The man goes from the village. He goes on foot. A fruit falls from a tree. The man gives the fruit to the boy. Then the man comes back to the village.
sequence.teaches: ग्राम in three cases in one passage: ग्रामे, ग्रामात्, ग्रामम्.

notes.en: agent — the one acting on its own
the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — a relation between two nouns, NOT one of the six कारकas
nominative — two nominatives, no verb; the sentence equates them
source — the fixed point moved away from
the thematic अ between root and ending
nominative — stands in for नरः, so the sentence need not repeat it

words.gloss: on foot (lit. by the two feet)

notes.en: instrument — the means by which the going happens
source again — same rule, different noun and different verb
agent here — the fruit is what falls
neuter nominative — फलम् serves as both प्रथमा and द्वितीया
the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — the one the giving is aimed at
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा appears as the stem यच्छ्
indeclinable — a narrative connective, takes no ending
goal of motion — what the agent reaches
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — आ reverses the direction of गम्

sequence.vyakhya: एकं ग्रामपदम् — त्रिषु विभक्तिषु। ग्रामे, ग्रामात्, ग्रामम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
ग्राम appears three times: ग्रामे where the man lives, ग्रामात् where he
leaves from, ग्रामम् where he returns to. One noun, three endings, and the
ending alone says which relation the village has to the verb. That is what
a कारक is — not a meaning the word carries, but a role the sentence
assigns it.

sequence.translation: The boy sees the fruit.
sequence.teaches: the neuter stem फल — प्रथमा and द्वितीया are the same form

notes.text: here प्रथमा and द्वितीया share one form, both फलम्

notes.role: अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem सु/अम् → अम्, so nom.sg फलम्
स्वमोर्नपुंसकात् — neuter सु and अम् behave alike: फलम् serves as both प्रथमा and द्वितीया

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समाने रूपे — फलम् इति।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
फलम् looks the same whether the fruit is doing something or having
something done to it — neuter nouns do not distinguish the two. Here the
boy is looking and the fruit is looked at, and you know that from बालः,
which does distinguish them, and from the sense.

sequence.translation: The fruit falls from the tree.
sequence.teaches: फलम् as the agent this time, with the ablative of source alongside

notes.role: फल is now कर्तृ — the same neuter form फलम् fills the agent role

notes.text: the neuter form is still फलम्

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी → वृक्षात्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: फलम् इह स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता, तथापि रूपम् तदेव।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same word फलम् that was the object above is the agent here — and looks identical, because the neuter does not distinguish them. The अपादान-पञ्चमी (वृक्षात्) is exactly as it was for ग्रामात्: the frame is unchanged.

sequence.translation: The man sees fruit in the river.
sequence.teaches: a feminine stem in -ई: नदी becomes नद्याम् in the locative, the ई turning to य् before the ending

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → नद्याम् (the locus)
स्त्रियाम् — the feminine, opening the stems नदी belongs to
ऋन्नेभ्यो ङीप् — नदी is a ङीप्-formed ī-stem feminine

notes.text: नदी + आम्

notes.role: ङेराम्नद्याम्नीभ्यः — ī-stem fem locative sg takes आम्: नदी+आम्

notes.text: → नद्याम्

notes.role: इको यणचि — ई before आम् becomes य्: नदी+आम् → नद्याम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: अधिकरणे सप्तमी — स्त्रीलिङ्गेऽपि सैव।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
ग्रामे and नद्याम् are the same case — both say "in" — but they look nothing
alike, because ग्राम and नदी belong to different stem-classes and take
different endings. The part a word plays decides WHICH case; the shape of
the stem decides what that case looks like on it.

sequence.translation: The two men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number: dual कर्तृ नरौ + dual verb

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two referents → द्विवचन (dual): नरौ, गच्छतः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
dual — the verb agrees with नरौ

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः द्विवचनम् — कर्तरि क्रियायाम् च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two referents call for the द्विवचन — in the noun (नरौ) and, agreeing, in the verb (गच्छतः). The role is still कर्तृ-प्रथमा, exactly as नरः was; only the count has changed.

sequence.translation: The men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number: plural कर्तृ नराः (नर+जस् → नराः) + plural verb

notes.role: बहुषु बहुवचनम् — many referents → बहुवचन (plural)

notes.text: नर + जस् → नराः

notes.role: प्रथमयोः पूर्वसवर्णः — नर + जस् (अस्) → नराः, the nom.pl

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: बहूनाम् बहुवचनम्। एकः नरः, द्वौ नरौ, बहवः नराः — एकैव विभक्तिः, भिद्यते वचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Many referents call for the बहुवचन. नरः, नरौ, नराः — one प्रथमा case across three numbers: the विभक्ति is constant, the वचन varies.

sequence.translation: The fruits are eaten by the men.
sequence.teaches: plural instrumental नरैः (अ+भिस् → ऐस्) + neuter plural फलानि

notes.en: here the agent of a passive verb, in the instrumental

notes.text: नर + भिस् → नरैः

notes.role: अतो भिस ऐस् — a-stem instrumental plural भिस् → ऐस्: नर+ऐस् → नरैः

notes.text: फल → फलानि

notes.role: जश्शसोः शिः — neuter जस्/शस् → शि (इ): फल+शि
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् inserted before the शि-ending: फल+न्+इ
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ — the stem vowel lengthens: फला-न्-इ → फलानि

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

sequence.vyakhya: बहुषु नरेषु करणभूतेषु तृतीया बहुवचनम्; फलानि नपुंसकबहुवचने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The instrumental plural नरैः; the neuter plural फलानि. Same roles as ever — only the number is new, and each stem-class spells the plural its own way.

sequence.translation: I go to the village.
sequence.teaches: person (पुरुष): the उत्तमपुरुष — speaker — selects a different ending

notes.text: the pronoun for the speaker

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — the तिङ् endings fall into three पुरुष: प्रथम, मध्यम, उत्तम
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending मिप् for उत्तम·एक → गच्छामि

sequence.vyakhya: वक्ता उत्तमपुरुषः। एकस्मिन् कर्तरि एकवचनम् — गच्छामि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The speaker is the उत्तमपुरुष. The verb's ending names who acts, just as the noun's ending named its role: गच्छति (he goes) and गच्छामि (I go) share one root, one tense — only the पुरुष differs.

sequence.translation: You go to the village.
sequence.teaches: person: the मध्यमपुरुष — the one addressed

notes.text: the pronoun for the one addressed

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: तिङ् ending सिप् for मध्यम·एक → गच्छसि

sequence.vyakhya: यम् प्रति उच्यते सः मध्यमपुरुषः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The one spoken to is the मध्यमपुरुष. Three persons now stand together: गच्छति (प्रथम, he), गच्छसि (मध्यम, you), गच्छामि (उत्तम, I) — one root, three endings.

sequence.translation: The boy went to the village.
sequence.teaches: tense (लकार): the past — लङ् replaces लट्, and an augment अ is prefixed

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् — for past (not of today) the लङ् replaces लट्

notes.text: अ-augment + गच्छ + त् → अगच्छत्

sequence.vyakhya: भूते अनद्यतने लङ्। धातुः स एव, कालः अन्यः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For the past, the लङ् stands where the present लट् stood. The root is the same √गम्; only the tense — the लकार — has changed. गच्छति (goes) → अगच्छत् (went): a new tense-slot, marked by the अ-augment in front.
sequence.note: // The full augment/ending derivation (3.4.100ff, 6.4.71) is later; here we state the siddha form अगच्छत् and cite the लकार choice 3.2.111. Stepwise derivation deferred to a Track-B path.

sequence.translation: The man is (becomes) in the village.
sequence.teaches: गुण of the root vowel — भू → भो → भव् before शप् gives भवति

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — भू → भो → भव्
the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् — present sense → लट्
कर्तरि शप् — when an agent is denoted, शप् (अ) is added after the root (the गण-1 vikaraṇa)
सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः — before शप् the root vowel takes गुण → ऊ → ओ → (before अ) अव् → भव्
तिप्तस्झि… — the तिङ् ending तिप् for प्रथम·एक → भवति

sequence.vyakhya: भू इति धातुः। शपि परतः ऊकारस्य गुणः ओकारः, सोऽवादेशम् आपद्यते — भव्। तिपि भवति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The root भू "be." Before शप् (the अ-vikaraṇa of गण 1, by कर्तरि शप्), the root vowel ऊ takes गुण (7.3.84): ऊ → ओ, which before the following अ becomes अव् — भू → भव्. With the प्रथम·एक ending तिप्, the present is भवति. Compare गच्छति: same लट्, same तिप्, but भू shows its गुण where गम् does not.

sequence.translation: The two men go to the village.
sequence.teaches: number on the verb — two agents take the तस् ending → गच्छतः

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — for two, the द्विवचन

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: तिङस्त्रीणि त्रीणि प्रथममध्यमोत्तमाः — each triad of तिङ् endings is प्रथम/मध्यम/उत्तम
तान्येकवचनद्विवचनबहुवचनान्येकशः — within a triad the three are एक/द्वि/बहुवचन
तिप्तस्झि… — the तस् ending (प्रथम·द्वि) → गच्छतः

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः कर्त्रोः द्विवचनम्। प्रथमपुरुषस्य द्विवचनं तस् — गच्छतः। एको गच्छति, द्वौ गच्छतः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Number lives on the verb too. नरौ are two, so the verb takes the द्विवचन ending: of the प्रथम triad तिप्-तस्-झि (1.4.101/102), the middle one तस् gives गच्छतः. Side by side: गच्छति (one goes), गच्छतः (two go) — same root, tense, person; only वचन shifts.

sequence.sentence: अहम् ग्रामम् गच्छामि। त्वम् अपि ग्रामम् गच्छसि। नरः ग्रामे भवति। नरौ ग्रामम् गच्छतः। बालाः ग्रामात् आगच्छन्ति। अहम् तत्र न अगच्छम्। त्वम् तत्र अगच्छः।
sequence.translation: I go to the village. You too go to the village. The man is in the village. The two men go to the village. The boys come back from the village. I did not go there. You went there.
sequence.teaches:
one stem across three persons and three numbers, then the past: गच्छामि,
गच्छसि, गच्छति, गच्छतः, आगच्छन्ति, अगच्छम्.

notes.en: the मि ending — first person singular

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — मिप् for the speaker, giving गच्छामि

notes.en: the सि ending — same stem गच्छ्, different person
the ति ending — भू takes गुण before शप्, भो → भव्
the तस् ending — the verb answers the dual agent
the अन्ति ending — third person plural
the past — the augment अ in front, and the ending shortens to अम्

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् — the past before today → अगच्छम्

notes.en: the same augment, second person — अगच्छम् beside अगच्छः

sequence.vyakhya: एकः धातुः, नव रूपाणि। पुरुषः वचनं च अन्ते दृश्येते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
गम् does not change. गच्छ् is the same stem in all seven verbs here; what
moves is the ending — मि, सि, ति, तः, अन्ति — and then the augment अ that
marks the past. Sanskrit puts person and number where English puts a
pronoun, which is why अहम् and त्वम् can be dropped without loss.

sequence.translation: The boy fears the wolves.
sequence.teaches: special government: a verb of fearing makes the feared thing अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: of/from the wolves — the thing feared

notes.en: source — here, what one shrinks from

notes.role: भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः — with verbs of fearing, the cause of fear is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → वृकेभ्यः

sequence.vyakhya: भयहेतुः अपादानम् — न तु कर्म। वृकेभ्यः बिभेति, न वृकान्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One might expect the feared thing to be the कर्मन् (the object fearing "reaches"). But Pāṇini names it अपादान — what one shrinks away from — so it takes the पञ्चमी, not the द्वितीया: वृकेभ्यः, not वृकान्. Knowing the verb tells you the case.

sequence.translation: The man owes Devadatta a hundred.
sequence.teaches: special government: √धारि 'owe' makes the creditor सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

notes.role: धारेरुत्तमर्णः — with √धारि (owe), the creditor (उत्तमर्ण) is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → देवदत्ताय

sequence.vyakhya: उत्तमर्णः सम्प्रदानम्। यस्य ऋणं धार्यते सः सम्प्रदानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The creditor — the one to whom the debt is owed — is the सम्प्रदान, just as a gift's recipient is. So देवदत्ताय (चतुर्थी), the same case as the boy received the fruit in. A specific verb extends a familiar role.

sequence.translation: The pupil learns from the teacher.
sequence.teaches: special government: in formal study, the teacher one learns from is अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: from the teacher — the source of the learning

notes.en: source — the one from whom knowledge is received

notes.role: आख्यातोपयोगे — in formal learning, the source-teacher is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → उपाध्यायात्

sequence.vyakhya: आख्यातोपयोगे उपाध्यायः अपादानम्। उपाध्यायात् अधीते — न उपाध्यायम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: In formal study (आख्यातोपयोगे), the teacher one receives knowledge from is named अपादान — the source of departure — so it takes the पञ्चमी, not the द्वितीया (1.4.29). उपाध्यायात् अधीते "learns from the teacher," parallel to "fears the wolves" (ex017): a special verb pins an unexpected case.

sequence.translation: The sweet is pleasing to the boy.
sequence.teaches: special government: with रुच् "please," the one pleased is सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

words.gloss: to the boy — the one pleased

notes.en: the one to whom (the thing) is pleasing

notes.role: रुच्यर्थानां प्रीयमाणः — with verbs of pleasing, the pleased one is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → बालाय

notes.en: grammatical subject — the thing that pleases
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: रुच्यर्थे प्रीयमाणः सम्प्रदानम्। बालाय रोचते — यः प्रीयते सः चतुर्थ्याम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With रुच् "please," the one who is pleased is treated as सम्प्रदान, the recipient — so the boy stands in the चतुर्थी, not the प्रथमा (1.4.33). मोदकः रोचते बालाय literally "the sweet is-pleasing to-the-boy" — the English subject ("the boy likes the sweet") is the Sanskrit dative. The pleasing thing (मोदकः) is the nominative.

sequence.translation: The boy longs for flowers.
sequence.teaches: special government: with स्पृह् "desire," the desired thing is सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

words.gloss: for the flowers — the thing desired

notes.en: the desired object, treated as the goal of longing

notes.role: स्पृहेरीप्सितः — with स्पृह्, the desired thing is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → पुष्पेभ्यः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: स्पृहेः ईप्सितः सम्प्रदानम्। पुष्पेभ्यः स्पृहयति — न पुष्पाणि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One expects the desired thing to be the object (कर्मन्, द्वितीया). But with स्पृह् "long for," Pāṇini names the desired thing सम्प्रदान — so it takes the चतुर्थी: पुष्पेभ्यः स्पृहयति "longs for flowers," not पुष्पाणि (1.4.36). Compare रुच् in ex120: a whole family of emotion-verbs routes their target through the dative.

sequence.translation: The boy is angry at the king.
sequence.teaches: special government: the target of क्रुध् "be angry" is सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

words.gloss: at the king — the target of the anger

notes.en: the one the anger is directed toward

notes.role: क्रुधद्रुहेर्ष्याऽसूयार्थानां यं प्रति कोपः — the target of anger is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → नृपाय

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: क्रुधेः यं प्रति कोपः स सम्प्रदानम्। नृपाय क्रुध्यति — चतुर्थ्याम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With क्रुध् "be angry" (and द्रुह् "harm," ईर्ष्या "envy," असूया "resent"), the one toward whom the feeling is aimed is सम्प्रदान — so it takes the चतुर्थी: नृपाय क्रुध्यति "is angry at the king" (1.4.37). The very next sūtra (ex123) shows what a preverb does to this — watch the case change.

sequence.translation: The boy rages against the king.
sequence.teaches: add a preverb to क्रुध् and the target shifts to कर्मन् → द्वितीया

words.gloss: the king — now the direct object

notes.en: object — when क्रुध् carries a preverb, the target becomes कर्मन्

notes.role: क्रुधद्रुहोरुपसृष्टयोः कर्म — with a preverb, the target of क्रुध्/द्रुह् is कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → नृपम्

notes.en: "be angry," here with the preverb अभि
अभि — the preverb that flips the government
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: उपसृष्टे क्रुधौ यं प्रति कोपः तत् कर्म। अभिक्रुध्यति नृपम् — द्वितीयायाम्, न चतुर्थ्याम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same verb क्रुध्, the same target — but add the preverb अभि and the case changes. Without a preverb the target is सम्प्रदान (चतुर्थी: नृपाय, ex122); WITH one it becomes a plain कर्मन् (द्वितीया: नृपम्), by 1.4.38. The minimal pair नृपाय क्रुध्यति / नृपम् अभिक्रुध्यति is Pāṇini's own demonstration that an उपसर्ग can rewrite कारक-assignment.

sequence.translation: The sage lies upon the mountain.
sequence.teaches: special government: with अधि + शी/स्था/आस्, the locus becomes कर्मन् → द्वितीया (not सप्तमी)

words.gloss: the mountain — the resting-place, here as object

notes.en: the locus, but treated as कर्मन् because of अधि + शी

notes.role: अधिशीङ्स्थाऽऽसां कर्म — with अधि+शी/स्था/आस्, the site is कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → गिरिम्

notes.en: अधि — makes the resting-site a कर्मन्

sequence.vyakhya: अधिपूर्वस्य शीङः आधारः कर्म। गिरिम् अधिशेते — द्वितीयायाम्, न गिरौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A resting-place is normally अधिकरण, taking the सप्तमी (गिरौ "on the mountain"). But after अधि, the verbs शी "lie," स्था "stand," and आस् "sit" take that very location as their कर्मन् — so it shifts to the द्वितीया: गिरिम् अधिशेते "lies upon the mountain" (1.4.46). Another case where the preverb, not the noun's role, decides the ending.

sequence.translation: The mother hides from her son.
sequence.teaches: special government: the one you hide from — whose sight you avoid — is अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: from the son — the one whose sight is avoided

notes.en: source — the one one withdraws from sight of

notes.role: अन्तर्द्धौ येनादर्शनमिच्छति — in hiding, the one you avoid being seen by is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → पुत्रात्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: अन्तर्द्धौ यस्मात् अदर्शनम् इच्छति तत् अपादानम्। पुत्रात् निलीयते — न पुत्रम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When you hide, the person you want NOT to be seen by is named अपादान — a point of withdrawal — so it takes the पञ्चमी (1.4.28). पुत्रात् निलीयते "hides from the son." Like the feared thing (ex017) and the teacher learned-from (ex119), this is अपादान stretched past literal motion: hiding is a kind of moving-away-from-sight.

sequence.translation: The Gaṅgā arises from the Himālaya.
sequence.teaches: special government: with भू "arise," the source the agent springs from is अपादान → पञ्चमी

words.gloss: from the Himālaya — the source of arising

notes.en: source — the origin the river springs from

notes.role: भुवः प्रभवः — with भू (arise), the source is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → हिमवतः

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — भू → भो → भव्
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: भुवः प्रभवः अपादानम्। हिमवतः गङ्गा प्रभवति — स्रोतसः उद्गमः पञ्चम्याम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With प्र + भू "arise, originate," the source the subject springs from is अपादान, in the पञ्चमी (1.4.31). हिमवतः गङ्गा प्रभवति "the Gaṅgā arises from the Himālaya." The river is the agent (नominative); its mountain-source is the point-of-departure. The same logic names the wax-source with जन् "be born" (1.4.30).

sequence.translation: The pupil flatters the teacher.
sequence.teaches: special government: with श्लाघ् "flatter," the one whose favour is courted is सम्प्रदान → चतुर्थी

words.gloss: to the teacher — the one whose favour is sought

notes.en: the one toward whom the flattery is aimed

notes.role: श्लाघह्नुङ्स्थाशपां ज्ञीप्स्यमानः — with श्लाघ् etc., the courted one is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → गुरवे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: श्लाघादीनां ज्ञीप्स्यमानः सम्प्रदानम्। गुरवे श्लाघते — यस्य प्रसादम् इच्छति सः चतुर्थ्याम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: With श्लाघ् "flatter," ह्नु "deny to," स्था "present oneself to," शप् "swear to," the person whose favour or notice is being courted (ज्ञीप्स्यमान) is सम्प्रदान — the चतुर्थी (1.4.34). गुरवे श्लाघते "flatters the teacher," i.e. praises him to win his good will. Another emotion/attitude verb that routes its target through the dative, like रुच् and क्रुध् (ex120, ex122).

sequence.translation: The cowherd milks milk from the cow.
sequence.teaches: अकथितं च: an unstated कारक (here the source, the cow) becomes a second कर्मन् → द्वितीया (a double-accusative verb)

words.gloss: the cow — the source, but here a second object

notes.en: the source (cow), unstated as अपादान, so taken as कर्मन्

notes.role: अकथितं च — a कारक not pinned to another role is taken as कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → गाम्

notes.en: the primary object — what is drawn out

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → पयः

sequence.vyakhya: दुह्यादीनां द्विकर्मकत्वम्। गौः अपादानम् इव, किन्तु अकथितत्वात् कर्म। गां पयः दोग्धि — द्वे द्वितीये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A handful of verbs (दुह् "milk," याच् "ask," etc.) take TWO accusatives. The cow is really the source (one would expect अपादान, पञ्चमी), but since that role is left unstated, by अकथितं च it is simply taken as a कर्मन् — so BOTH the cow and the milk stand in the द्वितीया: गां पयः दोग्धि "milks milk from-the-cow." This is the first double-accusative in the reader.

sequence.translation: The teacher makes the pupil go to the village.
sequence.teaches: causative णिच्: in the causative of a motion-verb, the underlying agent (the goer) becomes a कर्मन् → द्वितीया

notes.en: agent of the causative (the प्रयोजक, the one who makes it happen)

words.gloss: the pupil — the one made to go

notes.en: the underlying goer, now object of the causative

notes.role: गतिबुद्धि…अणि कर्ता स णौ — the base-agent of a motion/knowing verb becomes कर्मन् in the causative
कर्मणि द्वितीया → शिष्यम्

words.gloss: to the village — the goal of motion

notes.en: goal of motion (the original object of गम्)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ग्रामम्
हेतुमति च — the causative affix णिच् → गमयति

sequence.vyakhya: गत्यर्थस्य अणि कर्ता णौ कर्म। गमयति शिष्यं — यः गन्ता सः कर्म। ग्रामम् अपि कर्म।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Make a verb causative (णिच्, 3.1.26: गम् → गमि "make go") and a new agent appears — the causer. For verbs of MOTION, knowing, and eating, the original agent (the one who actually goes) is demoted to कर्मन्, taking the द्वितीया (1.4.52). गुरुः शिष्यं ग्रामं गमयति "the teacher makes the pupil go to the village" — two accusatives: शिष्यम् (the demoted goer) and ग्रामम् (the goal). The first causative in the reader.

sequence.translation: The master makes the servant carry the load.
sequence.teaches: हेतु / causative: with a non-motion verb, the prompted base-agent is हेतु and stands in the करण → तृतीया

words.gloss: by the servant — the one made to carry

notes.en: the prompted base-agent (the actual carrier), treated as करण

notes.role: तत्प्रयोजको हेतुश्च — the driver of the कर्तृ is हेतु (a करण)
साधकतमं करणम् — the most effective means is करण
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → दासेन
कर्मणि द्वितीया → भारम्
हेतुमति च — the causative affix णिच् → वाहयति

sequence.vyakhya: अगत्यर्थे प्रयोज्यः कर्ता हेतुः, करणत्वात् तृतीयायाम्। दासेन वाहयति — न दासम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Contrast ex129. With a NON-motion verb like वह् "carry," the causative does NOT demote the base-agent to कर्मन्; instead the prompted doer is हेतु — a kind of करण, the means by which the causer accomplishes the act — and takes the तृतीया (1.4.55 + 1.4.42). स्वामी दासेन भारं वाहयति "the master makes the servant carry the load," literally "...carries the load BY-the-servant." The minimal contrast ex129/ex130 — accusative goer vs instrumental causee — is the heart of causative कारक.

sequence.sentence: बालः वने वृकात् बिभेति। सः मात्रे क्रुध्यति, यतः सा तम् वनम् न नयति। मुनिः गिरिम् अधिशेते। बालः मुनये श्लाघते, मुनेः फलेभ्यः च स्पृहयति। मुनिः बालाय फलानि यच्छति। बालाय फलानि रोचन्ते। सः गृहम् आगच्छति, मातुः च न बिभेति।
sequence.translation: In the forest the boy is afraid of a wolf. He is angry at his mother, because she does not take him to the forest. A sage lies upon the mountain. The boy flatters the sage, and longs for the sage's fruits. The sage gives the boy fruits. The fruits please the boy. He comes home, and is no longer afraid of his mother.
sequence.teaches:
six verbs, each choosing its own case. वृकात् and मात्रे sit in adjacent
clauses: two objects of emotion, two different cases.

notes.en: the thing feared — treated as what one shrinks away FROM

notes.role: भीत्रार्थानां भयहेतुः — with verbs of fearing, the cause of fear is अपादान → वृकात्

notes.en: the one angered at — NOT the accusative one might expect

notes.role: क्रुधद्रुहोरुपसृष्टयोः… — the target of क्रुध् is सम्प्रदान → मात्रे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — नी → ने → नय्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — नी + शप् → गुण ने → नय्
the locus turned OBJECT — अधि+शी makes it द्वितीया, not सप्तमी

notes.role: अधिशीङ्स्थासां कर्म — with अधि + शी/स्था/आस्, the locus becomes कर्मन् → गिरिम्

notes.en: शी is आत्मनेपदी — the ending is ते, not ति
the one whose favour is courted
dative — इ-stem takes गुण in the oblique, मुनि → मुनये
genitive — a relation, not a कारक
the thing desired — स्पृह् makes its object सम्प्रदान

notes.role: स्पृहेरीप्सितः — what is longed for is सम्प्रदान → फलेभ्यः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — here the ORDINARY dative, not a special government

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → फलानि

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा has the stem यच्छ्
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present plural — the FRUITS are the agent here, not the boy

notes.role: रुच्यर्थानां प्रीयमाणः — the one pleased is सम्प्रदान → बालाय

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
भी again — a SECOND meeting with the rule, different noun

sequence.vyakhya: क्रियया विभक्तिः नियम्यते। भीत्रार्थे पञ्चमी, क्रुधार्थे चतुर्थी — एकस्मिन् वाक्ये उभे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The boy fears the wolf and is angry at his mother in consecutive clauses.
Both are objects of an emotion; neither takes the accusative; and they take
DIFFERENT cases — वृकात् ablative, मात्रे dative. Nothing about the nouns
explains that. Only the verb does.

That is the whole content of special government, and a sentence like
बालः वृकेभ्यः बिभेति cannot show it, because with one verb on the page
there is no choice being made. Here the verb arrives first and the case
follows from it.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice.
sequence.teaches: the verb's ending is परस्मैपद — the active-voice set of तिङ् endings

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
active voice — the तिप्-तस्-झि set of endings

notes.role: लः परस्मैपदम् — the तिङ् endings replacing a लकार are by default परस्मैपद

sequence.vyakhya: लादेशाः परस्मैपदम् — तिप्तस्झ्यादयः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The endings that replace a लकार are, in general, परस्मैपद — the active set (तिप्, तस्, झि …). पचति is one of them. A second set, the आत्मनेपद, stands beside it for the middle voice.

sequence.translation: The man cooks rice (for himself).
sequence.teaches: the आत्मनेपद — the middle-voice set, action for the agent's own sake

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
middle voice — the त-आताम्-झ set of endings

notes.role: तङानावात्मनेपदम् — the तङ् (and शानच्/कानच्) replacements are आत्मनेपद
तान्येकवचन… — the nine endings distribute as 3 पुरुष × 3 वचन (एक/द्वि/बहु)

sequence.vyakhya: पचति परस्मैपदम्, पचते आत्मनेपदम् — स एव धातुः, फलम् अन्यत्र वा स्वे वा।
sequence.vyakhya_en: One root, two ending-sets. पचति (परस्मैपद) cooks for another; पचते (आत्मनेपद) cooks for oneself. The nine endings of each set fill the same grid — three पुरुष across three वचन — so a verb-form names person, number, and voice all at once.

sequence.translation: Homage to the gods.
sequence.teaches: नमः and its companions (स्वस्ति, स्वाहा …) govern the चतुर्थी

notes.en: nominative — the salutation itself, with अस्तु understood

notes.text: the word of salutation

notes.role: नमःस्वस्ति… — with नमः (and स्वस्ति, स्वाहा, स्वधा, अलम्, वषट्) the word takes चतुर्थी
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → देवेभ्यः

sequence.vyakhya: नमसा योगे चतुर्थी। नमो देवेभ्यः, न देवान्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A handful of fixed words — नमः foremost — govern the चतुर्थी by themselves, no verb needed. "नमो देवेभ्यः," homage to the gods (चतुर्थी), never देवान्. Learn the word, and its case comes with it.

sequence.translation: The man studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: duration and extent (काल, अध्वन्) in continuous connection take द्वितीया

notes.en: object — here, the span filled by the action

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a time-word (or distance) in unbroken connection takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: अत्यन्तसंयोगे कालाध्वनोः द्वितीया। मासम् अधीते — कृत्स्नं कालम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When an action fills a whole stretch of time or space without a break, that span stands in the द्वितीया: मासम् अधीते, "studies through a whole month." The accusative here measures extent, not an object reached.

sequence.translation: He goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: गत्यर्थ — with a verb of motion, the goal (कर्म) takes द्वितीया

notes.en: the goal of motion is treated as the object

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → the most-desired goal is कर्मन्
गत्यर्थकर्मणि द्वितीयाचतुर्थ्यौ — with a motion-verb the goal takes द्वितीया (or चतुर्थी)

notes.text: ग्रामम् → ग्रामं (final म् → anusvāra before ग)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: वर्तमाने लट् → present

sequence.vyakhya: गत्यर्थस्य धातोः कर्म गन्तव्यं द्वितीयायाम्। ग्रामो गन्तव्यः, अतः ग्रामम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A verb of motion (गम् "go") makes its destination the कर्मन् — the goal one most wants to reach (1.4.49) — and that takes the accusative (2.3.12). So "go TO the village" is simply ग्रामम् (acc.), no preposition needed. The same rule allows चतुर्थी (a dative of goal) in Vedic and poetry; classical prose prefers द्वितीया.

sequence.translation: He studies for a month.
sequence.teaches: अत्यन्तसंयोग — unbroken extent of time/space takes द्वितीया

notes.en: extent — the span over which the action runs without break

notes.role: कालाध्वनोरत्यन्तसंयोगे — a word of time or distance spanning an unbroken stretch takes द्वितीया

sequence.vyakhya: कालस्य अध्वनश्च अत्यन्तसंयोगे द्वितीया। मासम् इति कालपरिमाणम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Duration and distance, when the action fills the whole stretch without a gap, stand in the accusative (2.3.5) — मासम् "(for) a month," क्रोशम् "(for) a krośa of road." Not "to a month" but "across the whole of it." This is why "he studies for a month" needs no "for": the bare accusative मासम् carries the span.

sequence.sentence: नरः ग्रामे वसति। तस्य पुत्रः बालः। प्रभाते नरः बालः च वनम् गच्छतः। वने वृक्षाः सन्ति। नरः वृक्षात् फलानि आहरति। बालः फलानि इच्छति। नरः बालाय फलम् यच्छति। बालः फलम् खादति। ततः नरौ ग्रामम् आगच्छतः।
sequence.translation: A man lives in a village. His son is a boy. At dawn the man and the boy go to the forest. In the forest there are trees. The man brings down fruits from a tree. The boy wants the fruits. The man gives the boy a fruit. The boy eats the fruit. Then the two of them come back to the village.
sequence.teaches:
all six कारकas across nine sentences of connected prose. प्रभाते and वने
share the सप्तमी — time and place take the same case. The dual opens and
closes the passage.

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
genitive — a relation, not a कारक
nominative — a nominal sentence, no verb needed
locus in TIME — the same सप्तमी that marks place
indeclinable — joins two agents, so the verb goes dual
dual verb — two agents joined by च take the तस् ending
goal of motion — what the agent reaches
locus — now the scene, not the goal
plural — अ-stem नर-type, so वृक्ष + जस् → वृक्षाः
source — the fixed point departed from

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → फलानि

notes.en: neuter plural — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, so फलानि serves either
the thematic अ between root and ending
recipient — the one the giving is aimed at
object — singular now, against the plural फलानि above
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — दा has the irregular stem यच्छ्
the thematic अ between root and ending
dual — the man and the boy, taken together

notes.role: द्व्येकयोर्द्विवचनैकवचने — two of them, so द्विवचन → नरौ

notes.en: dual verb — तस् ending agrees with नरौ, closing the frame

sequence.vyakhya: एकस्मिन् वाक्ये यत् पृथक् दृष्टं तत् अत्र सङ्गतम्। षट् कारकाणि एकस्याम् कथायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Nothing here is new, and none of it is the point. ग्रामे is where the man
lives, not an example of the सप्तमी; वृक्षात् is where the fruit comes
from, not a demonstration of अपादान.

sequence.translation: "curds, Indra" → दधीन्द्रः (curds-Indra)
sequence.teaches: सवर्णदीर्घ — two like (सवर्ण) vowels merge into one long vowel

notes.text: दधि + इन्द्रः: इ meets इ

notes.en: homogeneous — vowels of the same place of articulation

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — a simple vowel before a like vowel; the two become one long vowel

notes.text: → ई → दधीन्द्रः

sequence.vyakhya: समाने सवर्णे अकः दीर्घ एकादेशः। इ + इ = ई।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When a simple vowel (अक्) meets a homogeneous vowel — इ with इ, उ with उ, अ with अ — the pair fuses into the single long vowel of that class. दधि + इन्द्रः gives दधीन्द्रः: two इ become one ई.

sequence.translation: "not here" → नेह
sequence.teaches: गुण — अ/आ before इ/उ/ऋ yields the गुण vowel (ए, ओ, अर्)

notes.text: न + इह: अ meets इ

notes.role: आद्गुणः — when अ/आ is followed by another vowel, the two become the single गुण vowel

notes.text: अ + इ → ए → नेह

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् अचि गुण एकादेशः। अ + इ = ए।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An अ or आ followed by इ, उ, or ऋ does not merge to a long vowel but shifts to the गुण grade: अ + इ → ए, अ + उ → ओ, अ + ऋ → अर्. So न + इह → नेह. The same अ behaves differently depending on the vowel it meets.

sequence.translation: "yours indeed" → तवैव
sequence.teaches: वृद्धि — अ/आ before ए/ऐ/ओ/औ yields the वृद्धि vowel (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: तव + एव: अ meets ए

notes.role: वृद्धिरेचि — when अ/आ is followed by एच् (ए ऐ ओ औ), the two become the वृद्धि vowel

notes.text: अ + ए → ऐ → तवैव

sequence.vyakhya: अवर्णात् एचि वृद्धिः एकादेशः। अ + ए = ऐ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When अ or आ meets one of the diphthong-grade vowels (ए, ऐ, ओ, औ), the result climbs to the वृद्धि grade: अ + ए → ऐ, अ + ओ → औ. So तव + एव → तवैव. गुण and वृद्धि are the two upward grades of इ and उ.

sequence.translation: "the wise one is to be served" → सुध्युपास्यः
sequence.teaches: यण् — इ/उ/ऋ before an unlike vowel become the glide य्/व्/र्

notes.text: सुधी + उपास्यः: ई meets उ (unlike)

notes.en: the glides य् व् र् ल्

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (इ उ ऋ ऌ) before any vowel becomes its corresponding यण् glide

notes.text: ई → य् → सुध्युपास्यः

sequence.vyakhya: इकः अचि यण् आदेशः। ई + उ → य् + उ = यु।
sequence.vyakhya_en: When इ, उ, or ऋ meets an unlike vowel, it does not merge but turns into its glide — य्, व्, र् — and the following vowel stands: सुधी + उपास्यः → सुध्युपास्यः. (Like meeting like gave the long vowel of ex023; unlike gives the glide here.)

sequence.translation: He too goes.
sequence.teaches: visarga → ओ before a voiced sound (अतो रोः → उ, then गुण ओ); the अवग्रह (ऽ) marks the elided अ

notes.text: विग्रह: सः + अपि; the अः before a voiced sound → ओ, and अ of अपि elides (ऽ)

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — अः (from रु) becomes उ before a voiced sound → स उ
आद्गुणः — अ + उ → गुण ओ → सो; the following अ drops (पूर्वरूप), marked ऽ

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: अतो रोः उत्वम्, ततः गुणः। सः + अपि = सोऽपि। लोपे अवग्रहः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The commonest visarga outcome: सः before a voiced sound. The अः (a visarga from रु, 8.2.66) becomes उ (6.1.113), then अ + उ fuse by गुण to ओ (6.1.87) → सो; the following short अ then drops, written with the अवग्रह ऽ. सः + अपि → सोऽपि "he too." This is why सः appears as सो only before voiced sounds — before a vowel other than अ, or a consonant, it shifts differently.

sequence.translation: Salutation to you.
sequence.teaches: visarga → स् before a त्-class stop (विसर्जनीयस्य सः)

notes.text: विग्रह: नमः + ते; the visarge before त् becomes स् (its homorganic sibilant)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before a sibilant/dental-स् context → नमस्

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सकारः सवर्णे। नमः + ते = नमस्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Before a dental, the visarga assimilates to स् (8.3.34, विसर्जनीयस्य सः). नमः + ते → नमस्ते "salutations to you" — the visarga of नमः becomes स् before the त् of ते. The same gives दुस्तर (दुः + तर), निस्तेज (निः + तेज): visarga takes the sibilant of the place that follows.

sequence.translation: He covers over.
sequence.teaches: छ-doubling (तुक्) — a short vowel before छ inserts त् → च्छ (छे च)

notes.text: विग्रह: आ + छादयति; before छ a त् (तुक्) is inserted → च्छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel (here the आ-preverb context) before छ takes the augment तुक् (त्) → च्छ

sequence.vyakhya: छकारे परे तुक् (त्); त् + छ = च्छ। आ + छादयति = आच्छादयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: छ never stands alone after a vowel: छे च (6.1.73) inserts the augment तुक् (त्), and त् + छ surfaces as च्छ. आ + छादयति → आच्छादयति "covers over." The same doubling gives तच्छ्रुत्वा (तत् + छ्रुत्वा... via श्), शिवच्छाया (शिव + छाया "Śiva's shade"): a vowel + छ always becomes -च्छ-.

sequence.translation: For this (is so).
sequence.teaches: before ह, a stop voices and doubles it — here त् + ह gives द्ध

notes.text: विग्रह: एतत् + हि; final त् → द् (जश्त्व) before voiced ह, and ह → ध (झयो हः)

notes.role: झलां जशोऽन्ते — final त् voices to द् before a voiced sound
झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् — ह after a झय् stop optionally becomes its voiced aspirate → ध

notes.en: "for, indeed" (the ह that triggers the change)

sequence.vyakhya: अन्त्यस्य जश्त्वम् (त्→द्), झयः परस्य हस्य घोषवदादेशः (ह→ध)। एतत् + हि = एतद्धि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two changes meet at त् + ह. First जश्त्व: the final त् voices to द् before the voiced ह (8.2.39). Then the ह, now after a voiced stop, optionally becomes that stop's voiced aspirate — झयो होऽन्यतरस्याम् (8.4.62) — so ह → ध and the cluster surfaces as द्ध: एतत् + हि → एतद्धि. The same gives तद्धित (तत् + हित), वाग्घरि (वाक् + हरि): a stop + ह coalesces into a doubled voiced aspirate.

sequence.translation: He delights again.
sequence.teaches: visarga → र् before a voiced sound — the other outcome, beside सोऽपि

notes.text: पुनः ends in रु; before a voiced sound the visarga surfaces as र् (not ओ)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — word-final स् → रु; its visarga becomes र् before a voiced sound
अतो रोः — applies to अ-final रु (सः→सो); पुनर् keeps र् because its base is पुनर्, not अतः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: रेफान्तस्य रुत्वम् घोषे। पुनः + रमते = पुनर् रमते। (अतो भिन्नत्वात् न ओत्वम्।)
sequence.vyakhya_en: Not every visarga becomes ओ. Words whose underlying final is -र् (पुनर्, अन्तर्, प्रातर्) show र् before a voiced sound, NOT the अ + उ → ओ fusion of ex155. पुनः + रमते → पुनर् रमते "delights again." Contrast सोऽपि (सः, base स-अः → सो) with पुनर् (base पुनर्): the visarga's outcome depends on what stands under it — an अ that fuses to ओ, or an र् that simply reappears.

sequence.sentence: रामः च लक्ष्मणः च → रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च।
sequence.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
sequence.teaches: visarga → श् before a च्-class stop (श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant)

notes.text: विग्रह: रामः + च; visarga → स् (8.3.34), then स् → श् before च् (श्चुत्व)

notes.role: विसर्जनीयस्य सः — visarga → स् before the following stop
स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — स्/त् before a च्-class sound become श्/च् → रामश्च

notes.text: same change: लक्ष्मणः + च → लक्ष्मणश्च

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः → श् before च

sequence.vyakhya: विसर्जनीयस्य सः, ततः श्चुत्वम्। रामः + च = रामश्च। द्वयोः योगे चकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The visarga before a च-class stop ends up as श्. First it becomes स् (8.3.34); then स् before च् is cerebralised — really palatalised — to श् by स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः (8.4.40). रामः च → रामश्च, लक्ष्मणः च → लक्ष्मणश्च, the standard "X and Y" linkage. The visarga's three sibilant outcomes — स् (before त्, ex156), श् (before च्, here), ष् (before ट्) — all follow the place of the stop that comes next.

sequence.sentence: रामश्च लक्ष्मणश्च वनमगच्छताम्। तत्रर्षिरुवाच — नमस्ते वीर, सोऽपि धर्मं रक्षति। तयोर्गुरुराच्छादयति वनम्। पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो नरौ।
sequence.translation: Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa went to the forest. There a sage said — "Homage to you, hero; he too protects dharma." Their teacher covers the forest. The two men come back to the village again.
sequence.teaches:
sandhi as it appears in text — joined and unmarked: रामश्च, तत्रर्षिरुवाच,
सोऽपि, पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो. The word-list gives the constituents.

notes.en: रामः + च — the visarga becomes श् before a च्-class stop

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — श्चुत्व applied to the visarga-sibilant → रामश्च

notes.en: लक्ष्मणः + च — the same join, immediately repeated
वनम् + अगच्छताम् — the म् simply carries onto the following vowel
वनम् is कर्मन्, goal of motion; अगच्छताम् is dual past (लङ्)
तत्र + ऋषिः + उवाच — अ + ऋ merge, then the visarga of ऋषिः → र्

notes.role: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः — तत्र + ऋषिः gives तत्रर्षिः

notes.en: नमः + ते — the visarga becomes स् before a त्-class stop
ते is dative — नमस् governs the चतुर्थी
सः + अपि — visarga → ओ, and the अ of अपि elides, marked by ऽ

notes.role: अतो रोरप्लुतादप्लुते — रु → उ, then गुण gives सो, and अपि loses its अ

notes.en: accusative — written with anusvāra before the following र्
the thematic अ between root and ending
तयोः + गुरुः + आच्छादयति — two visargas → र्, then आ + छ doubles the छ

notes.role: छे च — a short vowel before छ takes the तुक् augment → आच्छादयति

words.gloss: come back to the village again

notes.en: पुनः + ग्रामम् + आगच्छतः — visarga → र्, then final visarga → ओ before न्

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the रु/visarga alternation running twice in one word-group

notes.en: nominative dual — agreeing with the dual verb आगच्छतः

sequence.vyakhya: सन्धिः पदच्छेदे ज्ञायते, न तु योजने। यत् पठसि तत् विभज।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A sandhi rule is usually shown from the pieces inward: रामः + च, and watch
them join. Text runs the other way. It gives you रामश्च and तत्रर्षिरुवाच
whole, and the work is taking them apart. That is पदच्छेद — sandhi is not
something performed in writing so much as undone in reading.

Nothing in the sentence is marked. The joins are easier to hear than to
see — रामश्च and पुनर्ग्राममागच्छतो resolve on the tongue before they
resolve on the page. The word-list carries the constituents for the ones
that don't.

sequence.translation: He did that (long ago / it is told).
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for remote or reported past; the root reduplicates

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार

notes.text: कृ reduplicates → च-कार → चकार

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। धातुः द्विरुक्तः — चकार।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For a past the speaker did not witness — the deep past of story and report — the लिट् is used, and the root doubles its first syllable: कृ → चकार, "he did" (out of sight, or long ago). Compare अकरोत् (लङ्, the past one saw): same act, different reach into time.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लृट् — the future; built on the root with a स्य-marker

notes.text: the adverb fixing the time as future

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — for what is yet to be, लृट् is used

notes.text: करि + ष्य + ति → करिष्यति

sequence.vyakhya: भविष्यति लृट्। करोति, अकरोत्, चकार, करिष्यति — एकः धातुः, चत्वारः कालाः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: For what is still to come, the लृट् is used. Now the whole time-axis stands on one root √कृ: करोति (does), अकरोत् (did, witnessed), चकार (did, long ago), करिष्यति (will do). The लकार is the verb's clock — choose it, and the tense is set.

sequence.translation: He did that yesterday.
sequence.teaches: लङ् — the imperfect, for a past before today (अनद्यतन)

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सः
अनद्यतने लङ् → the imperfect for a not-today past → अकरोत्
तिङ्: तिप् (3·sg) on the past base → अकरोत् (with अट्-augment)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भूते लङ्। ह्यः इति अनद्यतनकालः, अतः अकरोत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the past three ways by *remoteness*. लङ् (the imperfect, 3.2.111) is the past that does NOT fall on the current day — hence ह्यः "yesterday" → अकरोत् "he did." The अ- prefix (अट्-augment) is the past marker you also saw in अगच्छत्. Same root √कृ as करोति "does," now in the not-today past.

sequence.translation: He did that long ago.
sequence.teaches: लिट् — the perfect, for a remote (परोक्ष) past beyond witness

notes.en: indeclinable — "of old" (marks the परोक्ष, beyond-sight, past)
perfect — remote past, not directly witnessed

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् → the perfect for a past beyond the speaker's witness → चकार (reduplicated)

sequence.vyakhya: परोक्षे भूते लिट्। अदृष्टं चिरातीतं — चकार। तदेव कृ-धातुः, द्विरुक्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115) is the *remote* past — परोक्ष, "beyond the eye," what the speaker did not himself witness (history, legend, "long ago"). √कृ reduplicates to चकार "he did (of old)." Contrast ex060: अकरोत् (लङ्) is yesterday's deed, चकार (लिट्) is the ancient deed. The tense itself tells you how far back, and whether anyone saw it.

sequence.translation: He did that today.
sequence.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the tense-neutral past (and today’s past)

notes.en: aorist — the general past (and the past of today)

notes.role: लुङ् → the aorist for past sense → अकार्षीत्
च्लेः सिच् — the aorist takes the सिच् (s-aorist) marker (derivation deferred)

sequence.vyakhya: भूते सामान्ये लुङ्। अद्यतनं भूतम् अपि लुङा — अकार्षीत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The aorist (लुङ्, 3.2.110) is the *unmarked* past — it states a past act without committing to remoteness, and it is the proper past for *today's* events (अद्य "today" → अकार्षीत् "he has done"). √कृ now spans all three pasts: अकरोत् (yesterday, लङ्) · चकार (long ago, लिट्) · अकार्षीत् (today, लुङ्). The full form-building (सिच्, वृद्धि) is a Track-B derivation.

sequence.translation: He will do that tomorrow.
sequence.teaches: लुट् — the periphrastic future, for a future beyond today (अनद्यतन)

notes.en: periphrastic future — a future not on the current day

notes.role: अनद्यतने लुट् → the लुट् future for a not-today future → कर्ता (= कर्तृ + an understood अस्ति)

sequence.vyakhya: अनद्यतने भविष्यति लुट्। श्वः इति अनद्यतनः, अतः कर्ता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sanskrit splits the FUTURE too. लुट् (3.3.15) is the future that does NOT fall today — श्वः "tomorrow" → कर्ता "he will do." It is "periphrastic": the form कर्ता is literally an agent-noun ("(he is) a doer (tomorrow)"). Contrast करिष्यति (लृट्, the general future, ex028). Past and future each have a today/not-today split — the लकार is the verb's calendar.

sequence.sentence: यदि सः अगमिष्यत् तर्हि सुखम् अलप्स्यत।
sequence.translation: Had he gone, he would have obtained happiness.
sequence.teaches: लृङ् — the conditional, for an act that never came about (क्रियातिपत्ति)

notes.role: लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ — when the act fails to happen, लृङ् → अगमिष्यत्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुखम्
लिङ्निमित्ते लृङ् क्रियातिपत्तौ → अलप्स्यत

sequence.vyakhya: क्रियायाः अनिष्पत्तौ लृङ्। यदि अगमिष्यत् — न तु अगच्छत्। फलमपि न लब्धम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The लृङ् conditional is for what would-have-been but was NOT — क्रियातिपत्ति, the act's non-occurrence (3.3.139). It looks like the future-stem (गमिष्य-, लप्स्य-) with the augment अ and the लङ् imperfect endings: अगमिष्यत्, अलप्स्यत. यदि सः अगमिष्यत् "had he gone" — implying he did not. This completes the ten लकारs: present, three pasts, two futures, three moods, and now the conditional.

sequence.translation: The village is gone-to by Rāma. (Rāma goes to the village.)
sequence.teaches: कर्मणि प्रयोग — the passive: the object becomes the nominative subject; agent → instrumental; यक् + आत्मनेपद

notes.en: the agent, now in the instrumental (not nominative)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in the passive → रामेण

words.gloss: the village — now the grammatical subject

notes.en: the logical object, raised to nominative subject in the passive

notes.role: प्रातिपदिकार्थ…प्रथमा → the कर्म, when verb-denoted, takes प्रथमा → ग्रामः

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — the passive विकरण यक् (य) → गम्यते
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix denotes the कर्म (passive) → ātmanepada ending
भावकर्मणोः — passive/impersonal take आत्मनेपद → गम्यते

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणि यक्, आत्मनेपदं च। रामः गच्छति → रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग) re-stages the same act: the OBJECT becomes the nominative subject (ग्रामः), the AGENT drops to the instrumental (रामेण), and the verb takes the passive marker यक् (य, 3.1.67) with ātmanepada endings (1.3.13) — गम्यते "is gone-to." Active रामः ग्रामं गच्छति = passive रामेण ग्रामः गम्यते. The ल-affix now points to the कर्म, not the कर्तृ (3.4.69).

sequence.translation: It is slept by Devadatta. (Devadatta sleeps.)
sequence.teaches: भावे प्रयोग — the impersonal passive of an intransitive verb: no subject, agent in the instrumental

notes.en: the agent, in the instrumental (no nominative exists)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → कर्तृ in भाव/passive → देवदत्तेन

notes.en: the passive विकरण — root + य, with आत्मनेपद endings

notes.role: …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः — for intransitive roots the ल-affix denotes भाव (the bare act)
भावकर्मणोः → आत्मनेपद → सुप्यते (3sg, no agreement with any noun)

sequence.vyakhya: अकर्मकात् भावे प्रयोगः। कर्तृ तृतीयायाम्, क्रिया एव प्रधाना। देवदत्तेन सुप्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: An intransitive verb has no object to promote, so its passive is IMPERSONAL — भावे प्रयोग, "the bare act" (3.4.69 …भावे चाकर्मकेभ्यः). There is no subject at all: the verb stands in a fixed 3rd-singular (सुप्यते), and the agent is instrumental (देवदत्तेन). Literally "it-is-slept by Devadatta" = "Devadatta sleeps." Sanskrit's way of foregrounding the action over the doer.

sequence.translation: He did (it). / He made (it).
sequence.teaches: लुङ् — the aorist, the simple/unmarked past (no restriction to a time-frame)

notes.role: लुङ् — past action without a time restriction → the aorist → अकार्षीत्

sequence.vyakhya: सामान्ये भूते लुङ्। अकार्षीत् — न अद्यतनानद्यतनविशेषः। कृ-धातोः सिजन्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The लुङ् aorist is the UNMARKED past: plain "did," with none of the today/before-today restrictions that लङ् (अकरोत्, imperfect) and लिट् (चकार, perfect) carry — 3.2.110 simply says लुङ् for past action. √कृ → अकार्षीत् "he did," with the augment अ and the सिच् marker. So √कृ now spans all four pasts-and-presents: करोति · अकरोत् · चकार · अकार्षीत्, plus the future करिष्यति. The full time-axis of one root.

sequence.translation: The boy cooks; the rice is cooked.
sequence.teaches: कर्तरि शप् vs कर्मणि यक् — the विकरण (stem-marker) shows the voice: active शप् (अ) vs passive यक् (य)

notes.role: कर्तरि शप् — in the active, the विकरण शप् (अ) → पच् + अ + ति → पचति

words.gloss: the rice — subject of the passive clause

notes.en: the object, raised to nominative in the passive

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — in the passive, the विकरण यक् (य) → पच् + य + ते → पच्यते

sequence.vyakhya: कर्तरि शप्, कर्मणि यक्। पच् + अ → पचति; पच् + य → पच्यते। विकरणः प्रयोगं सूचयति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: What tells active from passive is the विकरण — the little stem-marker between root and ending. Active uses शप्, अ (3.1.68 कर्तरि शप्): पच् + अ + ति → पचति "cooks." Passive uses यक्, य (3.1.67 सार्वधातुके यक्): पच् + य + ते → पच्यते "is cooked." Same root पच्, same tense; the विकरण अ vs य, and the ending परस्मै- vs आत्मनेपद, carry the whole voice contrast.

sequence.sentence: भवामि भवावः भवामः। भवसि भवथः भवथ। भवति भवतः भवन्ति।
sequence.translation: Present tense of भू "be", all nine cells: I/we-two/we am/are; you/you-two/you-all are; he/those-two/they are.
sequence.teaches: the whole present-tense paradigm — three पुरुष across three वचन

notes.role: तिप्तस्झि… — the ending series; 1sg मिप् → भवामि
तिप्तस्झि… → 3sg तिप् → भवति
बहुषु बहुवचनम् → plural → भवन्ति

sequence.vyakhya: लटि परस्मैपदस्य नव तिङः — त्रयः पुरुषाः त्रीणि वचनानि च। भू + शप् + तिङ् = भवति इत्यादि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: You met the तिङ् frame one cell at a time (ex014–016, ex092). Here is the WHOLE present-tense paradigm of भू "be" in one place — the verbal counterpart to the देव declension table (ex094). Read across each row for a person (उत्तम / मध्यम / प्रथम), down each column for a number (sg · dual · pl). The nine endings come from one master sūtra, तिप्तस्झि… (3.4.78); the stem is भू + शप् (अ) → भव-. Learn these nine and every parasmaipada present (गच्छति, पठति, वदति) falls into place.

sequence.sentence: बालः ओदनम् पचति। बालेन ओदनः पच्यते।
sequence.translation: The boy cooks the rice. The rice is cooked by the boy.
sequence.teaches:
the same event twice, and the case of every noun changes. In the first the
agent is nominative and the object accusative; in the second the object has
become nominative and the agent instrumental. The verb's ending is what
decides which.

notes.en: agent — expressed by the verb's ending, so the noun is nominative
object — NOT expressed by the ending here, so it takes a case of its own

notes.role: अनभिहिते — a रोल takes its case only when the verb has not already expressed it

notes.en: the ending ति expresses the AGENT — so बालः needs no case of its own

notes.role: लस्य — the तिङ् endings replace the लकार, and carry agent or object with them

notes.en: still the agent — but now the ending expresses the OBJECT, so the agent takes a case

notes.role: अनभिहिते — unexpressed by the verb, the agent falls back to the तृतीया

notes.en: the same object as ओदनम् above, now expressed by the ending
nominative — what the verb expresses stands in the प्रथमा
the passive विकरण — पच् + य + ते
the ending ते expresses the OBJECT

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — आत्मनेपद endings in the passive → पच्यते

sequence.vyakhya: अनभिहिते इति अधिकारः। यत् तिङा उक्तं तत् प्रथमायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Both sentences describe one boy cooking one pot of rice. What moves is
which participant the verb's ending points at.

ति in पचति points at the cooker, so the cooker needs no case of its own and
stands in the प्रथमा; the rice, unmentioned by the ending, takes the
द्वितीया. ते in पच्यते points at what is cooked, so now the rice stands in
the प्रथमा and the boy — no longer pointed at — falls back to the तृतीया.

The rule behind it is one word: अनभिहिते, "when not already expressed." A
noun takes a case for its role only if the verb has not already said it.

sequence.translation: The fire blazes.
sequence.teaches: an इ-stem masculine: nominative अग्निः (नर-like सु, but on an इ-stem)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → अग्निः

notes.text: अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
