sequence.vyakhya_en: The gerund (क्त्वा, the "absolutive") chains two acts of ONE agent, marking the EARLIER (3.4.21): गत्वा … खादति = "having gone … (he) eats." First go, then eat — one man, two actions, the क्त्वा-form taking the first. It is indeclinable (1.1.40). When a prefix is present it becomes ल्यप् instead (आगत्य "having come"), but the meaning — "having ___, then ___" — is the same. This is how Sanskrit strings narrative: a row of gerunds ending in one finite verb.

source.ref: Bhāgavata 10.9 — the नवनीतचोर (butter-thief) episode
source.curated: our graded prose telling the famous butter-theft; not the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: यशोदा गृहे नवनीतम् रक्षति। किन्तु कृष्णः नवनीतम् इच्छति। सः शनैः गृहम् प्रविशति, उच्चैः च नवनीतम् चोरयति। ततः सः मित्रेभ्यः तत् नवनीतम् यच्छति, स्वयम् च खादति। यशोदा तं पश्यति, क्रुध्यति च।
sequence.translation: Yaśodā keeps butter in the house. But Kṛṣṇa wants the butter. He quietly enters the house and steals the butter from up high. Then he gives that butter to his friends and eats it himself. Yaśodā sees him and grows angry.
sequence.teaches: a scene rather than a sentence — किन्तु and ततः joining clauses, the adverbs शनैः, उच्चैः, स्वयम्, and मित्रेभ्यः as सम्प्रदान

notes.en: object — the prize of the whole episode (neuter a-stem)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → नवनीतम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the thematic अ between root and ending
the thematic अ between root and ending
adverb — "aloft" (the butter hung high; Kṛṣṇa reaches it)
recipients — to whom he gives the butter

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → मित्रेभ्यः (dat. pl., as देवेभ्यः)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → तं

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: दृश्यं विस्तृतम् — किन्तु, ततः, च इति योजकैः वाक्यानि सम्बद्धानि। नवनीतम् कर्म, मित्रेभ्यः सम्प्रदानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Now a whole scene, not a single fact. Sentences link by connectives — किन्तु ("but," turning Yaśodā's guarding into Kṛṣṇa's wanting), ततः ("then"), च ("and") — so the action flows. The new pieces are small and natural: adverbs (शनैः "quietly," उच्चैः "high up," स्वयम् "himself") and a chain of present verbs (इच्छति, प्रविशति, चोरयति, यच्छति, खादति). The case-roles are all known — नवनीतम् the object, मित्रेभ्यः the dative of recipient. You are reading a story now.

source.ref: a girl in the forest — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

sequence.sentence: कन्या वने तिष्ठति। सा लताम् पश्यति, मालाम् च रचयति। गङ्गायाम् जलम् अस्ति। कन्या तत्र स्नाति, देवीम् च नमति। सेना अपि आगच्छति, किन्तु कन्या न बिभेति।
sequence.translation: A girl stands in the forest. She sees a creeper, and makes a garland. In the Ganges there is water. The girl bathes there, and bows to the goddess. An army comes too, but the girl is not afraid.
sequence.teaches:
कन्या, लता, माला, देवी — new words, all in endings already met: सेना's आ
in the nominative, सभाम्'s द्वितीया, सभायाम्'s सप्तमी.

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — an a-stem feminine takes टाप् (आ) → कन्या

notes.en: nominative — the same आ-ending met on सेना
present — स्था has the stem तिष्ठ्
accusative — the आकारान्त feminine adds म्, as सभाम्
locative — the आकारान्त feminine takes याम्, as सभायाम्
accusative — देवी is an ई-stem feminine, like नदी

sequence.vyakhya: कन्या लता माला देवी — नूतनानि पदानि, प्रसिद्धेषु प्रत्ययेषु। सेनायाः इव आकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Four new words here, and not one new ending. कन्या, लता, माला all close in
the same आ that सेना carries; लताम् and मालाम् take the accusative म् of
सभाम्; गङ्गायाम् takes the locative याम् of सभायाम्. देवी follows नदी. The
words are new, the grammar is not — that is the whole reason they can arrive
together, without a sentence apiece.

sequence.translation: The teacher tells the lesson.
sequence.teaches: a उ-stem masculine: nom गुरुः (parallel to अग्निः)

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → गुरुः

notes.text: गुरु + सु → गुरुः, just as अग्नि + सु → अग्निः

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → पाठम्

sequence.vyakhya: उकारान्तं पुंलिङ्गम् गुरुशब्दः। प्रथमायाम् गुरुः, यथा अग्निः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: गुरु ends in उ, as अग्नि ends in इ — and they decline alike. The nominative singular is गुरुः, formed exactly as अग्निः was. The उ-stem differs from the इ-stem only in which vowel it carries, not in how it behaves.

sequence.translation: He gives fruit to the teacher.
sequence.teaches: the उ-stem dative गुरवे — उ takes गुण by the same rule that gives अग्नये

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → the recipient गुरु takes चतुर्थी

notes.en: the grade ओ (उ → ओ, written अव् before the vowel)

notes.role: घेर्ङिति — the SAME rule that gave अग्नये; before a ङित् ending the उ-stem takes गुण; गुरु + ए → गुरवे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: घेः ङिति गुणः — इकारे एकारः, उकारे ओकारः। अग्नये, गुरवे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The one rule घेर्ङिति strengthens both classes before the dative: इ → ए gave अग्नये; उ → ओ gives गुरवे (the ओ written as अव् before the following vowel). One principle of गुण, each vowel to its own grade — अग्नये and गुरवे are the same move on different vowels.

sequence.translation: The king goes.
sequence.teaches: न-stem राजन् — the bare पद loses its final न् → राजा

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → राजन् is the agent
प्रथमा for the bare prātipadika-sense

notes.text: राजन् + सु; the सु drops, leaving the पद राजन्

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य → a पद-final न् drops → राजा (with lengthening, 6.4.8)
सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → the penultimate आ-lengthening that gives राजा

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य नकारस्य लोपः। राजन् → राजा। पदान्ते न् न तिष्ठति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Consonant stems behave differently from the vowel stems you have met. राजन् ("king") ends in न् — but a word-final (पद-final) न् DROPS (8.2.7), and the penultimate lengthens (6.4.8), so the nominative is राजा, not *राजन्*. The stem hides its न् whenever it stands bare at a word's end. This single न-loss shapes the whole paradigm.

sequence.translation: He sees the king.
sequence.teaches: राजन् in the accusative — a सर्वनामस्थान ending keeps the न् and lengthens → राजानम्

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → राजानम्

notes.text: राजन् + अम्; अम् is a सर्वनामस्थान (strong) ending — the न् stays

notes.role: सर्वनामस्थाने चासम्बुद्धौ → before a strong ending the penultimate lengthens → राजान् → राजानम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वनामस्थाने नकारः तिष्ठति, उपधा च दीर्घा। राजन् + अम् → राजानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Where the bare पद lost its न्, a *strong* ending (सर्वनामस्थान — the nom./acc. endings) keeps it and lengthens the vowel before it (6.4.8): राजन् + अम् → राजानम्. So the king is राजा when bare, राजानम् as object. The consonant stem is "strong" (full न्, long vowel) before some endings and "weak" before others — the split that defines this whole family.

sequence.translation: Going is better. / The going is preferable.
sequence.teaches: ल्युट् — the action-noun ("the ___ing"), a कृत् abstract

words.gloss: the going, the act of going

notes.en: the ल्युट् affix (→ अन) — names the action

notes.role: ल्युट् च → ल्युट् after a root for the action's name → गम् + अन → गमनम्

sequence.vyakhya: भावे ल्युट् — गमनम्। क्रियायाः नाम नपुंसकम्। घञापि भावः (यथा "यागः")।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Beyond participles, कृत् affixes also build action-NOUNS — "the going," "the doing." ल्युट् (→ अन, 3.3.115) gives गमनम् "going," दर्शनम् "seeing," a neuter अ-stem that declines like फल. The affix घञ् does the same with a different shape and grade (यज् → यागः "sacrifice," 3.3.18 भावे). So one root yields a whole family: गतः (gone), गच्छन् (going), गन्तुम् (to go), गत्वा (having gone), गमनम् (the going) — the कृदन्त system entire.

sequence.sentence: महाबलः नृपः प्रतिदिनम् देवगृहम् अगच्छत्। तत्र सः देवम् अपश्यत्, नमः च अकरोत्।
sequence.translation: The mighty king went to the temple every day. There he saw the god, and made obeisance.
sequence.teaches:
three compound types in one errand — महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि), प्रतिदिनम्
(अव्ययीभाव), देवगृहम् (तत्पुरुष).

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the one whose strength is great

notes.text: विग्रह: महत् बलं यस्य सः — "he whose strength is great"

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

notes.en: adverbial — प्रति heads it (distributive), and the whole is indeclinable

notes.text: विग्रह: दिनं दिनं प्रति — "day by day"

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: determinative — गृहम्, the second member, is the head; देवस्य गृहम्

notes.text: विग्रह: देवस्य गृहम् — "the house of the god"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (देवस्य) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: the thing made — नमः + कृ, "to make obeisance"

sequence.vyakhya: त्रयः समासाः एकस्मिन् वाक्ये — महाबलः, प्रतिदिनम्, देवगृहम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
One short errand carries three of the compound types. महाबलः is a बहुव्रीहि,
the one whose strength is great — the king, not the strength. प्रतिदिनम् is an
अव्ययीभाव, प्रति heading it in the distributive "day by day" and the whole
going indeclinable. And देवगृहम् is a तत्पुरुष — देवस्य गृहम्, the god's house,
the temple — its second member the head.

sequence.sentence: राजा सभाम् आगच्छति। जनाः राजानम् पश्यन्ति। गुरुः अपि तत्र। राजा गुरवे धनम् यच्छति, गुरुः च राज्ञे धर्मम् कथयति। गमनम् श्रेयः इति राजा वदति। ततः राजानौ अपि आगच्छतः।
sequence.translation: The king comes to the assembly. The people see the king. The teacher is there too. The king gives wealth to the teacher, and the teacher tells the king about dharma. "Going is better," says the king. Then the two kings also arrive.
sequence.teaches:
राजन् in four grades — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञे, राजानौ — with गुरुः / गुरवे
alongside. गमनम् closes as an action-noun.

notes.en: nominative — the bare पद loses its final न्, leaving राजा

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the final न् of राजन् drops → राजा

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the strong stem — the न् returns and the अ lengthens
indeclinable — the sentence needs no verb
dative — उ takes गुण, गुरु → गुरवे

notes.role: घेर्ङिति — गुण before the ङित् ending → गुरवे

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
the weak stem — राजन् loses its अ before a vowel ending, giving राज्ञ्
neuter nominative — the act itself, not the one who acts

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes the action-noun गमनम् from गम्

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
strong again, now in the dual — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञे, राजानौ

sequence.vyakhya: राजा राजानम् राज्ञे राजानौ — एकं नाम, त्रयः आदेशाः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
राजन् appears four times and looks different each time: राजा without its
न्, राजानम् and राजानौ with the न् back and the vowel long, राज्ञे with the
अ squeezed out. The word never changes its meaning. What changes is which
ending follows, and whether that ending belongs to the strong set.

sequence.translation: The king's son.
sequence.teaches: राजन् weak/oblique — before a vowel ending the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञः

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → the relational genitive → राज्ञः

notes.text: राजन् + अस् (gen.sg); this is a भ weak base before a vowel ending

notes.role: अल्लोपोऽनः → in a भ stem the अ of अन् drops → राज्ञ् + अस् → राज्ञः

sequence.vyakhya: भसंज्ञके अनो अकारलोपः। राजन् + अस् → राज्ञः। दुर्बले अङ्गे न तिष्ठति अकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The third face of राजन्: before a vowel-initial weak ending (the भ base), the अ of -अन् itself drops (6.4.134), giving राज्ञ्- — so the genitive is राज्ञः "of the king." Now the full pattern stands: राजा (bare, न-loss), राजानम् (strong, full + long), राज्ञः (weak, अ-loss). One stem, three shapes, each triggered by the ending's strength — the heart of consonant declension.

sequence.translation: The mind is pure.
sequence.teaches: अस्-stem neuter मनस् — प्रथमा = द्वितीया, final स् → visarga

notes.en: neuter (an अस्-stem; nom. = acc., like फल)

notes.text: मनस् bare पद; final स् → रु → visarga before pause

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः → word-final स् → रु → मनः
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — context for neuter forms (नुम् where due); here शुद्धम् stands nom.=acc.

sequence.vyakhya: अकारान्तवत् नपुंसके प्रथमा द्वितीया च समे। मनस् → मनः, सान्तस्य रुत्वम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Another consonant family: the अस्-stems, here neuter मनस् ("mind"). Like every neuter, its nominative equals its accusative (मनः = मनः). The final स् of the bare word becomes रु → visarga (8.2.66, the same tail that gave नरः), so मनस् surfaces as मनः. The strengthening (अस् → आस् before strong endings, by 6.4.14) appears in the oblique — मनांसि "minds" — the next cell to add.

sequence.translation: a great man (विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः)
sequence.teaches: कर्मधारय — a तत्पुरुष whose members share one case (adjective + noun)

notes.text: विग्रह: महान् पुरुषः — "a man who is great"

notes.en: a तत्पुरुष of adjective + noun, both in the same case

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः समानाधिकरणः कर्मधारयः — a तत्पुरुष whose members are co-referential (same case) is कर्मधारय
विशेषणं विशेष्येण — a qualifier (महत्) combines with the qualified (पुरुष)

sequence.vyakhya: समानाधिकरणः तत्पुरुषः कर्मधारयः। महान् च असौ पुरुषः च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A कर्मधारय is a तत्पुरुष where the two members refer to the SAME thing — adjective and noun, both nominative: महान् पुरुषः → महापुरुषः, "great man." Unlike राजपुरुषः (the king's man — two different things, genitive relation), here महत् simply describes पुरुष. (महत् → महा in the compound.)

sequence.translation: the three worlds (विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः)
sequence.teaches: द्विगु — a numeral-first तत्पुरुष, denoting an aggregate

notes.text: विग्रह: त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः — "the aggregate of three worlds"

notes.en: a numeral-first compound, naming a counted aggregate

notes.role: संख्यापूर्वो द्विगुः — a तत्पुरुष with a number (त्रि) as its first member is द्विगु

sequence.vyakhya: संख्यापूर्वः तत्पुरुषः द्विगुः। त्रयाणां लोकानां समाहारः त्रिलोकी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A द्विगु is a तत्पुरुष whose first member is a numeral: त्रि (three) + लोक (world) → त्रिलोकी, "the three worlds" taken as one set. It names a counted aggregate — द्वि-गु itself means "worth two cows." Same तत्पुरुष frame (second member heads), special first member: a number.

sequence.translation: The descendant of Daśaratha is "Dāśarathi" (= Rāma).
sequence.teaches: अपत्य — the patronymic; इञ् after an अ-stem, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" that the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → दशरथस्य (the analysis; the तद्धित condenses it)
मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अपत्यं

notes.en: the SENSE the affix carries — "descendant of"
a secondary derivative — noun made from a noun

notes.role: तस्यापत्यम् → in the sense "descendant of ___", a तद्धित affix
अत इञ् → after an अ-stem the affix is इञ् → दशरथ + इ → दाशरथि (आदिवृद्धि अ→आ)

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य अपत्यम् इति अर्थे इञ्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। दशरथ → दाशरथिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A तद्धित attaches to a *finished* word and makes a new one. The patronymic: "descendant of X" (4.1.92) becomes a single word by adding इञ् after an अ-stem (4.1.95), with vṛddhi of the first vowel — दशरथ → दाशरथिः "son of Daśaratha." The genitive phrase दशरथस्य अपत्यम् collapses into one derived noun. (Other bases take अण् → गार्ग्यः, यञ् → for गोत्र lines.)

sequence.translation: One born/found in Mathurā is "Māthura."
sequence.teaches: तत्र भवः — "born in / belonging to a place", with आदिवृद्धि

notes.en: locus — the सप्तमी base of the derivation

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → मथुरायाम् (the विग्रह "in Mathurā")
तत्र भवः → "being in (that place)" → an affix after the locative base → माथुरः (आदिवृद्धि)

sequence.vyakhya: तत्र भवः इति अर्थे अण्; मथुरा → माथुरः। देशकालादेः भवार्थः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "Born in / found in / belonging to a place" — तत्र भवः (4.3.53) — turns a locative phrase into one adjective: मथुरायां भवः → माथुरः "of Mathurā," with vṛddhi (मथुरा → माथुर). The same family gives "relating to X" (तस्येदम्, 4.3.120) and "good for X" (तस्मै हितम्, 5.1.5). These locative/genitive/dative taddhitas are how Sanskrit forms its everyday relational adjectives.

sequence.translation: He who has wealth is "wealthy" (dhanavān).
sequence.teaches: मतुप् — the possessive "having ___"

notes.en: "be" — the विग्रह "X is his / in him"

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् → मतुप् "it is his / in him" → धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्
उगिदचां सर्वनामस्थाने → the मतुप् (वत्) stem inserts नुम् before strong endings → धनवान्

sequence.vyakhya: तत् अस्य अस्ति इति मतुप् — मत्वर्थः। धन + मतुप् → धनवान् (बुद्धिमान् वत्)।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The possessive: "having X / in whom X is" — मतुप् (5.2.94). धन + मतुप् → धनवान् "wealthy," बुद्धि + मतुप् → बुद्धिमान् "wise" (the affix shows as -वत्/-मत्, declining राजन्-style with नुम्). You met गुणवान् and वीरवत्तमं in real text; this is the rule behind them — the workhorse that turns any noun into "the one who has it."

sequence.translation: This one is cleverer than that.
sequence.teaches: तरप् — the comparative ("more ___ than")

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अयं
पञ्चमी विभक्ते → the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → ततः
द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ → तरप् (तर)/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → पटु + तर → पटुतरः

sequence.vyakhya: द्वयोः विभजने तरप्; पञ्चमी विभक्ते। पटु → पटुतरः, अन्यस्मात्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Comparing TWO: तरप् → -तर (5.3.57), "more X (than the other)" — पटु → पटुतरः "cleverer." The thing surpassed stands in the ablative (पञ्चमी, 2.3.42): ततः पटुतरः "cleverer than that." The matching ईयस् (-ीयस्) is the irregular comparative (श्रेयस्, the श्रेयः you met). For surpassing ALL — the superlative — it is तमप्/इष्ठन् (5.3.55): पटुतमः "cleverest" (you saw रत्नधातमम्, वीरवत्तमम्).

sequence.translation: The state of being heavy/a-teacher is "gurutva" (heaviness / gravity).
sequence.teaches: त्व/तल् — the abstract noun ("-ness, the state of")

words.gloss: of the heavy one / of the teacher

notes.en: genitive — the base whose "-ness" is named (उ-stem गुरु → गुरोः)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → गुरोः

words.gloss: heaviness, gravity; the state of being a guru

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ → त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of ___" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य भावः इति त्व-तलौ। गुरुत्वम् (नपुंसकम्), गुरुता (स्त्री)। भाववाचकम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The abstract: "the state of being X" — त्व and तल् (5.1.119). गुरु → गुरुत्वम् "heaviness/gurutva" (neuter, with -त्व) or गुरुता "guru-hood" (feminine, with -ता). देव → देवत्वम्/देवता. This is Sanskrit's "-ness / -hood": take any noun or adjective, add त्व or ता, and you have named its quality as a thing. Patronymic, place-adjective, possessive, comparative, abstract — the तद्धित system's productive core.

sequence.translation: Among all the clever, this one is the cleverest.
sequence.teaches: तमप् — the superlative ("most ___ of all"); निर्धारण in सप्तमी

notes.role: यतश्च निर्धारणम् → the group one is singled out from → सप्तमी (or षष्ठी) → सर्वेषु

notes.en: the class — locative plural, parallel to सर्वेषु

notes.role: मोऽनुस्वारः — word-final म् becomes anusvāra before a consonant → अयं
अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ → तमप् (तम)/इष्ठन् for surpassing all → पटु + तम → पटुतमः

sequence.vyakhya: अतिशायने तमप्; निर्धारणे सप्तमी। सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The superlative completes the pair: तमप् → -तम (5.3.55), "most X of all" — पटु → पटुतमः "the cleverest." The group one is singled out FROM takes निर्धारण-सप्तमी (2.3.41): सर्वेषु पटुषु "among all the clever." So तर/तम are the degree-affixes — पटुतरः "cleverer (of two)," पटुतमः "cleverest (of all)" — closing the productive तद्धित set the reader needs.

sequence.translation: This belongs to Upagu — it is "Aupagava" (Upagu's).
sequence.teaches: तस्येदम् — "belonging to / coming from X"; अण् with आदिवृद्धि (उपगु → औपगव)

notes.en: genitive — the विग्रह "of ___" the affix replaces

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → उपगोः
तस्येदम् → in the sense "belonging to ___", the affix अण्
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि उ→औ → औपगव

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य इदम् इति अर्थे अण्; आदेर्वृद्धिः। उपगु → औपगवम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The "possession / belonging" affix: तस्येदम् "this is X's" (4.3.120) condenses into one word with अण्, plus आदिवृद्धि — vṛddhi of the first vowel (7.2.117). उपगोः इदम् "Upagu's" → औपगवम्. The same आदिवृद्धि you saw in the patronymic दाशरथिः (ex080) is the signature of this whole अण् family.

sequence.translation: A modification of gold is "golden" (made of gold).
sequence.teaches: तस्य विकारः — "made of / a modification of X"; अण् with आदिवृद्धि

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुवर्णस्य

notes.en: the sense — "a thing made of / changed from X"

notes.role: तस्य विकारः → in the sense "modification/product of ___", अण्
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि उ→औ → सौवर्ण

sequence.vyakhya: तस्य विकारः इति अर्थे अण्। सुवर्ण → सौवर्णम् "स्वर्णमयम्"।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "Made of X / a product of X": तस्य विकारः (4.3.134) → अण् with आदिवृद्धि. सुवर्णस्य विकारः "a modification of gold" → सौवर्णम् "golden, of gold." This is the material-adjective: the same shape names "made of wood" (दारु → दारवम्), "made of clay," and so on.

sequence.translation: A cloth dyed with ochre is a "kāṣāya" (ochre robe).
sequence.teaches: तेन रक्तं रागात् — "dyed with X"; अण् from the name of a dye, with आदिवृद्धि

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → कषायेण

notes.en: अर्थ — here the specialised "dyed-with" sense (तेन रक्तम्)

notes.role: तेन रक्तं रागात् → "dyed with (a dye)", अण् from the dye-name
तद्धितेष्वचामादेः → आदिवृद्धि अ→आ → काषाय

sequence.vyakhya: तेन रक्तम् इति रागवाचिनः अण्। कषाय → काषायम्। (मुनीनां वस्त्रम्।)
sequence.vyakhya_en: From the name of a dye, "dyed with X": तेन रक्तं रागात् (4.2.1) → अण् with आदिवृद्धि. कषायेण रक्तम् "dyed with ochre" → काषायम् — the ochre robe of ascetics. Notice the विग्रह uses the तृतीया (कषायेण, "by the dye"), the instrument; the affix swallows it into one adjective.

sequence.translation: That which is good for all is the "all-good."
sequence.teaches: तस्मै हितम् — "good for / suited to X"; the relational set (विग्रह in चतुर्थी)

notes.en: the one it is good FOR

notes.role: तस्मै हितम् → in the sense "good for ___", a तद्धित affix

words.gloss: good for all, the common good

notes.role: तस्मै हितम् → the affix condensing "good for ___"

sequence.vyakhya: तस्मै हितम् इति अर्थे प्रत्ययः; विग्रहे चतुर्थी। सर्वस्मै हितं सर्वहितम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A relational affix whose विग्रह uses the चतुर्थी: तस्मै हितम् "good FOR X" (5.1.5). सर्वस्मै हितम् "good for all" → सर्वहितम्. This sits beside तत्र भवः (place, 4.3.53, ex081) and तस्येदम् (possession, ex131): a family of affixes each replacing one case-relation — dative here, locative and genitive there.

sequence.translation: He comes from the village.
sequence.teaches: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — the adverb-affix तसिल् (-तस्) in the ablative sense ("from ___")

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् → in the पञ्चमी (ablative) sense, the affix तसिल् → -तस्

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — ग्राम + तस् = ग्रामतः ("from the village")
indeclinable (it does not take सुप् endings)
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: पञ्चम्यर्थे तसिल्; ग्राम + तस् = ग्रामतः अव्ययम्। ग्रामात् = ग्रामतः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Instead of the case-ending पञ्चमी (ग्रामात्), the same ablative sense can be carried by a तद्धित adverb: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् (5.3.7) adds -तस् → ग्रामतः "from the village," an indeclinable. So ग्रामात् आगच्छति and ग्रामतः आगच्छति say the same thing — the second with an अव्यय taddhita. This affix gives ततः, यतः, सर्वतः, and the like.

sequence.translation: He studies like a brahmin.
sequence.teaches: तेन तुल्यं…वतिः — the affix वति (-वत्), "like / in the manner of X"

words.gloss: like a brahmin, in a brahmin's manner

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → in the sense "like ___ (in action)", the affix वति

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — ब्राह्मण + वत् = ब्राह्मणवत् ("brahmin-like")

sequence.vyakhya: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेत् वतिः। ब्राह्मण + वत् = ब्राह्मणवत् "ब्राह्मणेन तुल्यम्"।
sequence.vyakhya_en: "Like X, in the manner of X (when comparing an action)": तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः (5.1.115) → the affix वति, -वत्. ब्राह्मणवत् अधीते "studies like a brahmin" = ब्राह्मणेन तुल्यम्. An indeclinable adverb of comparison — the same वत् gives मातृवत् "like a mother," राजवत् "like a king."

source.ref: Bhāgavata 10.9 — the दामबन्धन (binding) episode
source.curated: our graded prose telling the दामोदर binding; not the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: क्रुद्धा यशोदा रज्ज्वा कृष्णम् बध्नाति। किन्तु रज्जुः सर्वदा ह्रस्वा भवति। सा पुनः पुनः यतते, तथापि बालम् बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति। अन्ते कृष्णः स्वयम् एव मातुः प्रेम्णा बद्धः। तेन सः दामोदरः इति प्रसिद्धः।
sequence.translation: Angry Yaśodā binds Kṛṣṇa with a rope. But the rope is always too short. She tries again and again, yet cannot bind the boy. In the end Kṛṣṇa is bound only by his mother's love, of his own accord. By this he became famous as "Dāmodara" (bound-at-the-belly).
sequence.teaches: longest yet — past participles (क्रुद्धा, बद्धः), an infinitive (बन्धितुम्) with शक्, तृतीया of means (रज्ज्वा, प्रेम्णा), closing name-etymology

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of क्रुध्, feminine, agreeing with यशोदा

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → क्रुद्ध; fem. क्रुद्धा

notes.en: instrument — that with which she binds

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → रज्ज्वा (ū-stem fem. instr.)
इको यणचि → रज्जु + आ → रज्ज्वा

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — भू → भो → भव्
the thematic अ between root and ending
the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् → बन्धितुम् (with शक्नोति)
षष्ठी शेषे → मातुः

notes.en: means — that by which he is bound (न-stem प्रेमन् instr.)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → प्रेम्णा

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of बन्ध् — the predicate "is bound"

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → बद्ध; passive past participle as predicate

notes.en: possessive compound — दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) → "(he) at whose belly is the rope"

sequence.vyakhya: कथा दीर्घतरा। क्रुद्धा बद्धः इति निष्ठे, बन्धितुम् इति तुमुन्, रज्ज्वा प्रेम्णा इति करणे। अन्ते नामनिर्वचनम् — दाम उदरे यस्य सः दामोदरः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The longest reading yet, weaving together what you met as isolated cells: past participles as adjective and predicate (क्रुद्धा "angry," बद्धः "bound"), an infinitive with "can" (बन्धितुम् न शक्नोति "cannot bind"), and the instrumental of means twice (रज्ज्वा "with a rope," प्रेम्णा "by love"). It closes the way Sanskrit tales love to — a name-etymology: दाम (rope) + उदर (belly) makes the बहुव्रीहि दामोदर, "the one with a rope at his belly." The grammar is familiar; the story now carries it.

sequence.sentence: दाशरथिः माथुरम् नगरम् गच्छति। सः धनवान् बलवान् च। तस्य गुरुत्वम् सर्वे जनाः जानन्ति। काषायम् वस्त्रम् धारयति सः, ब्राह्मणवत् च अधीते। ग्रामतः आगताः जनाः तम् पश्यन्ति। अयम् पटुतरः, सर्वेषु पटुषु पटुतमः इति ते वदन्ति।
sequence.translation: The son of Daśaratha goes to the city of Mathurā. He is wealthy and strong. All people know his weightiness. He wears an ochre robe, and studies like a brahmin. People come from the village and see him. "This one is cleverer; among all the clever ones, the cleverest," they say.
sequence.teaches:
तद्धित words in use rather than in their विग्रह — दाशरथिः as a name,
माथुरम् qualifying a city. धनवान् declines; ब्राह्मणवत् does not.

notes.en: the इञ् patronymic suffix, अर्थ = अपत्य; इञ् with vṛddhi, दशरथ → दाशरथि

notes.role: अत इञ् — इञ् forms the patronymic from an अ-stem → दाशरथिः

notes.en: nominative — used here as a name, not as a derivation
the sense 'belonging to a place' — अण् with vṛddhi, मथुरा → माथुर

notes.role: तत्र भवः — the place-relational affix → माथुरम्

notes.en: गम् appears as गच्छ् + अ + ति

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — the possessive → धनवान्

notes.en: nominative — a वत्-stem in its strong form
the same affix on a second stem, बल + मतुप्
the abstract — "the state of being गुरु"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व makes the abstract noun → गुरुत्वम्

notes.en: present plural — ज्ञा takes श्ना, not शप्
the sense 'dyed with X' — अण् with vṛddhi, कषाय → काषाय

notes.role: तेन रक्तं रागात् — the dye-affix → काषायम्

notes.en: the sense 'in the manner of X' — the affix makes an indeclinable, not a noun

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः — the comparison-affix → ब्राह्मणवत्

notes.en: indeclinable — it takes no ending, unlike धनवान् above
the affix -तस् in the ablative sense — an adverb, not a case-form

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the sense of the पञ्चमी → ग्रामतः

notes.en: past participle, nominative plural agreeing with जनाः
दृश् appears as पश्य् + अ + न्ति

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — the comparative → पटुतरः

notes.en: the सप्तमी of selection — "of all, the most"
the superlative — the same stem पटु, one affix further

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — the superlative → पटुतमः

sequence.vyakhya: तद्धितान्तं पदम् — न विग्रहः। दाशरथिः नाम, न तु दशरथस्य अपत्यम् इति वाक्यम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Every तद्धित reading before this one is a विग्रह — दशरथस्य अपत्यं दाशरथिः,
the analysis and the word side by side. That shows how the word is made and
never shows it working. Here दाशरथिः is simply his name.

Watch धनवान् against ब्राह्मणवत्. Both are built with a वत्-shaped affix,
and they behave completely differently: धनवान् is a noun and declines,
ब्राह्मणवत् is an indeclinable and does not. The affix decides what kind of
word comes out, not just what it means.

sequence.translation: He who is lord of the world — he is "Being" itself.
sequence.teaches: क्विप् — the kṛt affix that vanishes entirely, leaving the bare root standing as a noun: भू → भूः

notes.text: क्विप् = a कृत् affix that wholly disappears (its क्, व्, प् are all इत्), leaving भू + सुप्

notes.role: क्विप् च — the affix क्विप् (zero) forms a kṛt-noun from the root → भू
अन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते — क्विप् is seen widely, beyond its named bases

notes.en: a kṛt noun with no visible suffix

sequence.vyakhya: क्विबन्तः प्रत्ययलोपे धातुरेव नाम। भू + क्विप् = भू, सुपि भूः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Most kṛt affixes add visible material (-त, -मान, -तुम्). क्विप् is the opposite: every one of its letters is an इत्-marker, so the WHOLE affix vanishes, and the bare root stands as a noun (3.2.76). भू "be" + क्विप् → भू, declined भूः "Being." This is how Sanskrit makes nouns like धी (thought, from ध्यै), स्तुत् (praiser), युज् (yoke-fellow) — roots used directly as words.

sequence.translation: He who gives wealth is a "wealth-giver."
sequence.teaches: क — the short kṛt: after an आ-ending root (with no preverb), क replaces the आ (दा → द)

notes.text: धन (object) + दा + क; the क affix shortens दा → द → धन-द-ः

notes.role: आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः — after an आ-final root without a preverb, the affix is क → -द
कर्मण्यण्… — an object compounded with a kṛt; here क (not अण्) by 3.2.3

sequence.vyakhya: आदन्तात् अनुपसर्गात् कः; आकारलोपः। धन + दा + क = धनदः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: After a root ending in आ, with no preverb, the agent-suffix is the short क — and it cuts the आ to nothing (3.2.3, आतोऽनुपसर्गे कः). दा "give" → -द; धनं ददाति "gives wealth" condenses to धनदः "wealth-giver." The same क gives गोदः "cow-giver," जलदः "water-giver = cloud," पयोदः. Contrast कुम्भकारः (ex with अण्): the root's final sound decides which kṛt applies.

sequence.translation: He goes along eating and eating (eating repeatedly).
sequence.teaches: णमुल् — the absolutive of repeated or intense action, reduplicated for "again and again"

notes.text: भुज् + णमुल् → भोजम्; doubled (आभीक्ष्ण्य) to mean "again and again"

notes.role: आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल् च — for repeated action, the absolutive णमुल् (-अम्), often doubled

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल्; द्विरुक्तिः। भुज् + णमुल् = भोजं भोजम् "पुनः पुनः भुक्त्वा"।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Beside क्त्वा "having Xed" (ex with गत्वा), णमुल् is a second absolutive — used for REPEATED or intense action and typically DOUBLED (3.4.22, आभीक्ष्ण्ये णमुल् च). भुज् "eat" → भोजं भोजम् "eating and eating, again and again." So स्मारं स्मारम् "remembering over and over," पायं पायम् "drinking repeatedly": an indeclinable that paints habitual or insistent action.

sequence.sentence: कर्ता, कर्तारम्, कर्त्रा, कर्त्रे, कर्तुः, कर्तरि।
sequence.translation: The agent-noun कर्तृ "doer" declined: nom, acc, instr, dat, gen/abl, loc (singular).
sequence.teaches: कर्तृ through its cases — the तृच् agent-noun is an ऋ-stem, and takes the same strong and weak grades as पितृ

notes.text: कृ + तृच् → कर्तृ "doer" (3.1.133); nom.sg कर्ता with vṛddhi, like पिता

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — the agent affixes ण्वुल् and तृच् → कर्तृ

notes.text: गुण-strengthened अर् in the strong cell → कर्तारम् (cf. पितरम्)

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — ऋ → गुण अर् in the strong cells → कर्तार्

notes.text: weak cell: ऋ stays → कर्त्र् + आ → कर्त्रा

sequence.vyakhya: तृजन्तम् ऋदन्तम्; पितृवत् नरबलदुर्बलभेदेन नमति। कर्ता — कर्तारम् — कर्त्रा …।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A तृच् agent-noun (कृ → कर्तृ "doer," 3.1.133) is not a fixed word — it DECLINES, exactly like the kinship ऋ-stem पितृ (ex043/044/141). Strong cells take गुण/vṛddhi (कर्ता nom, कर्तारम् acc), weak cells keep ऋ (कर्त्रा, कर्त्रे, कर्तुः, कर्तरि). So दातृ → दाता/दातारम्, नेतृ → नेता/नेतारम्: every agent-noun is an ऋ-stem paradigm. This closes the loop between कृदन्त (how the word is formed) and सुप् (how it then declines).

sequence.translation: He who presses the soma is a "soma-presser."
sequence.teaches: क्विप् in an upapada compound — the root (here सु "press") stands as the second member, suffix elided

notes.text: सोम (object) + सु + क्विप्; the affix vanishes, leaving सु → सुत् (with त्-augment in the cluster)

notes.role: सत्सूद्विषद्…उपसर्गेऽपि क्विप् — सू and the listed roots take क्विप् even in compounds → -सुत्

sequence.vyakhya: क्विबन्तः उपपदे; प्रत्ययलोपात् धातुः अन्त्यपदम्। सोमं सुनोति = सोमसुत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: क्विप् (the zero affix, ex161) is especially common in COMPOUNDS, where the root becomes the second member and the suffix vanishes (3.2.61). सोमं सुनोति "presses the soma" → सोमसुत् "soma-presser." The same gives अग्निचित् "fire-piler" (चि), धृतव्रत "vow-holder" type, ऋत्विज् "season-sacrificer" (यज्). Such root-final compounds fill the Vedic vocabulary — now you can parse them: object + bare root + क्विप्.

sequence.translation: The brahmin gives food; he is a giver.
sequence.teaches: तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता "giver" from दा.

notes.en: the root दा, as finite verb

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ → तृच् on दा → दातृ → दाता (agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: दा-धातोः तृच्प्रत्यये दातृशब्दः सिध्यति, प्रथमैकवचने दाता इति रूपम्। यो ददाति स दाता।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.1.133 (ण्वुल्तृचौ) every root may take तृच् (the affix तृ) to name its agent. On दा "give" this yields the stem दातृ, whose nominative singular is दाता "giver". The agent-noun simply names the one who performs the verb's action — here, the one who gives.

sequence.translation: Devadatta is a habitual doer.
sequence.teaches: तृन् forms a habitual-agent noun कर्तृ → कर्ता from कृ.

notes.en: primary derivative naming the habitual agent

notes.role: तृन् on कृ → कर्तृ → कर्ता (habitual agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: तृन्प्रत्यये कृ-धातोः कर्तृशब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने कर्ता। यः शीलेन करोति स कर्ता उच्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.135 (तृन्) the affix तृन् (तृ) comes after a root to name one who does the action habitually or by disposition (शील). On कृ "do" it gives the stem कर्तृ, nominative singular कर्ता. Unlike a plain agent, this names a characteristic doer — one whose nature it is to act.

sequence.translation: The boy habitually goes to the village.
sequence.teaches: णिनि with an उपपद forms the habit-agent गामिन् → गामी from गम्.

notes.en: the word-in-composition (द्वितीया) standing with the affix
primary derivative naming the habitual agent (ताच्छील्य)

notes.role: णिनि on गम् with उपपद ग्रामम् → गामिन् → गामी (habit agent-noun)

sequence.vyakhya: ताच्छील्ये गम्यमाने उपपदे सति गम्-धातोः णिनिप्रत्यये गामिन्शब्दः, प्रथमैकवचने गामी। यः शीलेन ग्रामं गच्छति स ग्रामं गामी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.2.78 (सुप्यजातौ णिनिस्ताच्छील्ये) the affix णिनि (इन्) attaches to a root when habit (ताच्छील्य) is meant and an उपपद — a noun in composition — stands with it. With उपपद ग्रामम् and root गम् "go", this yields the stem गामिन्, nominative singular गामी. The whole phrase ग्रामं गामी names one who customarily goes to the village.

sequence.translation: The cooking (the act of cooking) is pleasing.
sequence.teaches: घञ् makes a भाव action-noun from a root; पच् → पाकः.

notes.en: the घञ् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: भावे घञ् → पच् → पाकः (action-noun in -अ)

notes.en: the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: धातोः भावे घञ् प्रत्ययः। पच् इत्यस्मात् पाकः इति कृदन्तं नाम जायते। तत् प्रथमायां कर्तृ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.18 the affix घञ् is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव). From पच् "to cook" we get पाकः, "the act of cooking", a कृदन्त noun. Here it stands in the nominative as the subject of रोचते.

sequence.translation: He wishes for victory.
sequence.teaches: अच् makes a भाव action-noun from an इ/ई-final root; जि → जयः.

notes.en: the अच् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: एरच् → जि → जयः (action-noun in -अ)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: इवर्णान्तात् धातोः भावे अच् प्रत्ययः। जि इत्यस्मात् जयः इति कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.56 (एरच्) the affix अच् is added to a root ending in इ/ई to name the action (भाव). From जि "to conquer" we get जयः, "victory". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of इच्छति.

sequence.translation: He begins the going (the departure).
sequence.teaches: ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun in -अन; गम् → गमनम्.

notes.en: the ल्युट् action-noun suffix — names the bare act (भाव)

notes.role: ल्युट् च → गम् → गमनम् (neuter action-noun in -अन)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: धातोः भावे ल्युट् प्रत्ययः, तस्य अन इति आदेशः। गम् इत्यस्मात् गमनम् इति नपुंसकं कृदन्तम्। तत् द्वितीयायां कर्म।
sequence.vyakhya_en: By 3.3.115 the affix ल्युट् (realized as -अन) is added to a root to name the bare action (भाव), giving a neuter noun. From गम् "to go" we get गमनम्, "going". Here it stands in the accusative as the object of आरभते.

sequence.sentence: ग्रामे बहवः बालाः सन्ति। रामः पटुः, कृष्णः तु रामात् पटुतरः। सर्वेषु बालेषु दामोदरः पटुतमः। सः धनवान् अपि, किन्तु धनस्य गुरुत्वम् न मन्यते।
sequence.translation: In the village are many boys. Rāma is clever, but Kṛṣṇa is cleverer than Rāma. Among all the boys Dāmodara is the cleverest. He is wealthy too, yet does not regard the weight of wealth.
sequence.teaches:
the four degree-and-quality तद्धितs together: रामात् पटुतरः (तरप्, with पञ्चमी),
सर्वेषु बालेषु पटुतमः (तमप्, निर्धारण-सप्तमी), धनवान् (मतुप्), and गुरुत्वम् (त्व).

notes.role: पञ्चमी विभक्ते — the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → रामात्

notes.en: the तरप् comparative suffix — "more" of two
degree of comparison — the comparative sense

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — तरप्/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → पटु + तर → पटुतरः
यतश्च निर्धारणम् — the group one is singled out from → सप्तमी → सर्वेषु

notes.en: the class — locative plural, parallel to सर्वेषु
the तमप् superlative suffix — "most" of all
degree of comparison — the superlative sense

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — तमप्/इष्ठन् for surpassing all → पटु + तम → पटुतमः

notes.en: the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having wealth" (shows as -वत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — "it is his / in him" → धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state/weight of"
भाव — the state or quality named as a thing

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

sequence.vyakhya: चत्वारः तद्धिताः एकत्र — तरप्, तमप्, मतुप्, त्व — मानस्य च द्वे विभक्ती।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The degree affixes stand side by side here. रामात् पटुतरः is the comparative
तरप् (5.3.57), and the one surpassed takes पञ्चमी — रामात्, "than Rāma." सर्वेषु
बालेषु पटुतमः is the superlative तमप् (5.3.55), and the group singled out from
takes निर्धारण-सप्तमी — "among all the boys." धनवान् is the possessive मतुप्
(5.2.94), "having wealth," and गुरुत्वम् is the abstract त्व (5.1.119), the
weight of a thing named as a thing.

source.ref: Hit_0.6 (pāda a)
source.curated: first quarter (पाद a) of the verse, taken whole; rest of the śloka omitted

sequence.translation: Knowledge gives humility.
sequence.teaches: a line of Hitopadeśa, read whole — an आ-stem feminine agent, a कर्मन् in the द्वितीया, a present verb

notes.text: an आ-stem feminine (formed with टाप्)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् — feminines like विद्या take टाप् (the आ-ending); विद्या stands in प्रथमा
वर्तमाने लट् → present tense
कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → विनय is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → विनयम्

sequence.vyakhya: विद्या कर्त्री, विनयः कर्म, ददाति क्रिया — सर्वं पूर्वोक्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Your first real sentence, from the Hitopadeśa — and you can already read it. विद्या (knowledge) is the कर्तृ in प्रथमा; विनयम् (humility) is the कर्मन् in द्वितीया; ददाति (gives) is a present-tense verb. Every piece is grammar you have met on toy sentences; here it stands in real Sanskrit, unchanged.

sequence.sentence: धनस्य दाता नरः श्रेष्ठः। सः सदा दानम् करोति, धर्मस्य च कर्ता।
sequence.translation: The giver of wealth is the best man. He always performs charity, and is a doer of dharma.
sequence.teaches:
the agent-noun तृच् with its object in षष्ठी — धनस्य दाता, धर्मस्य कर्ता (the
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति genitive) — and the action-noun दानम् (ल्युट्).

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → धनस्य

notes.en: the तृच् agent-suffix — "the one who gives"

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun → दा + तृ → दातृ; nom.sg दाता

notes.en: the ल्युट् action-suffix (shows as -अन) — दा + ल्युट् → दानम्, "the giving"

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् in the भाव/action sense → दा + ल्युट् → दानम्
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → धर्मस्य

notes.en: the तृच् agent-suffix — "the one who does"

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun → कृ + तृ → कर्तृ; nom.sg कर्ता

sequence.vyakhya: कृति कर्तृकर्मणोः षष्ठी — धनस्य दाता, धर्मस्य कर्ता। तृच् कर्तरि।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The agent-noun तृच् turns a root into "the one who does it" — दा → दाता, कृ →
कर्ता — and it declines (कर्ता, कर्तारम्, कर्त्रा…). What it acts on stands in
the genitive, not the accusative: धनस्य दाता "the giver of wealth," धर्मस्य
कर्ता "the doer of dharma" (कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति, 2.3.65). Beside them दानम् is the
action-noun in ल्युट् — the giving itself, named as a thing.

sequence.sentence: बुद्धिमान् नरः बलवतः श्रेष्ठतरः। जनाः ततः बुद्धेः गुरुत्वम् जानन्ति।
sequence.translation: A wise man is better than a strong one. From that, people know the weight of intelligence.
sequence.teaches:
the तद्धितs in a maxim: बुद्धिमान् and बलवतः (मतुप्), बलवतः श्रेष्ठतरः (तरप्,
with पञ्चमी), ततः (तसिल्), गुरुत्वम् (त्व).

notes.en: the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having intelligence" (shows as -मत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — "it is his / in him" → बुद्धि + मतुप् → बुद्धिमत् → बुद्धिमान्

notes.en: possessive derivative — बल + मतुप् → बलवत् ("having strength")

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — बल + मतुप् → बलवत् ("strong")
पञ्चमी विभक्ते — the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → बलवतः

notes.en: the तरप् comparative suffix — "more" of two
degree of comparison — the comparative sense

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — तरप्/ईयसुन् for comparison of two → श्रेष्ठ + तर → श्रेष्ठतरः
पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — in the पञ्चमी (ablative) sense, the affix तसिल् → -तस् → ततः

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — तद् + तस् = ततः
indeclinable (it does not take सुप् endings)
the त्व abstract suffix — "the state/weight of"
भाव — the state or quality named as a thing

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व (and तल् → ता) for "the state of" → गुरु + त्व → गुरुत्वम्

sequence.vyakhya: तद्धिताः सुभाषिते — मतुप्, तरप्, तसिल्, त्व — बुद्धेः प्रशंसा।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A maxim carries the same तद्धितs the intros gave singly. बुद्धिमान् and बलवत्
are the possessive मतुप् (5.2.94), "having intelligence," "having strength." The
stronger is surpassed: बलवतः श्रेष्ठतरः is the comparative तरप् (5.3.57) with the
surpassed term in पञ्चमी. ततः is the तसिल् ablative adverb (5.3.7), "from that,"
and गुरुत्वम् the abstract त्व (5.1.119) — the weight of a quality named as a
thing.

sequence.sentence: यः अन्नम् ददाति सः दाता। दानम् तस्य धर्मः। नित्यम् कर्ता सः नरः, न तु भोक्ता। गमनम् आरभते, ग्रामम् गामी भवति। तस्य पाकः अपि रोचते। कर्तारम् तम् जनाः पश्यन्ति।
sequence.translation: He who gives food is a giver. Giving is his dharma. That man is a constant doer, not an enjoyer. He begins the going, becomes a goer to the village. His cooking, too, is pleasing. People see him as the doer.
sequence.teaches:
agent-nouns beside action-nouns, so the affix makes the difference: दाता /
दानम्, कर्ता / गमनम्. Then कर्ता declines into कर्तारम्.

notes.en: nominative — the relative, answered by सः
agent-noun from दा — the one who does the action

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun दातृ → दाता
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → दानम्

notes.en: action-noun suffix — the ACT (भाव), not the actor; set directly against दाता
the HABITUAL agent — तृन्, not तृच्; the habit is what नित्यम् marks
another agent-noun, from भुज् — same affix, different root
action-noun in -अन from गम् — the going, not the goer

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes a neuter भाव action-noun → गमनम्

notes.en: the उपपद — the goal, standing before the agent-noun
habit-agent with an उपपद — ग्रामं गामी "one who goes to the village"
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — भू → भो → भव्
the thematic अ between root and ending
action-noun from पच् with vṛddhi — पच् → पाकः
the root vowel strengthens before शप् — रुच् → रोच्
the thematic अ between root and ending
present — the one pleased would stand in the चतुर्थी
कर्ता DECLINES — the agent-noun is an ऋ-stem, strong अर् in the acc.
the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: दाता ददाति, दानम् दीयते। कर्ता करोति, करणम् क्रियते। कर्तुः कर्म भिन्नम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
दाता and दानम् come from the same root by different affixes, and the affix
is the whole difference: one names the giver, the other the giving. So with
कर्ता and गमनम्, भोक्ता and पाकः. A कृत् affix does not add a meaning to the
root so much as decide WHICH PART of the action the new word names — the
doer, the deed, or the instrument.

Then कर्ता becomes कर्तारम्. The agent-noun is not a frozen label; it is an
ऋ-stem noun and declines like पितृ. Both facts are usually met apart from
each other; here they arrive in one paragraph.

sequence.sentence: राजपुरुषः धर्मस्य रक्षिता। ततः जनाः तम् पूजयन्ति।
sequence.translation: The king's man is a protector of dharma. Therefore the people honor him.
sequence.teaches:
three at once — राजपुरुषः (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष), रक्षिता (the तृच् agent-noun, with
its object धर्मस्य in षष्ठी), and ततः (the तसिल् adverb).

notes.en: determinative — राज्ञः पुरुषः; पुरुषः is the head

notes.text: विग्रह: राज्ञः पुरुषः — "the king's man"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose last member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (राज्ञः) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → धर्मस्य

notes.en: the तृच् agent-suffix — "the one who protects"

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun → रक्ष् + तृ → रक्षितृ; nom.sg रक्षिता

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — तद् + तस् = ततः
the तसिल् suffix (-तस्), the ablative sense

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → तद् + तस् → ततः

sequence.vyakhya: राजपुरुषः धर्मस्य रक्षिता; ततः सः पूज्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
One line, three formations. राजपुरुषः is a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष — राज्ञः पुरुषः, "the
king's man" (2.2.8). रक्षिता is the agent-noun in तृच् (3.1.133), "protector,"
and what it protects, धर्मस्य, stands in the षष्ठी that a कृत्-noun governs
(2.3.65). And ततः is the तसिल् adverb (5.3.7), "from that, therefore" — the
people's honour follows.

sequence.sentence: धर्मस्य रक्षणम् नृपस्य कर्तव्यम्। तेन जनाः सुखम् लभन्ते।
sequence.translation: The protection of dharma is the king's duty. By that, people obtain happiness.
sequence.teaches:
the कृत्-governed षष्ठी twice — धर्मस्य, the object of the action-noun रक्षणम्
(ल्युट्), and नृपस्य, the agent of the gerundive कर्तव्यम्.

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → धर्मस्य

notes.en: the ल्युट् action-suffix (shows as -अन) — रक्ष् + ल्युट् → रक्षणम्

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् in the भाव/action sense → रक्ष् + ल्युट् → रक्षणम्
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — agent of a कृत् takes षष्ठी → नृपस्य

notes.en: the तव्य gerundive suffix — "ought to be done"

sequence.vyakhya: धर्मस्य रक्षणम् नृपस्य कर्तव्यम्; तेन जनाः सुखम् लभन्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Two कृदन्त forms, and the षष्ठी each governs. रक्षणम् is the action-noun in
ल्युट् — "the protecting" — and what is protected, धर्मस्य, stands in the षष्ठी
a कृत्-noun takes (2.3.65). कर्तव्यम् is the gerundive "to be done," and its
doer, नृपस्य, stands in the same षष्ठी. From that duty done, जनाः सुखम्
लभन्ते — people obtain happiness.

sequence.sentence: धनवान् जनः बहूनि मित्राणि लभते। किन्तु गुणस्य महत्त्वम् धनतः श्रेष्ठतरम्। यतः गुणवत्ता सर्वैः पूज्यते।
sequence.translation: A wealthy man gains many friends. But the greatness of virtue is greater than wealth — because virtuousness is honored by all.
sequence.teaches:
the तद्धित degrees and abstracts together: धनवान् (मतुप्), महत्त्वम् / गुणवत्ता
(त्व and तल्), धनतः / यतः (तसिल्), श्रेष्ठतरम् (तरप्, with the तसिल् standard).

notes.en: the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having wealth" (shows as -वत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — धन + मतुप् → धनवत् → धनवान्

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being महत् (great)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → महत् + त्व → महत्त्वम्

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — धन + तस् = धनतः ("from/than wealth")
the तसिल् suffix (-तस्), the ablative sense

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → धन + तस् → धनतः

notes.en: degree of comparison — the comparative sense

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — तरप् for comparison of two → श्रेष्ठ + तर → श्रेष्ठतर

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — यद् + तस् = यतः ("from which, because")

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → यद् + तस् → यतः

notes.en: the तल् abstract suffix (→ -ता, feminine) — "the state of being गुणवत् (virtuous)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — तल् (→ ता) for "the state of" → गुणवत् + तल् → गुणवत्ता

notes.en: passive — गुणवत्ता is honored, सर्वैः the agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive पूज्यते

sequence.vyakhya: तद्धिताः सुभाषिते — मतुप्, त्व-तल्, तसिल्, तरप् — गुणवत्तायाः प्रशंसा।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A maxim gathers the तद्धितs. धनवान् is the possessive मतुप् (5.2.94). Two
abstracts name qualities as things: महत्त्वम्, the त्व of महत् "greatness," and
गुणवत्ता, the तल् (→ता) of गुणवत् "virtuousness" (5.1.119). श्रेष्ठतरम् is the
comparative तरप् (5.3.57), and its standard धनतः is the तसिल् adverb (5.3.7),
"than wealth" — as is यतः, "because." What is virtuous सर्वैः पूज्यते, is
honored by all.

sequence.translation: ā, ai, au — these bear the name "vṛddhi."
sequence.teaches: the संज्ञा वृद्धि — Pāṇini's name for the strongest vowel grade (आ ऐ औ); the term every "vṛddhi" rule invokes

notes.en: a technical term DEFINED here, used everywhere after

notes.role: वृद्धिरादैच् — आत् (आ) and ऐच् (ऐ, औ) are named वृद्धि

words.gloss: ā and the ऐच् pair (ऐ, औ)

notes.text: आत् = आ; ऐच् = the प्रत्याहार for ऐ, औ — together the वृद्धि vowels

sequence.vyakhya: आ ऐ औ इति वृद्धिसंज्ञकाः। एषा संज्ञा "आदिवृद्धिः" "वृद्धिरेचि" इत्यादिषु प्रयुज्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Before any rule can SAY "take vṛddhi," the term must be DEFINED — and 1.1.1, the very first sūtra of the Aṣṭādhyāyī, does it: वृद्धिः = आ, ऐ, औ, the strongest vowel grade. You have already SEEN वृद्धि act — दशरथ → दाशरथिः (आदिवृद्धि, ex080), तव + एव → तवैव (ex with वृद्धि-sandhi). Now you know its name. This is metalanguage: a संज्ञा is a label the grammar pins on a set of sounds so later rules can refer to them in one word.

sequence.translation: a, e, o — these bear the name "guṇa."
sequence.teaches: the संज्ञा गुण — the middle vowel grade (अ ए ओ); the term behind every गुण operation (अग्नये, नयति)

notes.role: अदेङ् गुणः — अत् (अ) and एङ् (ए, ओ) are named गुण

words.gloss: the इक् vowels (इ उ ऋ ऌ) — what guṇa/vṛddhi apply TO

notes.text: इको गुणवृद्धी (1.1.3): गुण/वृद्धि, when ordered without specifics, fall on the इक् vowels

notes.role: इको गुणवृद्धी — गुण and वृद्धि operate on इक् (इ उ ऋ ऌ)

sequence.vyakhya: अ ए ओ इति गुणसंज्ञकाः; इको गुणवृद्धी इति इकां गुणवृद्धी भवतः। नी → ने (नयति), अग्नि → अग्नये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: गुण, the MIDDLE grade, is named in 1.1.2: अ, ए, ओ. And 1.1.3 (इको गुणवृद्धी) says where it lands — on the इक् vowels (इ, उ, ऋ, ऌ): इ→ए, उ→ओ, ऋ→अर्. You have watched this everywhere — अग्नि → अग्नये (इ→ए, ex029), गुरु → गुरवे (उ→ओ, ex048), पितृ → पितरम् (ऋ→अर्, ex044). गुण and वृद्धि are the two strengthenings; इक् is what they strengthen. Three sūtras (1.1.1–3) underwrite half the sandhi and declension you have done.

sequence.translation: Sounds made at the same place with the same effort are "savarṇa" (homorganic).
sequence.teaches: the संज्ञा सवर्ण — same-place-and-effort sounds; the term behind सवर्णदीर्घ (अ+अ→आ)

notes.role: तुल्यास्यप्रयत्नं सवर्णम् — same आस्य (place) + प्रयत्न (effort) → सवर्ण

notes.text: आस्य = the mouth-position (कण्ठ, तालु…); प्रयत्न = the manner/effort

sequence.vyakhya: समानस्थानप्रयत्नौ वर्णौ सवर्णौ। अ इ-वर्गादीनां स्वस्ववर्गे सावर्ण्यम्। अतः अ + अ → आ (सवर्णदीर्घः)।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Why does अ + अ fuse to आ but अ + इ to ए? Because the first pair is सवर्ण — "homorganic," made at the same place with the same effort (1.1.9) — and the second is not. This संज्ञा is the hinge of सवर्णदीर्घ (दधि + इन्द्रः → दधीन्द्रः, ex with 6.1.101): two सवर्ण vowels lengthen into one. The term sorts every sound into क-class, च-class, and so on — the grid behind both sandhi and the सवर्ण-exclusions in declension.

sequence.sentence: उपदेशे हल् अन्त्यम् इत्, तस्य लोपः।
sequence.translation: A consonant at the end of an affix-citation is an "it"-marker — and it drops.
sequence.teaches: the इत् mechanism — affixes carry silent marker-letters that trigger rules, then vanish (क्विप्, तृच्, ण्वुल् are all named by their इत्s)

notes.role: हलन्त्यम् — a final consonant in an उपदेश (citation form) is इत्
उपदेशेऽजनुनासिक इत् — a nasalised vowel in citation is also इत्
तस्य लोपः — that इत् is then dropped, leaving only its effect

sequence.vyakhya: उपदेशे अन्त्यो हल् इत्संज्ञकः, स च लुप्यते; कार्यं तु करोति। यथा तृच् → तृ (च् इत्); क्विप् → शून्यम् (सर्वे इतः)।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Affixes are cited with extra letters that never appear in the final word — they are इत्, silent markers (1.3.3 for a final consonant, 1.3.2 for a nasal vowel) that DROP by तस्य लोपः (1.3.9), having done their job of triggering rules. तृच् is really just तृ — the च् is an इत् (it conditions accent/operations). क्विप् is ALL इत् — every letter vanishes, which is why it leaves the bare root (ex161, भूः). Decoding इत्-markers is how you read Pāṇini's affix-names: शतृ = अत्, ल्युट् = अन, घञ् = अ.

sequence.translation: A genitive (in a rule) means "in the place of"; and the substitute is the one nearest (to the original).
sequence.teaches: the two परिभाषाs that drive every substitution (आदेश) — what the षष्ठी means in a rule, and how to pick the replacement

words.gloss: "in-the-place-of" — how a rule's genitive is read

notes.role: षष्ठी स्थानेयोगा — a षष्ठी in a sūtra means "in the place of X" (X is replaced)
स्थानेऽन्तरतमः — among possible substitutes, the one closest to the original is chosen

sequence.vyakhya: सूत्रस्थषष्ठी स्थानिनं सूचयति (तस्य स्थाने आदेशः); बहुषु आदेशेषु अन्तरतमः ग्राह्यः। एताभ्यां सर्वः आदेशविधिः प्रवर्तते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: These two are not about Sanskrit words — they are about reading the GRAMMAR. 1.1.49: when a rule puts a word in the genitive (इकः, अचः…), it means "IN THE PLACE OF that" — a substitution. 1.1.50: when several substitutes are possible, take the अन्तरतम, the one nearest in place/effort to the original. Together they govern every आदेश you have met — why ऋ becomes अर् (the nearest गुण) and not something else, why इ + vowel goes to य् (the nearest semivowel, यण्). The परिभाषाs are the operating system under the rules.

sequence.translation: A form ending in a सुप् (noun-ending) or तिङ् (verb-ending) is a "pada" (word).
sequence.teaches: the संज्ञा पद — what counts as a finished word, which decides where पद-level sandhi and the final-consonant rules apply

notes.role: सुप्तिङन्तं पदम् — what ends in सुप् or तिङ् is a पद

words.gloss: ending in a सुप् or a तिङ्

notes.text: सुप् = the 21 noun-endings (4.1.2); तिङ् = the 18 verb-endings (3.4.78)

notes.en: "that which has सुप्/तिङ् at its end"

sequence.vyakhya: यत् सुबन्तं तिङन्तं वा तत् पदम्। पदान्ते एव जश्त्वादीनि, पदयोः सन्धिः च प्रवर्तते। नरः, गच्छति — पदे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Many rules say "at the end of a पद" or "between पदs" — so the term must be fixed: a पद is anything ending in a noun-ending (सुप्) or a verb-ending (तिङ्), by 1.4.14. नरः (सुबन्त) and गच्छति (तिङन्त) are both पदs; a bare stem नर or root गम् is not. This संज्ञा gates the whole final-tail of the grammar — जश्त्व (वाक्→वाग्), न-lopa (राजन्→राजा), म्→anusvāra all fire at पद-end, and external sandhi happens between पदs. The word-boundary is itself a defined object.

sequence.sentence: पूतना राक्षसी गोकुलं आगत्य शिशुरूपेण तिष्ठति। सा कृष्णं स्तनयित्वा विषेण हन्तुम् इच्छति। किन्तु कृष्णेन सः स्तनः पीतः, विषं च पीतम्। एवम् पूतना कृष्णेन हता।
sequence.translation: The demoness Pūtanā comes to Gokula and stands there in the form of a child (i.e. a woman). She wishes to kill Kṛṣṇa by nursing him with poison. But by Kṛṣṇa the breast was suckled, and the poison too was drunk. Thus Pūtanā was slain by Kṛṣṇa.
sequence.teaches: passive construction (कर्मणि क्त — पीतः, हता, with instrumental of agent); gerund आगत्य (prior action); accusative object (कृष्णम्, विषम्)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → गोकुलम्

notes.en: gerund (क्त्वा after prefix → ल्यप्) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् (prefix + root → आगत्य)

कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → विषेण

भावकर्मणोः — passive ल-affixes become आत्मनेपद; क्त signals the same कर्मणि sense

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगः — इह कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायाम्। कृष्णेन पूतना हता इति न कर्तरि, कर्मणि। दोषाः — आगत्य स्तनयित्वा इति पूर्वकालकृदन्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The grammar turn: for the first time the story is told in the **passive** (कर्मणि). In active voice Kṛṣṇa is the subject (कर्तृ) and takes the nominative; in passive he becomes the agent (still the doer, but now marked by तृतीया — instrumental — while the object rises to nominative). The past-passive participle क्त (निष्ठा, 3.2.102) carries this sense: पीतः (was drunk, masc.), पीतम् (neuter), हता (fem.). Two gerunds (क्त्वा / ल्यप्) chain the prior actions: Pūtanā "comes, then nurses, then wishes to kill" — each gerund hands off to the next.

sequence.translation: From humility one attains worthiness.
sequence.teaches: the next quarter of the same verse — विनयात् is अपादान, the पञ्चमी of "from"

notes.en: source — that from which one proceeds

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the starting point (humility, whence worthiness comes) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → विनयात् (→ विनयाद् before the voiced य, by जश्त्व)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म → पात्रता is the कर्मन्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → पात्रताम्

sequence.vyakhya: विनयात् इति अपादानम्, पात्रताम् इति कर्म। एकस्माद् गुणाद् अन्यः फलति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The verse continues: from humility (विनयाद्, अपादान/पञ्चमी) one attains worthiness (पात्रताम्, कर्मन्/द्वितीया). Note विनयात् → विनयाद् — the final त् softens to द् before the voiced य (जश्त्व, the consonant-sandhi you met). Real text, real sandhi, all grammar you hold. The chain so far: knowledge → humility → worthiness.

sequence.sentence: गुणवान् शिष्यः गुरुणा पूज्यते। सः अन्येभ्यः श्रेष्ठतरः।
sequence.translation: A virtuous pupil is honored by his teacher. He is better than the others.
sequence.teaches:
the possessive मतुप्, the comparative तरप्, and the passive together —
गुणवान् (मतुप्), श्रेष्ठतरः (तरप्, its standard अन्येभ्यः in पञ्चमी), पूज्यते (passive).

notes.en: the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having virtue" (shows as -वत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — गुण + मतुप् → गुणवत् → गुणवान्

notes.en: the one honored — subject of the passive verb
passive — शिष्यः is honored, गुरुणा the agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive पूज्यते
पञ्चमी विभक्ते — the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → अन्येभ्यः

notes.en: the तरप् comparative suffix — "more/better" of two
degree of comparison — the comparative sense

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — तरप् for comparison → श्रेष्ठ + तर → श्रेष्ठतरः

sequence.vyakhya: गुणवान् शिष्यः गुरुणा पूज्यते; सः अन्येभ्यः श्रेष्ठतरः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Three तद्धित-and-voice facts in one line. गुणवान् is the possessive मतुप्
(5.2.94), "having virtue." पूज्यते is the passive (कर्मणि, 3.4.69): the pupil
is the one honored, गुरुणा — the teacher — the agent in तृतीया. And श्रेष्ठतरः
is the comparative तरप् (5.3.57), with the ones surpassed, अन्येभ्यः, in the
पञ्चमी of comparison.

sequence.sentence: गुरुः धर्मशास्त्रस्य ज्ञाता। ततः शिष्याः तम् सेवन्ते।
sequence.translation: The teacher is a knower of the treatise on dharma. Therefore the pupils serve him.
sequence.teaches:
the same three in a different scene — धर्मशास्त्रस्य (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष, and the
कृत्-governed षष्ठी), ज्ञाता (the तृच् agent-noun), ततः (the तसिल् adverb).

notes.en: determinative — धर्मस्य शास्त्रम्, "the treatise of dharma"; शास्त्रम् is the head

notes.role: षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (धर्मस्य) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → धर्मशास्त्रस्य

notes.en: the तृच् agent-suffix — "the one who knows"

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun → ज्ञा + तृ → ज्ञातृ; nom.sg ज्ञाता

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — तद् + तस् = ततः
the तसिल् suffix (-तस्), the ablative sense

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → तद् + तस् → ततः

sequence.vyakhya: गुरुः धर्मशास्त्रस्य ज्ञाता; ततः शिष्याः तम् सेवन्ते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The trio again, now among students. धर्मशास्त्रस्य is a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष —
धर्मस्य शास्त्रम् (2.2.8) — and it also stands in the षष्ठी a कृत्-noun governs
(2.3.65), as the object of ज्ञाता, the तृच् agent-noun "knower" (3.1.133). ततः
is the तसिल् adverb (5.3.7): from his knowing follows their service.

sequence.translation: From worthiness one obtains wealth.
sequence.teaches: third link of the same chain — the अपादान→कर्मन् pattern is now a rhythm

notes.role: ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् — the source (worthiness) is अपादान
अपादाने पञ्चमी → पात्रत्वात् (→ पात्रत्वाद् before the voiced ध, जश्त्व)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → धनम्

sequence.vyakhya: पात्रत्वाद् इति अपादानम्, धनम् इति कर्म — स एव विधिः।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same shape a third time: from worthiness (पात्रत्वाद्, पञ्चमी) one obtains wealth (धनम्, द्वितीया). Once you see the अपादान→कर्मन् rhythm — "from X, attain Y" — the verse reads itself. पात्रत्वात् → पात्रत्वाद् again by जश्त्व before ध.

sequence.sentence: बलवान् वीरः शत्रून् जयति। सः सर्वेभ्यः शूरतरः। तस्य जयः सर्वत्र गीयते।
sequence.translation: The strong hero conquers his enemies. He is braver than all. His victory is sung everywhere.
sequence.teaches:
the same three, closed on a hero — बलवान् (मतुप्), शूरतरः (तरप्, सर्वेभ्यः the
पञ्चमी standard), and जयः गीयते, "is sung," the passive.

notes.en: the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having strength" (shows as -वत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — बल + मतुप् → बलवत् → बलवान्
पञ्चमी विभक्ते — the term compared-from takes पञ्चमी → सर्वेभ्यः

notes.en: the तरप् comparative suffix — "braver" of two
degree of comparison — the comparative sense

notes.role: द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ — तरप् for comparison → शूर + तर → शूरतरः

notes.en: what is sung — subject of the passive
passive — जयः is sung; no expressed agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive गीयते

sequence.vyakhya: बलवान् वीरः सर्वेभ्यः शूरतरः; तस्य जयः सर्वत्र गीयते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The trio closes on a hero. बलवान् is again the possessive मतुप् (5.2.94).
शूरतरः is the comparative तरप् (5.3.57), and those he surpasses, सर्वेभ्यः,
stand in the पञ्चमी of comparison. And his victory गीयते, "is sung" — the
passive of गै (3.4.69), जयः the thing sung.

sequence.sentence: शत्रुसेनायाः जेता वीरः। कुतः तस्य भयम्? ततः सः न बिभेति।
sequence.translation: The hero is a conqueror of the enemy army. Whence his fear? Therefore he does not fear.
sequence.teaches:
the three closed on a hero — शत्रुसेनायाः (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष, कृत्-governed
षष्ठी), जेता (the तृच् agent-noun), and कुतः / ततः (the तसिल् adverb, twice).

notes.en: determinative — शत्रोः सेना, "the enemy's army"; सेना is the head

notes.role: षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (शत्रोः) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष
कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति — object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → शत्रुसेनायाः

notes.en: the तृच् agent-suffix — "the one who conquers"

notes.role: ण्वुल्तृचौ — तृच् forms the agent-noun → जि + तृ → जेतृ; nom.sg जेता

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — किम् + तस् = कुतः
the तसिल् suffix (-तस्), the ablative sense — "from what?"

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → किम् + तस् → कुतः

notes.en: an indeclinable तद्धित — तद् + तस् = ततः
the तसिल् suffix (-तस्), the ablative sense

notes.role: पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् — तसिल् in the ablative sense → तद् + तस् → ततः

sequence.vyakhya: शत्रुसेनायाः जेता वीरः; कुतः तस्य भयम्? ततः सः न बिभेति।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The trio a last time, on a hero. शत्रुसेनायाः is a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष — शत्रोः सेना
(2.2.8) — standing in the षष्ठी that a कृत्-noun governs (2.3.65), the object of
जेता, the तृच् agent-noun "conqueror" (3.1.133). Twice the तसिल् adverb turns
(5.3.7): कुतः "whence?" and ततः "therefore" — whence would his fear come, and
so he has none.

sequence.sentence: एकदा कृष्णः मृत्तिकाम् अभक्षयत् इति बालाः यशोदां अवदन्। यशोदा पुत्रं पप्रच्छ — "किम् त्वं मृत्तिकाम् अखादः?" कृष्णः उवाच — "न अखादम्।" तदा यशोदा मुखं विवृणुष्व इति उक्त्वा दृष्टवती। तस्मिन् मुखे सा सर्वम् जगत् अपश्यत् — खम्, भूमिम्, देवान्, नक्षत्राणि च।
sequence.translation: Once the children told Yaśodā that Kṛṣṇa had eaten mud. Yaśodā asked her son — "Did you eat mud?" Kṛṣṇa said — "I did not eat." Then Yaśodā said "open your mouth" and looked. In that mouth she saw all the world — sky, earth, gods, and stars.
sequence.teaches: लिट् perfect (पप्रच्छ, उवाच), लङ् past (अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत्), direct speech with इति, relative-demonstrative यस्मिन् / तस्मिन्, accusative-list object

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → मृत्तिकाम्
अनद्यतने लङ् — past (not today) → अभक्षयत्

notes.en: quotative — closes reported speech ("that he had eaten")
person told — indirect object of telling

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् → अवदन् (3pl past)
परोक्षे लिट् → पप्रच्छ (reduplication पप्र्, 3sg perf.)

notes.en: interrogative pronoun — here a question marker

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् → अखादः (2sg लङ्)
परोक्षे लिट् → उवाच (3sg perf., irregular)

notes.en: temporal adverb correlating with the question

notes.role: लोट् च — command takes लोट् → विवृणुष्व (2sg āt. लोट्)

notes.en: gerund (क्त्वा) — prior action of same agent

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → उक्त्वा
निष्ठा → क्तवतु → दृष्टवत् (masc.), दृष्टवती (fem.)
सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि — सर्व is a pronoun-class word
अनद्यतने लङ् → अपश्यत् (3sg लङ्, root √दृश् → √पश् in लङ्)

notes.en: item seen — in the list of what the cosmos contains

sequence.vyakhya: इह कालभेदः स्पष्टः — बालाः अवदन्, यशोदा पप्रच्छ, कृष्णः उवाच इति लिट् परोक्षे; परन्तु स्मृत्या न परोक्षं — नाटकीयतया लिट् उचितः। लङ् तु अनद्यतने — अभक्षयत्, अखादः, अखादम्, अपश्यत् इति। लोट् विवृणुष्व इति विधौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Two tenses meet in this reading. **लिट् perfect** (परोक्षे लिट्, 3.2.115) appears where the narrator stands at a remove — पप्रच्छ "she asked," उवाच "he said" — verbs of reported or narrated speech. **लङ्** (अनद्यतन, 3.2.111) marks the events directly recalled: the eating (अभक्षयत्), Kṛṣṇa's denial (न अखादम्), and Yaśodā's vision (अपश्यत्). One **लोट् imperative** (3.3.162) lives inside the quoted command — विवृणुष्व "open (your mouth)!" The vision that follows — sky, earth, gods, stars — is the whole universe listed in a single accusative string, with one past-active participle (दृष्टवती, क्तवतु fem.) as the main predicate: "she who saw."
