sequence.sentence: कृष्णे गच्छति सति गोप्यः अतीव अरुदन्। याः गोप्यः कृष्णम् प्रेम्णा अपश्यन्, ताः सर्वाः शोकेन मग्नाः अभवन्। रथे स्थितः कृष्णः ताः रुदतीः दृष्ट्वा अपि न न्यवर्तत। तस्य हृदये तु ताः एव सर्वदा अवसन्।
sequence.translation: When Kṛṣṇa was leaving, the gopīs wept bitterly. Those gopīs who used to look upon Kṛṣṇa with love — all of them were sunk in grief. Kṛṣṇa, seated in the chariot, though he saw them weeping, did not turn back. Yet in his heart they alone dwelt always.
sequence.teaches: locative absolute (सति-सप्तमी — कृष्णे गच्छति सति, 2.3.37); relative-correlative याः…ताः over a full clause; present participle as object (रुदतीः "weeping ones"); gerund दृष्ट्वा with concessive अपि

notes.role: यस्य च भावेन भावलक्षणम् → सति-सप्तमी — "when Kṛṣṇa…"

notes.en: present participle (शतृ, loc. sg.) in the absolute construction

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → गच्छत्; loc. गच्छति

notes.en: present participle of √अस् (सत्), loc. — the marker of the सति-सप्तमी

notes.role: the absolute locative — "(it) being so"
अनद्यतने लङ् → अरुदन् (3pl)
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → प्रेम्णा (न्-stem instr.)
अनद्यतने लङ् → अपश्यन् (3pl)

notes.en: correlative pronoun (तद्, fem. nom. pl.) — answers याः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सर्वाः
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → शोकेन
निष्ठा → क्त → मग्न
अनद्यतने लङ् → अभवन्
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → रथे

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of √स्था — "seated," attributive to कृष्णः

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → स्थित

notes.en: present participle (शतृ, fem. acc. pl.) — agreeing with ताः

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ → रुदत्; fem. रुदती, acc. pl. रुदतीः
समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → दृष्ट्वा
अनद्यतने लङ् → न्यवर्तत (आत्मनेपद 3sg)
भावकर्मणोः — वृत् takes आत्मनेपद here
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → हृदये
अनद्यतने लङ् → अवसन् (3pl)

sequence.vyakhya: अधिकरणं त्रिविधम् इह — सति-सप्तमी (कृष्णे गच्छति सति) कालार्थे; रथे हृदये इति देशाधिकरणे। याः…ताः इति वाक्यद्वये सम्बन्धः। रुदतीः इति शतृ कर्मणि (ताः रुदतीः)। दृष्ट्वा अपि इति अनुमत्यर्थे — "दृष्ट्वापि न न्यवर्तत"।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Three locatives, three jobs. The **locative absolute** (सति-सप्तमी, 2.3.37) sets the scene in time — कृष्णे गच्छति सति "Kṛṣṇa being-in-the-act-of-going," i.e. "as Kṛṣṇa was leaving": a whole subordinate clause folded into two locative words. Ordinary locatives of place follow — रथे "in the chariot," हृदये "in the heart" (2.3.36). The relative-correlative याः … ताः now spans a full clause ("those gopīs who used to look on him — they all sank in grief"). And the शतृ participle appears for the first time **as an accusative object** — ताः रुदतीः "them, the weeping ones." दृष्ट्वा अपि "even having seen" gives the concessive: he saw, yet did not turn.

sequence.sentence: अ॒ग्निर्होता॑ क॒विक्र॑तुः स॒त्यश्चि॒त्रश्र॑वस्तमः। दे॒वो दे॒वेभि॒रा ग॑मत्॥
sequence.translation: Agni the invoker, wise in will, true, most brilliant in fame — a god, may he come with the gods.
sequence.teaches: nominative epithets predicated without a verb, a बहुव्रीहि compound, and the instrumental of accompaniment

notes.en: epithet (in apposition to अग्निः) — an ऋ-stem nominative होता

notes.text: padapāṭha splits कवि-क्रतु (saṃhitā कविक्रतुः); कवि "sage" + क्रतु "will"

notes.en: possessive compound — "(one) whose क्रतु is that of a कवि"

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming an external possessor

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्रश्रवः-तम; चित्र "bright" + श्रवस् "fame" + तम superlative

notes.role: सहयुक्तेऽप्रधाने → the accompanier takes तृतीया → देवेभिः ("with the gods")

notes.text: an aorist-subjunctive (लुङ्/लेट्) sense — "may he come"

sequence.vyakhya: होता कविक्रतुः सत्यः चित्रश्रवस्तमः देवः — सर्वाणि अग्निविशेषणानि प्रथमायाम्। देवेभिः इति सहार्थे तृतीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Verse 1 strung accusatives; this one strings NOMINATIVES. होता, कविक्रतुः, सत्यः, चित्रश्रवस्तमः, देवः — all प्रथमा, all naming अग्निः (predication, no copula needed). कविक्रतुः is a बहुव्रीहि: "(one) whose क्रतु is a sage's." Then देवेभिः is the तृतीया of accompaniment — "with the gods" — the सह-sense you met in पुत्रेण सह. आ गमत्: "may he come hither."

source.ref: Hit_0.4 — विद्या is the unsurpassed wealth
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, ||Hit_0.4||)

sequence.sentence: सर्वद्रव्येषु विद्यैव द्रव्यम् आहुर् अनुत्तमम्। अहार्यत्वाद् अनर्घत्वाद् अक्षयत्वाच् च सर्वदा॥
sequence.translation: Among all forms of wealth they call knowledge alone the unsurpassed wealth — because it cannot be stolen, is priceless, and is imperishable, always.
sequence.teaches:
three त्व-abstracts giving the reason in the ablative — अहार्यत्वात् (unstealable),
अनर्घत्वात् (priceless), अक्षयत्वात् (imperishable); "they call" is the perfect आहुः.

notes.text: सर्व + द्रव्य — "all substances / all wealth"
विद्या + एव → विद्यैव (आ + ए → ऐ, वृद्धिसन्धि); एव = "alone, indeed"

notes.en: predicate object of आहुः ("call it wealth")
perfect — the defective root अह् survives only in the परोक्ष (आह, आहुः)

notes.text: आहुः → आहुर् before अ (visarga → र्)

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अहार्य (not to be stolen)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अहार्य + त्व → अहार्यत्व

notes.en: ablative of cause — "because of ___" (अहार्यत्वात् → अहार्यत्वाद् before अ)
the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अनर्घ (priceless)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अनर्घ + त्व → अनर्घत्व

notes.en: the त्व abstract suffix — "the state of being अक्षय (imperishable)"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → अक्षय + त्व → अक्षयत्व

notes.en: ablative of cause (अक्षयत्वात् → अक्षयत्वाच् before च)

sequence.vyakhya: सर्वद्रव्येषु विद्या एव अनुत्तमम् द्रव्यम् — अहार्यत्वात् अनर्घत्वात् अक्षयत्वात् च।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Of all wealth, knowledge alone (विद्यैव) they call the unsurpassed — द्रव्यम्
and अनुत्तमम् both द्वितीया, the double object of आहुः "they call." The reason
comes in three त्व-abstracts in the ablative of cause: अहार्यत्वात्, "because it
cannot be stolen"; अनर्घत्वात्, "because it is priceless"; अक्षयत्वात्, "because
it never runs out" — each the त्व noun (5.1.119) of a quality, and सर्वदा,
always so.

sequence.sentence: सकलार्थशास्त्रसारं जगति समालोक्य विष्णुशर्मेदम्। तन्त्रैः पञ्चभिर् एतच् चकार सुमनोहरं शास्त्रम्॥
sequence.translation: Having surveyed in the world the essence of all the treatises on statecraft, Viṣṇuśarman composed this charming work in five tantras.
sequence.teaches:
the Pañcatantra's own opening — a long तत्पुरुष सार-compound as object of the
ल्यप् gerund समालोक्य, and the perfect चकार "he composed."

words.gloss: the essence of all the treatises on statecraft

notes.en: determinative — सारम्, the head, is qualified by the rest; सकलानाम् अर्थशास्त्राणाम् सारम्

notes.text: विग्रह: सकलानाम् अर्थशास्त्राणाम् सारम् — "the essence of all the arthaśāstras"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose last member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष

notes.en: gerund — a कृदन्त that does not decline
the ल्यप् suffix — a क्त्वा-gerund WITH a preverb (सम्-आ), so आगत्य-style

notes.role: समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् — क्त्वा becomes ल्यप् after a preverb → -आलोक्य

notes.en: सम् + आ — the preverbs that select ल्यप् over क्त्वा
agent — विष्णुशर्मा, the one who composed
nominative — an अन्-stem, so the न् drops (विष्णुशर्मा)

notes.text: विष्णुशर्मा + इदम् → विष्णुशर्मेदम् (आ + इ → ए, गुणसन्धि); इदम् = "this work," द्वितीया

notes.en: instrument — "by means of the five books"

notes.text: पञ्चभिः + एतत् → पञ्चभिर् (visarga → र् before a voiced sound)
एतत् + चकार → एतच् चकार (त् → च् before च, श्चुत्व 8.4.40)

notes.en: perfect — the remote or reported past (परोक्ष)

notes.role: परोक्षे लिट् — for a past beyond direct witness, लिट् replaces the लकार → चकार

sequence.vyakhya: सकलार्थशास्त्रसारं समालोक्य विष्णुशर्मा पञ्चभिः तन्त्रैः शास्त्रम् चकार।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The Pañcatantra names itself in its second verse. The object of the gerund is
one long तत्पुरुष — सकल-अर्थशास्त्र-सारम्, "the essence of all the treatises on
statecraft" — which Viṣṇuśarman, having surveyed (समालोक्य, the ल्यप् gerund),
made into a charming work. चकार is the perfect (लिट्, 3.2.115), the tense of
reported past: "he composed it." तन्त्रैः पञ्चभिः, "by five books" — the five
that give the book its name.

sequence.sentence: यदं॒ग दा॒शुषे॒ त्वमग्ने॑ भ॒द्रं क॑रि॒ष्यसि॑। तवेत्तत्स॒त्यमं॑गिरः॥
sequence.translation: Whatever good you will do for the worshipper, O Agni — that, indeed, is your truth, O Aṅgiras.
sequence.teaches: दाशुषे "for the giver" as सम्प्रदान in the चतुर्थी, and करिष्यसि in the future

notes.en: relative — here introducing the whole clause

words.gloss: for the worshipper, for the giver (of offerings)

notes.en: recipient — the one for whom the good is done

notes.role: कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् → the worshipper is सम्प्रदान
चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने
लृट् शेषे च → future → करिष्यसि (√कृ; 2sg, "you will do")
षष्ठी शेषे → तव ("your")

notes.en: vocative — a second address to Agni

sequence.vyakhya: यत् भद्रं दाशुषे करिष्यसि, तत् तव सत्यम्। दाशुषे इति सम्प्रदाने चतुर्थी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A यत्…तत् sentence with two new turns. दाशुषे is the सम्प्रदान — the dative (चतुर्थी), "for the worshipper," the same "for whom" case you met in नमो देवेभ्यः. करिष्यसि is a FUTURE (लृट्), "you will do" — √कृ now in the future, 2nd person. Two vocatives frame it: अग्ने and अङ्गिरः (a name of Agni). The sense: whatever blessing you will do for the giver — *that* is your truth.

sequence.sentence: यन् नवे भाजने लग्नः संस्कारो नान्यथा भवेत्। कथाच्छलेन बालानां नीतिस् तद् इह कथ्यते॥
sequence.translation: Since an impression set on a new vessel cannot become otherwise, statecraft is here told to children through the guise of story.
sequence.teaches:
the book's method, and a passive. लग्नः is a क्त participle; भवेत् is the
optative; and नीतिः कथ्यते — "is told" — is the passive (कर्मणि) of कथ्.

notes.en: relative — "in that / since" (यत् → यन् before न, परसवर्ण)
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — "stuck, set" (लग् → लग्न)
nominative (संस्कारः → संस्कारो before न, visarga उत्व)
adverb — "otherwise"; न + अन्यथा → नान्यथा (आ + अ → आ), "not otherwise"

words.gloss: by the guise of a story

notes.en: determinative — कथायाः छलम्, "the pretext of a story"
the thing told — subject of the passive verb
pronoun — resuming नीतिः (तत् → तद् before इ)
passive — नीतिः is what is told; no expressed agent

notes.role: लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive कथ्यते

sequence.vyakhya: नवे भाजने लग्नः संस्कारः अन्यथा न भवेत् — तथा कथाच्छलेन बालानां नीतिः कथ्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
An image explains the method. As a संस्कार, an impression लग्नः "set" (the क्त
participle) on a नव भाजन, a new vessel, cannot नान्यथा भवेत् "become otherwise"
(the optative), so — कथाच्छलेन, "by the guise of story" — statecraft is taught
to the young while their minds are new. नीतिः कथ्यते, "is told": कथ्यते is the
passive of कथ् (3.4.69), the नीति the thing told.

sequence.sentence: न हि तद् विद्यते किञ्चिद् यद् अर्थेन न सिध्यति। यत्नेन मतिमान् तस्माद् अर्थम् एकम् प्रसाधयेत्॥
sequence.translation: There is nothing at all that is not achieved by wealth; therefore the wise man should, by effort, secure wealth above all.
sequence.teaches:
an optative maxim. प्रसाधयेत् is विधिलिङ्, "should secure"; मतिमान् is the
मतुप् possessive "the one having wit"; अर्थेन / यत्नेन are the तृतीया of means.

notes.en: किम् + चित् — the indefinite "anything" (किंचित् → किञ्चिद् before य)
the मतुप् possessive suffix — "having wit" (मति + मतुप् → मतिमत्)

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — मति + मतुप् → मतिमत् → मतिमान्

notes.en: from that — the causal ablative (तस्मात् → तस्माद् before अ)

sequence.vyakhya: अर्थेन सर्वम् सिध्यति; तस्मात् मतिमान् अर्थम् एकम् प्रसाधयेत्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A maxim in the optative. Nothing, तद् किञ्चित्, is found यद् — which — is not
achieved अर्थेन, "by wealth" (the तृतीया of means, as is यत्नेन "by effort").
So the मतिमान्, the one who HAS wit (मति + मतुप्, 5.2.94), should — प्रसाधयेत्,
the विधिलिङ् "ought to secure" — wealth एकम्, above all. The whole force sits in
that optative: not "does" but "should."

sequence.sentence: यः कंसः चिरम् कृष्णस्य वधम् इच्छति स्म, सः एव अधुना भयेन कम्पते। कृष्णः मथुराम् प्रविश्य रङ्गभूमौ मल्लान् अहन्। ततः सः उच्चासनात् कंसम् आकृष्य भूमौ अपातयत्। यम् राजानम् सर्वे जनाः अबिभयुः, सः कृष्णेन क्षणेन एव हतः। एवम् अधर्मस्य अन्तः, धर्मस्य च जयः अभवत्।
sequence.translation: He who for long had wished for Kṛṣṇa's death — that very one now trembles with fear. Kṛṣṇa, having entered Mathurā, killed the wrestlers in the arena. Then he dragged Kaṃsa down from his high throne and threw him to the ground. The king whom all people had feared — he was killed by Kṛṣṇa in but a moment. Thus came the end of unrighteousness, and the victory of dharma.
sequence.teaches: climax — two relative-correlatives (यः…सः on the subject, यम्…सः on the object); अपादान (भयस्य source → उच्चासनात् ablative, अबिभयुः with 5th); causative अपातयत्; षष्ठी of object with कृत् (कृष्णस्य वधम्, 2.3.65); passive close (हतः)

notes.en: object of the action-noun वधम् — "(the) killing OF Kṛṣṇa"

notes.role: कर्तृकर्मणोः कृति → object of a कृत्-noun takes षष्ठी → कृष्णस्य

notes.en: object of इच्छति — what Kaṃsa wished for
the thematic अ between root and ending
with लट् → past habitual — "had been wishing"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → भयेन

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् → अपातयत् (causative 3sg)

sequence.vyakhya: कथायाः शिखरम् — द्वौ सम्बन्धौ यद्-तद्। कर्तरि यः…सः (यः इच्छति स्म सः कम्पते); कर्मणि यम्…सः (यं अबिभयुः सः हतः)। अपादानम् द्विधा — उच्चासनात् (departure), भयस्य हेतुः भी-धातुना अबिभयुः। वधम् इति कृत्, तत्र कर्म षष्ठ्याम् (कृष्णस्य वधम्)। अन्ते कर्मणि हतः — कथार्धम् सर्वम् कर्मणि समाप्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The climax, and it gathers everything. Two relative-correlatives frame it, one on each axis: यः … सः on the **subject** ("he who long wished Kṛṣṇa's death — that one now trembles") and यम् … सः on the **object** ("the king whom all feared — he was killed"). Two ablatives of separation: उच्चासनात् "from the high throne" (2.3.28) and the fear-source folded into अबिभयुः. The action-noun वधम् "killing" takes its object in the **genitive** — कृष्णस्य वधम् "the killing OF Kṛṣṇa" (2.3.65, the कृत्-षष्ठी). The arc that began with butter and a rope ends as it must, in the passive: हतः "was killed" — and the whole Kṛṣṇa-childhood sequence closes on its grammatical signature, the कर्मणि क्त, now carrying the weight of a death rather than a game.

sequence.sentence: उप॑ त्वाग्ने दि॒वेदि॑वे॒ दोषा॑वस्तर्धि॒या व॒यं। नमो॒ भरं॑त॒ एम॑सि॥
sequence.translation: To you, O Agni, day by day, by night and dawn, we come in thought, bearing homage.
sequence.teaches: a first-person plural verb एमसि "we come," with वयम् and धिया "by thought" as the means

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

notes.text: the आम्रेडित दिवे-दिवे (met in rd010) — "every day"
padapāṭha splits दोषा-वस्तः; दोषा "at night" + वस्तर् "at dawn"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → धिया (तृतीया of the ई-stem धी)

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) agreeing with वयम् — "(we) bearing"

sequence.vyakhya: वयं धिया नमो भरन्तः दिवेदिवे त्वा उप आ इमसि। एमसि इति उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The worshippers speak now in their own voice: वयम् "we," and एमसि (उप…आ…इमसि) "we come" — a 1st-person PLURAL verb (उत्तमपुरुष बहुवचन), the same person you met as -मि in गच्छामि, now plural. To you (त्वा, accusative) we come, day by day (दिवेदिवे), at night and dawn (दोषावस्तः), in thought (धिया, तृतीया of means), bearing homage (नमः भरन्तः). A whole sentence of grammar you already hold.

sequence.sentence: विद्या शस्त्रम् च शास्त्रम् च द्वे विद्ये प्रतिपत्तये। आद्या हास्याय वृद्धत्वे द्वितीया आद्रियते सदा॥
sequence.translation: Knowledge is of two kinds — weapon-craft and the śāstra — two knowledges for mastery. The first is for ridicule in old age; the second is honored always.
sequence.teaches:
two derived nouns of purpose. प्रतिपत्तये is the क्तिन् action-noun "for
mastery"; हास्याय is the ण्यत् gerundive "for (being) laughed at."

notes.en: nominative (neuter) — one of the two kinds
the क्तिन् feminine action-noun — प्रति + पद् + क्तिन् → प्रतिपत्ति

notes.role: स्त्रियां क्तिन् — क्तिन् forms a feminine action-noun → प्रतिपत्ति ("attainment")

notes.en: the ण्यत् gerundive suffix (with वृद्धि) — हस् → हास्य

notes.role: ऋहलोर्ण्यत् — ण्यत् after a हल्-final root → हस् + ण्यत् → हास्य
तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व for "the state of" → वृद्ध + त्व → वृद्धत्व
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive आद्रियते

sequence.vyakhya: विद्या द्विविधा — शस्त्रम् शास्त्रम् च; प्रतिपत्तये द्वे। आद्या हास्याय, द्वितीया सदा आद्रियते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Two derivations carry the sense. प्रतिपत्तये is the क्तिन् action-noun of
प्रति-पद्, "for mastery" (3.3.94), in the dative of purpose; हास्याय is the
ण्यत् gerundive of हस्, "for being laughed at" (3.1.124), the same dative. The
first knowledge — weapon-craft — comes to that, हास्याय वृद्धत्वे, "ridicule in
old age" (वृद्धत्व, the त्व abstract); the second, the śāstra, आद्रियते सदा,
"is honored always" — the passive of आ-दृ.

sequence.sentence: गुरुणा शिष्याः पाठ्यन्ते। तैः शास्त्राणि पठ्यन्ते, वचनानि च श्रूयन्ते। गुरुः तान् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति। श्वः ते ग्रामम् गमिष्यन्ति। तत्र धनम् धान्यम् च लप्स्यन्ते। नद्याः तीरे तिष्ठन्ति, जलम् पिबन्ति च।
sequence.translation: The students are taught by the teacher. By them the treatises are read, and the sayings are heard. The teacher wishes to see them. Tomorrow they will go to the village. There they will obtain wealth and grain. They stand on the river's bank, and drink water.
sequence.teaches:
four passives against two actives. The same students appear as शिष्याः,
तैः, ते and तान् — the case follows what the verb's ending points at.

notes.en: the agent of a passive — unexpressed by the ending, so it takes a case
what is taught — expressed by the ending, so it stands nominative

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म — what the agent most aims at is the कर्मन् → शिष्याः

notes.en: the passive विकरण on a causative stem — पाठि + य + अन्ते

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — आत्मनेपद endings in the passive → पाठ्यन्ते
नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → शास्त्राणि

notes.en: the plain passive beside the causative passive above — पठ् + य + अन्ते
neuter nominative plural — the same नुम् as शास्त्राणि

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before शि → वचनानि

notes.en: a third passive — श्रु + य + अन्ते

notes.role: भावकर्मणोः — the passive takes आत्मनेपद → श्रूयन्ते

notes.en: now an ACTIVE agent — nominative, because the ending expresses it

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → गुरुः

notes.en: the object of an ACTIVE verb — accusative, not nominative
infinitive — what the wishing is directed at

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् — the infinitive → द्रष्टुम्

notes.en: इष् appears as इच्छ् + अ + ति
the ending expresses the agent — contrast the four passives above

notes.role: ससजुषो रुः — final स् → रु → visarga → श्वः
लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → गमिष्यन्ति

notes.en: joined with धान्यम् by च — two things counted together

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate pair धनम् धान्यम् च

notes.en: a second future, this one आत्मनेपद — लभ् is middle

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — the future → लप्स्यन्ते

notes.en: genitive — ī-stem, the ई becoming य् before the ending

notes.role: इको यणचि — इ/ई before a vowel becomes य् → नद्याः

notes.en: स्था appears as तिष्ठ् + अ + न्ति
object of an active verb — accusative again
पा appears as पिब् + अ + न्ति

sequence.vyakhya: तैः पठ्यन्ते, ते गच्छन्ति। एकः कर्ता, द्वे विभक्ती।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The same students appear four times and are named three different ways.
शिष्याः when the passive points at them, तैः when the passive points past
them at what they read, ते when the verb is active and points at them
again, तान् when someone else's verb points at them.

Nothing about the students changed. Each time, the case answers one
question: has the verb's ending already said this? If yes, प्रथमा. If no,
whatever case the role calls for.

sequence.sentence: राजं॑तमध्व॒राणां॑ गो॒पामृ॒तस्य॒ दीदि॑विं। वर्ध॑मानं॒ स्वे दमे॑॥
sequence.translation: (To you,) ruling over the rites, the guardian of truth, the shining one, growing in your own home.
sequence.teaches: accusative epithets continuing from the previous verse, with अध्वराणां "of the rites" in the genitive plural and स्वे दमे "in his own home" in the locative

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the accusative — "(you who are) ruling"

notes.en: accusative (apposed to the त्वा of verse 7)
genitive plural — that over which one rules

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → अध्वराणाम् ("of/over the rites")
षष्ठी शेषे → ऋतस्य

notes.text: a middle present participle (शानच्) in the accusative — "(you) growing"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → स्वे (सप्तमी, agreeing with दमे)

words.gloss: in the home, in the abode

sequence.vyakhya: राजन्तं गोपां दीदिविं वर्धमानं — सर्वाणि कर्माणि (पूर्वस्या ऋचः त्वा-शब्दस्य विशेषणानि)। अध्वराणाम् ऋतस्य च षष्ठी; स्वे दमे इति सप्तमी।
sequence.vyakhya_en: This verse has no new finite verb — it continues verse 7's "to you we come," piling accusative epithets onto that त्वा: राजन्तम् (ruling), गोपाम् (guardian), दीदिविम् (shining), वर्धमानम् (growing). Two participles (राजन्तम् active, वर्धमानम् middle) decline like nouns in the accusative. The genitives अध्वराणाम् (over the rites) and ऋतस्य (of truth) mark domain; स्वे दमे — सप्तमी — locates it: "in his own home." Cases you hold, stacked into Vedic praise.

sequence.sentence: महाबलः नृपः सभाम् आगच्छत्। तस्य पार्श्वे मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ आस्ताम्। नीलाम्बरः दूतः प्रविश्य उपसभम् अतिष्ठत्। सः महाबलम् अवदत् — शत्रुसेना पराजिता, राष्ट्रम् च रक्षितम्।
sequence.translation: The mighty king came to the assembly. At his side were the minister-and-priest. A blue-clad messenger, having entered, stood near the assembly. He said to the mighty one — "The enemy-army is defeated, and the kingdom protected."
sequence.teaches:
the four compound types again, none of them new: महाबलः (बहुव्रीहि),
मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ (द्वन्द्व), उपसभम् (अव्ययीभाव), शत्रुसेना (तत्पुरुष).

words.gloss: the mighty one (whose strength is great)

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; it names the one who HAS great strength

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the possessor) form a बहुव्रीहि

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: possessive — the one whose garment is blue
gerund — a कृदन्त that does not decline
the ल्यप् suffix — a क्त्वा-gerund WITH a preverb (प्र), so आगत्य-style not आगत्वा
प्र — the preverb that selects ल्यप् over क्त्वा
adverbial — उप heads it, and the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: possessive — here standing for the king himself
determinative — सेना, the second member, is the head; शत्रोः सेना

notes.text: विग्रह: शत्रोः सेना — "the army of the enemy"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (शत्रोः) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: agent — subject of the passive predicate
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — passive, "was defeated"
passive — agrees with शत्रुसेना, no finite verb
the thing protected — subject of the passive predicate
the क्त निष्ठा suffix — passive, "was protected"

sequence.vyakhya: चत्वारः समासाः एकस्मिन् दृश्ये — महाबलः, मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ, उपसभम्, शत्रुसेना।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
All four kinds in one scene, and each doing ordinary work. महाबलः is a
बहुव्रीहि — not "great" and not "strength" but the one who HAS great strength,
the king. मन्त्रिपुरोहितौ is a द्वन्द्व, minister and priest taken as a pair.
उपसभम् is an अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying it and the whole going indeclinable. And
शत्रुसेना is a तत्पुरुष — शत्रोः सेना, the enemy's army — whose defeat the
passive participle पराजिता reports without a finite verb.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1 — the lion and the clever rabbit (सिंहः शशकश्च)
source.curated: our graded prose; the fable is canonical, the sentences are ours

sequence.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् वने भासुरको नाम सिंहः वसति स्म। सः बलवान् आसीत्, किन्तु अतीव क्रूरः। प्रतिदिनम् सः बहून् पशून् अहन्। तेन सर्वे मृगाः भयेन कम्पन्ते स्म। ते मिलित्वा सिंहम् ऊचुः — "हे स्वामिन्, मा सर्वान् पशून् हन्। वयम् एव प्रतिदिनम् एकम् पशुम् तव आहाराय प्रेषयिष्यामः।"
sequence.translation: In a certain forest there lived a lion named Bhāsuraka. He was strong, but exceedingly cruel. Every day he killed many animals. Because of this all the beasts trembled with fear. They, having gathered, said to the lion — "O master, do not kill all the animals. We ourselves will send one animal every day for your food."
sequence.teaches: the fable opens: कस्मिंश्चित् as an indefinite locative, the prohibitive मा with लङ् in मा हन्, a first-person plural future प्रेषयिष्यामः, आहाराय as a dative of purpose, and ऊचुः in the perfect

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — कस्मिन् + चित्, the न् going श् before च् → कस्मिंश्चित्

notes.en: indefinite pronoun (किम् + चित्), locative — "in some / a certain"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → कस्मिंश्चित् (loc.)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending
with लट् → past — "used to dwell, lived"

notes.role: अनद्यतने लङ् → आसीत्
अनद्यतने लङ् → अहन्

notes.en: pronoun (तद्, instr.) — "by that → because of this"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सर्वे
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → भयेन

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → मिलित्वा
परोक्षे लिट् → ऊचुः (3pl perfect)

notes.en: prohibitive particle — with लङ् (no augment) forbids the act

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → सर्वान्
लुङ् — after मा the prohibitive takes augmentless लुङ् (मा हिंसीः type)

notes.en: purpose — dative of purpose ("for the sake of food")

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → आहाराय (purpose-dative)
लृट् शेषे च → प्रेषयिष्यामः (future, 1pl)

sequence.vyakhya: नूतनकथारम्भः — पञ्चतन्त्रात्। कस्मिंश्चित् वने इति लोकप्रसिद्धम् आख्यानारम्भपदम्। मा हन् इति प्रतिषेधे लुङ् अनद्यतनः अनागमकः। आहाराय इति तादर्थ्ये चतुर्थी; प्रेषयिष्यामः इति लृट् उत्तमपुरुषबहुवचने।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new story begins — from the Pañcatantra, and it opens with the formula every Sanskrit tale is built on: कस्मिंश्चित् वने "in a certain forest" (कः + चित् = the indefinite "some"). One genuinely new construction: the **prohibitive** — मा with an augmentless past (मा … हन् "do not kill"), the standard way Sanskrit says "don't." Against it stands the animals' **future promise** — प्रेषयिष्यामः "we will send" (लृट्, 1st plural). The dative आहाराय "for food" is the dative of purpose (तादर्थ्य). All the rest — past tenses, gerund मिलित्वा, instrumental of cause भयेन — is grammar you already own, now carrying a fable instead of a god.

source.ref: RV 1.1.9 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the hymn
source.curated: complete verse, taken whole; the final verse of the hymn. Accent verbatim from sri-aurobindo.co.in

sequence.sentence: स नः॑ पि॒तेव॑ सू॒नवेऽग्ने॑ सूपाय॒नो भ॑व। सच॑स्वा नः स्व॒स्तये॑॥
sequence.translation: Be to us, O Agni, easy of approach, as a father to his son; abide with us for our well-being.
sequence.teaches: the simile पिता इव "like a father," datives of the one addressed — सूनवे, नः, स्वस्तये — and the imperatives भव and सचस्व

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → नः ("for us")

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पिता-इव; पिता (nom, the ऋ-stem you met) + इव "like"

notes.en: recipient — "(as a father) to a son"

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सूनवे (an उ-stem dative, गुण → सूनवे, like अग्नये)
सम्बोधने च → अग्ने

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-उपायन; सु "well, easy" + उपायन "approach"

notes.en: predicate adjective of भव — "be (one) easy to approach"
imperative — "be!" (the command mood you met in गच्छतु)

notes.role: लोट् च — imperative → भव (2sg "be!")
लोट् च — imperative → सचस्व

notes.text: नः again — here "with us" (object/goal of सचस्व)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → स्वस्तये (an इ-stem dative, like अग्नये)

sequence.vyakhya: पिता सूनवे इव, अग्ने नः सूपायनः भव; नः स्वस्तये सचस्व। चतुर्थ्यः बह्व्यः — सूनवे नः स्वस्तये।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with a prayer, dense with the चतुर्थी (dative): नः "for us," सूनवे "to a son," स्वस्तये "for well-being" — three datives, all the "for whom" case (सम्प्रदान). The heart is a simile: पिता इव सूनवे — "as a father (is) to a son." Two imperatives (लोट्) carry the request: भव "be!" and सचस्व "abide!" — the command mood you met in गच्छतु, here in real Vedic. With this you have read the whole first hymn of the Ṛgveda, end to end, with its accent.

source.ref: Bhāgavata 1.2.11 — Brahman, Paramātman, Bhagavān
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_bhAgavatapurANa, ||BhP_01.02.011||)

sequence.sentence: वदन्ति तत् तत्त्वविदस् तत्त्वम् यज् ज्ञानम् अद्वयम्। ब्रह्मेति परमात्मेति भगवान् इति शब्द्यते॥
sequence.translation: The knowers of truth declare that truth — the knowledge that is without-a-second — and it is named "Brahman," "Paramātman," "Bhagavān."
sequence.teaches:
the नञ्-तत्पुरुष अद्वयम् ("not-two"), and a passive naming — शब्द्यते, "is
called," of what the knowers declare.

notes.en: compound — तत्त्वं विदन्ति, "who know the truth" (उपपद-तत्पुरुष)
relative pronoun (यत् → यज् before ज, श्चुत्व)

notes.text: विग्रह: न द्वयम् — "not two"

notes.role: नञ् — नञ् (न) compounds with a following word → नञ्-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: nominative — the name given; ब्रह्म + इति → ब्रह्मेति (अ + इ → ए)
nominative — a second name; परमात्मा + इति → परमात्मेति (आ + इ → ए)
possessive derivative — भग + मतुप् → भगवत् ("having fortune")

notes.role: तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् — भग + मतुप् → भगवत्
सान्तमहतः संयोगस्य — penult lengthening in the strong stem → भगवान्
लः कर्मणि च — the ल-affix (लट्) denotes the कर्मन् → passive शब्द्यते

sequence.vyakhya: तत्त्वविदः तत् तत्त्वम् अद्वयम् ज्ञानम् वदन्ति; तत् ब्रह्म परमात्मा भगवान् इति शब्द्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The knowers of truth declare तत्त्वम्, and name it three ways. What they
declare is अद्वयम् ज्ञानम् — "knowledge not-two," a नञ्-तत्पुरुष, न द्वयम्
(2.2.6). And the naming is passive: ब्रह्म, परमात्मा, भगवान् — इति शब्द्यते,
"is called," the passive of the denominative शब्द् (3.4.69). भगवान् itself is
the मतुप् possessive भगवत्, "the one having fortune."

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1.5 — the world befriends the rich
source.curated: the whole verse; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_1.5||)

sequence.sentence: इह लोके हि धनिनाम् परोऽपि स्वजनायते। स्वजनोऽपि दरिद्राणाम् सर्वदा दुर्जनायते॥
sequence.translation: In this world, even a stranger behaves as kin toward the rich; even one's own kin always behaves as an enemy toward the poor.
sequence.teaches:
the denominative — a whole verb built from a noun: स्वजनायते "acts as one's
own," दुर्जनायते "acts as a foe," the क्यङ् formation "behave like X."

notes.en: possessive derivative — धन "wealth" → धनिन् "having wealth, rich"

notes.role: अत इनिठनौ — after an अ-final stem denoting a possessum, इनि (and ठन्) in the "possessing" sense → धन + इनि → धनिन्

notes.en: genitive plural — "for/toward the rich" (the one behaved-toward)
denominative — a verb made from the noun स्वजन "one's own kin," "to act like/as ___"

notes.role: उपमानादाचारे — from a standard-of-comparison (उपमान), in the sense of behaving toward someone like it (आचार), a denominative affix is introduced
कर्तुः क्यङ् — that affix is क्यङ् (आत्मनेपद) when the behaving is self-referential → स्वजन + क्यङ् → स्वजनायते

notes.en: genitive plural — "for/toward the poor" (the one behaved-toward)
denominative from दुर्जन "a wicked man, foe" — "to act like a foe"

notes.role: कर्तुः क्यङ् (उपमानादाचारे) — दुर्जन + क्यङ् → दुर्जनायते "behaves like a foe"

sequence.vyakhya: नामधातुप्रधानः श्लोकः। स्वजनायते दुर्जनायते इति उपमानात् आचारे क्यङ् — "स्वजन इव आचरति" इत्यर्थे। धनिनाम् दरिद्राणाम् इति शेषे षष्ठी (आचरितव्यविषये)। धनिन् इति धनशब्दात् इनिः मतुबर्थे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A verse built on the नामधातु — the denominative verb. Sanskrit can turn
almost any noun into a verb; here स्वजन "one's own" → स्वजनायते "acts as one's
own," and दुर्जन "a foe" → दुर्जनायते "acts as a foe." The rule is
3.1.10–11: from an उपमान (a standard of comparison), in the sense of
**आचार** (behaving toward someone as if they were that thing), a root is
formed, and it takes **क्यङ्** with आत्मनेपद endings (-आयते). Around it:
धनिनाम् and दरिद्राणाम् are genitives of the one behaved-toward, and धनिन्
itself is धन + इनि (5.2.115), the "possessing wealth" derivative — the same
इनि you meet in दण्डिन्, बलिन्, मनस्विन्.

source.ref: Rāmāyaṇa 1.32.7 — forgiveness, the ornament
source.curated: the first hemistich, a maxim on its own; text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_rAmAyaNa, R_1.032.007ab)

sequence.sentence: अलंकारो हि नारीणाम् क्षमा तु पुरुषस्य वा॥
sequence.translation: Forgiveness is the ornament of women — and of a man as well.
sequence.teaches:
a balanced maxim of genitives: नारीणाम् "of women" (with णत्व, न → ण after
the र of नारी) and पुरुषस्य "of a man" (the अ-stem genitive स्य).

notes.role: रषाभ्यां नो णः — a dental न् becomes retroflex ण् when a र् or ष् precedes (even across vowels); the र of नारी retroflexes the न of the नाम् ending → नारीणाम्
टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः — after an अ-stem, the genitive-singular ending ङस् is replaced by स्य → पुरुष + स्य → पुरुषस्य

notes.en: "or, as well" — extending the claim to men

sequence.vyakhya: सुभाषितम्। नारीणाम् इति नारीशब्दस्य षष्ठीबहुवचनम् — रेफात् नकारस्य णत्वम् (रषाभ्यां नो णः)। पुरुषस्य इति अकारान्तस्य ङसः स्यादेशः (टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः)। क्षमा प्रथमा; अलंकारो विसर्गसन्धौ ओकारः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A single-line subhāṣita, and a tidy pairing of genitives. नारीणाम् "of
women" is where you catch **णत्व** at work: the न् of the genitive-plural
ending नाम् turns retroflex ण् because the र of नारी precedes it (8.4.1
रषाभ्यां नो णः — र/ष retroflex a following न even across vowels). Its partner
पुरुषस्य "of a man" shows the ordinary अ-stem genitive singular, the ending
ङस् becoming स्य (7.1.12). Between them sits क्षमा, an आ-stem feminine
nominative, the whole balanced by तु … वा "for women — and for men too."

source.ref: Manu 3.56 — where women are honored
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated per GRETIL's analysis segmentation (avagraha/vṛddhi sandhi shown split); every form is Manu's. Text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_manusmRti, Manu_3.56)

sequence.sentence: यत्र नार्यः तु पूज्यन्ते रमन्ते तत्र देवताः। यत्र एताः तु न पूज्यन्ते सर्वाः तत्र अफलाः क्रियाः॥
sequence.translation: Where women are honored, there the gods rejoice; where they are not honored, all rites are fruitless.
sequence.teaches:
the passive voice on the page — पूज्यन्ते "are honored," with the यक्
passive-marker, the honored women standing as the grammatical subject; and
a यण्-सन्धि (नारी → नार्यः) and a नञ्-compound (अफलाः "fruitless").

notes.en: relative adverb of place (correlative of तत्र)

notes.role: इको यणचि — an इक् vowel (here ī) becomes the corresponding semivowel य् before a vowel → नारी + अस् (जस्) → नार्यः

notes.en: the honored ones — grammatical subject of the passive (कर्मणि उक्त)
the passive विकरण — inserted between root and ending in the कर्मणि

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — before a सार्वधातुक ending in the कर्मणि/भावे, यक् is the विकरण → पूज् + यक् → पूज्य…

notes.en: subject of the passive न पूज्यन्ते

notes.role: नञ् — the negative नञ् (न → अ) compounds with फल → अफल "fruitless"

sequence.vyakhya: कर्मणिप्रयोगप्रधानः श्लोकः। पूज्यन्ते इति यकि लट् कर्मणि (सार्वधातुके यक्)। नार्यः इति ईकारस्य यणादेशः (इको यणचि)। अफलाः इति नञ्समासः बहुव्रीहिः। यत्र…तत्र इति नित्यसम्बन्धे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A verse in the **passive**. पूज्यन्ते "are honored" and न पूज्यन्ते "are not
honored" show the कर्मणि प्रयोग — the thing-acted-upon (the women) becomes the
grammatical subject in the nominative, and the verb carries the passive marker
**यक्** (3.1.67, सार्वधातुके यक्). Two more points earn their place: नार्यः,
where the ī of नारी turns to य् before the ending (6.1.77 इको यणचि, the
यण्-सन्धि), and अफलाः "fruitless," a नञ्-compound (2.2.6). The frame is the
यत्र … तत्र correlative — "where … there."

source.ref: Rāmāyaṇa 1.1.1 — Vālmīki questions Nārada
source.curated: the whole opening verse, word-separated (pausa forms shown; compounds kept whole); every form is Vālmīki's. Text from Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_rAmAyaNa, R_1.001.001)

sequence.sentence: तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतम् तपस्वी वाग्विदाम् वरम्। नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिः मुनिपुंगवम्॥
sequence.translation: Vālmīki the ascetic questioned Nārada — the best of the eloquent, that bull among sages, ever devoted to austerity and study.
sequence.teaches:
the very first verse of the Rāmāyaṇa — and with it the perfect tense,
परिपप्रच्छ "questioned" (लिट्, the reduplicated past of "remote" narration),
a verb of asking that takes the person asked as its object.

notes.en: compound — "engaged in (निरत) tapas and svādhyāya," a तत्पुरुष qualifying नारदम्
the best OF the eloquent — governed by वरम्
in apposition to नारदम् — "the best (of the eloquent)"
the one questioned — object of परिपप्रच्छ (a verb of asking, अकथितं च)

notes.role: अकथितं च — प्रच्छ् "ask" takes the person asked as कर्मन् → नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ
परोक्षे लिट् — for a remote (परोक्ष) past, the लिट् (perfect) is used; प्रच्छ् reduplicates → परि + पप्रच्छ

notes.en: compound — पुंगव "bull" as "best of" → "the foremost of sages" (उपमान)

sequence.vyakhya: आदिश्लोकः। परिपप्रच्छ इति प्रच्छेः लिटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम् (परोक्षे लिट्, द्वित्वम्)। नारदम् इति प्रच्छेः द्विकर्मकत्वात् पृष्टः कर्म (अकथितं च)। तपस्वी इति तपस्शब्दात् विनिः; वाग्विदाम् मुनिपुंगवम् इति समासौ; वरम् इति षष्ठ्यन्तेन योगे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The Rāmāyaṇa opens on a single sentence, and it brings the **perfect tense**:
परिपप्रच्छ "questioned," the लिट् of परि-प्रच्छ्, its reduplication (प + प्रच्छ)
the tense's signature. The लिट् is the tense of *remote*, narrated past — 3.2.115
परोक्षे लिट् — the register in which epics tell of long ago. Notice too that
प्रच्छ् "ask" takes the **person asked** as its object: नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ (the
same अकथितं च, 1.4.51, you met with याच्). Everything else is the epic's dense
apposition — तपस्वी (तपस् + विनि), वाग्विदाम् and मुनिपुंगवम् (compounds), वरम्
"the best of…" — all bending toward the one accusative, नारदम्.

source.ref: Pañcatantra 1.42 — the wise man and the king
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; compounds kept whole); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_viSNuzarman-paJcatantra, ||Panc_1.42||)

sequence.sentence: राजानम् एव संश्रित्य विद्वान् याति पराम् गतिम्। विना मलयम् अन्यत्र चन्दनम् न प्ररोहति॥
sequence.translation: Only by taking refuge with a king does the learned man reach the highest station — sandalwood grows nowhere but the Malaya hills.
sequence.teaches:
the gerund of a prefixed root — संश्रित्य "having resorted to," which is
ल्यप् (not क्त्वा) precisely because सम्- is prefixed; and the strong-stem
accusative राजानम्.

notes.en: gerund of सम्-श्रि "resort to, depend on"

notes.role: समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् — when the root carries a prefix (सम्-), the क्त्वा gerund is replaced by ल्यप् (-य) → संश्रि + ल्यप् → संश्रित्य

notes.en: the gerund suffix for prefixed roots

sequence.vyakhya: ल्यबन्तप्रधानः श्लोकः। संश्रित्य इति सोपसर्गात् श्रयतेः क्त्वो ल्यप् (समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप्) — उपसर्गयुक्ते धातौ क्त्वा न, किन्तु ल्यप्। राजानम् इति नकारान्तस्य सर्वनामस्थाने बलवद्रूपम्। विना इति द्वितीयायोगे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The verse turns on one form: **संश्रित्य** "having resorted to." You already
know the gerund क्त्वा (गत्वा, कृत्वा) — but the moment a root takes a prefix,
क्त्वा is replaced by **ल्यप्** (7.1.37, समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप्): सम् +
श्रि → संश्रित्य, not *संश्रित्वा. That -य ending is the mark of every prefixed
gerund (आदाय, विहाय, प्रणम्य). Beside it: राजानम्, the strong-stem accusative
of राजन्, and विना "except," which here governs the accusative मलयम्.

sequence.sentence: पीताम्बरः गुरुः शिष्यैः सह उपवनम् अगच्छत्। ते सर्वे धर्मशास्त्राणि अपठन्। तेषु रामकृष्णौ पटुतमौ आस्ताम्। ज्येष्ठः बालः गुरुम् अपृच्छत् — कः धर्मः इति।
sequence.translation: The yellow-robed teacher went with his pupils to the forest's edge. They all read the treatises on dharma. Among them Rāma and Kṛṣṇa were the cleverest. The eldest boy asked the teacher — "What is dharma?"
sequence.teaches:
the compounds again, and the superlative beside them: पीताम्बरः (बहुव्रीहि),
उपवनम् (अव्ययीभाव), धर्मशास्त्राणि (तत्पुरुष), रामकृष्णौ (द्वन्द्व), and the
तमप्/इष्ठन् pair पटुतमौ, ज्येष्ठः.

notes.en: possessive — neither member is the head; the one whose garment is yellow

notes.role: शेषो बहुव्रीहिः — the remaining kind of compound is बहुव्रीहि
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words denoting ANOTHER thing (the wearer) form a बहुव्रीहि

notes.en: adverbial — उप heads it, and the whole compound is indeclinable

notes.role: अव्ययीभावः — a compound headed by an indeclinable is अव्ययीभाव

notes.en: determinative — शास्त्राणि, the second member, is the head; धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि

notes.text: विग्रह: धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि — "the treatises of dharma"

notes.role: तत्पुरुषः — a compound whose second member carries the main sense is तत्पुरुष
षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (धर्मस्य) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

notes.en: copulative — both members are heads, joined as "and"

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — words standing in the sense of "च" (and) form a द्वन्द्व

notes.en: secondary derivative — पटु + the superlative तमप्
the तमप् superlative suffix — "most" of the whole set
degree of comparison — the superlative sense

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — तमप्/इष्ठन् in the sense of the highest degree; पटु + तमप् → पटुतम

notes.en: secondary derivative — the इष्ठन् superlative on the root-grade
the इष्ठन् superlative suffix — "most" (irregular base, वृद्ध → ज्येष्ठ)
degree of comparison — the superlative sense

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — तमप्/इष्ठन् in the sense of the highest degree

sequence.vyakhya: पञ्च समासा-अतिशायनानि एकस्मिन् दृश्ये — पीताम्बरः, उपवनम्, धर्मशास्त्राणि, रामकृष्णौ, पटुतमौ, ज्येष्ठः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The compound types recur here in a quieter scene, and the superlative sits
among them. पीताम्बरः is a बहुव्रीहि, the one whose robe is yellow — the
teacher, not the colour. उपवनम् is an अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying वन and the whole
going indeclinable. धर्मशास्त्राणि is a तत्पुरुष — धर्मस्य शास्त्राणि, the
treatises of dharma. रामकृष्णौ pairs two names as a द्वन्द्व. And of the pupils
पटुतमौ (पटु + तमप्) and ज्येष्ठः (the इष्ठन् base) name the highest degree —
the same superlative sense in its two suffixes.

source.ref: Manu 4.138 — speak truth, speak kindly
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated per GRETIL's analysis segmentation; every form is Manu's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_manusmRti, Manu_4.138)

sequence.sentence: सत्यम् ब्रूयात् प्रियम् ब्रूयात् न ब्रूयात् सत्यम् अप्रियम्। प्रियम् च न अनृतम् ब्रूयात् एष धर्मः सनातनः॥
sequence.translation: One should speak the truth, one should speak what is kind; one should not speak an unkind truth. And one should not speak a pleasant falsehood — this is the eternal law.
sequence.teaches:
the optative of precept, four times over — ब्रूयात् "one should speak," the
लिङ् of ब्रू; and two नञ्-compounds, अप्रियम् "unkind" and अनृतम्
"untruth," which shows नञ् in its अन्- shape before a vowel.

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — in the sense of precept (विधि), the optative लिङ् → ब्रू + लिङ् → ब्रूयात्
नञ् — the negative नञ् compounds with प्रिय → अप्रिय; before a consonant नञ् appears as अ
नञ् — नञ् + ऋत "truth" → अनृत; before a vowel नञ् takes its अन्- shape → अन् + ऋत

sequence.vyakhya: विध्यर्थलिङ्प्रधानः श्लोकः। ब्रूयात् इति ब्रुवः विधिलिङि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम् (चतुर्वारम्)। अप्रियम् अनृतम् इति नञ्समासौ — व्यञ्जने अ, अचि अन् (अनृतम्)। एष धर्मः सनातनः इति समापने।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The verse is built on a single form repeated four times: **ब्रूयात्** "one
should speak," the optative (लिङ्) of ब्रू in its precept sense (3.3.161).
This is the mood of moral instruction — "one ought." Two नञ्-compounds carry
the balance of the thought: अप्रियम् "unkind" (नञ् as अ- before a consonant)
and अनृतम् "untruth" (नञ् as **अन्-** before the vowel of ऋत). Four clauses,
one rule of conduct: truth, but kind; kindness, but true.

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 0.6 — knowledge gives humility
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_0.6)

sequence.sentence: विद्या ददाति विनयम् विनयात् याति पात्रताम्। पात्रत्वात् धनम् आप्नोति धनात् धर्मम् ततः सुखम्॥
sequence.translation: Knowledge gives humility; from humility one reaches worthiness; from worthiness one gains wealth; from wealth, dharma; and from that, happiness.
sequence.teaches:
a chain of ablatives — विनयात्, पात्रत्वात्, धनात्, each "from ___," the
अपादान case of a source; and the abstract-noun suffixes त्व/तल् (पात्रता,
पात्रत्व, "the state of being fit").

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी — the source from which something proceeds (अपादान) takes the पञ्चमी → विनयात् "from humility"

notes.en: abstract noun — पात्र "fit vessel" + तल् (→ ता) "the state of being fit"

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — the "state/quality of being X" is expressed by त्व or तल् → पात्र + तल् → पात्रता

notes.en: abstract noun — पात्र + त्व, the same "fitness" (neuter)

notes.role: तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ — त्व, the other abstract suffix → पात्र + त्व → पात्रत्व

sequence.vyakhya: पञ्चमीश्रृङ्खला। विनयात् पात्रत्वात् धनात् इति अपादाने पञ्चमी — "अमुष्मात् एतत्" इति। पात्रता पात्रत्वम् इति भावप्रत्ययौ (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ) — तल् स्त्रियाम्, त्वं नपुंसके। श्लोकः सोपानक्रमेण विद्यायाः फलम् आचष्टे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
A ladder built out of **ablatives**. Each rung names a *source*: विनयात्
"from humility," पात्रत्वात् "from worthiness," धनात् "from wealth" — the
अपादान कारक, in the पञ्चमी (2.3.28, "the point one proceeds from"). The verse
also pairs the two **abstract-noun** suffixes of 5.1.119 (तस्य भावस्त्वतलौ):
तल् gives feminine पात्र-ता, त्व gives neuter पात्र-त्व — both "the state of
being a fit vessel." Read it as a single sentence and it is a chain: knowledge
→ humility → worth → wealth → dharma → happiness.

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 1.71 — the whole earth a family
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; वसुधैव kept fused to show the सन्धि); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_1.71)

sequence.sentence: अयम् निजः परः वा इति गणना लघुचेतसाम्। उदारचरितानाम् तु वसुधैव कुटुम्बकम्॥
sequence.translation: 'This one is my own, that one a stranger' — such reckoning belongs to the small-minded. For the noble-hearted, the whole earth is but one family.
sequence.teaches:
the बहुव्रीहि, the possessive compound that points outside itself:
लघुचेतसाम् "of those whose mind is small," उदारचरितानाम् "of those whose
conduct is noble" — neither word names mind or conduct as its subject.

notes.role: अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — several words compound to denote a third thing (the possessor) → लघु + चेतस् → लघुचेतस् "small-minded"
अनेकमन्यपदार्थे — a बहुव्रीहि naming the possessor → उदार + चरित → उदारचरित
वृद्धिरेचि — आ/अ before ए/ओ becomes the वृद्धि vowel → वसुधा + एव → वसुधैव

sequence.vyakhya: बहुव्रीहिप्रधानः सुप्रसिद्धः श्लोकः। लघुचेतसाम् उदारचरितानाम् इति बहुव्रीही (अनेकमन्यपदार्थे) — न चेतः न चरितं मुख्यम्, किन्तु तद्वान् पुरुषः। वसुधैव इति वसुधा-एव इति वृद्धिसन्धिः (वृद्धिरेचि)। षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The verse everyone quotes — and it turns on the **बहुव्रीहि**, the compound
that describes something *outside* its own members. लघुचेतस् does not mean
"small mind"; it means "one whose mind is small" — the person, not the mind,
is what the word points to (2.2.24, अनेकमन्यपदार्थे, "denoting another
thing"). Same with उदारचरित "one whose conduct is noble." Both stand in the
genitive of belonging: the reckoning belongs to the small-minded, the earth-
as-family to the noble. And वसुधैव hides the vṛddhi सन्धि — वसुधा + एव → वसुधैव
(6.1.88).

source.ref: Hitopadeśa 1.14 — the mark of the wise
source.curated: the whole verse, word-separated (pausa forms; compounds kept whole); every form is the text's. From Ambuda's GRETIL edition (ambuda-org/gretil, sa_nArAyaNa-hitopadeza, Hit_1.14)

sequence.sentence: मातृवत् परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु लोष्ट्रवत्। आत्मवत् सर्वभूतेषु यः पश्यति सः पण्डितः॥
sequence.translation: He who looks on others' wives as on a mother, on others' wealth as on a clod of earth, on all beings as on himself — he is the wise one.
sequence.teaches:
the वति suffix — "just like ___": मातृवत् "as (one would toward) a mother,"
लोष्ट्रवत् "like a clod," आत्मवत् "as oneself." One little suffix turns a
noun into an adverb of comparison.

notes.en: adverb of likeness — मातृ "mother" + वति "just as with a ___"

notes.role: तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः — when an action is done "equally with / just as toward" something, वति is added → मातृ + वति → मातृवत्
तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → लोष्ट्र + वति → लोष्ट्रवत् "just as (toward) a clod"
तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः → आत्म + वति → आत्मवत् "just as toward oneself"

sequence.vyakhya: वतिप्रत्ययप्रधानः श्लोकः। मातृवत् लोष्ट्रवत् आत्मवत् इति तुल्यक्रियायां वतिः (तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः) — अव्ययम्। परदारेषु परद्रव्येषु सर्वभूतेषु इति विषयसप्तमी। यः … सः इति नित्यसम्बन्धे।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The verse turns on one suffix: **वति**, "just as with ___." Add it to a noun
and you get an indeclinable adverb of comparison — मातृ-वत् "as (one behaves)
toward a mother," लोष्ट्र-वत् "as toward a clod," आत्म-वत् "as toward oneself"
(5.1.115, तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः, "when the action is equal-to that"). The
locatives परदारेषु / परद्रव्येषु / सर्वभूतेषु are the "in the matter of ___"
sphere-locative, and यः … सः is the relative-correlative frame that holds the
definition together: the one who sees this way *is* the wise one.

sequence.sentence: वाय॒वा या॑हि दर्शते॒मे सोमा॒ अरं॑कृताः। तेषां॑ पाहि श्रु॒धी हवं॑॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, come, beautiful one; these Soma-draughts are made ready — drink of them, hear our call.
sequence.teaches: a new hymn (वायु); the invocation pattern — सम्बोधन (वायो) answered by imperatives (आ याहि, पाहि, श्रुधि)

notes.en: vocative — direct address (उ-stem वायु → वायो, गुण, like गुरो)

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → the vocative; वायो addresses the god
लोट् च — imperative → याहि

words.gloss: O beautiful one, O visible one

notes.en: vocative epithet — addressing Vāyu as "fair to see"
demonstrative pronoun "this" (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सोमाः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → इदम् is a सर्वनाम

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अरम्-कृत; अरम् "enough, fitly" + कृत "made"

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → तद्
षष्ठी शेषे → तेषाम् (drink OF them)
लोट् च → पाहि
लोट् च → श्रुधि
कर्मणि द्वितीया → हवम् ("hear the call")

sequence.vyakhya: वायो इति सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि पाहि श्रुधि इति लोडर्थाः। सोमाः कर्तारः, तेषां पाहि — षष्ठ्यर्थे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new god — but the grammar is the invocation pattern you just met closing hymn 1. वायो is the सम्बोधन (vocative of the उ-stem वायु, गुण → वायो like गुरो), and it is answered by a volley of imperatives (लोट्): आ याहि "come!", पाहि "drink!", श्रुधि "hear!". The Somas (सोमाः, nominative plural) stand ready (अरंकृताः); drink *of them* — तेषाम्, a genitive (षष्ठी) in the partitive sense — and hear the call (हवम्, accusative). The whole verse is address + command, the heartbeat of Vedic prayer.

sequence.sentence: एकदा शशकस्य वारः आगच्छत्। सः बुद्धिमान् शशकः चिरम् विचिन्त्य एकम् उपायम् अकरोत्। सः मन्दम् मन्दम् सिंहस्य समीपम् अगच्छत्। क्रुद्धः सिंहः अपृच्छत् — "किमर्थम् त्वम् विलम्बेन आगतः?" शशकः अवदत् — "मार्गे अन्यः बलवान् सिंहः माम् अरुणत्। सः त्वाम् एव स्वामिनम् न मन्यते।" तत् श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धः सिंहः तम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति स्म।
sequence.translation: One day the rabbit's turn came. That clever rabbit, after thinking for a long time, devised a plan. He went very slowly toward the lion. The angry lion asked — "Why have you come late?" The rabbit said — "On the road another strong lion stopped me. He does not regard you alone as master." Having heard that, the angry lion wished to see him.
sequence.teaches: longer dialogue — किमर्थम् (why?), past participle as predicate (आगतः "have come"), gerund विचिन्त्य + श्रुत्वा, accusative of person stopped (माम् अरुणत्), infinitive of purpose (द्रष्टुम्), मन्यते आत्मनेपद

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → शशकस्य
अनद्यतने लङ् → आगच्छत्

notes.en: gerund (ल्यप् — after prefix वि-) — prior action

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → ल्यप् → विचिन्त्य
अनद्यतने लङ् → अकरोत्
अनद्यतने लङ् → अगच्छत्
निष्ठा → क्त → क्रुद्ध
अनद्यतने लङ् → अपृच्छत्
कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → विलम्बेन

notes.en: past participle (क्त) of आ-गम् as predicate — "(you are) come"

notes.role: निष्ठा → क्त → आगत
अनद्यतने लङ् → अवदत्
सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → मार्गे
सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → अन्यः
अनद्यतने लङ् → अरुणत् (रुध्, 7th class)
भावकर्मणोः — मन् takes आत्मनेपद → मन्यते
समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले क्त्वा → श्रुत्वा
निष्ठा → क्त → क्रुद्ध
तुमुन्ण्वुलौ → द्रष्टुम् (infinitive)

notes.en: the thematic अ between root and ending

sequence.vyakhya: संवादः दीर्घतरः। किमर्थम् इति हेतुप्रश्ने; आगतः इति निष्ठा कर्तरि ("त्वम् आगतः")। माम् अरुणत् इति रुध्-धातोः सप्तमगणे लङ्। स्वामिनम् इति द्विकर्मके मन्यतेः अभिन्ननिर्देशे। द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति तुमुन् इष्-धातुना।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The dialogue lengthens — the trick is told, not just narrated. New touches: किमर्थम् "why? for what purpose?" (the interrogative of cause); the past participle as a finite-like **predicate** — त्वम् … आगतः "you have come" (क्त standing in for "you came/are come"); and a double-accusative with मन्यते — त्वाम् स्वामिनम् न मन्यते "does not regard you AS master," the object and its predicate-complement both accusative. The infinitive द्रष्टुम् इच्छति "wishes to see" closes on the hook that will spring the trap. Everything else is consolidation: four लङ् pasts, two gerunds (विचिन्त्य, श्रुत्वा), locatives, the मतुप् adjectives बलवान्/बुद्धिमान्.

sequence.sentence: वाय॑ उ॒क्थेभि॑र्जरंते॒ त्वामच्छा॑ जरि॒तारः॑। सु॒तसो॑मा अह॒र्विदः॑॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, the singers praise you with hymns — Soma-pressers who know the days.
sequence.teaches: the worshippers named as agents — जरितारः, an ऋ-stem nominative plural — with उक्थेभिः "with hymns" as the means

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो

notes.en: means — that with which they praise

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → उक्थेभिः (तृतीया plural, Vedic -एभिः for -ऐः)
कर्मणि द्वितीया → त्वाम् ("you")

notes.en: indeclinable — "toward" (governs the praising directed AT Vāyu)

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → जरितारः (the agents; an ऋ-stem nom. plural, like कर्तारः)

words.gloss: those who have pressed the Soma

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सुत-सोम; सुत "pressed" + सोम

notes.en: possessive compound — "(those) by whom Soma is pressed"

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अहः-विद्; अहर् "day" + विद् "knowing"

sequence.vyakhya: जरितारः कर्तारः, त्वां कर्म, उक्थेभिः इति करणम्। सुतसोमाः अहर्विदः च तेषां विशेषणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Hymn 1 ended with "we come"; here the worshippers are NAMED — जरितारः, "the singers," the agents (कर्तृ, an ऋ-stem nominative plural like कर्तारः). They praise (जरन्ते, 3rd-person plural) you (त्वाम्, accusative) with hymns (उक्थेभिः) — the तृतीया of means, the same "with/by" you met in नरैः and धिया. Two epithets describe them: सुतसोमाः ("Soma-pressed," a बहुव्रीहि) and अहर्विदः ("day-knowers"). All grammar you hold.

sequence.sentence: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठाम् त्वम् अगमः शाश्वतीः समाः। यत् क्रौञ्चमिथुनाद् एकम् अवधीः काममोहितम्॥
sequence.translation: May you never, O hunter, reach rest for the long years to come — since you killed one of the pair of krauñca birds, deluded by passion.
sequence.teaches:
the first verse of Sanskrit poetry. मा with the aorist forbids — मा … अगमः,
"may you not reach"; अवधीः is the aorist "you killed" of हन्.

notes.en: prohibitive particle — with the aorist, a negative wish/command
aorist — with मा it is the prohibitive ("may you not reach")
duration — "for the years" (the द्वितीया of extent of time)

words.gloss: from the pair of krauñca birds

notes.en: compound — क्रौञ्चयोः मिथुनम्, "the pair of the two krauñcas"
source — the one taken from the pair

notes.role: अपादाने पञ्चमी — the point of separation takes पञ्चमी → क्रौञ्चमिथुनात्

notes.en: aorist — 2nd sg of हन् (the वध्-substitute), "you slew"

sequence.vyakhya: मा निषाद प्रतिष्ठां त्वम् अगमः — यत् क्रौञ्चमिथुनात् एकम् अवधीः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The verse grief wrung from Vālmīki, and with it Sanskrit poetry began. मा
with the aorist is the prohibition: मा … अगमः, "may you never reach"
प्रतिष्ठाम्, a resting place, शाश्वतीः समाः, for the endless years. The reason
follows on यत्: because from the क्रौञ्च-pair (क्रौञ्चमिथुनात्, the ablative of
what one is taken FROM) you killed एकम्, one — अवधीः, the aorist of हन् — while
it was काममोहितम्, lost in love.

sequence.sentence: वायो॒ तव॑ प्रपृंच॒ती धेना॑ जिगाति दा॒शुषे॑। उ॒रू॒ची सोम॑पीतये॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu, your nourishing stream goes to the worshipper, broad, for the Soma-drinking.
sequence.teaches: a feminine subject धेना "stream," तव in the genitive of possession, and two datives — दाशुषे and सोमपीतये, the second one of purpose

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो
षष्ठी शेषे → तव

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्र-पृञ्चती; प्र + पृच् "fill, mingle"

notes.en: present participle (feminine, शतृ + ई) qualifying धेना

notes.role: स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता → धेना (the subject)

notes.en: recipient — to whom the stream goes

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → दाशुषे (the dative you met in hymn 1)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सोम-पीतये; सोम + पीति "drinking"

notes.en: purpose — "for the sake of" (the dative of purpose)

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → सोमपीतये (इ-stem dative, like स्वस्तये)

sequence.vyakhya: तव धेना दाशुषे जिगाति। दाशुषे सोमपीतये च चतुर्थ्यौ — सम्प्रदाने तादर्थ्ये च।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A feminine subject leads: धेना ("stream," an आ-stem feminine like विद्या), with two feminine adjectives agreeing — प्रपृञ्चती ("nourishing") and उरूची ("broad"). It is तव ("yours," genitive) and it जिगाति ("goes") दाशुषे ("to the worshipper," dative). The last word shows a second flavour of the dative: सोमपीतये — *for the purpose of* Soma-drinking. One case (चतुर्थी), two senses: "to whom" (दाशुषे) and "for what" (सोमपीतये).

sequence.sentence: शशकः सिंहम् एकम् कूपम् अनयत्। "अत्र सः शत्रुः वसति" इति सः अवदत्। सिंहः कूपम् अपश्यत्। जले तस्य एव प्रतिबिम्बम् आसीत्, किन्तु सः तत् अन्यम् सिंहम् अमन्यत। क्रुद्धः सः गर्जितुम् आरभत। कूपात् प्रतिशब्दः श्रूयते स्म। तेन सः अतीव अक्रुध्यत्। "अहम् एनम् हनिष्यामि" इति उक्त्वा सः कूपे अपतत्। तत्र मग्नः सिंहः अम्रियत। एवम् बुद्ध्या शशकः सर्वान् मृगान् अरक्षत्। बलम् बुद्धिः च — तयोः बुद्धिः एव श्रेष्ठा।
sequence.translation: The rabbit led the lion to a well. "Your enemy lives here," he said. The lion looked into the well. In the water was his own reflection, but he took it for another lion. Enraged, he began to roar. An echo was heard from the well. At that he grew still angrier. Saying "I will kill him," he leapt into the well. Sunk there, the lion died. Thus by his wit the rabbit saved all the beasts. Strength and intelligence — of the two, intelligence is the better.
sequence.teaches:
the close of the सिंह-शशक story. Eight past verbs against one future —
हनिष्यामि, the thing the lion intends and does not accomplish.

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म — what the agent most aims at is कर्मन् → सिंहम्

notes.en: agent — the same animal as सिंहम् above, now acting
past — the augment अ, and नी takes गुण → नय्
present — inside the quotation, so present rather than past

notes.role: अतोऽम् — the neuter a-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा/द्वितीया → प्रतिबिम्बम्

notes.en: past of अस् — a standing state, against the narrative verbs around it
मन् is आत्मनेपदी — the ending is त, not त्

notes.role: तङानावात्मनेपदम् — the तङ् set is आत्मनेपद → अमन्यत

notes.en: past participle used as an adjective of the agent

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् — the infinitive → गर्जितुम्

notes.en: आ + रभ् takes the middle — आरभत, not आरभत्
source — where the sound came from
what is heard — the passive makes it the nominative subject
the passive विकरण — श्रु + य + ते

notes.role: सार्वधातुके यक् — यक् in the passive → श्रूयते
भावकर्मणोः — the passive takes आत्मनेपद endings → ते

notes.en: with a present verb, स्म makes it narrative past
past — क्रुध् is दिवादि, so श्यन् not शप्; the vowel stays weak
accusative — the enclitic form of एतद्
the future — the lion's boast, in the first person

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → हनिष्यामि

notes.en: gerund — the saying precedes the leaping

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले — क्त्वा for the earlier of two acts → उक्त्वा

notes.en: past participle — the state he was in, not an action he did
मृ takes the middle — a third आत्मनेपद verb in this passage
instrument — what the saving was done by
instrumental — इ-stem, बुद्धि → बुद्ध्या with यण्

notes.role: इको यणचि — इ before a vowel becomes य् → बुद्ध्या
तस्माच्छसो नः पुंसि — the masculine accusative plural → सर्वान्
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → बलम्

notes.en: joined with बुद्धिः by च — two things counted together

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate pair बलम् बुद्धिः च

notes.en: genitive dual — the निर्धारण, selecting from a pair

notes.role: अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ — the superlative इष्ठन् → श्रेष्ठ

sequence.vyakhya: बलवान् सिंहः मृतः, बुद्धिमान् शशकः जीवति। न बलेन, बुद्ध्या जयः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The lion never sees another lion. He sees himself and cannot tell, and the
echo he answers is his own voice returning. The story spends its whole
length on that one joke, and the last line names it: बलम् बुद्धिः च, and
of the two, बुद्धिः.

Nine finite verbs here and eight of them are past — अनयत्, अपश्यत्,
अमन्यत, अक्रुध्यत्, अपतत्, अम्रियत, अरक्षत्, आसीत्. Against them stand
वसति and श्रूयते inside quoted or reported speech, where the present holds,
and हनिष्यामि, the only future in the passage: the one thing the lion
intends and does not accomplish.

sequence.sentence: इंद्र॑वायू इ॒मे सु॒ता उप॒ प्रयो॑भि॒रा ग॑तं। इंद॑वो वामु॒शंति॒ हि॥
sequence.translation: O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed (Somas) are here — come with delights; the drops long for you both.
sequence.teaches: the dual arrives all at once — the paired deity इन्द्रवायू, the imperative आ गतम् "come, you two," and वाम्

notes.en: a dual द्वन्द्व compound — इन्द्र + वायु, two deities as one pair

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः → इन्द्रवायू ("Indra and Vāyu")

notes.en: demonstrative (इदम्), nom. plural agreeing with सुताः

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → इदम्

notes.en: subject — the offerings (past participle of सु "press", used as noun)

words.gloss: with delights, with offerings of joy

notes.text: padapāṭha splits प्रयः-भिः; प्रयस् "delight, dainty" (अस्-stem)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → प्रयोभिः (तृतीया plural)

notes.en: imperative — but DUAL: "come, you two" (मध्यम द्विवचन)
subject (second clause) — the bright drops (उ-stem nom. plural)
object — whom the drops long for

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्रवायू इति द्वन्द्वः द्विवचने; आ गतम् इति द्विवचनलोट्; वाम् इति द्विवचनम्। द्वौ देवौ, द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The DUAL arrives — Sanskrit's third number, for exactly two. The pair इन्द्रवायू is a द्वन्द्व compound ("Indra and Vāyu") in the dual (द्विवचन, 1.4.22), and everything addressed to them is dual too: आ गतम् "come, *you two*" (a dual imperative), and वाम् "you two" (the dual of युष्मद्). Between, सुताः ("the pressed Somas") and इन्दवः ("the drops") are plural subjects. Singular, plural, and now dual — the वचन triad is complete, here in real Vedic.

sequence.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च चेतथः सु॒तानां॑ वाजिनीवसू। तावा या॑त॒मुप॑ द्र॒वत्॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, you two take note of the pressed (Somas), O rich in plenty — come, you both, swiftly.
sequence.teaches: the dual through the whole verse: चेतथः "you two perceive," the epithet वाजिनीवसू, and तौ

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो

notes.en: nominative in form, vocative in sense here — the nom-form joined to वायो by च ("Vāyu and Indra")
genitive plural — that of which they take note

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुतानाम्

words.gloss: O you two rich in plenty

notes.text: padapāṭha splits वाजिनी-वसु; वाजिनी "abundance" + वसु "wealth"

notes.en: vocative DUAL epithet — addressing the pair
pronoun — the DUAL of तद् ("those two / you two")

notes.role: सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि → तद्

notes.en: imperative DUAL — "come, you two" (as आ गतम् in rd020)

sequence.vyakhya: वायुः इन्द्रश्च — द्वौ; चेतथः यातम् इति द्विवचने तिङन्ते। सर्वं द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The dual you just met now drives the VERB. वायो and इन्द्रः, joined by च, are two — so चेतथः ("you two perceive") is a dual finite verb, तौ ("you two") is the dual pronoun, यातम् ("come, you two") the dual imperative, and वाजिनीवसू a dual vocative epithet. Everything addressed to the pair is dual. They take note सुतानाम् — "of the pressed Somas," a partitive genitive (षष्ठी). The whole verse is a drill in द्विवचन.

source.ref: Pañcatantra I — ब्राह्मणः नकुलः च, the mongoose
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit telling of the well-known episode; NOT the verbatim text

sequence.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् ग्रामे एकः ब्राह्मणः वसति स्म। तस्य गृहे एकः नकुलः आसीत्। ब्राह्मणस्य पत्नी बालम् रक्षन्ती गृहे तिष्ठति स्म। एकदा सा जलम् आनेतुम् बहिः अगच्छत्। तस्मिन् काले एकः कृष्णसर्पः बालस्य समीपम् आगच्छत्। तम् दृष्ट्वा नकुलः सर्पेण सह अयुध्यत। तेन सर्पः हतः, नकुलस्य मुखम् च रक्तेन लिप्तम् आसीत्। पत्नी प्रत्यागच्छत्। रक्तानि नकुलस्य मुखे दृष्ट्वा सा अचिन्तयत् — "अनेन मम बालः खादितः" इति। क्रुद्धा सा घटम् तस्य उपरि अक्षिपत्। नकुलः अम्रियत। गृहम् प्रविश्य सा बालम् सुप्तम् अपश्यत्, हतम् सर्पम् च। तदा सा अतीव अरोदीत् — "अहम् मूढा, विचार्य न कृतवती" इति।
sequence.translation: In a certain village there lived a brahmin. In his house was a mongoose. The brahmin's wife, guarding the child, used to stay at home. One day she went out to fetch water. At that time a black snake came near the child. Seeing it, the mongoose fought with the snake. By that the snake was killed, and the mongoose's mouth was smeared with blood. The wife returned. Seeing the blood on the mongoose's mouth, she thought — "My child has been eaten by this one." Enraged, she threw a pot upon him. The mongoose died. Entering the house, she saw the child asleep, and the snake killed. Then she wept bitterly — "I am a fool; I did not act after thinking."
sequence.teaches:
the mongoose story, told in participles. The tragedy turns on one of them:
रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा, seeing the blood, and what the wife concludes from it.

notes.role: स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — कस्मिन् + चित्, the न् going श् before च् → कस्मिंश्चित्

notes.en: locative — the indefinite, with the particle चित्
with a present verb, स्म gives narrative past
present participle, feminine — she guards WHILE staying

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → रक्षन्ती
अतोऽम् — neuter a-stem takes अम् → जलम्

notes.en: infinitive of purpose — why she went out

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् — the infinitive → आनेतुम्

notes.en: locative — the सर्वनाम locative in स्मिन्
adjective + noun in one case — "black snake"
gerund — the seeing precedes the fighting

notes.role: समानकर्तृकयोः पूर्वकाले — क्त्वा for the earlier act → दृष्ट्वा

notes.en: युध् is आत्मनेपदी — the ending is त
what was killed — the participle makes it nominative
past passive participle — no finite verb needed

notes.role: निष्ठा — क्त forms the past participle → हतः
अतोऽम् — the neuter अ-stem takes अम् in प्रथमा and द्वितीया → मुखम्

notes.en: a second past participle, neuter, agreeing with मुखम्
neuter accusative plural — the नुम् before the plural ending

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before शि in the neuter plural → रक्तानि

notes.en: the agent of a passive — the तृतीया of the doer
what was eaten — nominative under the participle
past passive participle — her whole inference rests on it
past participle, feminine, describing her state
the gerund with a preverb takes ल्यप्, not क्त्वा — प्र + विश् → प्रविश्य
past — what she finally sees, after acting
past participle — the child was never in danger
हतः above, now accusative — the snake she never saw
the aorist — the ordinary narrative past

notes.role: लुङ् — the aorist for a completed past act → अरोदीत्

notes.en: a past participle used as a predicate — "I am one deluded"
a second preverbed gerund — वि + चर् → विचार्य
the ACTIVE past participle, feminine — she did it, against खादितः

sequence.vyakhya: रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा सा अमन्यत। दर्शनम् सत्यम्, अनुमानम् मिथ्या।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Everything the wife sees is true. There is blood on the mongoose's mouth.
What she adds is the inference, and the story hangs the whole tragedy on
the gap between them — रक्तानि दृष्ट्वा, seeing the blood, and then
खादितः, "he has been eaten", which she never saw at all.

The participles carry it. हतः, लिप्तम्, सुप्तम्, हतम् are all states
someone else could have verified; खादितः is the one she supplied. And the
last word answers it: कृतवती, the active past participle — not something
done to her, but the thing she did.

sequence.sentence: वाय॒विंद्र॑श्च सुन्व॒त आ या॑त॒मुप॑ निष्कृ॒तं। म॒क्ष्वि१॒॑त्था धि॒या न॑रा॥
sequence.translation: O Vāyu and Indra, come to the presser's prepared (offering), swiftly, even so, through thought, O strong ones.
sequence.teaches: निष्कृतं as the goal they come up to, सुन्वतः as the genitive of the one pressing, and the dual vocative नरा

notes.role: सम्बोधने च → वायो

notes.en: nominative in form, vocative in sense (joined by च)

notes.text: a present participle of सु "press", used as a noun

notes.en: genitive — "of the presser" (whose offering they approach)

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुन्वतः

words.gloss: the prepared place / the readied offering

notes.text: padapāṭha splits निः-कृत; निस् + कृत "made ready"

notes.en: goal of motion — "up to the readied (offering)"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → निष्कृतम् (the goal of गति takes द्वितीया)

notes.en: means — "by thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → धिया

words.gloss: O you two men / strong ones

notes.text: नरा = नरौ — the dual of नर, your very first noun, now in the vocative dual

sequence.vyakhya: सुन्वतः निष्कृतम् उप आ यातम् — गत्यर्थे द्वितीया। नरा इति द्विवचनसम्बोधनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The pair is called again — यातम्, "come, you two" — but now with a goal: उप … निष्कृतम्, "up to the prepared offering," where the goal of motion takes the accusative (द्वितीया, just as a destination does). सुन्वतः ("of the presser") is a genitive: whose offering it is. धिया ("by thought") is the instrumental of means you already hold. And the address नरा is नरौ — the DUAL of नर, the very first noun you ever declined, now standing in the vocative dual.

source.ref: RV 1.2.7 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha)

sequence.sentence: मि॒त्रं हु॑वे पू॒तद॑क्षं॒ वरु॑णं च रि॒शाद॑सं। धियं॑ घृ॒ताचीं॒ साधं॑ता॥
sequence.translation: I call Mitra of pure discernment and Varuṇa the foe-destroyer, who make perfect the lucid thought.
sequence.teaches: Mitra and Varuṇa enter as accusative objects, with हुवे "I call" and the dual participle साधन्ता

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → मित्रम्

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पूत-दक्ष; पूत "purified" + दक्ष "skill, discernment"

notes.en: possessive compound qualifying मित्रम् — "(he) whose दक्ष is pure"
object of साधन्ता — "(who perfect) the thought"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → धियम्

notes.text: a present participle (शतृ) in the DUAL — "the two perfecting"

notes.en: apposed to मित्रम् + वरुणम् (the pair) — accusative dual

sequence.vyakhya: मित्रं वरुणं च हुवे — द्वितीयायाम्। साधन्ता इति द्विवचनं कृदन्तम्, तयोः विशेषणम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new divine pair enters — Mitra and Varuṇa. Here they are OBJECTS: मित्रम् … वरुणम् च, accusatives, "I call (हुवे, 1st-person singular) Mitra and Varuṇa," each with its epithet (पूतदक्षम् "pure-skilled," रिशादसम् "foe-destroying"). They jointly perfect धियं घृताचीम् ("the luminous thought," accusative) — and साधन्ता, "the two who perfect," is a participle in the DUAL, agreeing with the pair. The dual now appears even on a participle.

sequence.sentence: नद्याः तीरे वणिजः वसन्ति स्म। तेषाम् गृहेषु धनम् धान्यम् च आसीत्। एकदा एकः वणिक् दूरम् देशम् गन्तुम् ऐच्छत्। मित्राणि तम् अवदन् — मार्गः दीर्घः, मा गच्छ इति। किन्तु सः अशृणोत् न। श्वः गमिष्यामि इति उक्त्वा सः रात्रौ यानम् असज्जयत्। प्रभाते तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि, नगरम् च त्यक्तम्।
sequence.translation: On the bank of a river lived merchants. In their houses were wealth and grain. One day one merchant wished to go to a distant country. His friends said to him — "The road is long; do not go." But he did not listen. Saying "I will go tomorrow," he made ready a cart in the night. At dawn the friends were left behind by him, and the city too was left.
sequence.teaches:
a merchant leaves against advice. Closes on तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि — two
participles and an instrumental agent, with no finite verb.

notes.en: genitive — the ī of नदी becoming य् before the ending

notes.role: इको यणचि — ई before a vowel becomes य् → नद्याः

notes.en: present with स्म, giving narrative past

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः — the coordinate pair धनम् धान्यम् च

notes.en: nominative singular — the ज् of वणिज् hardens to क् at the word end

notes.role: कर्तुरीप्सिततमं कर्म — what the agent most aims at → देशम्

notes.en: infinitive — what the wishing is aimed at

notes.role: तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम् — the infinitive → गन्तुम्

notes.en: past — the augment अ merging with the इ of इष् to give ऐ
agent — मित्र is neuter even of people

notes.role: नपुंसकस्य झलचः — नुम् before the neuter plural ending → मित्राणि
ससजुषो रुः — the ending स् becomes रु, then visarga → मार्गः

notes.en: the prohibitive — takes a past form without its augment
imperative under मा — a prohibition, not a command
past — श्रु takes श्नु, so the stem is शृणो
the future, first person — inside his own speech

notes.role: लृट् शेषे च — लृट् for the future → गमिष्यामि

notes.en: gerund — the saying before the readying
the agent of a passive participle — instrumental, not nominative
past passive participle, neuter plural agreeing with मित्राणि
what is left stands nominative — no finite verb needed
the same participle, now singular for a single city

sequence.vyakhya: मा गच्छ इति उक्तम्, तथापि सः अगच्छत्। तेन मित्राणि त्यक्तानि।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The last sentence has no finite verb in it. त्यक्तानि and त्यक्तम् are
participles, and they carry the whole statement — the friends left, the
city left, and तेन telling you by whom.

Classical Sanskrit prefers this to a past-tense verb, which is why so much
narrative reads as a chain of participles with the agent in the
instrumental. Once मित्राणि त्यक्तानि stops needing to be translated as a
passive, it starts reading as ordinary past narration.

sequence.translation: By the Truth, O Mitra-Varuṇa, increasers of Truth, touchers of Truth — you two have won a vast will.
sequence.teaches: the द्वन्द्व vocative मित्रावरुणौ, ऋतेन as the means, and आशाथे — a dual verb in the perfect

words.gloss: by the Truth, through cosmic order

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → ऋतेन

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व compound — Mitra + Varuṇa as one pair

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः → मित्रावरुणौ ("Mitra and Varuṇa")

words.gloss: O you two who increase the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-वृध्; ऋत "Truth" + वृध् "increasing"

words.gloss: you two who touch the Truth

notes.text: padapāṭha splits ऋत-स्पृश्; ऋत + स्पृश् "touching"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → क्रतुम् (an उ-stem accusative)

words.gloss: you two have attained, have won

notes.en: perfect — "have won" (the लिट् you met in चकार)

sequence.vyakhya: ऋतेन इति करणम्; मित्रावरुणौ ऋतावृधौ ऋतस्पृशा — द्विवचनसम्बोधनानि; बृहन्तं क्रतुम् आशाथे — लिटि द्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Now Mitra-Varuṇa are ADDRESSED, as a single dual द्वन्द्व: मित्रावरुणौ (vocative dual), with two dual epithets, ऋतावृधौ ("Truth-increasers") and ऋतस्पृशा ("Truth-touchers"). The line opens with ऋतेन — "by the Truth," the instrumental of means. And the verb is new: आशाथे, "you two have attained" — a PERFECT (लिट्, the tense of चकार) in the DUAL. Tense, number, and compound all converge on the pair.

sequence.sentence: क॒वी नो॑ मि॒त्रावरु॑णा तुविजा॒ता उ॑रु॒क्षया॑। दक्षं॑ दधाते अ॒पसं॑॥
sequence.translation: Two seers, Mitra and Varuṇa, of mighty birth, wide-dwelling — they hold for us a working skill.
sequence.teaches: dual nominative epithets — कवी, तुविजाता, उरुक्षया — with the dual verb दधाते and नः in the dative

notes.text: कवी = the DUAL of कवि — "two seers"

notes.role: चतुर्थी सम्प्रदाने → नः

notes.en: dual द्वन्द्व — here NOMINATIVE (the agents), vs vocative in rd024

notes.role: चार्थे द्वन्द्वः → मित्रावरुणा

notes.text: padapāṭha splits तुवि-जात; तुवि "much, mighty" + जात "born"
padapāṭha splits उरु-क्षय; उरु "wide" + क्षय "dwelling"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → दक्षम्

words.gloss: the two hold, the two establish

notes.en: "hold, place" (the दा/धा you met in ददाति)

sequence.vyakhya: कवी मित्रावरुणा तुविजाता उरुक्षया — द्विवचनप्रथमायाम्; नः दक्षम् अपसं दधाते — द्विवचनतिङन्तम्। हिमवत् सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with the pair as SUBJECTS, all in the nominative dual: कवी ("two seers"), मित्रावरुणा (now agents, not addressed), तुविजाता ("mightily born"), उरुक्षया ("wide-dwelling"). They दधाते — "the two hold" — a present DUAL verb of √धा, the same root as ददाति "gives." For us (नः, dative) they hold दक्षम् अपसम् ("a working skill," accusative). You have now read the whole second hymn, and through it drilled the entire dual — noun, pronoun, adjective, participle, and verb across three tenses.

source.ref: the king and the sage's counsel — our own telling
source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

sequence.sentence: कस्मिंश्चित् देशे धनवान् राजा आसीत्। तस्य पिता वृद्धः दरिद्रः च अभवत्। राजा पितरम् न अपश्यत्, न च तम् अस्मरत्। एकदा भगवान् मुनिः सभाम् आगच्छत्। सः राजानम् अवदत् — पितरि भक्तिः एव धर्मः। यः पितरम् त्यजति सः राज्ञः नाम न अर्हति। तत् श्रुत्वा राज्ञा शिरः अवनतम्। ततः सः पितुः गृहम् अगच्छत्, तस्य पादौ च अस्पृशत्।
sequence.translation: In a certain country there was a wealthy king. His father had become old and poor. The king did not look at his father, nor did he remember him. One day the Blessed One, a sage, came to the assembly. He said to the king — "Devotion toward one's father is dharma itself. He who abandons his father does not deserve the name of king." Having heard that, the king's head was bowed. Then he went to his father's house, and touched his feet.
sequence.teaches:
a king who forgets his father. पितृ appears in four cases across the
story — पिता, पितरम्, पितरि, पितुः.

sequence.vyakhya: पिता पितरम् पितरि पितुः — चतुर्षु स्थानेषु एकः जनः।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
One man, four shapes: पिता when he is named, पितरम् when the king fails to
look at him, पितरि when devotion is owed toward him, पितुः when his house
is meant. Nothing about the father changes across the story.

The king does the same — राजा, राजानम्, राज्ञः, राज्ञा — and the last of
those, राज्ञा शिरः अवनतम्, has no finite verb: a participle and an
instrumental agent, which is how classical narrative most often reports
what someone did.
