sequence.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ यज्व॑री॒रिषो॒ द्रव॑त्पाणी॒ शुभ॑स्पती। पुरु॑भुजा चन॒स्यतं॑॥
sequence.translation: O Aśvins, swift-handed lords of bliss, take pleasure in the worshipper's offerings, you of many bounties.
sequence.teaches: the Aśvins addressed as a pair in the vocative, with इषः as accusative plural and the dual imperative चनस्यतम् "take pleasure, you two"

notes.text: अश्विना = the dual of अश्विन् — the two horsemen-gods, addressed as a pair

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → इषः (acc. pl.)

शुभः (gen.) + पती (dual of पति) — "lords of welfare/bliss"

words.gloss: O you of many enjoyments, much-bestowing

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-भुजा; पुरु "much" + भुज "enjoying, bestowing"

notes.en: "take delight in" (denominative) — here addressed to the pair
2nd person — DUAL imperative ("you two, take pleasure")

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → चनस्यतम्

sequence.vyakhya: अश्विना — सम्बोधने द्विवचनम्; यज्वरीः इषः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती पुरुभुजा — सम्बोधनद्विवचनविशेषणानि; चनस्यतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: A new hymn, a new dual pair: the अश्विन्s, the twin horsemen, addressed throughout in the dual vocative — अश्विना, द्रवत्पाणी ("swift-handed"), शुभस्पती ("lords of bliss"), पुरुभुजा ("of many bounties"). They are asked to चनस्यतम् — "take pleasure, you two" — a DUAL imperative (लोट्), the same dual-of-command you met as आ गतम् in rd020. What they enjoy is यज्वरीः इषः, "the worshipper's offerings," an accusative PLURAL object (कर्मन्). The dual you drilled across RV 1.2 now carries to a fresh pair.

sequence.sentence: अश्वि॑ना॒ पुरु॑दंससा॒ नरा॒ शवी॑रया धि॒या। धिष्ण्या॒ वन॑तं॒ गिरः॑॥
sequence.translation: O Aśvins of many deeds, O heroes, with your forceful thought, attentive ones, win our songs of praise.
sequence.teaches: धिया "by thought" as करण, गिरः as accusative plural, and नरा — the same नर of the opening sentences, here in its Vedic dual

notes.text: padapāṭha splits पुरु-दंससा; पुरु "much" + दंसस् "deed, wondrous act"
नरा = नरौ, the DUAL of नर — the very first noun you declined, now vocative in the hymn

notes.en: instrument — "by means of thought" (the धिया you met in rd014)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → धिया
लोट् च → imperative → वनतम्

notes.en: object — what they are to win

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → गिरः (acc. pl.)

sequence.vyakhya: अश्विना नरा धिष्ण्या — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; शवीरया धिया — तृतीयैकवचनं करणे; गिरः — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि; वनतम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The Aśvins again, addressed as नरा — which is नरौ, the dual of नर, the first noun this whole reader ever declined, now standing in a Vedic hymn. They are to वनतम् ("win, you two," dual imperative) the गिरः, "songs of praise" (accusative plural object). The means is शवीरया धिया, "with forceful thought" — an INSTRUMENTAL (करण, तृतीया), the same धी "thought" you met as धिया in rd014. One verse braids three threads you already hold: the dual address, the accusative object, and the instrument of means.

sequence.sentence: राजा वनम् गच्छन् एकम् मुनिम् अपश्यत्। मुनिः वृक्षस्य अधः उपविशन् शिष्यान् अवदत् — कर्तव्यम् धर्मम् जानीत। राज्ञः भ्राता अपि तत्र आसीत्। सः पितुः वचनम् स्मरन् मुनिम् अपृच्छत् — किम् मया करणीयम्। मुनिः अवदत् — भ्रातरम् रक्ष, राजानम् सेव, पितरम् च मा त्यज। एतत् त्रयम् सर्वदा स्मरणीयम्। तत् श्रुत्वा भ्रातरौ शान्तौ अभवताम्।
sequence.translation: The king, going to the forest, saw a sage. The sage, sitting beneath a tree, said to his students — "Know the dharma that is to be done." The king's brother was there too. He, remembering his father's words, asked the sage — "What is to be done by me?" The sage said — "Protect your brother, serve the king, and do not abandon your father. These three are always to be remembered." Having heard that, the two brothers became calm.
sequence.teaches:
three participles doing the work of "while" — गच्छन्, उपविशन्, स्मरन् —
and three gerundives stating obligation with no verb: कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्,
स्मरणीयम्.

sequence.vyakhya: गच्छन् उपविशन् स्मरन् — त्रीणि शतृ-रूपाणि। कर्तव्यम् करणीयम् स्मरणीयम् — त्रीणि कृत्य-रूपाणि।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Three participles here do what English does with "while": राजा वनम् गच्छन्
is "the king, as he went to the forest". None of them is the sentence's
main verb, and none needs a conjunction.

Then three gerundives state obligation without any verb at all —
कर्तव्यम्, करणीयम्, स्मरणीयम्. Two different affixes, तव्य and अनीयर्,
with no difference in sense; a writer picks whichever fits the line.
किम् मया करणीयम् is the whole question: what, by me, is to-be-done.

source.ref: RV 1.3.3 (whole ṛc; saṃhitā + padapāṭha) — closes the Aśvins triplet

sequence.sentence: दस्रा॑ यु॒वाक॑वः सु॒ता नास॑त्या वृ॒क्तब॑र्हिषः। आ या॑तं रुद्रवर्तनी॥
sequence.translation: O wondrous Nāsatyas, the pressed soma-draughts are yours, the sacred grass is strewn — come, O you whose path is Rudra's.
sequence.teaches: dual-nominative predicates — युवाकवः, सुता, वृक्तबर्हिषः — closing on आ यातम् "come, you two"

notes.en: vocative dual — the Aśvins as "wondrous ones"

notes.text: युवाकु "directed toward you two" — derived from युवाम् (you two)

notes.en: predicate adjective of the soma — "yearning for you"

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press" — the pressed soma

notes.en: vocative dual — a name of the Aśvins

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — the same आ यातम् of rd020

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → यातम्

words.gloss: O you whose path is Rudra's

notes.text: padapāṭha splits रुद्र-वर्तनी; रुद्र + वर्तनि "track, path"

sequence.vyakhya: दस्रा नासत्या रुद्रवर्तनी — सम्बोधनद्विवचनम्; युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — प्रथमायां प्रत्ययनामानि; आ यातम् — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषद्विवचनम्। अश्विसूक्तं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The triplet to the Aśvins closes with a NOMINATIVE string describing the offering: युवाकवः सुताः वृक्तबर्हिषः — "the pressed (soma), yearning for you, with sacred grass strewn." These are predicates: the rite is ready. The pair, addressed as दस्रा ("wondrous"), नासत्या ("truthful"), रुद्रवर्तनी ("of Rudra's path"), are bidden आ यातम् — "come, you two" — the very dual imperative you first met as आ गतम् in rd020. The Aśvin hymn is complete.

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि चित्रभानो सु॒ता इ॒मे त्वा॒यवः॑। अण्वी॑भि॒स्तना॑ पू॒तासः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra of bright splendour — these pressed (soma-draughts) are longing for you, purified through the fine (filter), in continuous flow.
sequence.teaches: the address turns singular: after the dual Aśvins, Indra alone — vocative इन्द्र and the singular imperative आ याहि, against the dual आ यातम् just before

notes.en: vocative SINGULAR — one god now addressed, not a pair
singular (contrast the dual अश्विना of rd026)
"go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as the dual आ यातम्
2nd person — SINGULAR imperative ("you, come"), vs dual यातम्

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → याहि

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चित्र-भानो; चित्र "bright" + भानु "radiance"
सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press"
त्वायु "yearning toward you" — built on त्वा (you, acc.)

notes.en: predicate adjective of सुताः — "(the draughts) longing for you"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → अण्वीभिः

notes.text: पूत = क्त-participle of पू "purify"; -आसः = Vedic nom. pl.

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र चित्रभानो — सम्बोधने एकवचनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम् (द्विवचनयातमः प्रतियोगि); सुताः इमे त्वायवः पूतासः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; अण्वीभिः तना — तृतीया करणे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn turns from the pair to a single god, and the grammar turns with it: इन्द्र is a SINGULAR vocative, and he is bidden आ याहि — "come!" — a 2nd-person SINGULAR imperative, exactly the dual आ यातम् of rd028 with one fewer. Hold the two side by side: यातम् = "come, you two," याहि = "come, you one." The soma is described in a nominative string (सुताः … त्वायवः … पूतासः, "pressed … longing for you … purified"), strained अण्वीभिः, "through the fine filter" (instrumental of means). The dual you drilled all through RV 1.2 now has its singular foil.

sequence.sentence: नद्याः तीरे तिष्ठन् राजा दूरात् आगच्छन्तम् भ्रातरम् अपश्यत्। भ्राता श्रान्तः आसीत्। राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् इति मन्त्री अवदत्। राजा स्वयम् जलम् अददात्। पिता तत् पश्यन् अवदत् — एतत् एव राज्ञः कर्म, न अन्यत्। स्मरणीयम् एतत् सर्वैः।
sequence.translation: Standing on the bank of a river, the king saw his brother coming from afar. The brother was tired. The minister said that water was to be given by the king. The king himself gave water. The father, seeing that, said — "This alone is a king's work, not anything else. This is to be remembered by all."
sequence.teaches:
three participles set against three finite verbs, with two gerundives in
between: दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम्, both stating obligation with no verb.

what is to be given — nominative under the gerundive
gerundive — obligation, with no finite verb

sequence.vyakhya: तिष्ठन् आगच्छन्तम् पश्यन् — शतृ। दातव्यम् स्मरणीयम् — कृत्य। क्रिया अन्यथा अपि उच्यते।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
Six of the words here would be verbs in English and are not. तिष्ठन्,
आगच्छन्तम् and पश्यन् are participles; दातव्यम् and स्मरणीयम् are
gerundives. Only अपश्यत्, आसीत्, अवदत् and अददात् are finite.

राज्ञा जलम् दातव्यम् has no verb at all — an instrumental agent, a
nominative object, and a word meaning "to-be-given". Sanskrit says a great
deal this way, and it reads as ordinary statement once it stops being
turned into an English passive.

sequence.sentence: ग्रामे कुलालः वसन् घटान् अकरोत्। एकदा राज्ञः भ्राता तम् ग्रामम् आगच्छत्। कुलालम् कार्यम् कुर्वन्तम् दृष्ट्वा सः अवदत् — मम गृहे शतम् घटाः स्थापनीयाः। कुलालः अवदत् — कर्तव्यम् एतत्, किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्। भ्राता हसन् अवदत् — पिता मे राजा आसीत्, अहम् न मूल्यम् ददामि। कुलालः अवदत् — तर्हि घटाः न सन्ति। तत् श्रुत्वा भ्राता लज्जितः अभवत्।
sequence.translation: In a village a potter lived, making pots. One day the king's brother came to that village. Seeing the potter doing his work, he said — "A hundred pots are to be placed in my house." The potter said — "This is to be done, but the price is to be given." The brother, laughing, said — "My father was a king; I do not give a price." The potter said — "Then there are no pots." Having heard that, the brother was ashamed.
sequence.teaches:
a potter refuses a prince. Four participles and three gerundives against
six finite verbs; पिता and भ्राता carry their ऋ-stem grades through it.

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → वसन्

notes.en: past — कृ is तनादि, taking उ rather than शप्
the weak stem — the अ drops before a vowel ending

notes.role: नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य — the stem-final न् is gone → राज्ञ्

notes.en: strong nom.sg — the ऋ lengthens to आ

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण of the ऋ-stem in the strong cases → भ्राता

notes.en: present participle in the accusative, qualifying कुलालम्

notes.role: लटः शतृशानचौ — शतृ replaces लट् → कुर्वन्तम्

notes.en: gerund — the seeing before the speaking
what is to be placed — nominative under the gerundive

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — अनीयर् forms the gerundive → स्थापनीयाः

notes.en: a second gerundive, the potter agreeing

notes.role: तव्यत्तव्यानीयरः — तव्य forms the gerundive → कर्तव्यम्

notes.en: a third gerundive — the potter's condition
strong nom.sg of an ऋ-stem, like भ्राता

notes.role: ऋतो ङिसर्वनामस्थानयोः — गुण in the strong cases → पिता

sequence.vyakhya: कर्तव्यम् एतत्, किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्। द्वे कृत्ये, द्वौ पक्षौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The potter's answer is two gerundives and nothing else: कर्तव्यम् एतत्,
किन्तु मूल्यम् दातव्यम्. He concedes the work and states his condition in
the same construction the prince used to give the order.

That is what makes it a refusal rather than a complaint. स्थापनीयाः was an
instruction; दातव्यम् answers it in kind.

sequence.sentence: शिष्यः वनम् अगच्छत्। तत्र सः फलानि अभक्षयत्, जलम् च अपिबत्। सायम् गुरुः अपृच्छत् — कुत्र आसीः। शिष्यः अवदत् — वने आसम्, गुरो। तत् श्रुत्वा गुरुः अवदत् — पठनम् एव तव कार्यम्, न तु वनगमनम्। शिष्यः अवदत् — क्षमस्व, अद्य प्रभृति पठेयम्। रामेण अपि तत् श्रुतम्, सः च अहसत्।
sequence.translation: The student went to the forest. There he ate fruits and drank water. In the evening the teacher asked — "Where were you?" The student said — "I was in the forest, teacher." Hearing that, the teacher said — "Studying alone is your work, not going to the forest." The student said — "Forgive me; from today I will study." Rāma too heard that, and he laughed.
sequence.teaches:
two action-nouns set against each other — पठनम् and वनगमनम् — and the
optative पठेयम् answering the teacher. अभक्षयत् and अपिबत् carry the
narrative; तच्छ्रुत्वा shows श्चुत्व at the join.

notes.en: past of अस्, second person — आसम् answers it below

notes.role: ल्युट् च — ल्युट् makes the neuter action-noun → पठनम्

words.gloss: work, what is to be done

notes.en: वनं गमनम् — the goal compounded onto the action-noun

notes.role: ल्युट् च — a second ल्युट् noun, here inside a compound → गमनम्

notes.en: the optative — a resolve, answering the teacher

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → पठेयम्

notes.en: the agent of a passive participle

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व across the intervening ए → रामेण

notes.en: the aorist — a single completed act, closing the scene

notes.role: लुङ् — the aorist for a completed past act → अहसत्

sequence.vyakhya: पठनम् वनगमनम् च — द्वे क्रियानाम्नी। एकम् कार्यम्, अन्यत् न।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
पठनम् and वनगमनम् are the same kind of word — an act named as a thing —
and the teacher sets one against the other. Sanskrit can compound the goal
straight into the noun: वनं गमनम् becomes वनगमनम्, going-to-the-forest, in
one word.

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि धि॒येषि॒तो विप्र॑जूतः सु॒ताव॑तः। उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि वा॒घतः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra, urged on by the thought, hastened by the seers — up to the prayers of the soma-pressing worshipper.
sequence.teaches: आ याहि again in the singular, उप governing ब्रह्माणि "the prayers" as its goal, and धिया as the means

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → याहि

notes.en: instrument — "urged BY the thought" (the धी met in rd027)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → धिया

notes.text: इषित = क्त-participle of इष् "impel" — "(you,) urged on"
padapāṭha splits विप्र-जूतः; विप्र "inspired seer" + जूत "sped, urged"

words.gloss: of the soma-presser, of him who has pressed (soma)

notes.text: सुतावत् = सुत "pressed soma" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"

notes.en: preverb — "toward," directing the motion to ब्रह्माणि
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ब्रह्माणि (neut. acc. pl.)

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the reciter

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धिया — तृतीया करणे; इषितः विप्रजूतः — क्तान्तविशेषणे; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया कर्मणि गत्यर्थे; सुतावतः वाघतः — षष्ठी सम्बन्धे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The same call — आ याहि, "come" — but now Indra is moved BY something and moves TO something. He is धिया इषितः, "urged on by the thought" (instrumental of means, the धी you met as धिया in rd027), and विप्रजूतः, "hastened by the seers." Where to? उप ब्रह्माणि वाघतः — "up to the prayers of the worshipper," where उप is a preverb steering the verb of motion onto an accusative goal (ब्रह्माणि), and वाघतः is a genitive ("of the worshipper"). Means in the instrumental, goal in the accusative, possession in the genitive — three cases you hold, in one line of the Veda.

sequence.sentence: इंद्रा या॑हि॒ तूतु॑जान॒ उप॒ ब्रह्मा॑णि हरिवः। सु॒ते द॑धिष्व न॒श्चनः॑॥
sequence.translation: Come, O Indra, hastening, up to the prayers, O lord of the bay steeds; at the pressing take delight in us.
sequence.teaches: सुते "at the pressing" as a locative of occasion, the middle imperative दधिष्व "take, for yourself," and नः in the dative

notes.en: 2nd person — singular imperative (third time in the triplet)

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → याहि

notes.text: तूतुजान = perfect middle participle of तुज् "speed" — "(you,) hastening"

notes.en: preverb directing motion to ब्रह्माणि (as in rd030)
goal of motion — "(come) up to the prayers"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → ब्रह्माणि (neut. acc. pl.)

words.gloss: O lord of the bay steeds

notes.text: हरिवत् = हरि "bay horse" + मतुप् (वत्) "possessing"; here vocative हरिवः

words.gloss: at the pressing, when (the soma) is pressed

notes.text: सुत = क्त-participle of सु "press," here LOCATIVE — "at the pressed (soma)"

notes.role: सप्तम्यधिकरणे च → अधिकरण → सुते

notes.en: "hold, place, take" — the same √धा of दधाते (rd025), here MIDDLE imperative
2nd person — singular MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative "take for yourself"

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → दधिष्व

notes.en: for us / in us — the enclitic नः
object — "take delight" (the चन- of चनस्यतम्, rd026, now as a noun)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → चनः

sequence.vyakhya: इन्द्र हरिवः — सम्बोधनम्; आ याहि — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषैकवचनम्; उप ब्रह्माणि — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे; सुते — सप्तमी अधिकरणे; दधिष्व — लोटि आत्मनेपदम्; नः चनः — आत्मने ग्रहणम्। इन्द्रसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The third and last call to Indra adds one new case: सुते, a LOCATIVE — "at the pressing," the occasion when the soma is pressed (अधिकरण, सप्तमी, by 2.3.36). The verb दधिष्व is √धा again — the root of दधाते "the two hold" in rd025 — but here a MIDDLE (आत्मनेपद) imperative, "take FOR YOURSELF," carrying delight (चनः, the noun of the very चनस्यतम् "take pleasure" that opened the hymn in rd026). The triplet to Indra is complete: three times "come," each adding a case — instrument, goal, and now occasion.

sequence.sentence: नगरे धनवान् वणिक् वसति स्म। सः चिन्तयत् — किम् मया कर्तव्यम्, केन मम जीवनम् सफलम् भवेत्। एकः मुनिः अवदत् — दानम् कुरु। तत् श्रुत्वा वणिक् दरिद्रेभ्यः अन्नम् अयच्छत्। तस्य दानेन बहवः जनाः अतुष्यन्। रामेण तत् दृष्टम्, सः च अवदत् — एतत् एव धर्मस्य आचरणम्।
sequence.translation: In a city there lived a wealthy merchant. He thought — "What should I do? By what would my life be fruitful?" A sage said — "Practise giving." Hearing that, the merchant gave food to the poor. By his giving many people were satisfied. Rāma saw that, and said — "This alone is the practice of dharma."
sequence.teaches:
दानम्, दानेन and आचरणम् name acts as things across one story. भवेत् asks
what would make a life fruitful; रामेण closes with णत्व across the ए.

notes.en: the strong form — नुम् inserted, then lengthening
nominative — the ज् of वणिज् hardens to क् at the word end
neuter nominative — the subject of the gerundive
the agent of a gerundive stands in the instrumental
gerundive — the whole predicate, with no verb
an action-noun used as an ordinary noun — the living, hence the life

notes.role: ल्युट् च — the neuter भाव action-noun → जीवनम्

notes.en: the sense 'having fruit' — describing the life, not naming a fruit
the optative — what would be the case, not what is

notes.role: विधिनिमन्त्रण… लिङ् — the optative → भवेत्

notes.en: the act named as a thing
imperative — an instruction, against भवेत् above
cause — the same action-noun, now the reason
past plural — तुष् is दिवादि, so श्यन्
the agent of a passive participle

notes.role: अट्कुप्वाङ्नुम्व्यवायेऽपि — णत्व reaches across the ए → रामेण

notes.en: a third action-noun — the practising, from आ + चर्

notes.role: ल्युट् च — the neuter भाव action-noun → आचरणम्

sequence.vyakhya: जीवनम् दानम् आचरणम् — त्रीणि क्रियानामानि एकस्याम् कथायाम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
जीवनम्, दानम्, आचरणम् — three acts named as things, and the story turns on
treating them that way. A life can be fruitful, a giving can satisfy people,
a practice can be pointed at. None of them needs a verb.

sequence.sentence: ओमा॑सश्चर्षणीधृतो॒ विश्वे॑ देवास॒ आ ग॑त। दा॒श्वांसो॑ दा॒शुषः॑ सु॒तं॥
sequence.translation: O helpers, upholders of men, O All-Gods, come — you bestowers, to the soma of the worshipper.
sequence.teaches: the address turns plural — after the dual Aśvins and Indra alone, the All-Gods as a crowd: विश्वे देवासः in the vocative plural, and आ गत "come, you all"

notes.text: ओमास् = Vedic nom./voc. pl. of ओमन् "helper, friend"

notes.en: vocative PLURAL — a whole company addressed
plural (contrast dual अश्विना rd026, singular इन्द्र rd029)

notes.text: padapāṭha splits चर्षणि-धृतः; चर्षणि "men, peoples" + धृत् "holding, upholding"

notes.en: "all" — qualifying देवासः, the standard epithet विश्वे देवाः "All-Gods"

notes.text: देवासः = Vedic voc./nom. pl. of देव (classical देवाः)

notes.en: "go, come" (with आ → "come hither") — same root as आ गतम् (dual, rd020)
2nd person — PLURAL imperative ("you all, come"), vs dual गतम्, sg याहि

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → गत

notes.text: दाश्वस् = perfect active participle of दाश् "give, worship" — "having given"

words.gloss: of the worshipper, of the giver

notes.text: दाशुषः = genitive sg of the SAME दाश्वस् stem — here "of the (human) worshipper"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्

sequence.vyakhya: ओमासः चर्षणीधृतः विश्वे देवासः दाश्वांसः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; आ गत — लोटि मध्यमपुरुषबहुवचनम्; दाशुषः — षष्ठी; सुतम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The number completes its circle. RV 1.3 has now addressed a DUAL (the Aśvins, आ यातम्), a SINGULAR (Indra, आ याहि), and here a PLURAL — विश्वे देवासः, "all the gods," a whole company, bidden आ गत, "come, you all." Set the three imperatives of √गम्/√या side by side: यातम् (two), याहि (one), गत (many). Every vocative here is plural too — ओमासः, चर्षणीधृतः, दाश्वांसः. They come दाशुषः सुतम्, "to the worshipper's pressed soma" (genitive + accusative goal). One hymn has now drilled the entire तीन वचन.

source.curated: our simple Sanskrit; not from any single source

sequence.sentence: अद्य दूतः नगरम् अगमत्। सः राज्ञः पुरतः अवादीत् — शत्रवः सेनाम् अनयन्, ग्रामान् च अदहन्। राजा तत् अश्रौषीत्, क्षणम् च तूष्णीम् आसीत्। ततः सः अवादीत् — यत् त्वया उक्तम् तत् सत्यम् चेत्, अहम् अद्य एव सेनाम् प्रेषयामि। मन्त्री अवदत् — देव, धैर्यम् एव बलम्। राजा अकार्षीत् यत् मन्त्री अवदत्।
sequence.translation: Today a messenger went to the city. He spoke before the king — "The enemies led out an army, and burned the villages." The king heard that, and was silent a moment. Then he spoke — "If what has been said by you is true, I send the army this very day." The minister said — "Your majesty, steadiness alone is strength." The king did what the minister said.
sequence.teaches:
अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अकार्षीत् — four aorists, the past of what
happened today. शत्रवः and राज्ञः show the visarga taking a sibilant and
a stop; तूष्णीम् holds its ष् unchanged.

notes.en: indeclinable — it is what makes the aorist the right past here
aorist — the plain past, and the past used of today's events

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अगमत्

notes.en: genitive — the न् of राजन् drops before the ending

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the ending's स् shows as visarga at the pause

notes.en: aorist of √वद् — the root vowel lengthens, इट् and सिच् follow

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अवादीत्

notes.en: nominative plural of a उ-stem — उ goes to अव् before the ending

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — final स् → visarga → शत्रवः

notes.en: past — beside the aorists, the ordinary narrative past
nominative — the न्-stem lengthens and loses its final न्
aorist of √श्रु — the उ takes वृद्धि before सिच्

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अश्रौषीत्
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the सिच् स् goes ष् after the ओ → अश्रौषीत्

notes.en: indeclinable — its ष् belongs to the word, not to a join

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of ततस् → visarga at the pause

notes.en: aorist — the second time, now beginning the king's own speech
agent of a passive participle — instrumental
neuter nominative — predicate, with no verb
indeclinable — it never stands first in its clause
indeclinable — it emphasises the word before it
present, first singular — a present used for what is settled now
nominative of an इन्-stem — the ending drops, the इ lengthens
aorist of √कृ — वृद्धि in the root, then सिच्

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अकार्षीत्

sequence.vyakhya: अद्येति लुङः निमित्तम्। अगमत् अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् अकार्षीत् इति चत्वारः लुङः। अनयन् अदहन् अवदत् इति लङः, तयोः भेदः कालमात्रे। यत् त्वया उक्तम् इति भावे क्तम्, त्वयेति कर्तरि तृतीया। चेदिति न वाक्यादौ तिष्ठति।
sequence.vyakhya_en: अद्य sets the tense: four verbs here are aorists — अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अकार्षीत् — and three are the ordinary past in लङ् — अनयन्, अदहन्, अवदत्. The two sit side by side in one paragraph, so the difference is a matter of what the sentence is doing rather than of what happened. अश्रौषीत् shows the ष् of सिच् after वृद्धि, while तूष्णीम् carries a ष् that no join produced. यत् त्वया उक्तम् puts the agent in the instrumental and the verb in a participle — the clause has no finite verb at all, and तत् सत्यम् answers it with none either.

sequence.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒प्तुरः॑ सु॒तमा गं॑त॒ तूर्ण॑यः। उ॒स्रा इ॑व॒ स्वस॑राणि॥
sequence.translation: O All-Gods, crossing the waters, swift, come to the soma — like cattle to their pastures.
sequence.teaches: the plural imperative again in आ गन्त, and a simile with इव — "like cattle to their pastures," a locative of goal inside a comparison

notes.text: padapāṭha splits अप्-तुरः; अप् "waters" + तुर् "crossing, speeding"

notes.en: goal of motion — "(come) to the soma"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → सुतम्
लोट् च → imperative → गन्त

words.gloss: like cows, like the ruddy cattle

notes.text: उस्राः "cattle" (nom. pl.) + इव "like" — the subject of the simile

notes.en: standard of comparison — "as cattle (come to pastures)"

words.gloss: to the pastures, to the home-stalls

notes.en: goal within the simile — "(as cattle come) to the pastures"

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → स्वसराणि (neut. acc. pl.)

sequence.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अप्तुरः तूर्णयः — सम्बोधनबहुवचनम्; सुतम् आ गन्त — द्वितीया गत्यर्थे लोटि बहुवचनम्; उस्राः इव स्वसराणि — उपमा (इव), द्वितीया गत्यर्थे।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The plural call repeats — सुतम् आ गन्त, "come to the soma, all of you" — but the verse closes with a SIMILE: उस्राः इव स्वसराणि, "like cattle (coming) to their pastures." इव "like" marks the comparison; उस्राः ("cattle") is the standard (nominative), and स्वसराणि ("pastures") is its accusative goal, mirroring सुतम्, the gods' own goal. The grammar of the simile is the grammar of the main clause — a goal-of-motion accusative in both halves. As cattle to the fold, so the gods to the soma.

sequence.sentence: द्वौ भ्रातरौ क्षेत्रम् अभजेताम्। ज्येष्ठः अवादीत् — अद्य अहम् अर्धम् अगृह्णाम्, त्वम् च अर्धम् गृहाण। कनिष्ठः तत् अश्रौषीत्, किन्तु न अतुष्यत्। सः ग्रामस्य वृद्धान् अपृच्छत् — केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता। वृद्धाः अवादिषुः — यः स्वयम् विभजति सः न स्वयम् गृह्णाति। तत् श्रुत्वा ज्येष्ठः लज्जितः अभूत्, कनिष्ठाय च वरम् अर्धम् अददात्।
sequence.translation: Two brothers divided a field. The elder spoke — "Today I have taken half; you take the other half." The younger heard that, but was not satisfied. He asked the village elders — "By whom was this land divided?" The elders spoke — "He who divides himself does not himself take." Hearing that, the elder became ashamed, and gave the better half to the younger.
sequence.teaches:
अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अवादिषुः, अभूत् — the aorist across three persons and
both numbers. विभक्ता names the act as done; वृद्धाः and अवादिषुः close on
visarga at the pause.

past, third dual — आत्मनेपद, the act done for their own sake
nominative — the superlative of वृद्ध, used as a noun

आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the सिच् स् goes ष् after the ओ

aorist of √भू — no सिच्, the root stands bare before the ending

sequence.vyakhya: लुङः चत्वारि रूपाणि — अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् इति प्रथमपुरुषे एकवचनम्, अवादिषुः इति बहुवचनम्, अभूत् इति भू-धातोः अपुसीयम्। ज्येष्ठः कनिष्ठः इति इष्ठन्प्रत्ययान्तौ। केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता इति कर्मणि क्तम्, कर्तरि तृतीया।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The aorist widens here: अवादीत् and अश्रौषीत् are third singular, अवादिषुः is third plural of the same verb as अवादीत्, and अभूत् is √भू with no सिच् at all — the ending sits straight on the root. ज्येष्ठः and कनिष्ठः are the same suffix इष्ठन् on two opposed adjectives, and they carry the whole plot between them. केन एषा भूमिः विभक्ता asks the question with a participle and an instrumental agent, and the elders answer with a present-tense generality rather than a fact about this field.

sequence.sentence: विश्वे॑ दे॒वासो॑ अ॒स्रिध॒ एहि॑मायासो अ॒द्रुहः॑। मेधं॑ जुषंत॒ वह्न॑यः॥
sequence.translation: The All-Gods, unfailing, of ever-approaching power, free of malice — may they, the bearers (of sacrifice), enjoy the offering.
sequence.teaches: the verse turns from address to statement: the gods now stand in the nominative, and जुषन्त "may they enjoy" closes the hymn on a wish

notes.en: "all" — now NOMINATIVE (the gods as subject, not addressed)

notes.text: देवासः — here NOMINATIVE (subject), not vocative as in rd032-033
अ-स्रिध् "not failing" (privative अ + स्रिध् "err")

words.gloss: of ever-approaching power, whose wisdom comes near

notes.text: padapāṭha splits एहि-मायासः; एहि "come!" + माया "power, wisdom" — bahuvrīhi
अ-द्रुह् "not hostile" (privative अ + द्रुह् "harm")

notes.en: object — what they are to enjoy

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → मेधम्

words.gloss: may they enjoy, let them take pleasure in

notes.en: "enjoy, take pleasure in" — 3rd-person PLURAL (injunctive, wish sense)
the Vedic subjunctive (लिङर्थे लेट्, 3.4.7) — the wish "may they enjoy"
3rd person plural — "may they enjoy" (the gods as subject)

words.gloss: the bearers (of the sacrifice), the conveyers

notes.text: वह्नि "bearer, conveyer" (from वह् "carry") — in apposition to देवासः

sequence.vyakhya: विश्वे देवासः अस्रिधः एहिमायासः अद्रुहः वह्नयः — प्रथमाबहुवचने कर्तृविशेषणानि; मेधम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; जुषन्त — प्रथमपुरुषबहुवचनम्। विश्वेदेवसूक्तत्रयं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn's grammar turns one last time: from ADDRESS to STATEMENT. Through rd032–033 the gods were vocatives ("O All-Gods, come!"); here देवासः is NOMINATIVE — the SUBJECT — qualified by a string of nominative adjectives (अस्रिधः "unfailing," एहिमायासः a bahuvrīhi "whose power approaches," अद्रुहः "guileless," वह्नयः "bearers"). The verb is no longer an imperative TO them but a 3rd-person wish ABOUT them: मेधं जुषन्त, "may they enjoy the offering." The same noun in two cases across one triplet — vocative when called, nominative when described — is the whole lesson of address vs predication. The Viśvedevas triplet, and three-quarters of RV 1.3, complete.

sequence.sentence: एकदा नरपतेः दूतः उपगोकुलम् आगच्छत्। सः राजपुरुषः नद्याः तीरे गोपकृष्णौ अपश्यत्। तौ ग्रामस्य पटुतमौ बालौ आस्ताम्। तयोः दामोदरः ज्येष्ठः महाबुद्धिः च आसीत्। दूतः तौ अवदत् — नरपतिः युवाम् द्रष्टुम् इच्छति इति। बालौ न अबिभीताम्, हसन्तौ च तेन सह अगच्छताम्।
sequence.translation: Once a king's messenger came to the vicinity of Gokula. That royal servant saw Gopa and Kṛṣṇa on the river's bank. The two were the cleverest boys of the village. Of them Dāmodara was the elder, and of great intelligence. The messenger said to them — "The king wishes to see you two." The boys were not afraid, and laughing they went with him.
sequence.teaches:
the compound types across a Gokula scene: नरपतेः and राजपुरुषः (तत्पुरुष),
उपगोकुलम् (अव्ययीभाव), गोपकृष्णौ (द्वन्द्व), दामोदरः (बहुव्रीहि), and the
superlative पटुतमौ, ज्येष्ठः.

notes.text: विग्रह: नराणाम् पतिः — "the lord of men"

षष्ठी — a षष्ठी-relation (नराणाम्) compounded → षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष

sequence.vyakhya: गोकुले पञ्च समासाः — नरपतेः, उपगोकुलम्, गोपकृष्णौ, दामोदरः, राजपुरुषः — अतिशायनम् च पटुतमौ।
sequence.vyakhya_en:
The messenger's errand carries the compound types through it. नरपतेः and
राजपुरुषः are तत्पुरुष — the lord of men, the king's man. उपगोकुलम् is an
अव्ययीभाव, उप carrying गोकुल and the whole going indeclinable. गोपकृष्णौ pairs
the two boys as a द्वन्द्व, and दामोदरः names Kṛṣṇa as a बहुव्रीहि — the one
with the cord at his belly. Of the pair पटुतमौ and ज्येष्ठः give the
superlative, तमप् beside इष्ठन्.

sequence.sentence: पा॒व॒का नः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ वाजे॑भिर्वा॒जिनी॑वती। य॒ज्ञं व॑ष्टु धि॒याव॑सुः॥
sequence.translation: Purifying Sarasvatī, rich in plenitudes through her abundances, treasure of thought — may she desire our sacrifice.
sequence.teaches: one feminine subject — सरस्वती, an ī-stem nominative — with वष्टु "may she desire" and वाजेभिः as accompaniment

notes.text: पावका = feminine of पावक "purifier" (टाप् आ by 4.1.4)

notes.role: अजाद्यतष्टाप् → feminine आ → पावका

notes.text: सरस्वती — feminine ई-stem (the नदी class you met as नदी in rd010)

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → वाजेभिः

notes.text: वाजिनीवती = वाजिनी "abundance" + मतुप् (वत्), feminine ई — "she who has abundance"

notes.en: object — what she is to desire

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

notes.en: 3rd person singular — a wish-imperative addressed about her

notes.role: लोट् च → imperative → वष्टु

words.gloss: treasure of thought, rich through insight

notes.text: padapāṭha splits धिया-वसुः; धी "thought" + वसु "wealth" — "wealthy through thought"

sequence.vyakhya: पावका सरस्वती वाजिनीवती धियावसुः — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; वाजेभिः — तृतीया; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; वष्टु — लोटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The last triplet of the hymn turns to a single FEMININE deity: सरस्वती, an ई-stem noun of the same नदी class you first declined in rd010. She is the subject (nominative), wrapped in feminine epithets — पावका ("purifying," with the टाप् feminine-आ of 4.1.4), वाजिनीवती ("rich in abundance"), धियावसुः ("treasure of thought"). The verb वष्टु is a 3rd-person SINGULAR imperative — "may she desire" — a wish made ABOUT her, not a command TO her. After the dual, singular-Indra, and plural triplets, the hymn closes on one goddess, in the feminine.

sequence.sentence: अद्य राजा सभाम् अगमत्। तत्र दूतः अवादीत् — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः च रक्षिताः। राजा तत् अश्रौषीत्, मन्त्रिणः च अपृच्छत् — केन एतत् कृतम्। मन्त्रिणः अवादिषुः — यः स्वयम् न भाषते सः एव अकार्षीत्। ततः राजा तम् वीरम् आह्वयत्, वरम् च अददात्। सः वीरः तूष्णीम् आसीत्, न च किञ्चित् अयाचत।
sequence.translation: Today the king went to the assembly. There a messenger spoke — "The enemies are defeated, and the villages protected." The king heard that, and asked the ministers — "By whom was this done?" The ministers spoke — "He who does not speak of himself is the very one who did it." Then the king summoned that hero, and gave a boon. That hero was silent, and asked for nothing.
sequence.teaches:
अगमत्, अवादीत्, अश्रौषीत्, अवादिषुः, अकार्षीत् — five aorists in one
scene. पराजिताः and रक्षिताः stand as predicates without a verb.

notes.role: लुङ् — past action → अगमत्
खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — final स् → visarga → शत्रवः

notes.en: past passive participle (क्त) with परा — predicate, no verb

notes.role: खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the plural स् → visarga → ग्रामाः
आदेशप्रत्ययोः — the सिच् स् goes ष् after the ओ

खरवसानयोर्विसर्जनीयः — the स् of ततस् → visarga

notes.en: neuter accusative with the indefinite particle

sequence.vyakhya: पञ्च लुङः एकस्मिन् प्रसङ्गे — अगमत् अवादीत् अश्रौषीत् अवादिषुः अकार्षीत्। पराजिताः रक्षिताः कृतम् इति कर्मणि क्तानि, तिङन्तम् अन्तरेण। मन्त्रिणः इति द्वितीयाबहुवचने प्रथमाबहुवचने च समानम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Five aorists carry the scene, and three of the sentences have no finite verb at all — शत्रवः पराजिताः, ग्रामाः रक्षिताः, केन एतत् कृतम् all rest on a participle. मन्त्रिणः appears twice, first as the accusative of the persons asked and then as the nominative of the persons answering; nothing in the form distinguishes them, only the verb each one stands beside. The hero's silence is the point of the last sentence and also its grammar — तूष्णीम् आसीत् and न किञ्चित् अयाचत say it twice, once with an indeclinable and once with a verb.

sequence.sentence: चो॒द॒यि॒त्री सू॒नृता॑नां॒ चेतं॑ती सुमती॒नां। य॒ज्ञं द॑धे॒ सर॑स्वती॥
sequence.translation: Impeller of true sayings, awakener of right thoughts — Sarasvatī has upheld the sacrifice.
sequence.teaches: two feminine agent-nouns governing the genitive — चोदयित्री … सूनृतानाम्, "impeller of true words" — and the perfect दधे "she has upheld"

notes.text: चोदयित्री = feminine agent-noun (तृच् → तृ + ई) of चुद् "impel" — "the urger"

notes.en: feminine agent-noun in apposition to सरस्वती (nominative)
genitive governed by the agent-noun — "impeller OF true words"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सूनृतानाम्

notes.text: चेतन्ती = feminine present participle (शतृ + ई) of चित् "perceive" — "awakening"

notes.en: feminine participle in apposition to सरस्वती

words.gloss: of right thoughts, of good intentions

notes.text: padapāṭha splits सु-मतीनाम्; सु "good" + मति "thought"

notes.en: genitive governed by the participle — "awakener OF good thoughts"

notes.role: षष्ठी शेषे → सुमतीनाम्
कर्मणि द्वितीया → यज्ञम्

words.gloss: she has upheld, she has established

notes.en: "hold, establish" — the √धा of दधाते (rd025) and दधिष्व (rd031), here PERFECT
3rd person singular — perfect middle "she has held"

sequence.vyakhya: चोदयित्री चेतन्ती सरस्वती — प्रथमैकवचने स्त्रीलिङ्गकर्तृविशेषणानि; सूनृतानां सुमतीनाम् — षष्ठी कर्तृकर्मसम्बन्धे; यज्ञम् — द्वितीया कर्मणि; दधे — लिटि प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: Sarasvatī is named by two feminine agent-words: चोदयित्री ("the impeller," a तृच्-agent-noun made feminine with ई) and चेतन्ती ("awakening," a present participle, शतृ + ई). Both GOVERN a genitive — चोदयित्री सूनृतानाम् "impeller OF true words," चेतन्ती सुमतीनाम् "awakener OF good thoughts" — the षष्ठी शेषे relation (2.3.50). Her act is दधे, "she has upheld," a PERFECT of √धा, the same root you have now seen as a present dual (दधाते, rd025), a middle imperative (दधिष्व, rd031), and now a perfect. One root, four tenses-and-moods, across the Saṃhitā.

sequence.sentence: म॒हो अर्णः॒ सर॑स्वती॒ प्र चे॑तयति के॒तुना॑। धियो॒ विश्वा॒ वि रा॑जति॥
sequence.translation: Sarasvatī makes the great flood known by her banner; she illumines all our thoughts.
sequence.teaches: two preverb+verb pairs (प्र चेतयति "makes known," वि राजति "shines over") + the instrument केतुना ("by her banner") — closing the whole hymn

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → अर्णः

words.gloss: by her banner, by her light-of-intelligence

notes.en: instrument — "BY her banner (she makes it known)"

notes.role: कर्तृकरणयोस्तृतीया → करण → केतुना

notes.en: object — what she illumines (the धी "thought" of rd027, now plural object)

notes.role: कर्मणि द्वितीया → धियः (acc. pl.)

notes.en: preverb — "apart, over," with राजति → "shines over, illumines"

sequence.vyakhya: महः अर्णः सरस्वती प्र चेतयति केतुना — द्वितीया कर्मणि, तृतीया करणे, प्रथमपुरुषैकवचनम्; धियः विश्वाः वि राजति — द्वितीयाबहुवचनं कर्मणि। ऋग्वेदस्य तृतीयं सूक्तं समाप्तम्।
sequence.vyakhya_en: The hymn closes with two preverb-verbs that mirror each other: प्र चेतयति, "she makes (it) forth-known," and वि राजति, "she shines over." Each preverb steers the sense of the verb. She makes known महः अर्णः, "the great flood" (accusative), केतुना, "by her banner" (instrument); she illumines धियः विश्वाः, "all the thoughts" (accusative plural) — the धी "thought" you have met since rd014, now the very thing the goddess of insight lights up. Object in the accusative, means in the instrumental, agent in the nominative: the कारक machinery of the whole reader, in the Veda's own words. **RV 1.3 is complete** — three hymns of the Ṛgveda (1.1, 1.2, 1.3) now read end to end.
